chapters.title: Chapter 201
paragraphs: “It’s been hard to catch sight of you lately.”
“Tell me about it. These days, I can’t tell whether I’m a bodyguard or a chief steward.”
Jin Wikyung laughed quietly at Wipeng’s complaint.
“Bear with it for a few more days. More importantly, how did those matters we discussed turn out?”
“Everything is proceeding smoothly. The Sect Leaders we brought into the fold are obedient, and the local authorities and merchant world are actively cooperating.”
If the Jin Family of Taiyuan was a ship sailing with a favorable wind, Jin Wikyung was its seasoned captain.
Starting with securing the loyalty of the smaller and mid-sized sects on the first day of the gathering, he had handled one major issue after another.
The Fire King kept the Murim side in line, while Prince Shangshan, a member of the imperial family, did the same with the authorities. As a result, there had been no trouble at all.
As for the merchant world, that went without saying.
Merchants were more sensitive to profit than anyone. Once they smelled money, it was only natural for them to come running.
After quickly organizing his thoughts, Jin Wikyung asked Wipeng, “What about the budget? How much do you think we’ll have left?”
“We’re short.”
“What?”
The corners of Wipeng’s mouth rose at Jin Wikyung’s startled expression.
“I mean we’re short on warehouses to store all the wealth.”
“...Phew.”
“Two warehouses were already full two days ago. Everything that has come in since then is being stored in empty pavilions.”
Jin Wikyung released a sigh of relief and gave a quiet laugh.
“What a windfall.”
“Great Hero Jeok’s announcement yesterday was decisive. It finally convinced those who had remained uncertain until the very end.”
“They’re the real heavyweights.”
“Indeed.”
The wider a person’s connections, the more likely they were to get pricked by thorns.

The Jin Family of Taiyuan was clearly a goose laying golden eggs, but there were also powerful sects and great families—including the Zhongnan Sect—with which it had an uneasy relationship because of the Fire King.
“That must be why Seok Family Manor suddenly requested a private meeting after remaining quiet all this time.”
Seok Family Manor was a giant that held tremendous sway over the merchant world.
The fact that they had finally stepped forward proved how certain they were of the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s potential.
“Weighing their options is what they do best. Since they came late, they’ll make up for it with a generous gift.”
“They’d better. Show them in.”
“Yes, my lord.”
Not long after Wipeng left, a plump middle-aged man entered the office.
“Oh, my! Lesser Family Head! How long has it been?”
“It’s been a long time, Chief Ha.”
The middle-aged man was an Outer Steward of Seok Family Manor. Though he was only one of five, he wielded immense authority.
Jin Wikyung smiled gently at the man as he repeatedly wiped away his sweat.
“It’s been three years since we last met. How is your Lord?”
“He’s as hale and hearty as a young man in his prime. As it happens, he heard the wonderful news and wishes to meet you. As you know, Lesser Family Head, he wasn’t feeling well the last time...”
“Yes, I remember. Quite clearly.”
Jin Wikyung vividly remembered that day three years ago.
He had waited a full fifteen days before being granted a private audience, only to leave Seok Family Manor as though he had been chased out without ever seeing the Lord’s face.
Finding the sedan chair of a high-ranking official outside Seok Family Manor’s main gate had been a coincidence.
That was what he had chosen to believe.
That’s how the Murim works.
But now their positions had changed.
The past three years had been short but eventful, and the arrogant Outer Steward who had once treated him like a beggar had somehow become a humble merchant.
So he does know how to speak politely. That’s a first.
With a strange sense of amusement, Jin Wikyung listened attentively to Chief Ha.
He readily accepted Seok Family Manor’s proposal to enter the Shanxi merchant world in earnest with the cooperation of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
Naturally, the details would need to be reviewed, but Seok Family Manor’s offer was extraordinarily generous.
“You’ve made a better offer than I expected. Generous enough to make me wonder whether this is really all right.”
Chief Ha rubbed his hands together and laughed.
“I’m a merchant to the bone. I never conduct business at a loss.”
There were different levels among merchants.
A Third Rate merchant exchanged goods. A Second Rate merchant purchased goods that could leave him a profit. A First Rate merchant bought the future.
Seok Family Manor was one of the greatest merchant houses in the world. They were aiming not for an immediate profit, but for returns dozens of times greater in the years to come.
You won’t make that much off us. Our family will never dance to your tune.
In stark contrast to his thoughts, Jin Wikyung smiled broadly.
Life was not so easy that one could say whatever one wished and reveal every honest feeling. That was especially true when dealing with a cunning merchant.
“I’ll arrange a place for you to stay. We can discuss the finer details then.”
“Thank you, Lesser Family Head.”
Chief Ha was about to rise from his seat when he stopped.
“Is there something else?”
“This is a difficult request, but might I be allowed to meet Great Hero Jeok?”

Being an Outer Steward of Seok Family Manor was a position of considerable authority, but the Fire King was an exception. Since arriving at the Jin Family of Taiyuan, Jeok Cheongang had not granted a private audience to a single honored guest.
Chief Ha continued wiping away his sweat.
“It has proved extraordinarily difficult. I tried visiting him myself, and I even sent a subordinate to discreetly request a meeting, but...”
“Oh, dear. Great Hero Jeok probably didn’t take that well.”
“Indeed. My man came back nearly crippled. That is why I have shamelessly come to ask you for this favor, Lesser Family Head.”
Suppressing his laughter, Jin Wikyung replied, “I’m not sure. It might be possible after the gathering ends, but the next few days will be difficult.”
“I noticed he hasn’t been seen since yesterday. May I ask why?”
“He must be instructing my second younger brother.”
“Ah, I see. My apologies for intruding.”
Once Chief Ha had left the office, Jin Wikyung could no longer hold back his laughter.
The exhaustion weighing on his body and mind after several days of hosting the gathering seemed to lift all at once. In a cheerful voice, he called for his most trusted subordinate.
“Wipeng. Who’s next?”
It was early morning, before the sun had even risen.
The person who woke me was neither Hyuk Mujin nor Cheongpung.
Splash!
“Gah!”
The first thing I saw after opening my eyes to the cold-water ambush was Jeok Cheongang, glaring at me with his eyes wide open.
“W-What are you doing?”
“You slept like the dead until this hour. Are you out of your mind?”
“I only slept for two shichen. How is that sleeping like the dead?”
Jeok Cheongang launched into a lecture as I stared at him in disbelief.
“In four hours, you bastard, this old man could swing a weapon a thousand more times. And where did you learn the disrespect of not even paying your morning respects to your Master?”
“...Master?”
Jeok Cheongang flinched and stammered for a moment.
“W-We need to look that way to other people, don’t we?”
“To avoid suspicion, we need to act like a real master! Like a real Disciple! That’s the bare minimum!”
“Ah, yes.”
So the pioneer of method acting in the Murim was right here.
At my lukewarm response, Jeok Cheongang’s face turned bright red.
“Regardless, I won’t stand for you loafing around like this. Come with me. Now.”
“Where?”
“There’s a place this old man has picked out.”
I assumed he had found a secluded training ground, but Jeok Cheongang led me out of the Jin Family estate altogether and into a nearby mountain.
Trees with trunks easily several meters around grew thickly in every direction, and the ground was firm.
“This will do.”
Jeok Cheongang stopped in a wide clearing and set the pack slung across his back on a tree stump.
“What’s that?”
“Never mind that. It’s something we’ll use later.”
“Later?”
“Yes. Things that will make you writhe with pleasure.”
Why was I suddenly thinking of whips, candlesticks, and masks?
As I cast an anxious sidelong glance at the pack, Jeok Cheongang spoke sternly.
“Stop sticking your nose where it doesn’t belong and take out your spear.”
“Ah, yes.”
I’d had the good sense to bring several spears, and I planted them in the ground.
The reason Jeok Cheongang had come to find me so early was obvious.
Training.
Though he tried hard not to show it, Jeok Cheongang wanted to take me as his Disciple.
He kept stubbornly denying it because he still wasn’t certain himself.
He’s already made one painful mistake.
The wound Jopil had left in Jeok Cheongang’s heart had not yet healed.
That was why he would surely keep watching and weighing whether he could accept someone like me as his Disciple before making his decision.
Even if he doesn’t pass down the Fire Gate Clan’s supreme martial arts right away, he’ll still do his best to teach me.
This was guidance from a Supreme Peak master.
A single word of advice from someone who had gone farther down this path than I had was worth more than a thousand pieces of gold.
I lifted a well-balanced iron spear and swallowed.
“What do I do now?”
“Come at me.”
“Pardon?”
“I said come at me. Use all your strength.”
A smile spread across Jeok Cheongang’s wrinkled lips.
“Thirty minutes. If you can make this old man retreat even one step, you win.”
Ding.

System Quest One Step Back has been created. Quest One Step Back Fire King Jeok Cheongang wants to see your true ability. Make him retreat within the time limit and prove your worth to him! Grade: Peak Restriction: Jin Taekyung Mission: One Step Back (Incomplete) Reward: ??? Failure: ???
Make him retreat one step?
At first glance, it seemed easy, but there was a reason it was a Peak-Grade Quest.
Especially when the opponent was Fire King Jeok Cheongang.
I looked away from the Quest window and found Jeok Cheongang waiting with a relaxed expression.
“All right. Begin.”
Beep.
System 29:59
The moment the time-limit window appeared in the air, I kicked off the ground and charged toward him.
Whoosh!
Whoosh!
The spearhead tore through the air. Compressed air burst outward, sending the old man’s white hair flying.
Jeok Cheongang dodged Jin Taekyung’s first thrust and thought,
What is this kid?
Fast.
And the spear carried enough force to shatter a boulder.
Even Jeok Cheongang, who had already examined Jin Taekyung’s body once, had not anticipated such speed and strength.
Whirl—whoosh! Boom!
Second strike, third, fourth...
He stabbed, slashed, and swept upward.
Every time Jeok Cheongang evaded the shower of spearheads pouring down like torrential rain, his astonishment grew like a snowball.
He’s seasoned. As if he were born on a battlefield.
He was only twenty-one. Yet the trajectories and movements traced by his spearhead were no worse than those of any famous master in the martial world.
No. If anything, they were better.
Having encountered countless martial artists during the Great Faction War, Jeok Cheongang had learned one thing well.
A true martial artist is forged through countless real battles.
The Nine Sects and One Gang.
The Five Great Families.
They were unquestionably great powers that held sway over the world, but only a small number of their members had ever survived at the brink of death.
That was why the Demonic Cult, which had grown through conquest and the principle of Might Makes Right, had managed to swallow half the Central Plains.
How many disciples of prestigious great sects had died at the beginning of the war?
But this kid is different.
There was nothing hollow in his opening stance, and not a trace of hesitation.
The spearhead relentlessly seeking every vital point on his body and those cold, hardened eyes were badges worn only by those who had fought countless real battles and seen blood.
Shriek—whoosh!
The spinning spearhead vibrated.
Humm. Humm. Humm.
It sounded like hundreds of bees beating their wings, and the spearhead shooting toward him was sharper than a venomous stinger.
He’s only been practicing martial arts for three months? This kid?
Judging by his movements alone, it looked more like three years.
No, thirty.
Jeok Cheongang knew nothing of the seven years Jin Taekyung had spent steeped in battle. He could only marvel.
...What an incredible kid.
Jeok Cheongang himself had spent his entire life obsessed with martial arts.
Yet even for someone who had achieved a great realm, what Jin Taekyung was displaying now was incomprehensible.
The greatest martial talent in history, was it?
Remembering Jin Wikyung’s words, Jeok Cheongang’s figure trembled with joy and awe.
Yes. You were right.
Overcome by the lingering emotion, he slowly closed his eyes.
Whoosh!
A streak of light shot toward his chest.
Jeok Cheongang’s eyes snapped half-open. At the same time, his wrinkled hand seized the spearhead.
Crack!
His hands blazed with red flames, crushing and melting the spearhead.
Molten metal dripped onto the ground hardened by the cold wind.
“...Wow, shit. Isn’t that cheating?”
Jin Taekyung muttered in disbelief.
Jeok Cheongang grinned at him.
“We’re just getting started.”

chapters.title: Chapter 202
paragraphs: Half an hour. A full thirty minutes.
Even if my opponent was the Fire King, I’d thought that if I put everything I had into it, I could make him retreat a little—just a little.
At least, I had until a moment ago.
How does that make any sense?
I backed away, appalled.
He had caught a spearhead spinning with internal energy in his bare hand. That made about as much sense as sticking your hand into a grinder.
But when that hand belonged to Fire King Jeok Cheongang, things were different.
Drip. Hiss.
Steam rose as molten metal struck the ground. Jeok Cheongang clicked his tongue at the sight.
“Maybe it melted so quickly because it was scrap iron. You must have come into plenty of money this time, so tell them to use better iron.”
“H-How did you do that?”
“You can do it too.”
“Me?”
“Of course. Once you possess at least two jiazi’s worth of internal energy and master our sect’s martial arts to their utmost limits.”
“Easy, right?”
As if.
When I stared at him in disbelief, Jeok Cheongang opened his mouth and let out a huge yawn.
“Taking it easy, aren’t you? If I were you, I’d spend that time swinging my spear one more time.”
“I was just about to.”
I glanced at the time limit floating in the air and pulled out another spear.
Sixteen minutes remained. Nearly half the time had already passed.
I only need to make him retreat one step. Just one step...
But that was easier said than done.
I glared at Jeok Cheongang, who still stood leisurely in the same spot, and drew a deep breath.
“Huuup—”
Whoosh!
I kicked off the ground and charged. One long stride erased the distance between us, and I thrust out my spear.
Screeeech!
The corners of Jeok Cheongang’s mouth rose as he watched me.
“I believe I said we were just getting started.”
Boom!
He stamped his foot once.
The effect was terrifying.
The ground shook as though an earthquake had struck, and a flock of birds perched on the bare branches took flight.
In the slowed-down world, Jeok Cheongang’s hand blurred for an instant and struck away dozens of stones floating in the air.
Straight toward me.
Shishishishik!
Dozens of stones, each propelled by internal energy. Every one of them was as deadly as a concealed weapon.
They must have carried even greater destructive power than the Head Elder’s finger-flicking technique I had faced in the past.
But...
I’ve grown stronger too.
Humm. Humm. Humm.
My spear let out a deep hum.
I felt a unity with it on an entirely different level from when I had still been First Rate.
The Jin Family’s Spear Technique, which had already reached Great Completion, and my footwork technique had merged into perfect harmony.
The insight I had gained from crossing the wall of the Peak realm flowed through them, revealing spear paths I could never have imagined before.
And then there were my increased stats.
I can do this.
Crack.
The spear shaft buckled beneath my crushing grip.
Then, in the next instant—
Whoooosh!
The power compressed like a spring exploded outward. Wind burst from the spearhead’s arc as I swung it sideways with all my strength.
It was internal energy unleashed—and a storm of my own making.
Pssshhh.
Fine dust scattered in every direction, the last remnants of the stones caught in the spear’s path.
“Well, look at you.”
The obstacle was gone. Now it was time to hit him.
I charged at Jeok Cheongang, whose expression was equal parts disbelief and delight.
Whoosh! Shishishishik!
The spearhead, brimming with internal energy, tore through the air.
Jeok Cheongang dipped lightly at the waist to evade it. At the same time, heat surged from his right hand.
Whoom!
Blazing flames shot toward me—a mass of condensed Scorching Yang Qi.
I gritted my teeth and swung the spear shaft.
Clang! Krrrra-boom!
A deafening roar erupted, and tremendous force and heat engulfed my entire body. Jeok Cheongang burst into laughter at the sight of me standing there, charred black from head to toe.
“What kind of idiot tries to knock that away?”
“...Hah. I almost had it.”
“Don’t make me laugh. If this old man had used his full strength, you would have died just now.”
I answered sullenly.
“I knocked it away because I thought I could.”
“And that’s why you look like that?”
“...I didn’t know this would happen.”
“I’ll give you credit for staying on your feet—and for actually blocking it.”
“But weren’t you only supposed to defend?”
“Who told you that?”
Damn. Come to think of it, he hadn’t.
I ripped off my half-charred shirt and tossed it aside.
“For someone bearing the mighty title of Fire King, aren’t you using a little too much force against a kid young enough to be your grandson?”
“You’re still wet behind the ears, yet you swing a spear at an old man old enough to be your great-grandfather? And you call yourself the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi?”
“You’re a Supreme Peak master, Old Master!”
“You possess the Heavenly Martial Physique.”
“Do you seriously call that mal?”
“If it isn’t mal—words—then is it a foal?”
“What? Why are you looking at me like that?”
Grind.
My hand tightened around the spear. I let out a hot breath.
“Hoo. Now I’m going to do this properly.”
Jeok Cheongang dug inside his ear with his pinky.
“Hm? What was that? I can’t hear a weakling who got turned into charcoal with one hit.”
God, I hated this.
When he’d been tearing apart the Roaring Fury Swordsman, his banter had been the most satisfying thing in the world. Now that I was on the receiving end, it made my stomach turn.
“What are you going to do if I really make you retreat even one step?”
“It would be faster for the Heavenly Demon to become the Abbot of Shaolin.”
“Grrk.”
“You should only have enough time left to drink a glass of cold water. Do you think you can make this old man retreat before then? Not a chance.”

“Hm?”

I couldn’t tell exactly what emotion lay in his gaze, but one thing was certain: he had taken the bait halfway.
I waved a hand as though I hadn’t noticed.

That sealed it.
“...Look at this brat.”
Jeok Cheongang’s cheek twitched, his expression difficult to describe. Finally, he nodded.
“I can see straight through your little scheme, but fine. Go ahead and try.”
“You mean it?”
“Haven’t you heard that the Fire King’s word is worth a thousand pieces of gold? Once this old man says something, he always keeps his word.”
“...Ah. Yes.”
He’d even changed the first word and plagiarized the proverb.
Either way, I’d achieved what I wanted. I discarded the half-charred spear and pulled out my third one.
This one will probably be single-use too.
But if that was the price of completing a Peak-Grade Quest, it was absurdly cheap.
Jeok Cheongang narrowed his eyes as I adjusted my stance.
“You aren’t planning to use poison or some underhanded trick, are you?”
“Come on. Of course not.”
I grinned and added,
“A man settles things with one big blow.”
Gooooong.
The spear shaft trembled after swallowing forty-five years of internal energy.
Kraaaaaash!
A massive boulder went flying, and a tree as thick as a man was torn up by the roots.
Jeok Cheongang stood tall at the center of the clearing, which looked as though a storm had just swept through it.
He had been driven back exactly five steps.
“You—you...”
Looking half-dazed, Jeok Cheongang stared back and forth between me and the devastated surroundings.
The beautiful wilderness from moments ago had become a grotesque landscape of broken and uprooted trees and displaced boulders.
All of it was the result of a single thrust—One Annihilation.
“W-What in the world did you do?”
“Well, I’m not sure. I didn’t expect it to be this powerful either.”
It was the first time I’d used One Annihilation since reaching the Peak realm.
I’d expected its destructive power to have increased now that my internal energy had grown by leaps and bounds, but I hadn’t imagined anything like this.
Jeok Cheongang shouted at my uncertain answer.
“You think that makes any sense?”
“That’s what I’m saying. Wow, this is seriously insa—”
The world spun before my eyes, and my legs buckled.
I had poured out every last shred of strength and internal energy without leaving so much as a speck behind.
A wrinkled hand caught me as I staggered. The gaze of the man looking down at me was impossibly complex.
“I’ll hear the whole story later. Rest for now.”
As he spoke, powerful energy flowed into me through my back. It had to be internal energy that Jeok Cheongang was channeling into me.
I’d expected it to be scorching, like swallowing the sun, but his internal energy was warm and vast.
Its gentle warmth brought on an irresistible wave of drowsiness.
“O-Old Master.”
“Don’t resist. Let yourself go.”
“...Right?”
“Hm?”
“I really won, right?”
Jeok Cheongang’s eyelids trembled. At last, he answered in a hoarse voice.
“Yes. This old man lost.”
“Heh heh heh.”
A laugh escaped me before I could stop it.
Even though the fight had been subject to countless restrictions, I was filled with joy at having made Jeok Cheongang—a master counted among the greatest under heaven—retreat.
Ding.
System Quest One Step Back was completed successfully! Quest reward...
The fading sound of the System notification was the last thing I heard before falling into a deep sleep.
That boy. He certainly sleeps well.
Jeok Cheongang stared silently at the dead-asleep Jin Taekyung for a long while.
His strong, open features made him look like an innocent boy, yet also like a young man who had already weathered the world once over.
What a strange boy. What a strange boy indeed.
The longer Jeok Cheongang watched him, the stronger that impression became.
He had thought he’d already peeled away one layer of the boy’s shell, only to discover even harder, more dazzling scales hidden beneath it.
A Hidden Dragon.
This young man, sleeping so peacefully that he was even snoring, was a dragon that had yet to obtain its dragon pearl.
That only made Jeok Cheongang more curious. How far would Jin Taekyung go? Would he live long enough to see the boy’s true limits?
Especially that final strike...
Jeok Cheongang looked around once more and let out a hollow laugh.
Could this really be the work of a young prodigy who had only just passed twenty?
He was certain that even the Sword Saint of years past had not been capable of this much.
The Martial God. Perhaps he could have done it.
A martial artist born human, yet called a god. The one person who had ever inspired awe in Fire King Jeok Cheongang.
What had he been like in his youth—the man revered not merely as the greatest under heaven, but as the greatest of all time?
As Jeok Cheongang imagined Jin Taekyung as he was now alongside the Martial God in his youth, a quiet laugh escaped him.
For this old man to entertain such a thought... The boy’s talent must truly be great enough to compare with the Martial God’s.
Jeok Cheongang gazed deeply at Jin Taekyung, then rose to his feet.
By now, a desire was rapidly taking root within him—the desire to place a dragon pearl in the hands of this young Hidden Dragon.
Fly freely above the clouds. Become a Heavenly Dragon capable of covering the world with rain and wind.
Grrrrrk.
At the snore that came instead of an answer, Jeok Cheongang burst into hearty laughter.

chapters.title: Chapter 203
paragraphs: I read through the System message floating before my eyes.
It was the Quest reward notification I hadn’t gotten a chance to check before passing out.
System Quest One Step Back was completed successfully! - You have acquired a large amount of EXP! - Level Up! - Level Up! - You have acquired 20 Bonus Points!
That’s insanely generous.
Two level-ups, plus bonus points. All told, a single Quest had given me the equivalent of roughly four levels.
Maybe the reward was bigger than expected because of who my opponent had been.
Close window.
Shhk.
The translucent holographic window disappeared, revealing Jeok Cheongang walking toward me.
He held the satchel he had brought with him.
“Are you awake?”
“Ah, yes. Just woke up.”
“How does your body feel?”
“Light as a feather.”
Jeok Cheongang looked me up and down, then nodded.
“I suppose young men really do recover quickly. We can move straight on to the next step.”
“Ah, the next step. Sounds good.”
“I knew you’d say that. This old man prepared something perfect for you. Let’s see...”
“Old Master.”
“Hm?”
“I mean, that’s all well and good, but...”
I gave him an awkward smile.
“Could you release my acupoints before we start?”
I meant that literally.
I had no idea what had happened, but my entire body had been frozen stiff ever since I opened my eyes.
Jeok Cheongang had struck my Paralysis Acupoint while I was asleep.
As things stood, the most I could do was speak.
“I’m sure you meant well, but we should probably get started on the next round of training... Heh heh.”
“Ah, yes. Training.”
Jeok Cheongang rummaged through the satchel.
“This is the next round of training.”
“Getting my acupoints sealed is training?”
Or was releasing them supposed to be the training?
While I was trying to figure that out, Jeok Cheongang pulled something from the satchel.
“Here it is. I forgot I’d stuffed it all the way at the bottom.”
“...Isn’t that a rope?”
“That’s right.”
He slung the sturdy rope over his shoulder, strode over, and hoisted me into the air.
“W-Wait. What are you doing?”
“You’ll find out soon enough.”
He carried me toward a massive boulder.
It had been lodged deep in the earth for who knew how long and was so large that several grown men with their arms outstretched couldn’t have encircled it.
“Hmm. This should do.”
Jeok Cheongang muttered under his breath and brought the edge of his hand down on the boulder.
Shhk. Shhk.
The red Force around his hand sliced the enormous boulder apart like cheesecake. After only a few cuts, he had transformed it into a five-star stone bed.
“This should be just right.”
“W-Wait a second. You’re not planning to tie me to this thing, are you?”
“Tie you? I’m securing you.”
How was that any different from calling shit feces?
At any rate, I was beginning to tremble.
Actually, the Paralysis Acupoint had been suspicious enough from the beginning. So was the satchel Jeok Cheongang had been rummaging through this whole time.
He’s not actually going to pull out a whip and a mask, is he?
While my pupils quaked, Jeok Cheongang began securing me to the boulder with the rope.
He wound it around various parts of my body, tied it tight, then smiled in satisfaction.
“This should keep you from falling off.”
“Phew.”
“What was that sigh of relief for?”
“I’m relieved it isn’t a tortoise-shell knot.”
“A tortoise-shell knot? What’s that?”
“...A type of restraint technique.”
“Restraint? Something they use in the military, I take it.”
Mostly Japanese guys use it.
Well, whatever.
I was now tied down with my arms and legs spread wide.
Both wrists, both ankles, my chest, stomach, and legs. It really did look as though he was trying to secure me rather than restrain me.
Then again, he already struck my Paralysis Acupoint. There’s no need to tie me up that tightly.
But what the hell was he planning to do?
As my eyes darted around, Jeok Cheongang finally opened the satchel.
At that very moment—
Whoosh!
“Gasp.”
An indescribable fragrance burst from it.
A crisp, refreshing sensation entered through my nose and spread throughout my body, strong enough to cure a chronic case of rhinitis on the spot.
My eyes widened as I stared at the objects inside.
“These are...”
Three roots lay neatly arranged within the satchel.
Jeok Cheongang picked up the reddish roots and laid them across his palm.
“Elixirs.”
“Whoa. Where did you find something this valuable?”
“I searched the storehouse. It was packed to the rafters with useless junk, so finding them was a damn nuisance.”
Mountains of silk, gold, silver, and jewels were nothing but worthless clutter in his eyes.
But he was a martial artist to his very bones. Elixirs or martial arts manuals that could improve his martial arts were another matter entirely.
“To be honest, these elixirs aren’t especially potent. If all you wanted was more internal energy, a hundred-year-old He Shou Wu or snow ginseng would be far better.”
“Then why...”
“You’re wondering why I bothered bringing these?”
“Yes.”
“Because only these can provide pure Scorching Yang Qi. Swallowing every elixir you can find might increase the amount of your internal energy, but its power would suffer.”
“Oh.”
I thought I understood what he meant.
Put simply, it was a matter of fuel. You could pile on all the firewood you wanted, but oil was what made a fire explode.
What he held wasn’t firewood. It was oil that would further strengthen the Scorching Yang Qi already inside me.
Still, I’m touched.
I hadn’t expected Jeok Cheongang to go this far for me.

For a man as cantankerous as him to endure the hassle of personally selecting and bringing me elixirs filled with Scorching Yang Qi could only mean that he truly intended to teach me the Fire Gate Clan’s martial arts.
And I’m not even officially his Disciple yet.
A man with a warm heart and warm internal energy.
That was the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.
When he met my heated gaze, he flinched and took a step back.
“W-What’s with that stare?”
“Nothing. You just seem like a really good person, Old Master.”
“You brought those for me to eat, right?”
Jeok Cheongang hesitated before answering.
“...They merely caught my eye, so I brought them along.”
“I see.”
“This old man kept the better ones for himself.”
“Yes. Heh heh.”
“Stop laughing!”
Jeok Cheongang barked, then hastily changed the subject.
“A-Anyway, this old man will now use these elixirs to open your acupoints.”
I had been thinking of teasing him a little more, but what he’d just said sounded serious. My ears perked up before I knew it.
“You’re going to open my acupoints?”

“You heard me. When this old man examined your body before, your muscles and bones were exceptional, just as one would expect of the Heavenly Martial Physique, but you had a considerable amount of turbid qi inside you.”
“Oh.”
“I heard that until recently, you spent your life drowning in wine and women. Even the finest sword will lose its edge if neglected for too long. The Heavenly Martial Physique is no exception.”
I couldn’t deny it.
The Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique was extremely stable, but it lacked power and efficiency when circulating internal energy.
I circulated my qi whenever I had the chance, but the traces left by twenty years of slacking off had yet to disappear.
“Then...”

“This old man will use the elixirs and my internal energy to burn every last bit of turbid qi from your body. For you, it should be far more effective than cleansing the sinews and washing the marrow.”
“That’s welcome news.”
“I doubt you’ll find it quite so welcome.”
“What?”
“You’ll find out soon enough.”
Before I could say anything else, he sealed my Mute Acupoint. My tongue went rigid, trapping a silent cry inside my mouth.
What the hell is this?
Now I really was a corpse with its eyes open.
Jeok Cheongang grinned down at me as I lay frozen like a plaster statue.
“First, let’s get those elixirs into you.”
His wrinkled fingers pried open my jaw and slipped all three roots into my mouth.
For a moment, the taste of dirt and a crisp coolness filled my mouth. Then the hard roots melted the instant they touched my tongue and flowed down my throat into my stomach.
The next moment—
Ding.

System You have consumed Fire Spirit Grass! - You have consumed Red Flower Grass! - You have consumed Flame Red Grass! - Quest Acupoint Opening has been created! - You cannot refuse this Quest. Forced progression will begin!
Gah!
System notifications rang out one after another as tremendous heat swept through my body.
Only then did I understand what Jeok Cheongang had meant.
It fucking hurts!
With my acupoints sealed, I couldn’t scream or thrash around. All I could do was stare wide-eyed.
Just as I hurriedly tried to draw up my internal energy, Jeok Cheongang rolled up his worn sleeves.
“All right, then. Shall we begin in earnest?”
“Bear with it, no matter how much it hurts. Pain is temporary, but martial arts last a lifetime.”
Tap. Tap-tap-tap-tap!
His fingers blurred as they jabbed and tapped all over my body.
Each impact scattered my internal energy, allowing the unfamiliar energy of the elixirs to race through me. Trapped in the boiling heat, I screamed without a sound.
AAAAAAAAARGH!
Unlike Jin Taekyung’s bloodshot eyes, strained by unbearable pain, Jeok Cheongang’s gleamed with fervor.
It’s proceeding smoothly. No, explosively.
Was this the Heavenly Martial Physique at work?
The speed at which the internal energy spread was astonishing. The more than thirty years of energy contained within the elixirs ran wild through every minor meridian in Jin Taekyung’s body.
Jin Taekyung tried to raise his own internal energy and suppress it, but that was not what Jeok Cheongang wanted.
He can tame it later. For now, it must be allowed to run wild.
A tamed fighting bull sometimes forgot how to charge.
The newly infused energy of thirty years had to break through everything in its path without restriction.
The attempt was dangerous enough that a single mistake could cause qi deviation. Even Jeok Cheongang, a Supreme Peak master, swallowed dryly as his fingers continued to move.
Gyeonjeong, Amun, Bongan, Ip-dong...
Tap. Tap-tap!
Following his guidance, hundreds of acupoints opened and closed over and over. Before long, black sweat poured from Jin Taekyung’s entire body, accompanied by a musty odor.
The stench was vile enough to make even someone with an iron stomach gag, but the corners of Jeok Cheongang’s mouth twitched with delight.
It worked!
This was proof that a tremendous amount of turbid qi was being expelled.
As if to confirm his conclusion, the sweat gradually lightened and the stench slowly faded.
Before long, the sweat became clear, and a pleasant body scent wafted through the air. Astonishment filled Jeok Cheongang’s eyes.
Already?
It was fast. Far too fast.
The process he had expected to take at least three shichen was already nearing completion in less than one.
Even more astonishing was the fact that the energy of the elixirs had barely diminished.
Ordinarily, a considerable amount of energy would be lost in the process of purging the turbid qi and circulating what remained.
Jin Taekyung was different.
As expected of the Heavenly Martial Physique... It truly lives up to its name.
At this rate, he could remove all the turbid qi and still gain the full thirty years of internal energy.
Yet instead of satisfaction, greed and indecision filled Jeok Cheongang’s eyes.
What if we push further?
The Conception Vessel and the Governor Vessel—the mountain known collectively as the Conception and Governor Vessels.
It was a realm most martial artists of the Murim could not reach even after devoting their entire lives to training.
Breaking through it required both enormous internal energy and enlightenment, but it might be possible now.
The Heavenly Martial Physique. And my help.
Even so, attempting to open the Conception and Governor Vessels at once was dangerous.
Leaving everything else aside, Jeok Cheongang’s greatest concern was whether Jin Taekyung could withstand the pain.
What should I do?
After agonizing over it again and again, Jeok Cheongang finally spoke.
“I think you can open the Conception and Governor Vessels.”
Jin Taekyung’s bloodshot eyes trembled as he endured the pain. Unable to answer, he could only listen as Jeok Cheongang continued.
“But you’ll have to accept the risks that come with it. The pain will likely be beyond anything you’ve experienced so far. A single mistake could cost you your life.”
“The choice is yours. If you trust this old man and wish to leave it in my hands, blink twice.”
The next moment, Jin Taekyung blinked without hesitation.
Two blinks, without the slightest trace of doubt.
Seeing the unwavering trust in his eyes, Jeok Cheongang felt something warm rise within his chest.
Has this brat truly trusted me that deeply?
Suppressing the swell of emotion, he forced the corners of his mouth upward.
“All right. Let’s give it a try.”
At the same time, an immense torrent of internal energy flowed from his fingertips into Jin Taekyung’s body.
Ding.
System Information for Quest Acupoint Opening has changed! - Quest Conception and Governor Vessels has been created! The difficulty and rewards have been adjusted to reflect the updated information!
As I listened to the System notification, one thought crossed my mind.
No, fuck...
I was sure I’d only blinked once.

sentences.text: I read through the System message floating before my eyes.
It was the Quest reward notification I hadn’t gotten a chance to check before passing out.
System Quest One Step Back was completed successfully! - You have acquired a large amount of EXP! - Level Up! - Level Up! - You have acquired 20 Bonus Points!
That’s insanely generous.
Two level-ups, plus bonus points.
All told, a single Quest had given me the equivalent of roughly four levels.
Maybe the reward was bigger than expected because of who my opponent had been.
Close window.
Shhk.
The translucent holographic window disappeared, revealing Jeok Cheongang walking toward me.
He held the satchel he had brought with him.
“Are you awake?”
“Ah, yes.
Just woke up.”
“How does your body feel?”
“Light as a feather.”
Jeok Cheongang looked me up and down, then nodded.
“I suppose young men really do recover quickly.
We can move straight on to the next step.”
“Ah, the next step.
Sounds good.”
“I knew you’d say that.
This old man prepared something perfect for you.
Let’s see...”
“Old Master.”
“Hm?”
“I mean, that’s all well and good, but...”
I gave him an awkward smile.
“Could you release my acupoints before we start?”
I meant that literally.

Jeok Cheongang had struck my Paralysis Acupoint while I was asleep.
As things stood, the most I could do was speak.
“I’m sure you meant well, but we should probably get started on the next round of training...
Heh heh.”
“Ah, yes.
Training.”
Jeok Cheongang rummaged through the satchel.
“This is the next round of training.”
“Getting my acupoints sealed is training?”
Or was releasing them supposed to be the training?

“Here it is.
I forgot I’d stuffed it all the way at the bottom.”
“...Isn’t that a rope?”
“That’s right.”
He slung the sturdy rope over his shoulder, strode over, and hoisted me into the air.
“W-Wait.
What are you doing?”
“You’ll find out soon enough.”
He carried me toward a massive boulder.
It had been lodged deep in the earth for who knew how long and was so large that several grown men with their arms outstretched couldn’t have encircled it.
“Hmm.
This should do.”
Jeok Cheongang muttered under his breath and brought the edge of his hand down on the boulder.
Shhk.
Shhk.
The red Force around his hand sliced the enormous boulder apart like cheesecake.
After only a few cuts, he had transformed it into a five-star stone bed.
“This should be just right.”
“W-Wait a second.
You’re not planning to tie me to this thing, are you?”
“Tie you?
I’m securing you.”
How was that any different from calling shit feces?
At any rate, I was beginning to tremble.
Actually, the Paralysis Acupoint had been suspicious enough from the beginning.
So was the satchel Jeok Cheongang had been rummaging through this whole time.
He’s not actually going to pull out a whip and a mask, is he?
While my pupils quaked, Jeok Cheongang began securing me to the boulder with the rope.
He wound it around various parts of my body, tied it tight, then smiled in satisfaction.
“This should keep you from falling off.”
“Phew.”
“What was that sigh of relief for?”
“I’m relieved it isn’t a tortoise-shell knot.”
“A tortoise-shell knot?
What’s that?”
“...A type of restraint technique.”
“Restraint?
Something they use in the military, I take it.”
Mostly Japanese guys use it.
Well, whatever.
I was now tied down with my arms and legs spread wide.
Both wrists, both ankles, my chest, stomach, and legs.
It really did look as though he was trying to secure me rather than restrain me.
Then again, he already struck my Paralysis Acupoint.
There’s no need to tie me up that tightly.
But what the hell was he planning to do?
As my eyes darted around, Jeok Cheongang finally opened the satchel.
At that very moment—
Whoosh!
“Gasp.”
An indescribable fragrance burst from it.
A crisp, refreshing sensation entered through my nose and spread throughout my body, strong enough to cure a chronic case of rhinitis on the spot.
My eyes widened as I stared at the objects inside.
“These are...”
Three roots lay neatly arranged within the satchel.
Jeok Cheongang picked up the reddish roots and laid them across his palm.
“Elixirs.”
“Whoa.
Where did you find something this valuable?”
“I searched the storehouse.
It was packed to the rafters with useless junk, so finding them was a damn nuisance.”
Mountains of silk, gold, silver, and jewels were nothing but worthless clutter in his eyes.
But he was a martial artist to his very bones.
Elixirs or martial arts manuals that could improve his martial arts were another matter entirely.
“To be honest, these elixirs aren’t especially potent.
If all you wanted was more internal energy, a hundred-year-old He Shou Wu or snow ginseng would be far better.”
“Then why...”
“You’re wondering why I bothered bringing these?”
“Yes.”
“Because only these can provide pure Scorching Yang Qi.
Swallowing every elixir you can find might increase the amount of your internal energy, but its power would suffer.”
“Oh.”
I thought I understood what he meant.
Put simply, it was a matter of fuel.
You could pile on all the firewood you wanted, but oil was what made a fire explode.
What he held wasn’t firewood.
It was oil that would further strengthen the Scorching Yang Qi already inside me.
Still, I’m touched.
I hadn’t expected Jeok Cheongang to go this far for me.

For a man as cantankerous as him to endure the hassle of personally selecting and bringing me elixirs filled with Scorching Yang Qi could only mean that he truly intended to teach me the Fire Gate Clan’s martial arts.
And I’m not even officially his Disciple yet.
A man with a warm heart and warm internal energy.
That was the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.
When he met my heated gaze, he flinched and took a step back.
“W-What’s with that stare?”
“Nothing.
You just seem like a really good person, Old Master.”
“You brought those for me to eat, right?”
Jeok Cheongang hesitated before answering.
“...They merely caught my eye, so I brought them along.”
“I see.”
“This old man kept the better ones for himself.”
“Yes.
Heh heh.”
“Stop laughing!”
Jeok Cheongang barked, then hastily changed the subject.
“A-Anyway, this old man will now use these elixirs to open your acupoints.”
I had been thinking of teasing him a little more, but what he’d just said sounded serious.
My ears perked up before I knew it.
“You’re going to open my acupoints?”
“You heard me.

When this old man examined your body before, your muscles and bones were exceptional, just as one would expect of the Heavenly Martial Physique, but you had a considerable amount of turbid qi inside you.”
“Oh.”
“I heard that until recently, you spent your life drowning in wine and women.
Even the finest sword will lose its edge if neglected for too long.
The Heavenly Martial Physique is no exception.”
I couldn’t deny it.
The Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique was extremely stable, but it lacked power and efficiency when circulating internal energy.
I circulated my qi whenever I had the chance, but the traces left by twenty years of slacking off had yet to disappear.
“Then...”
“This old man will use the elixirs and my internal energy to burn every last bit of turbid qi from your body.
For you, it should be far more effective than cleansing the sinews and washing the marrow.”
“That’s welcome news.”
“I doubt you’ll find it quite so welcome.”
“What?”
“You’ll find out soon enough.”
Before I could say anything else, he sealed my Mute Acupoint.
My tongue went rigid, trapping a silent cry inside my mouth.
What the hell is this?
Now I really was a corpse with its eyes open.
Jeok Cheongang grinned down at me as I lay frozen like a plaster statue.
“First, let’s get those elixirs into you.”
His wrinkled fingers pried open my jaw and slipped all three roots into my mouth.
For a moment, the taste of dirt and a crisp coolness filled my mouth.
Then the hard roots melted the instant they touched my tongue and flowed down my throat into my stomach.
The next moment—
Ding.
System You have consumed Fire Spirit Grass! - You have consumed Red Flower Grass! - You have consumed Flame Red Grass! - Quest Acupoint Opening has been created! - You cannot refuse this Quest.
Forced progression will begin!

chapters.title: Chapter 204
paragraphs: Whooosh!
A tremendous surge of internal energy began racing along the path.
Opening the Conception Vessel required passing through a pathway of twenty-four acupoints, beginning with the Huiyin Acupoint.
The problem was that the Huiyin Acupoint happened to be located in a rather important part of the body.
No. No!
A forced opening?!
No scream escaped my lips. The internal energy transformed into a raging bull and slammed into the Huiyin Acupoint.
Boom!
It was a sensation only someone who had experienced it could understand. My vision went white as though I’d arrived in heaven, and all my senses faded away.
The faces of those dearest to me flashed before my eyes one after another.
Mom. Hayeon. And among them, the unfamiliar face of a newborn baby.
Y-You’re...
Waaaaah!
A baby’s cry echoed through my head like an auditory hallucination.
Only then did I realize who it was.
Oh, my baby!
Jin Taekyung Junior, whom I had yet to meet.
The child I might now never meet at all.
The baby’s innocent eyes seemed to ask me:
“Daddy, can’t I come out?”
The next moment, my vision returned—and unimaginable pain shot straight up from my lower body.
Kyaaaaaaah!
As I screamed from the depths of my soul, an urgent voice lashed my ears.
“Get a hold of yourself! If you can’t endure this pain, you’ll die!”
Death? Me? And in such a disgraceful way?
My mind snapped back into focus as if someone had dumped cold water over my head.
The pain stabbing into my lower abdomen like a knife hadn’t lessened, but I summoned superhuman endurance.
I can’t die like this!
I had survived countless bloody battles. Even when I’d suffered injuries severe enough to threaten my life, I’d gritted my teeth and held on.
This was only this much—no, it wasn’t only this much, but still, I wasn’t so impatient that I’d let my life end over something like this.
Hng!
As I endured with everything I had, the tremendous surge of internal energy tore through the twenty-four acupoints without pause.
And finally...
Boom!
It crashed into the gate known as the Conception Vessel.
Pain nearly as intense as what I’d felt at the Huiyin Acupoint surged through me like a wave.
The difference was that this collision didn’t end with a single blow.
Boom! Boom! Boom!
Once, twice, three times. Thunderous booms and vibrations rang out inside my body like thunder from the heavens.
Only then did I understand why Jeok Cheongang had pressed my Paralysis Acupoint and Mute Acupoint. And why he had secured me with ropes on top of that.
Gnnngh!
My entire body trembled despite my sealed acupoints. Faced with pain beyond anything it could bear, my body was reacting on its own.
Pop.
The tiny blood vessels in my wide-open eyes burst.
Through my blood-red vision, I saw Jeok Cheongang roaring.
“Endure it! This is the last one!”
The last one? Really?
Whether it was true or not didn’t matter. His words gave me strength.
Just a little more. More!
I drew up the internal energy lying dormant in my dantian.
Forty-five years of internal energy raced through the wide-open acupoint pathways, where all the turbid qi and obstacles had been removed, and surged upward in one burst.
Then it joined the elixir’s energy, which was already pounding against the Conception Vessel, and Jeok Cheongang’s internal energy.
The three energies merged into a single battering ram and struck the gate with greater force and sharpness than ever before.
Bang! Kwoooong!
That blow put an end to it.
The long struggle was over.
The tightly sealed Conception Vessel crumbled, and the energies poured through like a conquering army.
For an instant, dizzying pain swept through me. Then pleasure and exhilarating clarity several times more intense than that pain flooded my entire body.
Ding.

System You have successfully opened the Conception Vessel! - The handling of qi has become much freer! - Your speed of circulating and accumulating internal energy has increased dramatically! - You have achieved the Conception Vessel Opening Achievement! - As a reward...
Ah... Ahhh!
My body trembled, no longer from pain but from sheer joy.
This was different. Everything I’d known until now had been no more than a drop in the ocean.
The difference was as vast as the gulf between First Rate and Peak.
How can it change this much?
I’d suffered unimaginable pain, but an achievement like this was worth it. No—I had to endure it.
As I marveled at the transformation, Jeok Cheongang beamed at me.
“You did very well!”
Seeing how genuinely delighted he was made something stir deep in my chest.
I couldn’t believe he had gone so far to help me. If my acupoints hadn’t been sealed, I would have dropped to the ground and given Jeok Cheongang a deep bow.
Jeok Cheongang, you really...
Just as my eyes began to grow moist, he spoke.
“We can open the Governor Vessel the same way.”
Oh, fuck.
I forgot about that.
He wants me to do this all over again?
No. I’m not doing it! At least let me rest for a while first!
Jeok Cheongang chuckled as I blinked desperately.
“You’re beside yourself with eagerness to begin at once. I was going to let you rest for a while, but... Very well. Let’s ride this momentum and open both the Conception and Governor Vessels!”
“Here we go!”
And so, the express train to hell departed once more.
One shichen later, I faintly heard a System notification through the haze clouding my mind.
Ding.
System You have opened the Governor Vessel! - Quest Conception and Governor Vessels was completed successfully! - You have achieved a rare Achievement! As a reward...
Whatever. Fuck this.
To hell with rare Achievements and everything else. I couldn’t take any more.
Having exhausted every last shred of mental strength, I plunged headfirst into endless darkness.
The moment Jeok Cheongang loosened the ropes, Jin Taekyung’s collapsing body fell into his careful embrace.
The sweat Taekyung had shed while enduring the pain and the turbid qi expelled from his body earlier combined into a terrible stench, but Jeok Cheongang didn’t care.
They were the traces left by a martial artist striving to reach a higher realm.
Jeok Cheongang gazed down at the unconscious Jin Taekyung with eyes deeper and gentler than ever.
The more I learn about him, the more remarkable he becomes.
At first, Jeok Cheongang had wondered one thing.
Why him, of all people?
In his eyes, Jin Taekyung had been neither white nor black. He was gray—the same ordinary gray found everywhere in the world.
He wasn’t exactly burning with a sense of justice, but neither was he evil.
Nor was he particularly devoted to training in martial arts.
From the moment Jeok Cheongang arrived at the Jin Family of Taiyuan, he’d heard about Jin Taekyung until his ears ached.
He hadn’t even needed to ask. Everyone around him was always talking about the boy.
His martial arts were Third Rate, while his drinking, womanizing, and gambling were First Rate. Unlike his two gifted older brothers, he had been called a disgrace to the family.
Upon learning that, Jeok Cheongang had resented the heavens, if only for a moment.
Why did you give the Heavenly Martial Physique to someone like him?
A fine sword ought to belong to a swordsman, not a farmer.
Yet the Jin Taekyung of the rumors was no different from a farmer holding a fine sword. Worse, he didn’t even possess a farmer’s diligence.
The only pursuits he approached diligently were drinking, womanizing, and gambling. What more was there to say?
But...
I was wrong.
Looking back, Jeok Cheongang realized that everything he had thought was merely an old man’s stubborn prejudice and contradiction.
He was no immortal sage. How could he divide someone he’d only just met into black or white? And what did it matter if Taekyung was gray?
A human heart. As long as he keeps hold of that, it is enough.
Judging by everything Jeok Cheongang had seen so far, Jin Taekyung was a decent young man.
Humans were imperfect beings to begin with. Trying to divide them into perfect white and black was absurd.
Perhaps gray was merely another name for a good person.
And on top of that, he possesses remarkable mental strength.
What good was being born with a fine physique? Opening the Conception and Governor Vessels was so difficult and agonizing that the process could only be called hellish.
Yet Jin Taekyung had done it—and done it splendidly.
It must have been unbearably difficult and painful. Even so, he had endured through sheer determination to become stronger.
Jin Taekyung possessed a mental strength as firm as his physique.
The Heavenly Martial Physique chose its master well.
A satisfied smile appeared around Jeok Cheongang’s mouth. After gazing at Jin Taekyung for a long while, he muttered:
“Perhaps... it may happen much sooner than I thought.”
As soon as he finished speaking, Jeok Cheongang’s wrinkled fingers began to tremble.
Even for him, the process had consumed a considerable amount of internal energy and mental strength. Before his mind could fully register the toll, his aging body had already made it clear.
“Not yet, you bastard. Hold out for just a few more years.”
Jeok Cheongang muttered bitterly and lifted Jin Taekyung into his arms.
They had crossed a great mountain. Now it was time to rest.
For the young man and the old man alike.
It was around noon when Ak Bulgun, a spear instructor at Heaven’s Gate Temple, arrived at Jin Wikyung’s office.
When he opened the door and entered, Jin Wikyung, who had been scribbling something across a bamboo slip, brightened and rose from his seat.
“Sir Ak, welcome. Thank you for accepting my invitation despite how busy you must be.”
“It only makes sense for the man with more time on his hands to make the trip. Please don’t concern yourself with it.”
The Shandong Yue Family was renowned throughout the Murim as a prestigious family of spear masters.
Yet despite being a direct descendant of such an illustrious family, Ak Bulgun was a straightforward man with little patience for empty formalities.
That personality showed plainly when he got straight to the point without even pausing for a sip of tea.
“Why did you summon me? Could it be...”
Jin Wikyung smiled faintly.
“Unfortunately, this isn’t about Mukyung.”
“I see.”
Ak Bulgun nodded, then added bluntly,
“Lesser Family Head, please understand that Heaven’s Gate Temple enforces its rules strictly.”
Heaven’s Gate Temple was both a treasure trove of outstanding talent and a gateway to advancement.

Anyone with sufficient talent could become a cadet regardless of their background. Its members consequently ranged from disciples of small sects in remote regions to the disciples and scions of prestigious major sects.
Despite bringing together people from such disparate backgrounds, Heaven’s Gate Temple had avoided serious conflict by enforcing the same strict rules upon every cadet.
“If he fails to return by the appointed date, he may be expelled. Even the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes are no exception.”
“I did go to see him myself, but...”
“Did he refuse?”
“Yes.”
After much deliberation, Jin Wikyung had gone to see him, but Jin Mukyung hadn’t even shown his face.
According to Childeuk, the martial artist stationed at the training hall, Mukyung hadn’t stepped outside once since entering.
He subsisted on fasting pills and refused to let anyone approach him. At least, when he heard that Jin Wikyung had come, he sent back a brief answer:
“I won’t return until I achieve Great Completion.”
Ak Bulgun let out a short laugh after hearing Jin Wikyung’s explanation.
Having taught Jin Mukyung several times before, he knew the young genius’s personality well.
“That sounds like him.”
“It’s unfortunate, but I don’t think even I can overcome my little brother’s stubbornness.”
“The Temple Master will be just as disappointed as you are, Lesser Family Head.”
Everyone had their own path to follow. Ak Bulgun nodded matter-of-factly and continued.
“I don’t believe I’ve heard why you asked to see me.”
“Ah, I wanted to deliver a message to you.”
“A message?”
Instead of answering, Jin Wikyung drew a small bamboo tube from inside his robe and handed it over.
Ak Bulgun examined the characters engraved into the blue bamboo tube and murmured,
“Heaven’s Gate Temple?”
“It arrived half a shichen ago. I thought it best to bring you here so I could hand it over personally.”
“Please excuse me for a moment.”
