sentences.text: Whooosh!
A tremendous surge of internal energy began racing along the path.
Opening the Conception Vessel required passing through a pathway of twenty-four acupoints, beginning with the Huiyin Acupoint.
The problem was that the Huiyin Acupoint happened to be located in a rather important part of the body.
No.
No!
A forced opening?!
No scream escaped my lips.
The internal energy transformed into a raging bull and slammed into the Huiyin Acupoint.
Boom!
It was a sensation only someone who had experienced it could understand.
My vision went white as though I’d arrived in heaven, and all my senses faded away.
The faces of those dearest to me flashed before my eyes one after another.
Mom.
Hayeon.
And among them, the unfamiliar face of a newborn baby.
Y-You’re...
Waaaaah!
A baby’s cry echoed through my head like an auditory hallucination.
Only then did I realize who it was.
Oh, my baby!
Jin Taekyung Junior, whom I had yet to meet.
The child I might now never meet at all.
The baby’s innocent eyes seemed to ask me:
“Daddy, can’t I come out?”
The next moment, my vision returned—and unimaginable pain shot straight up from my lower body.
Kyaaaaaaah!
As I screamed from the depths of my soul, an urgent voice lashed my ears.
“Get a hold of yourself!
If you can’t endure this pain, you’ll die!”
Death?
Me?
And in such a disgraceful way?
My mind snapped back into focus as if someone had dumped cold water over my head.
The pain stabbing into my lower abdomen like a knife hadn’t lessened, but I summoned superhuman endurance.
I can’t die like this!
I had survived countless bloody battles.
Even when I’d suffered injuries severe enough to threaten my life, I’d gritted my teeth and held on.
This was only this much—no, it wasn’t only this much, but still, I wasn’t so impatient that I’d let my life end over something like this.
Hng!
As I endured with everything I had, the tremendous surge of internal energy tore through the twenty-four acupoints without pause.
And finally...
Boom!
It crashed into the gate known as the Conception Vessel.
Pain nearly as intense as what I’d felt at the Huiyin Acupoint surged through me like a wave.
The difference was that this collision didn’t end with a single blow.
Boom!
Boom!
Boom!
Once, twice, three times.
Thunderous booms and vibrations rang out inside my body like thunder from the heavens.
Only then did I understand why Jeok Cheongang had pressed my Paralysis Acupoint and Mute Acupoint.
And why he had secured me with ropes on top of that.
Gnnngh!
My entire body trembled despite my sealed acupoints.
Faced with pain beyond anything it could bear, my body was reacting on its own.
Pop.
The tiny blood vessels in my wide-open eyes burst.
Through my blood-red vision, I saw Jeok Cheongang roaring.
“Endure it!
This is the last one!”
The last one?
Really?
Whether it was true or not didn’t matter.
His words gave me strength.
Just a little more.
More!
I drew up the internal energy lying dormant in my dantian.
Forty-five years of internal energy raced through the wide-open acupoint pathways, where all the turbid qi and obstacles had been removed, and surged upward in one burst.
Then it joined the elixir’s energy, which was already pounding against the Conception Vessel, and Jeok Cheongang’s internal energy.
The three energies merged into a single battering ram and struck the gate with greater force and sharpness than ever before.
Bang!
Kwoooong!
That blow put an end to it.
The long struggle was over.
The tightly sealed Conception Vessel crumbled, and the energies poured through like a conquering army.
For an instant, dizzying pain swept through me.
Then pleasure and exhilarating clarity several times more intense than that pain flooded my entire body.
Ding.

System You have successfully opened the Conception Vessel! - The handling of qi has become much freer! - Your speed of circulating and accumulating internal energy has increased dramatically! - You have achieved the Conception Vessel Opening Achievement! - As a reward...
Ah...
Ahhh!
My body trembled, no longer from pain but from sheer joy.
This was different.
Everything I’d known until now had been no more than a drop in the ocean.
The difference was as vast as the gulf between First Rate and Peak.
How can it change this much?
I’d suffered unimaginable pain, but an achievement like this was worth it.
No—I had to endure it.
As I marveled at the transformation, Jeok Cheongang beamed at me.
“You did very well!”
Seeing how genuinely delighted he was made something stir deep in my chest.
I couldn’t believe he had gone so far to help me.
If my acupoints hadn’t been sealed, I would have dropped to the ground and given Jeok Cheongang a deep bow.
Jeok Cheongang, you really...
Just as my eyes began to grow moist, he spoke.
“We can open the Governor Vessel the same way.”
Oh, fuck.
I forgot about that.
He wants me to do this all over again?
No.
I’m not doing it!
At least let me rest for a while first!
Jeok Cheongang chuckled as I blinked desperately.
“You’re beside yourself with eagerness to begin at once.
I was going to let you rest for a while, but...
Very well.
Let’s ride this momentum and open both the Conception and Governor Vessels!”
“Here we go!”
And so, the express train to hell departed once more.
One shichen later, I faintly heard a System notification through the haze clouding my mind.
Ding.
System You have opened the Governor Vessel! - Quest Conception and Governor Vessels was completed successfully! - You have achieved a rare Achievement!
As a reward...
Whatever.
Fuck this.
To hell with rare Achievements and everything else.
I couldn’t take any more.
Having exhausted every last shred of mental strength, I plunged headfirst into endless darkness.
The moment Jeok Cheongang loosened the ropes, Jin Taekyung’s collapsing body fell into his careful embrace.
The sweat Taekyung had shed while enduring the pain and the turbid qi expelled from his body earlier combined into a terrible stench, but Jeok Cheongang didn’t care.
They were the traces left by a martial artist striving to reach a higher realm.
Jeok Cheongang gazed down at the unconscious Jin Taekyung with eyes deeper and gentler than ever.
The more I learn about him, the more remarkable he becomes.
At first, Jeok Cheongang had wondered one thing.
Why him, of all people?
In his eyes, Jin Taekyung had been neither white nor black.
He was gray—the same ordinary gray found everywhere in the world.
He wasn’t exactly burning with a sense of justice, but neither was he evil.
Nor was he particularly devoted to training in martial arts.
From the moment Jeok Cheongang arrived at the Jin Family of Taiyuan, he’d heard about Jin Taekyung until his ears ached.
He hadn’t even needed to ask.
Everyone around him was always talking about the boy.
His martial arts were Third Rate, while his drinking, womanizing, and gambling were First Rate.
Unlike his two gifted older brothers, he had been called a disgrace to the family.
Upon learning that, Jeok Cheongang had resented the heavens, if only for a moment.
Why did you give the Heavenly Martial Physique to someone like him?
A fine sword ought to belong to a swordsman, not a farmer.
Yet the Jin Taekyung of the rumors was no different from a farmer holding a fine sword.
Worse, he didn’t even possess a farmer’s diligence.
The only pursuits he approached diligently were drinking, womanizing, and gambling.
What more was there to say?
But...
I was wrong.
Looking back, Jeok Cheongang realized that everything he had thought was merely an old man’s stubborn prejudice and contradiction.
He was no immortal sage.
How could he divide someone he’d only just met into black or white?
And what did it matter if Taekyung was gray?
A human heart.
As long as he keeps hold of that, it is enough.
Judging by everything Jeok Cheongang had seen so far, Jin Taekyung was a decent young man.
Humans were imperfect beings to begin with.
Trying to divide them into perfect white and black was absurd.
Perhaps gray was merely another name for a good person.
And on top of that, he possesses remarkable mental strength.
What good was being born with a fine physique?
Opening the Conception and Governor Vessels was so difficult and agonizing that the process could only be called hellish.
Yet Jin Taekyung had done it—and done it splendidly.
It must have been unbearably difficult and painful.
Even so, he had endured through sheer determination to become stronger.
Jin Taekyung possessed a mental strength as firm as his physique.
The Heavenly Martial Physique chose its master well.
A satisfied smile appeared around Jeok Cheongang’s mouth.
After gazing at Jin Taekyung for a long while, he muttered:
“Perhaps... it may happen much sooner than I thought.”
As soon as he finished speaking, Jeok Cheongang’s wrinkled fingers began to tremble.
Even for him, the process had consumed a considerable amount of internal energy and mental strength.
Before his mind could fully register the toll, his aging body had already made it clear.
“Not yet, you bastard.
Hold out for just a few more years.”
Jeok Cheongang muttered bitterly and lifted Jin Taekyung into his arms.
They had crossed a great mountain.
Now it was time to rest.
For the young man and the old man alike.
It was around noon when Ak Bulgun, a spear instructor at Heaven’s Gate Temple, arrived at Jin Wikyung’s office.
When he opened the door and entered, Jin Wikyung, who had been scribbling something across a bamboo slip, brightened and rose from his seat.
“Sir Ak, welcome.
Thank you for accepting my invitation despite how busy you must be.”
“It only makes sense for the man with more time on his hands to make the trip.
Please don’t concern yourself with it.”
The Shandong Yue Family was renowned throughout the Murim as a prestigious family of spear masters.
Yet despite being a direct descendant of such an illustrious family, Ak Bulgun was a straightforward man with little patience for empty formalities.
That personality showed plainly when he got straight to the point without even pausing for a sip of tea.
“Why did you summon me?
Could it be...”
Jin Wikyung smiled faintly.
“Unfortunately, this isn’t about Mukyung.”
“I see.”
Ak Bulgun nodded, then added bluntly,
“Lesser Family Head, please understand that Heaven’s Gate Temple enforces its rules strictly.”
Heaven’s Gate Temple was both a treasure trove of outstanding talent and a gateway to advancement.
Anyone with sufficient talent could become a cadet regardless of their background.
Its members consequently ranged from disciples of small sects in remote regions to the disciples and scions of prestigious major sects.
Despite bringing together people from such disparate backgrounds, Heaven’s Gate Temple had avoided serious conflict by enforcing the same strict rules upon every cadet.
“If he fails to return by the appointed date, he may be expelled.
Even the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes are no exception.”
“I did go to see him myself, but...”
“Did he refuse?”
“Yes.”
After much deliberation, Jin Wikyung had gone to see him, but Jin Mukyung hadn’t even shown his face.
According to Childeuk, the martial artist stationed at the training hall, Mukyung hadn’t stepped outside once since entering.
He subsisted on fasting pills and refused to let anyone approach him.
At least, when he heard that Jin Wikyung had come, he sent back a brief answer:
“I won’t return until I achieve Great Completion.”
Ak Bulgun let out a short laugh after hearing Jin Wikyung’s explanation.
Having taught Jin Mukyung several times before, he knew the young genius’s personality well.
“That sounds like him.”
“It’s unfortunate, but I don’t think even I can overcome my little brother’s stubbornness.”
“The Temple Master will be just as disappointed as you are, Lesser Family Head.”
Everyone had their own path to follow.
Ak Bulgun nodded matter-of-factly and continued.
“I don’t believe I’ve heard why you asked to see me.”
“Ah, I wanted to deliver a message to you.”
“A message?”
Instead of answering, Jin Wikyung drew a small bamboo tube from inside his robe and handed it over.
Ak Bulgun examined the characters engraved into the blue bamboo tube and murmured,
“Heaven’s Gate Temple?”
“It arrived half a shichen ago.
I thought it best to bring you here so I could hand it over personally.”
“Please excuse me for a moment.”
After asking permission, Ak Bulgun silently read through the message.
He checked it twice, then a third time, before raising his head and staring at Jin Wikyung.
“Lesser Family Head.”
“I’m going to need your help.”

chapters.title: Chapter 205
paragraphs: How long had I been unconscious?
My body felt as light as a feather, and my mind was clear. It felt as though I’d only slept for a moment, yet the world had changed a great deal while I was out.
What’s going on?
The room held only simple furniture and a few decorations. The faint scent of fresh timber lingered in the recently built room.
It was a familiar sight, one I’d seen countless times before. Yet it had never felt so strange.
This is...
I looked around, my eyes trembling.
I could feel qi saturating the air, and everything around me was so bright that it was as if someone had implanted night-vision goggles in my eyes.
Even the moon beyond the latticed window seemed bizarre.
Why was the moon out when it was this bright? Wasn’t that actually the sun?
I sat there in a daze for a long while, as though bewitched, before finally realizing the truth.
“Oh.”
This world—the Murim—was exactly as I remembered it. Nothing had changed except me.
A small voice slipped from my lips before I realized it.
“The Conception and Governor Vessels...”
When a blocked tunnel is opened, light pours in.
Anyone accustomed to the darkness inside would naturally find that light strange. That was exactly how I felt now.
Only after removing the enormous obstacle known as the Conception and Governor Vessels could I finally see a light I’d never known existed.
“You’re awake.”
The owner of the sudden voice stood leaning against the doorway.
There wasn’t even a lamp in the room, yet I could make out every age spot and wrinkle covering his face.
“Old Master.”
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, answered as if he’d been waiting for me.
“Yeah.”
“You’re really old.”
For a moment, he was struck speechless. I added one more thing.
“And strong. Stronger than anyone I’ve ever seen.”
This wasn’t an attempt to take back what I’d just said, nor was it empty flattery. I meant it with one hundred percent sincerity.
Now that I had opened the Conception and Governor Vessels, I could glimpse, however faintly, the terrifying martial arts hidden within that small frame.
“Ahem. You’re stating the obvious.”
Jeok Cheongang cleared his throat in embarrassment and changed the subject.
“So, how do you feel?”
“Fantastic.”
There was no need to read a System message or circulate my internal energy to examine my body. I could feel it the moment I opened my eyes.
The corners of his mouth twitched at my immediate answer.
“Of course you do. Do you have any idea how much trouble this old man went through—no, I handled it with ease, but it’s still not something just anyone could do. Indeed.”
“I’m telling the truth!”
“I didn’t say anything.”
“That look on your face is disrespectful! That look!”
That was because his intentions were painfully obvious.
His martial arts might be unfathomable, but his personality was completely transparent.
Violent and impossibly eccentric, yet surprisingly easy to understand—that was how I saw Jeok Cheongang.
“I have ptosis, so people often misunderstand my expression.”
I put on an utterly shameless face and denied everything. Jeok Cheongang began to snort.

“Why is everyone here like this? That so-called Lesser Family Head keeps neglecting major family business to come by and see you, and those physicians are all quacks who do nothing but gossip about whether you’re going to live or die.”
“Wait. Die? Did someone get seriously hurt?”
“Who else would it be?”
At his meaningful stare, I asked with a sinking feeling:
“Are you talking about me?”
“That’s right. The whole place was in an uproar for the past seven days and nights. If I’d known this would happen, I would’ve shoved you under a rock until you came to your senses.”
I didn’t even hear the rest. I blinked at him in a daze.
“I was unconscious for seven whole days and nights?”
“Not seven whole days and nights. Only seven. I thought you’d be lying there for at least a month, but the Heavenly Martial Physique truly is remarkable.”
“This isn’t some kind of side effect, is it?”
“Listen to the insolence in this brat’s voice. I went through all that trouble to open your Conception and Governor Vessels, and what do I get? ‘Side effect’?”
“You just said you handled it with ease.”
Jeok Cheongang froze, then shouted:

“That’s beside the point! Even after you take a shit, you still have to wipe your ass. I removed all the turbid qi that had been piling up inside your body, layer upon layer. Obviously, you’d need time to adjust to your new body!”
He was so worked up that the analogy was a little strange, but I understood what he meant.
Some kind of optimization process, maybe?

Come to think of it, it would be strange for someone on the verge of death to leap to his feet just because his Conception and Governor Vessels had been opened. Even after leveling up, mental fatigue could still build up and knock a person unconscious.
Even so, an entire week?
“Then the gathering must be over.”
“The gathering—or half a gathering—ended three days ago.”
Still visibly sulking, Jeok Cheongang continued:
“That fellow Ak Bulgun is still here.”
I tilted my head at the unexpected name.
Ak Bulgun, an instructor at Heaven’s Gate Temple, had originally come to the Jin Family of Taiyuan to take Jin Mukyung back.
Could he really be planning to wait until Jin Mukyung finished his seclusion?
“Why is Sir Ak still here?”
“Ask him yourself.”
“Come on. I was wrong, so stop being angry and tell me.”
Jeok Cheongang replied curtly:
“Do I look that petty to you? I mean he’s on his way here, so you can hear it directly from him.”
“Oh.”
Sure enough, he was right. Not long afterward, approaching footsteps announced the arrival of two people.
“My youngest!”
Jin Wikyung’s voice trembled with emotion when he saw that I had awakened after seven days and nights. Behind him came Ak Bulgun’s blunt voice.
“It seems Great Hero Jeok is here as well. I have something important to discuss with you. Would that be all right?”
Jeok Cheongang answered firmly:
“No. Get out.”
“It concerns Jin Taekyung’s plans as well.”
“...Damn it.”
Jeok Cheongang muttered a quiet curse and perched on a chair.
As his appearance suggested, Ak Bulgun was not much of an orator. After listening to his entire dry explanation, I spoke.
“So you’re inviting us to that... Star... Star-Array...”
What was it called again? His explanation had been so boring that I could barely remember what I’d heard.
When I faltered, Jeok Cheongang supplied the name.
“The Star-Array Grand Banquet.”
“Ah, right. The Star-Array Grand Banquet.”

“It is a grand event where martial artists from across the world gather in one place to vie for supremacy and reinforce their bonds. It is held once every two or three years, and this year’s Star-Array Grand Banquet will take place in Henan.”
At Ak Bulgun’s additional explanation, Jeok Cheongang gave a derisive laugh.
“Reinforce the bonds of the Murim, my ass. It’s a place where powerful people cheer each other on, flatter one another, and build connections.”
Talk about a mercilessly blunt assessment.
Ak Bulgun gave a small nod without offering any real objection. It seemed Jeok Cheongang wasn’t wrong.
Jeok Cheongang continued in a cutting tone:
“It was the same forty years ago. The Demonic Cult had barely been driven out, and already they were fighting over their interests... I saw more than enough ugliness.”
I could more or less picture what it had been like.
A time of chaos was also a time of opportunity. The greedy and powerful never let an opportunity pass them by.
It might even have been partly related to why Jeok Cheongang had gone into seclusion on Mount Jiuhua again.
Still, it sounds like an enormous event.
Jeok Cheongang narrowed his eyes at my curious stare.
“What are you looking at?”
“It’s nothing. I was just wondering why someone who hates crowds and anything troublesome would go to a place like that.”
“I was asked to.”
Was Jeok Cheongang really the sort of person to comply simply because someone asked him to?
The question vanished as soon as I heard the title of the person who had asked.
“The Martial God.”
“Oh.”
The Martial God, whom I’d only ever heard about.
They said there were Ten Kings on earth, Three Saints in the heavens, and one god above them all.
If the request had come from that Martial God, even Jeok Cheongang probably couldn’t have refused easily.
“He was the one who created the Star-Array Grand Banquet and asked this old man to attend. That was the first and last time the One God, Three Saints, and Ten Kings gathered in one place.”
As though recalling those days, Jeok Cheongang tapped the armrest of his chair with a distant look in his eyes. Then he suddenly turned to Ak Bulgun.
“How is he doing?”
“He has not shown himself for many years. There are even disturbing rumors circulating...”
“You’re worried the Martial God might be dead? Ha. There are far too many idiots with nothing but shit in their heads.”
Jeok Cheongang let out a hollow laugh, then turned back to me.
“So, what do you think?”
“Hmm.”

“Even if it is a feast for the powerful, there is no denying that the Star-Array Grand Banquet is a gathering of martial artists from across the world. Anyone can display their abilities to the fullest, regardless of their background.”
“I’m not sure.”
I scratched the back of my head, unable to answer easily.
The Star-Array Grand Banquet. A gathering where martial artists from across the world assembled to reinforce their bonds and vie for supremacy.
It was a chance to face outstanding masters and make a name for myself throughout the Central Plains.
But...
Was that really so important?
Ever since coming to the Murim, I’d found myself wondering about that from time to time.
Why did I practice martial arts? Why did I keep training even after becoming strong enough to protect my own life and the people precious to me?
After thinking about it for a long time, I’d finally found the answer not long ago.
Because it’s fun.
Just as I’d told Cheongpung, I liked martial arts. They were fun.
Even if I gained more money and fame than I could possibly imagine, I would never stop training.
I was already addicted to martial arts. I’d discovered just how thrilling and satisfying it was to become stronger.
“Young Hero Jin.”
Ak Bulgun’s quiet voice broke through my thoughts. It was time to answer.
I took a deep breath and opened my mouth.
The expressions of all three men changed strangely when they heard my answer.
The three men left.
Alone in the room, I thought back to my final exchange with Jeok Cheongang.
You want to become stronger. Is that your answer?
Yes.
Does that mean you’ll attend the Star-Array Grand Banquet?
It doesn’t matter where I go, as long as I can become stronger than I am now.
You’re still young, and you’re already strong enough. If you attend the Star-Array Grand Banquet, you could etch your name into the Murim and gain wealth and fame. Aren’t you tempted by those things?
I am. By martial arts. By a higher realm.
Jeok Cheongang had stared at me with trembling eyes for a long while before leaving me with a single command.
Come to my quarters at dawn.
Remembering his final words, I sat down on the bed.
My field of vision was as bright as midday, and I could hear the footsteps and breathing of people outside the pavilion as clearly as if they were right beside me.
You’re already strong enough.
Jeok Cheongang himself had said those words before leaving. The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, had acknowledged me.
But there was something else I wanted to hear.
You’re stronger than anyone.
Back when I was an F-rank Hunter, my wish had been to become an E-rank Hunter. When I first set foot in the Murim, my goal had been to surpass Hyuk Mujin.
As time passed, I grew stronger, and my dreams grew more ambitious.
Some people might call that greed. But greed and dreams were different.
I had a dream now. The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, was the guide who could lead me toward it.
I’m looking forward to morning.
There were roughly three shichen left until dawn.
It looked like tonight would be a long one—for both me and Jeok Cheongang.
Especially for me. It’ll be a night longer than I can even imagine.
I lay flat on my back.
It was time to leave behind everything that had happened in the Murim and return.
Logout.
Ding.
With the cheerful System notification, my eyes slowly closed.

“The gathering—or half a gathering—ended three days ago.”
Still visibly sulking, Jeok Cheongang continued:
“That fellow Ak Bulgun is still here.”
I tilted my head at the unexpected name.
Ak Bulgun, an instructor at Heaven’s Gate Temple, had originally come to the Jin Family of Taiyuan to take Jin Mukyung back.
Could he really be planning to wait until Jin Mukyung finished his seclusion?
“Why is Sir Ak still here?”
“Ask him yourself.”
“Come on.
I was wrong, so stop being angry and tell me.”
Jeok Cheongang replied curtly:
“Do I look that petty to you?
I mean he’s on his way here, so you can hear it directly from him.”
“Oh.”
Sure enough, he was right.
Not long afterward, approaching footsteps announced the arrival of two people.
“My youngest!”
Jin Wikyung’s voice trembled with emotion when he saw that I had awakened after seven days and nights.
Behind him came Ak Bulgun’s blunt voice.
“It seems Great Hero Jeok is here as well.
I have something important to discuss with you.
Would that be all right?”
Jeok Cheongang answered firmly:
“No.
Get out.”
“It concerns Jin Taekyung’s plans as well.”
“...Damn it.”
Jeok Cheongang muttered a quiet curse and perched on a chair.
As his appearance suggested, Ak Bulgun was not much of an orator.
After listening to his entire dry explanation, I spoke.
“So you’re inviting us to that...
Star...
Star-Array...”
What was it called again?
His explanation had been so boring that I could barely remember what I’d heard.
When I faltered, Jeok Cheongang supplied the name.
“The Star-Array Grand Banquet.”
“Ah, right.
The Star-Array Grand Banquet.”
“It is a grand event where martial artists from across the world gather in one place to vie for supremacy and reinforce their bonds.
It is held once every two or three years, and this year’s Star-Array Grand Banquet will take place in Henan.”
At Ak Bulgun’s additional explanation, Jeok Cheongang gave a derisive laugh.
“Reinforce the bonds of the Murim, my ass.
It’s a place where powerful people cheer each other on, flatter one another, and build connections.”
Talk about a mercilessly blunt assessment.
Ak Bulgun gave a small nod without offering any real objection.
It seemed Jeok Cheongang wasn’t wrong.
Jeok Cheongang continued in a cutting tone:
“It was the same forty years ago.
The Demonic Cult had barely been driven out, and already they were fighting over their interests...
I saw more than enough ugliness.”
I could more or less picture what it had been like.
A time of chaos was also a time of opportunity.
The greedy and powerful never let an opportunity pass them by.
It might even have been partly related to why Jeok Cheongang had gone into seclusion on Mount Jiuhua again.
Still, it sounds like an enormous event.
Jeok Cheongang narrowed his eyes at my curious stare.
“What are you looking at?”
“It’s nothing.
I was just wondering why someone who hates crowds and anything troublesome would go to a place like that.”
“I was asked to.”
Was Jeok Cheongang really the sort of person to comply simply because someone asked him to?
The question vanished as soon as I heard the title of the person who had asked.
“The Martial God.”
“Oh.”
The Martial God, whom I’d only ever heard about.
They said there were Ten Kings on earth, Three Saints in the heavens, and one god above them all.
If the request had come from that Martial God, even Jeok Cheongang probably couldn’t have refused easily.
“He was the one who created the Star-Array Grand Banquet and asked this old man to attend.
That was the first and last time the One God, Three Saints, and Ten Kings gathered in one place.”
As though recalling those days, Jeok Cheongang tapped the armrest of his chair with a distant look in his eyes.
Then he suddenly turned to Ak Bulgun.
“How is he doing?”
“He has not shown himself for many years.
There are even disturbing rumors circulating...”
“You’re worried the Martial God might be dead?
Ha.
There are far too many idiots with nothing but shit in their heads.”
Jeok Cheongang let out a hollow laugh, then turned back to me.
“So, what do you think?”
“Hmm.”
“Even if it is a feast for the powerful, there is no denying that the Star-Array Grand Banquet is a gathering of martial artists from across the world.
Anyone can display their abilities to the fullest, regardless of their background.”
“I’m not sure.”
I scratched the back of my head, unable to answer easily.
The Star-Array Grand Banquet.
A gathering where martial artists from across the world assembled to reinforce their bonds and vie for supremacy.
It was a chance to face outstanding masters and make a name for myself throughout the Central Plains.
But...
Was that really so important?
Ever since coming to the Murim, I’d found myself wondering about that from time to time.
Why did I practice martial arts?
Why did I keep training even after becoming strong enough to protect my own life and the people precious to me?
After thinking about it for a long time, I’d finally found the answer not long ago.
Because it’s fun.
Just as I’d told Cheongpung, I liked martial arts.
They were fun.
Even if I gained more money and fame than I could possibly imagine, I would never stop training.
I was already addicted to martial arts.
I’d discovered just how thrilling and satisfying it was to become stronger.
“Young Hero Jin.”
Ak Bulgun’s quiet voice broke through my thoughts.
It was time to answer.
I took a deep breath and opened my mouth.
The expressions of all three men changed strangely when they heard my answer.
The three men left.
Alone in the room, I thought back to my final exchange with Jeok Cheongang.
You want to become stronger.
Is that your answer?
Yes.
Does that mean you’ll attend the Star-Array Grand Banquet?
It doesn’t matter where I go, as long as I can become stronger than I am now.
You’re still young, and you’re already strong enough.
If you attend the Star-Array Grand Banquet, you could etch your name into the Murim and gain wealth and fame.
Aren’t you tempted by those things?
I am.
By martial arts.
By a higher realm.
Jeok Cheongang had stared at me with trembling eyes for a long while before leaving me with a single command.
Come to my quarters at dawn.
Remembering his final words, I sat down on the bed.
My field of vision was as bright as midday, and I could hear the footsteps and breathing of people outside the pavilion as clearly as if they were right beside me.
You’re already strong enough.
Jeok Cheongang himself had said those words before leaving.
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, had acknowledged me.
But there was something else I wanted to hear.
You’re stronger than anyone.
Back when I was an F-rank Hunter, my wish had been to become an E-rank Hunter.
When I first set foot in the Murim, my goal had been to surpass Hyuk Mujin.
As time passed, I grew stronger, and my dreams grew more ambitious.
Some people might call that greed.
But greed and dreams were different.
I had a dream now.
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, was the guide who could lead me toward it.
I’m looking forward to morning.
There were roughly three shichen left until dawn.
It looked like tonight would be a long one—for both me and Jeok Cheongang.
Especially for me.
It’ll be a night longer than I can even imagine.
I lay flat on my back.
It was time to leave behind everything that had happened in the Murim and return.
Logout.
Ding.
With the cheerful System notification, my eyes slowly closed.

chapters.title: Chapter 206
paragraphs: Ding.
System Logout completed.
I hadn’t opened my eyes, but I knew.
The moment the System notification sounded, everything around me changed.
Instead of a fur-covered bed and a hard wooden pillow, I felt the soft cushions of a sofa beneath me. Water bubbled nearby, and a familiar smell hit my nose.
Th-This is...
Ramen. And not just any ramen—ramen cooked to perfection!
The instant I realized what it was, my stomach began churning violently. After more than a month in the Murim, it was desperate for seasoning.
“I’m hungry!”
The cry came straight from my soul. My eyes snapped open, and a familiar face popped out from the brightly lit kitchen.
Sparse stubble. Greasy, matted hair. Jinho wiped his steam-fogged glasses and beamed at me.
“Oh, my beloved little brother Taekyung. Did you sleep well?”
His revoltingly sweet tone was nothing like his usual voice, but the smell of ramen had already driven me out of my mind.
“Ramen!”
“Jesus, what’s gotten into you?”
“Kimchi!”
“You were really out cold. I was going to shake you awake, but...”
“Cold rice! At least five bowls!”
“...Uh, all right. I was about to bring it over anyway.”
A short while later, I stared at the pot filled to the brim with noodles and broth and murmured in bliss.
“This is insane...”
“Lift the top layer of noodles a little. There’s a soft-boiled egg underneath.”
“Gasp.”
Just as he’d said, when I carefully lifted the noodles, a perfectly intact soft-boiled egg appeared beneath them.
As I sucked in a breath, Jinho held out two small side dishes.
“Here. Kimchi and pickled radish. The rice is plain white rice I took out an hour ago. Once you finish the noodles and drink a few mouthfuls of broth, drop in the cold rice and...”
“Are you...”
“Hm?”
“Are you God?”
Jinho placed an exam-prep book beneath the pot and answered solemnly.
“Genesis, chapter one, verse one. Thus spoke Seong Jinho: ‘If you do not eat now, the broth shall grow cold, and the noodles shall become hopelessly soggy.’”
“Ah... Ahhh...”
“Little lamb, why dost thou flap thy gums with ramen before thee? Lick the pot clean and leave not a single drop of broth behind.”
I’d been nonreligious my entire life.
Not anymore.
I gazed reverently up at Jinho and raised my chopsticks.
“Amen.”
“Ramen.”
Today, I wouldn’t have minded dying with my nose buried in ramen broth.
I buried my head over the huge pot and moved my chopsticks without pause. Because the distance between my mouth and the chopsticks was so short, the noodles kept disappearing into me.
Slurp! Slurp! Slurrrrrp!
Springy noodles. Spicy broth. When I broke open the soft-boiled egg, the bliss and regret were so overwhelming that a single tear rolled down my cheek.
It’s delicious. So delicious.
I love seasoning. It’s the best.
Drunk on that artificial flavor found only in the modern world, I kept inhaling food.
By the time I came to my senses, there was nothing in front of me but an empty pot and bowls. Even the bowl that had held a heaping mound of cold rice was spotless.
“Buuurp.”
“You’ve got to be kidding me.”
Jinho stared at me in horror as I rubbed my stomach and let out a tremendous belch.
“You ate seven packets of ramen and five bowls of rice by yourself in ten minutes? Are you even human?”
“Carbonation! Cola!”
“...C-Calm down. I’ll get some.”
Only after draining three 1.5-liter bottles of cola in a row did I finally return to something resembling sanity.
“Whew. That hit the spot. I’m full.”
“That’s strange. Why am I hungry?”
“Bear with it. You would’ve done the same if you were me.”
I answered absently and collapsed back against the sofa behind me.
What kind of monster hide had they said this was made from? Whatever it was, it felt incredible.
“Man, this is comfortable.”
If this had been my goshiwon room, there wouldn’t even have been space for a sofa.
Jinho would have had to cook the ramen in the communal lounge instead of a kitchen, or bring in a portable burner.
“Moving here really was the right choice.”
Jinho scraped the bottom of the pot with a spoon as he answered.
“Yeah. It’s a nice place.”
“Right? Mom and Hayeon are going to love it when they see... it.”
A realization flashed through my mind like lightning.
I stared blankly around the room, my mouth hanging open. The space and furniture were nothing like what I’d had in the goshiwon.
And one particular person had blended seamlessly into both the space and the situation.
“I’m still hungry. Should I make some Jjapagetti?”
“I’m not giving you any this time. If you want some, say so now.”
I barely managed to squeeze out my voice.
“Hm?”
“Why the hell are you here, you bastard!”
My roar shattered the dark dawn and shook the residential neighborhood of Ilsan.
After hearing the whole story, I could only ask in disbelief.
“You were inside the capsule?”
Jinho knelt politely with both arms raised above his head and looked away.
“Yeah. I held my breath and stayed perfectly still.”
No wonder the mover had struggled so much.
Even I hadn’t noticed anything unusual. My Strength had grown several times over since I’d first found and moved the capsule, and my Qi Sense hadn’t been nearly as sharp back then as it was now.
And there was one more thing.
No, for fuck’s sake. Who would’ve imagined that?
No matter how expensive or sophisticated an alarm system was, it couldn’t detect an intruder when the power was off.
It had never even occurred to me that someone might be hiding inside the capsule.
“Whew. What happened to the place you were going to get? Didn’t you say you were moving in with a friend?”
“Y-You know Kim Jong-su, right? My college classmate. You had drinks with us once a couple of years ago.”
His face was hazy in my memory, but I did remember that.
Hadn’t he been a fairly successful used-car dealer at the time? If he hadn’t bought us beef that day, I probably would’ve forgotten him completely.
“That’s the friend you were going to live with?”
“Yeah. Though he’s not my friend anymore.”
“Hyung, did he...?”
“Five million won for the deposit. That bastard took it and ran.”
Why did bad premonitions always come true?
I rubbed my throbbing forehead.
“How did that happen?”
“Well, my exam is coming up soon, so he said he’d handle all the details...”
I raised a hand to stop him before he could continue.
I didn’t need to hear the rest. It was a clichéd trick, but it kept working for a reason.
“You just handed him the money without checking anything?”
“I’d known him for over ten years. How was I supposed to know he’d do that over a few million won?”
“But those few million won were your entire fortune, weren’t they?”
If he’d gone so far as to sneak in here inside the capsule, he clearly didn’t even have enough left to pay this month’s goshiwon rent.
Was he from Jeju Island or something?
A special A-grade black cow.
There wasn’t a bigger black cow—a bigger sucker—anywhere.
At the look in my eyes, Jinho hung his head.
“I was only going to impose on you for a couple of months, until I could scrape some money together.”
“You should’ve just told me.”
“I agonized over it, but I couldn’t bring myself to say anything. I’m your hyung. I can’t burden my little brother.”
What the hell did this man consider a burden?
“I’m sorry. I really am.”
His voice turned mournful as he lowered his arms. His eyes were already glistening.
“Taekyung...”
“Jinho hyung...”
I continued in a sympathetic voice.
“Who told you to lower your arms?”
“Hm?”
“Put them back up before I beat you.”
“...Yes, sir.”
Jinho hurriedly raised his arms again, and a sigh escaped me.
The whole ridiculous situation had come out of nowhere, but at the same time, it left me feeling heavyhearted.
You should’ve told me sooner.
Maybe I couldn’t have done much for him in the past, but now I had more than enough means to help. No, even back then, I would’ve supported him in every way I could.
After all the time we’ve spent together.
We weren’t related by blood, but he was as good as a real brother to me. That was who Jinho was.
I’d even considered asking him to live with me for a while because I felt uneasy about leaving him on his own.
I was planning to tell Mom and Hayeon after the college entrance exam anyway, so there’s still some time, but...
I looked around the house, deep in thought. It looked different from the home in my childhood memories, but it was still the house my family had finally reclaimed.
A house that still held traces of my father, whose voice had faded in my memory.
At last, I made up my mind and opened my mouth.
“This house won’t work, hyung. I know you’ll be disappointed, but try to understand.”
Jinho forced a bright expression and shook his head.
“Why would I be disappointed? This is all my fault.”
“What about your stuff? Have you unpacked?”
“Not yet. It’s only a few books and some clothes, so there isn’t much. I’ll just leave with you when you go to work.”
Come to think of it, it had been bright outside for a while. It was already eight o’clock. Between the traffic and the distance from Ilsan to Bucheon, I was cutting it pretty close.
“I think we’ll have to leave separately. Get your things ready.”
“Okay.”
“And clean the new place from top to bottom before I get off work.”
“Don’t get the wrong idea. I’m not talking about this house. Give me a second.”
I pulled out my phone and searched through my messages.
At last, I found the address I wanted in my chat with Team Leader Choi, whom I’d saved as “Designer-Brand Junkie.”
“Ah, here it is. I just sent the address to your phone. Find your own way there.”
“Wait. What address?”
“An officetel.”
“Huh?”
“The Guild offered to provide me with a place. I turned it down last time because accepting it felt like too much, but I might as well take them up on it now.”
A quiet laugh escaped me when I saw Jinho’s eyes widen.
“Why are you so surprised? I’m doing pretty well these days.”
“This house needs remodeling anyway, so let’s live there together. It’ll make my commute easier too.”
“Ta-Taekyung.”
I turned away, pretending not to hear the tremor in Jinho’s voice.
I had no desire to deal with an embarrassing scene first thing in the morning. Nor did I particularly want to be thanked by the man who had comforted me through the hardest period of my life.
It’s fine.
Yeah. This was enough.
It was mid-September. The worst of the heat had passed, but the morning commute hadn’t changed.
The taxi driver honked at the occasional inconsiderate driver cutting into traffic on the congested road, then turned up the radio.

An F-rank Gate has appeared in Uldae-ri, Jangheung-myeon, Yangju City, and an immediate evacuation order has been issued. With nearby Hunters and military units cooperating to suppress it quickly, the confirmed number of casualties currently stands at six...
“Goddamn it. As if the traffic wasn’t bad enough, now those monster bastards are raising hell too.”
After delivering the colorful curse, he glanced at me in the passenger seat.
“You’re a Hunter too, right?”
“For now.”
At this point, I wasn’t entirely sure whether I was a Hunter or a Murim warrior.
Officially, at least in the modern world, I was a C-rank Hunter with Peace Guild.
The taxi driver grinned at my answer.
“I knew it. You can tell a Hunter at a glance.”
“I suppose so.”
It was like the difference between a herbivore and a carnivore.
There were exceptions, but everyone gave off a certain air. Someone my size carrying a large case had to be one of two things:
A musician who liked working out, or a Hunter.
You can tell at a glance.
It wasn’t anything particularly remarkable, especially for a taxi driver who met countless passengers every day.
But this middle-aged man’s mouth never stopped moving.
“Hey, can I ask you something?”
“Sure.”
“It feels like Gates have been opening more often lately. Can’t anything be done about that?”
“...What?”

“I mean, how are ordinary people like me supposed to live without worrying? A Gate could open in my apartment parking lot the moment I wake up in the morning. What’s the point of working my butt off taking fares when safe-zone land costs a fortune?”
I stared at him incredulously.
“That’s true, but why are you asking me?”
“I know. I’m just frustrated, that’s all. Frustrated.”
“...So am I.”
I was a Hunter, not a prophet.
How was I supposed to predict something even Nostradamus couldn’t?

No one could predict when a Gate would form. The only reason they could suppress them quickly was because they had spent astronomical sums installing magical-power measuring devices all over the place.
Just like the breaking news now coming over the radio.

Breaking news. The F-rank Gate reported earlier in Yangju City has been stabilized. Hunters and military forces have exterminated a total of fifty-eight goblins and are conducting a search for any remaining monsters...
“Every time you turn around, it’s Gates and monsters. I’m sick to death of it.”
Beep.
The taxi driver switched off the radio with an irritated jab.
An uncomfortable silence settled over the car, but I was more than happy to spend the rest of the trip in peace.
I wonder what Mom and Hayeon are doing right now.
I was gazing out the window, lost in thought, when it happened.
Honk! Hoooonk!
A faint blare pierced my ears, followed by a jumble of overlapping noises. I hurriedly rolled down the window.
What is that? Was there an accident?
The taxi driver stared at me in confusion.
“Why are you opening the window when I’ve got the air conditioner on—”
“Wait. Just give me a second.”
My serious tone silenced him. I drew up my internal energy.
My hearing and vision, already far beyond the limits of an ordinary human, swept across the congested road.
“Huh?”
Far in the distance, a black dot shot into the air.
It began to fall in an arc, and I realized what it was.
“...A car?”
It had been crushed into a ball, but I could still see it clearly.
The crumpled hood. The twisted scrap metal.
The shower of glass spilling from it as it hurtled toward us.
And exactly where it was going to land.
Whoooooosh!
Oh, shit.
Why here of all places?

“Put them back up before I beat you.”
“...Yes, sir.”
Jinho hurriedly raised his arms again, and a sigh escaped me.
The whole ridiculous situation had come out of nowhere, but at the same time, it left me feeling heavyhearted.
You should’ve told me sooner.
Maybe I couldn’t have done much for him in the past, but now I had more than enough means to help.
No, even back then, I would’ve supported him in every way I could.
After all the time we’ve spent together.
We weren’t related by blood, but he was as good as a real brother to me.
That was who Jinho was.
I’d even considered asking him to live with me for a while because I felt uneasy about leaving him on his own.
I was planning to tell Mom and Hayeon after the college entrance exam anyway, so there’s still some time, but...
I looked around the house, deep in thought.
It looked different from the home in my childhood memories, but it was still the house my family had finally reclaimed.
A house that still held traces of my father, whose voice had faded in my memory.
At last, I made up my mind and opened my mouth.
“This house won’t work, hyung.
I know you’ll be disappointed, but try to understand.”
Jinho forced a bright expression and shook his head.
“Why would I be disappointed?
This is all my fault.”
“What about your stuff?
Have you unpacked?”
“Not yet.
It’s only a few books and some clothes, so there isn’t much.
I’ll just leave with you when you go to work.”
Come to think of it, it had been bright outside for a while.
It was already eight o’clock.
Between the traffic and the distance from Ilsan to Bucheon, I was cutting it pretty close.
“I think we’ll have to leave separately.
Get your things ready.”
“Okay.”
“And clean the new place from top to bottom before I get off work.”
“Don’t get the wrong idea.
I’m not talking about this house.
Give me a second.”
I pulled out my phone and searched through my messages.
At last, I found the address I wanted in my chat with Team Leader Choi, whom I’d saved as “Designer-Brand Junkie.”
“Ah, here it is.
I just sent the address to your phone.
Find your own way there.”
“Wait.
What address?”
“An officetel.”
“Huh?”
“The Guild offered to provide me with a place.
I turned it down last time because accepting it felt like too much, but I might as well take them up on it now.”
A quiet laugh escaped me when I saw Jinho’s eyes widen.
“Why are you so surprised?
I’m doing pretty well these days.”
“This house needs remodeling anyway, so let’s live there together.
It’ll make my commute easier too.”
“Ta-Taekyung.”
I turned away, pretending not to hear the tremor in Jinho’s voice.
I had no desire to deal with an embarrassing scene first thing in the morning.
Nor did I particularly want to be thanked by the man who had comforted me through the hardest period of my life.
It’s fine.
Yeah.
This was enough.
It was mid-September.
The worst of the heat had passed, but the morning commute hadn’t changed.
The taxi driver honked at the occasional inconsiderate driver cutting into traffic on the congested road, then turned up the radio.
An F-rank Gate has appeared in Uldae-ri, Jangheung-myeon, Yangju City, and an immediate evacuation order has been issued.
With nearby Hunters and military units cooperating to suppress it quickly, the confirmed number of casualties currently stands at six...
“Goddamn it.
As if the traffic wasn’t bad enough, now those monster bastards are raising hell too.”
After delivering the colorful curse, he glanced at me in the passenger seat.
“You’re a Hunter too, right?”
“For now.”
At this point, I wasn’t entirely sure whether I was a Hunter or a Murim warrior.
Officially, at least in the modern world, I was a C-rank Hunter with Peace Guild.
The taxi driver grinned at my answer.
“I knew it.
You can tell a Hunter at a glance.”
“I suppose so.”
It was like the difference between a herbivore and a carnivore.
There were exceptions, but everyone gave off a certain air.
Someone my size carrying a large case had to be one of two things:
A musician who liked working out, or a Hunter.
You can tell at a glance.
It wasn’t anything particularly remarkable, especially for a taxi driver who met countless passengers every day.
But this middle-aged man’s mouth never stopped moving.
“Hey, can I ask you something?”
“Sure.”
“It feels like Gates have been opening more often lately.
Can’t anything be done about that?”
“...What?”
“I mean, how are ordinary people like me supposed to live without worrying?
A Gate could open in my apartment parking lot the moment I wake up in the morning.
What’s the point of working my butt off taking fares when safe-zone land costs a fortune?”
I stared at him incredulously.
“That’s true, but why are you asking me?”
“I know.
I’m just frustrated, that’s all.
Frustrated.”
“...So am I.”
I was a Hunter, not a prophet.
How was I supposed to predict something even Nostradamus couldn’t?
No one could predict when a Gate would form.
The only reason they could suppress them quickly was because they had spent astronomical sums installing magical-power measuring devices all over the place.
Just like the breaking news now coming over the radio.
Breaking news.
The F-rank Gate reported earlier in Yangju City has been stabilized.
Hunters and military forces have exterminated a total of fifty-eight goblins and are conducting a search for any remaining monsters...
“Every time you turn around, it’s Gates and monsters.
I’m sick to death of it.”
Beep.
The taxi driver switched off the radio with an irritated jab.
An uncomfortable silence settled over the car, but I was more than happy to spend the rest of the trip in peace.
I wonder what Mom and Hayeon are doing right now.
I was gazing out the window, lost in thought, when it happened.
Honk!
Hoooonk!
A faint blare pierced my ears, followed by a jumble of overlapping noises.
I hurriedly rolled down the window.
What is that?
Was there an accident?
The taxi driver stared at me in confusion.
“Why are you opening the window when I’ve got the air conditioner on—”
“Wait.
Just give me a second.”
My serious tone silenced him.
I drew up my internal energy.
My hearing and vision, already far beyond the limits of an ordinary human, swept across the congested road.
“Huh?”
Far in the distance, a black dot shot into the air.
It began to fall in an arc, and I realized what it was.
“...A car?”
It had been crushed into a ball, but I could still see it clearly.
The crumpled hood.
The twisted scrap metal.
The shower of glass spilling from it as it hurtled toward us.
And exactly where it was going to land.
Whoooooosh!
Oh, shit.
Why here of all places?

chapters.title: Chapter 207
paragraphs: Whoooosh.
An unidentified black sphere plummeted with a terrifying roar, tearing through the air.
As its shadow fell across the taxi, the driver, Mr. Park, knew he was going to die.
So this is how it ends.

The faces of his daughter, who had started high school that year, and his beloved wife flashed before his eyes. They had planned to go out for seolleongtang after work. Who knew that would be foreshadowing?
And today wasn’t even lucky.
He didn’t wonder what the thing was. Finding out wouldn’t change the fact that he was about to die.
All he could do was sit frozen like a statue and stare helplessly as death drew closer by the second.
Whoooom!
It was time to depart for the afterlife.
The sphere’s shadow swallowed the driver’s seat. Mr. Park squeezed his eyes shut and finally screamed.
“Gaaaaaaaaah!”
Boom! Craaash!
Sheet metal crumpled like paper, and shards of glass flew in every direction. Then, in the next instant—
“Whoa, my eardrums almost burst. You’ve got quite a set of lungs on you.”
“Gaaah... Huh?”
A voice pierced his ears.
Mr. Park stopped screaming and blinked.
“Huh? Huhhh?”
He couldn’t tell whether he was dreaming or awake.
He had definitely been sitting in the driver’s seat a second ago—no, half a second ago—but now he was sitting on the shoulder of the road roughly five meters away.
“W-What the hell...”
Mr. Park stared blankly at his taxi, now crushed flat, then looked up.
His savior was standing there—the man who had snatched him from the jaws of death.
“Y-You’re the passenger?”
The sturdily built young man, Jin Taekyung, did not answer. He was frowning at something in the distance.
“Sir.”
Mr. Park’s heart pounded. He already understood it instinctively. Something terrible was happening, and if he wanted to survive, he had to do exactly as this Hunter said.
“Run back the way we came. Don’t look back. Just keep running.”
“Y-Yes, sir!”
“And don’t forget to warn everyone else.”
“W-Warn them about what?”
Jin Taekyung pointed ahead.
Bright morning sunlight poured from the clear sky, but darkness was gathering where his finger pointed.
He spoke calmly to Mr. Park, whose mouth hung open in shock.
“A Gate has opened.”
At that moment, a bloodcurdling roar erupted from the far end of the road.
—Gwooooooar!
The monster’s roar was more effective than any loudspeaker.
The moment people realized what was happening, panic swept through them. They abandoned their cars and ran.
“A Gate! A Gate has appeared!”
“Run!”
“Seokjun! Honey!”
The gridlocked road descended into chaos in an instant.
Piercing screams and frantic shouts rang out from every direction.
I avoided the people sprinting back the way they had come and raced forward across the roofs of the cars. A System notification rang in my ears.
Ding.
System A sudden Quest, Gate Suppression, has been created. - You cannot refuse the Quest. - The Quest has been forcibly accepted!
Now it isn’t even giving me a choice.
Couldn’t it at least ask first?
I clicked my tongue and opened the Quest window. A translucent holographic panel popped into the air.

System Quest Gate Suppression An unexpected Gate has appeared! The monsters that have set foot on Earth are hungry for blood, and delicious prey surrounds them. Minimize casualties and eliminate the monsters to suppress the Gate. Grade: Peak Restriction: None Mission: Eliminate monsters (Incomplete) Reward: ??? Failure: ???
This was a goddamn disaster.
Of all places, a Gate had appeared on a road jammed with morning commuters—not at sea or in the mountains.
Worse, the monsters weren’t small fry like goblins or Orcs.
—Gwoooooooooar!
Boom! Krrr-boom!
They were larger than cargo trucks, with fangs bigger and sharper than industrial saw blades. Every swing of their dark iron clubs smashed concrete and cars to pieces.
In both strength and appearance, they were monsters in every sense of the word.
I never thought I’d run into creatures I’d only seen in monster encyclopedias on my way to work.
I muttered under my breath.
“Ogres...”
They were classified as B-rank monsters, but their strength and destructive instincts went far beyond that.
During the early days of the Great Cataclysm, it had been ogres who served as the vanguard of the monster legions and destroyed countless cities.
That must be why they’re considered top-tier even among B-rank monsters.
And now they had appeared right here.
The Gate had yet to open fully, so there were only five or six of them. Even that was an enormous threat.
I have to stop them before the casualties get any worse.
I wasn’t the only one who thought so. Eight hundred meters ahead, I saw about twenty figures charging toward the ogres as they swung their weapons in every direction.
“Stop them!”
Clang-clang-clang!
Gleaming armor, shields, and all manner of weapons.
They were Hunters.
B-rank Hunter Hwang Cheol Soo broke out in a cold sweat.
A Gate... appeared?
What were the odds of a Gate appearing? He didn’t know the exact figure, but he had heard they were lower than the odds of most natural disasters.

After the death of Demon King Asmodeus brought the Great Cataclysm to an end, the dozens of Gates that had once formed around the world each day became far less frequent. Leading scholars rushed to publish papers about the change.
Humanity’s Victory: The End of Gates.
The Connection Between Demon King Asmodeus and the Gates.
Complete Peace Within Ten Years.
But they had all been wrong.
Gates had once appeared only once or twice every year or two, yet this was already the fourth to form in the country this year.
Worse, that fourth Gate had opened at the tollgate Hwang Cheol Soo was responsible for.
And it’s a B-rank Gate.
That alone was horrifying enough, but the creatures emerging from it were ogres, classified as top-tier even among B-rank monsters.
Boom! Thud-thud-thud!
“Guh!”
“Healer!”
“Archers, keep firing! Tanks, draw their attention!”
Thud-thud-thud!
The tollgate team—two B-rank Hunters and fifteen C-rank Hunters—was being driven back helplessly.
After only two or three blows from an ogre’s iron club, tower shields shattered and the tanks went flying one after another.
What am I looking at?
Hwang Cheol Soo was only thirty.
He possessed neither combat instincts nor leadership ability. He was merely a public-service Hunter whose high rank had secured him a comfortable job and a generous pension.
What do I do? How am I supposed to handle this...?
As Hwang Cheol Soo stood frozen like a plaster statue, the assistant team leader shouted at him.
“Team Leader! Pull yourself together! We have to hold out until support arrives, no matter what it takes!”
“Y-Yeah. Right. We only have to last five more minutes.”
“We can take them once the special forces regiment and the nearby Hunters arrive. So—”
Wham! Boom!
Hwang Cheol Soo stared blankly as the assistant team leader was hurled into a refrigerated truck. A huge chunk of concrete had flown out of nowhere and struck him.
“Healer!”
The instant Hwang Cheol Soo shouted, he realized something.
The team had only two healers, and the assistant team leader had been the last one still standing.
Of the seventeen team members, Hwang Cheol Soo included, fewer than half remained on their feet.
“W-What the hell...”
Only one minute had passed since the battle began.
But the outcome had already been decided.
The gap between top-tier B-rank monsters and Hunters who had been lulled into peace while playing mobile games at a tollgate was simply overwhelming.
And their ordeal wasn’t over yet.
“Team Leader!”
“The Gate! Look at the Gate!”
Grkkk, grkkk—
At the team members’ shouts, the rift in the air began to widen.
Magical power churned within the pitch-black darkness as it spewed out enormous bodies.
—Gwoooooar!
—Kraaaagh!
Boom! Boom! Boom!
The ogres landed with savage bellows, and groans of despair rose from all around.
“Fuck...”
The Hunters had been overwhelmingly outmatched even with nearly three times the numbers.
Now that the number of ogres had risen to ten, despair settled heavily over them.
“T-Team Leader...”
“W-What do we do now?”
Hwang Cheol Soo swallowed dryly.
The difference in strength was overwhelming. The outcome was no longer in question.
Only one thought filled his mind.
Can I survive?
He wasn’t the only one wondering that. Everyone there shared the same question.
And they were waiting for their commander to give them the answer they wanted.
“Team Leader!”
Before he could finish speaking, Hwang Cheol Soo’s feet were already edging backward.
He had once sworn to become humanity’s shield and protect the people from the threat of monsters.
But he had no intention of dying like a dog here.
Even with reinforcements, we can’t kill those things.
That left only one option.
“B-Based on the commander’s judgment, we’ll make a strategic retreat...”
The moment Hwang Cheol Soo began speaking in a trembling voice—
Whoooooosh! Boom!
A streak of light shot past.
It flew over the heads of the Hunters slowly backing away, punched straight through its target, and blew it apart.
Splash.
What fell from the air in scattered droplets wasn’t rain, but blood. Chunks of rotten-smelling flesh followed, pelting down like hail.
Boom.
As someone let out a dazed murmur, the ogre’s enormous body toppled like a rotten old tree.
—Gwo?
“What the...?”
Humans and monsters alike stared blankly at the surreal sight.
Then—
“Whoa. What’s with that firepower?”
The cheerful voice was completely out of place.
Hwang Cheol Soo whirled around to find its owner, and goose bumps ran down his skin.
“Gasp.”
He hadn’t sensed the slightest trace of the newcomer’s presence. Even now, while staring directly at him, he still couldn’t.
But the figure standing tall atop a tour bus was neither a ghost nor a monster.
His eyes curved like half-moons between his roughly tousled black-brown hair.
“Hello.”
“W-Who are you?”
“Just someone on his way to work.”
“P-Pardon?”
“Uh, may I skip the formalities and get straight to the point?”
That was exactly what Hwang Cheol Soo wanted. The ogres had already recovered from their brief confusion and were approaching, dragging their iron clubs across the ground.
The Hunters nodded frantically. The young man, Jin Taekyung, grinned.
“If you’re not going to fight, all of you go stay tucked away in a corner.”
“Oh, and if I catch you stealing EXP, you’re dead.”
EXP? Stealing?
Before they could even figure out what he meant, the spear in Jin Taekyung’s hand turned into light and shot forward.
Whoooooosh!
Shriiiing! Crunch!
The spearhead punched through a thick jaw.
It tore through hide, flesh, tongue, and palate in succession before jutting out through the top of the ogre’s skull.
Iron clubs came hurtling in from both sides.
Whoooosh!
The air split with a terrifying shriek.
But I was already gone.
I slipped in close against one ogre’s body, pulled a dagger from my Inventory, and drove it precisely into its Huiyin Acupoint.
Stab!
—Gwoooooooooooooooooar!
“Congratulations on opening your Conception Vessel.”
There was a world of difference between having a pathway forced open and opening one up.
The ogre dropped to its knees with a howl that came from the depths of its soul.
Before it had time to feel any more pain, I slashed its throat with the dagger.
Squelch!
Monster blood and screams filled the air, while a succession of sweet sounds tickled my ears.
Ding. Ding. Ding.
System You have defeated Lv.84 Ogre! - You have acquired a considerable amount of EXP! - You have defeated Lv.83 Ogre! - You have acquired a considerable amount of EXP!
Buuuuurp.
Man, I’m stuffed.

I slipped in close against one ogre’s body, pulled a dagger from my Inventory, and drove it precisely into its Huiyin Acupoint.
Stab!
—Gwoooooooooooooooooar!
“Congratulations on opening your Conception Vessel.”
There was a world of difference between having a pathway forced open and opening one up.
The ogre dropped to its knees with a howl that came from the depths of its soul.
Before it had time to feel any more pain, I slashed its throat with the dagger.
Squelch!
Monster blood and screams filled the air, while a succession of sweet sounds tickled my ears.
Ding.
Ding.
Ding.
System You have defeated Lv.84 Ogre! - You have acquired a considerable amount of EXP! - You have defeated Lv.83 Ogre! - You have acquired a considerable amount of EXP!
Buuuuurp.
Man, I’m stuffed.

chapters.title: Chapter 208
paragraphs: Ranging unchecked in every direction.
That was me now. Wherever I looked, whatever came within reach, I cut, stabbed, and smashed my way through it. Every flash of my spearhead sent blood spraying and split flesh from bone.
I moved freely among the enormous ogres with nothing to stop me.
Srrk! Krrrunch!
—Gwooooooar!
With a death rattle, the three-meter-tall hulk dropped to its knees.
The Gate continued spewing out ogres, but they posed no problem for me. When two came out, I killed three. When three came out, I killed four.
This is easy. Almost ridiculously so.
The last time I had assigned points was during my duel with Chulwoo.
But opening my Conception and Governor Vessels had pushed my control and explosive power over my internal energy—as well as my senses—to an entirely new level.
Even when the ogres’ iron clubs came crashing down from every direction with tremendous force, they looked unbelievably slow.
To me, the ogres were nothing but idiots who had no idea how to use their own strength.
Whoooosh! Thud!
—Grrrgh...
Another ogre—I’d lost count by now—dropped to its knees with a wet, blood-choked rattle.
Its furry hand reached for the spearhead piercing straight through its Adam’s apple, then went limp and fell away.
Ding.
System You have defeated Lv.85 Ogre! - You have acquired a considerable amount of EXP! - Level Up!
“Oh.”
I’d leveled up already.
Clearing them out by myself was raking in EXP at an insane rate.
Is it because every last one of these bastards is higher-level than me?
My current Level was somewhere in the mid-to-high seventies, putting the ogres anywhere from five to ten Levels above me.
And since I was slicing through them like slabs of pork shoulder at a butcher shop, it was only natural that my Level would rise quickly.
The EXP was far more generous than I’d expected.
No, wait.
A thought flashed through my mind.
Eyes shining, I stared at the Gate as it churned and spat out another ogre.
This place was practically...
The hottest restaurant in town.
The Gate kept spitting out EXP—or rather, monsters—and I kept killing them. If that cycle continued...
So this is where the conveyor-belt sushi place was hiding.
The EXP from the ogres was sweeter than tuna belly.
My mouth curled into a grin at the thought of chewing up every ogre that came out and digesting them into points.
That was when it happened.
Vroooom. Rat-a-tat-tat-tat!
—Hold! Hold!
—Drop!
Three or four combat helicopters flew in on a blast of wind and circled overhead. Around twenty Hunters dropped from them like bolts of lightning.
Shu-shu-shu-shu!
They were falling from a height of more than twenty meters. From that high up, even Hunters equipped with magical Equipment were bound to strain their knees on landing.
But these newcomers weren’t the incompetent amateurs who had been here before I arrived.
“Feather Fall.”
At the mage’s incantation, a ripple of mana passed through the air.
The bodies plunging rapidly toward the ground began to slow. The ogres about to swing their iron clubs hesitated when their timing was thrown off, and then the second spell activated.
“Grease!”
—Gwo?
Boom! Crash!
The four remaining ogres lost their balance. Some staggered, while others collapsed to the ground.
“Now!”
At the shout, the spell slowing the Hunters’ descent was released, and the melee fighters shot forward like streaks of light.
The ogres let out low growls as they sensed their imminent deaths.
That was when—
Clang! Clang-clang!
The Hunters who had been about to plunge their weapons into the ogres’ chests stared at me in disbelief.
What the hell did this bastard just do?
Is he insane?
That was exactly what their faces said.
I had knocked aside every one of their attacks with a single swing. In my most reasonable voice, I said, “Come on. Let’s show a little professional courtesy.”
These bastards were trying to steal mobs I already had dead to rights.
“That really happened?”
At the captain’s question, the Hunter Team Leader nodded.
“Yes. I’ve been on the support team for two years, and I’ve never seen anyone like him.”
“He sounds interesting.”
“Interesting? He’s a complete psycho.”
“Perhaps.”
The captain slowly surveyed the area.
The tollgate had collapsed so completely that its original shape was unrecognizable, and monster blood lay splattered across the half-destroyed road.
There were overturned and wrecked cars as well, but not many.
“How many casualties?”
Soldiers and Hunters had different statuses, but both were registered with the government as members of military support teams.
The Hunter Team Leader promptly answered his superior’s question.
“So far, four dead and five severely injured. We’ll know more once we finish checking.”
“Four dead and five severely injured.”
The captain calmly repeated the figures, then continued.
“This is already the second Gate occurrence today.”
“Tell me about it. An F-rank Gate erupted near Yangju City about an hour ago. I don’t know if something serious is going on.”
The captain clicked his tongue.
“Hey, Team Leader Jeong.”
“Yes, sir.”
“An F-rank Gate that appeared in the town center, or a B-rank Gate that appeared in the middle of a road packed with commuters. Which one looks more serious?”
“Well...”
“But the F-rank Gate caused more casualties. Ten dead and more than twenty severely injured.”
“What? That can’t be right. The breaking news said...”
“They downplayed it. Covered it up. You’ve been doing this for two years. You should know how things work around here by now.”
The captain let out a deep sigh.
“As far as we’re concerned, a hundred bows wouldn’t be enough to thank him. He’s a civilian hero who single-handedly prevented a catastrophe.”
“That’s true. He does seem a little crazy, though.”
“Team Leader Jeong.”
“Ah, no, that’s not what I meant. I mean he’s insanely strong and crazy. He killed more than ten ogres by himself, so he must be an A-rank Hunter or something.”
“Either way, watch what you say. There are plenty of ears around.”
“They’re all our people. What ears could there be—ah.”
Team Leader Jeong followed the captain’s gaze and immediately scowled.
A skinny, middle-aged man carrying an expensive camera was approaching with an excited spring in his step.
“Captain Yoo! Team Leader Jeong! Where have you two been hiding? I’ve been looking everywhere.”
The Hunter Team Leader replied with open displeasure.
“Hiding from you, Reporter Kim.”
“Oh, come on. Why are you so prickly today, Team Leader Jeong? I’m part of the support team too.”

“You’re only part of the team at times like this, huh? The rest of the time, you’re a military correspondent. You’re usually drowning in a hangover, and now you’re beside yourself just because you landed a scoop.”
The reporter flinched, and the captain stepped in.
“That’s enough. And Reporter Kim, please be more mindful in the future. This is an accident scene. Running around by yourself in high spirits because you found a scoop doesn’t look good.”
“...Ahem. I’ll be more careful from now on.”
Even as he answered, anticipation gleamed in the reporter’s eyes.
A Gate occurrence was nothing short of a natural disaster. In some ways, it was even worse.

If a typhoon was going to strike the Korean Peninsula, people could at least predict when and how it would arrive and which areas might be damaged. There was no predicting where or when a Gate would form.
Two Gates in one day was already unprecedented, and one of them was even B-rank.
A tollgate security team helplessly overrun, followed by the heroic arrival of an unknown Hunter who prevented a rush-hour catastrophe!
It was a great story.
The reporter had already sketched the whole article out in his head, and he was itching to get started.
“So where’s our hero? He’s an A-rank Hunter, right? What’s his name? A fresh new face would sell better for a story like this.”
“A new face? Give me a break.”
The Hunter Team Leader pointed behind the reporter.
“He’s over there. Your new face.”
“Where? I don’t see him.”
No matter how much he looked around, there was no sign of a hero clad in gleaming armor.
All he could see were military personnel busily cleaning up the accident scene.
The reporter’s eyes swept across the area before suddenly stopping.
“There, Team Leader Jeong. Is that him? In front of the ogre corpse...”
“The man in the sweatpants? Yes, that’s him.”
Swish. Srrk, srrk.
Squatting as if he were making a huge batch of kimchi, the young man deftly separated the fat, meat, and hide from the corpse. The reporter muttered,
“...Now that’s a new face.”
“Fresh, right? Isn’t that the picture you wanted?”
“The ogre meat certainly looks fresh.”
“He’s been at it for a while. The staff offered to do it for him, but he won’t let them touch anything. Says it’s all his.”
Even funnier, his butchering technique was unbelievably good. The two employees assigned to process the corpses kept sneaking glances at his hands and copying his movements.
“Is he really an A-rank Hunter?”
“Who knows? He must be if he can wipe out ogres by himself, but the longer I look at him, the less convinced I am.”
“Team Leader Jeong asked him, but he said they could talk once he finished butchering.”
The three men exchanged looks filled with equal parts belief and doubt.
That was when—
“Whew. Finished.”
The A-rank Hunter, who had cut the notoriously tough ogre meat into pieces like mackerel, straightened his back and stood up.
The reporter took in his sweatpants, baggy at the knees, and his three-striped slides, then muttered,
“Why does a guy who makes that much money live like this?”
Was this some kind of humblebrag?
It was absurd, yet the longer the reporter looked, the more novel the whole thing seemed. After all, nothing mattered more in the media than character.
A down-to-earth A-rank Hunter with a fierce sense of justice. This will make a great story. He’s handsome, too, with bold, clean-cut features.
Yes, this was much better than some polished model-student image.
The reporter grinned and raised his camera.
He wanted a natural shot with no staging whatsoever.
That’s an ogre for you. Not a single part goes to waste.
I looked over the neatly separated by-products with a satisfied smile.
Ogres were practically symbols of strength, which made them popular among men.
There were plenty of customers, but because ogres were classified among the highest tier of B-rank monsters, the supply was limited.
Good thing I only went for their vital spots.
I was humming as I sorted the by-products when—
Click.
I turned toward the mechanical sound that had come out of nowhere.
A middle-aged man repeatedly pressing his camera shutter smiled amiably at me.
“Oh dear, did I startle you?”
What the hell is with this guy?
I stared at him incredulously. “Most people are surprised when someone takes their picture without permission. You expect me to be happy about it?”
“You might be once you’re in tomorrow’s newspaper.”
“The newspaper?”
“Ah, I haven’t introduced myself yet. Here, let’s start with my business card.”
I accepted the military-camouflage business card and read it aloud.
“Military correspondent.”
“You know the Capital Defense Command, right? I’m the military correspondent assigned to Support Team 25.”
“Ah, yes.”
“And the two gentlemen coming up behind me are from the support team as well.”
The reporter smiled and gave me a thumbs-up as two men approached from behind him.
One wore a Special Forces uniform and the other wore armor. They were, well, dressed like your stereotypical soldier and Hunter.
“Nice to meet you. I’m Captain Yoo Sijin, Team Leader of Support Team 25.”
“Ah, yes.”
For some reason, that sounded like a name the sun might regret.
I tilted my head and exchanged introductions with the two men.
The perfunctory introductions and praise for my heroic deed had barely ended when the military correspondent, who had been staring at me with fervent eyes, spoke up.
“You said you’re Hunter Jin Taekyung, correct?”
“Yes. Why?”
“Given the field I cover, I know nearly every A-rank Hunter. But...”
Ah, I had a pretty good idea what he was trying to say.
It was something I would have to deal with sooner or later.
I answered readily, “I’m not A-rank.”
“What?”
“And I’m not S-rank either, of course.”
Question marks seemed to appear on all three faces at once. I couldn’t help chuckling.
This is fun.
After being knocked around this way and that in another world, I hide my strength in reality.
That would make a decent novel title.
When I merely smiled without answering, the reporter spoke in a faltering voice.
“Th-Then perhaps you’re B-rank?”
“No. I’m C-rank.”
“...C-rank? You mean C-rank, not C-cup?”
“Yes.”
What kind of bullshit is C-cup? And why the hell is he looking at my chest?
I ignored their waves of disbelief and continued, “I was on my way to the Guild when a Gate happened to open...”
“Th-Then what?”
I couldn’t answer the reporter’s urgent question.
I had just remembered something I’d momentarily forgotten.
“...By any chance, what time is it?”
Damn it. I’m late.
