chapters.title: Chapter 209
paragraphs: Ten in the morning.
Im Kkeokjeong, a D-rank Hunter with the Peace Guild, arrived at work after a blissful vacation and stopped dead, his mouth hanging open.
“Whoa. What is this?”
His reaction was understandable.
Before his vacation—just one week ago—the Guild House had looked like a run-down neighborhood corner store on the verge of collapse.
But now, right before his eyes, stood a sign made of gleaming marble and luxurious lettering.
<Peace Guild>
“Wow. They really went all out on the remodeling.”
As Kkeokjeong admired the exterior, a familiar voice came from somewhere.
“Why are you standing outside instead of coming in?”
Startled, he looked around. But there wasn’t so much as an ordinary security camera or intercom in sight, so he cautiously spoke up.
“Te-Team Leader Choi? Is that you?”
“Yes. It’s me.”
“What is this? How are you talking to me?”
The reply came without a moment’s hesitation, as though he had been waiting for that exact question.
“It’s nothing special. We commissioned Vercheni, a venerable Italian family of artisans, to custom-make it for us. It incorporates message, observation, and alarm magic...”
“Ah, no. You don’t have to explain all that.”
“Oh. Then simply open the mahogany door, which is covered in the hide of a fire-resistant salamander, and come inside...”
“I’m coming in! I said I’m coming in!”
Click.
The locked door slid open along with the strangely dejected reply.
The interior of the Guild House had changed just as dramatically as the exterior. Three people were waiting for Kkeokjeong inside.
“Welcome back.”
“Hunter Im.”
“Uncle, you’re here?”
There was Team Leader Choi, the true power behind the Peace Guild; Butler Kim, its nominal Guild Master; and Song Song, the guild’s sole female member.
The three of them were seated around a round table. As they greeted him in turn, Im Kkeokjeong let out a good-natured laugh.
“Maybe it’s because it’s been a while, but it’s good to see you all. Did everyone get plenty of rest over the vacation?”
The moment he finished speaking, the expressions of all three changed strangely.
After a brief silence, Song Song spoke.
“I got some rest. There were so many bugs at home that they kept bothering me, though.”
“Bugs?”
“Yes. Didn’t you have any bugs at your place, Uncle?”
Kkeokjeong tilted his head.
Come to think of it, his wife had complained about something similar a few times during their vacation.
“Nothing much, just a fly or two. She said they kept coming in no matter how many she caught, so I left them alone, and then they quieted down. They hardly flew around, either.”
“Oh, really?”
“Yeah. I’ve never seen such well-behaved flies.”
Song Song shuddered uneasily.
“There were so many of them that I felt too creeped out to shower. It was like the bugs were watching me.”
“The bugs? Hahaha! Miss Song, you sure know how to joke around.”
Im Kkeokjeong threw his head back and laughed. He failed to notice the other three exchanging meaningful looks and words he could not hear.
Hunter Im doesn’t seem to know.
Looks like he didn’t notice.
Wow. How can this guy be so oblivious?
Unlike the other three, who had spent their entire vacation under surveillance by Familiars sent by the Sangdong Guild, Kkeokjeong had enjoyed a truly blissful break without knowing a thing.
It wasn’t that he hadn’t been watched. He had been watched; he simply didn’t know it.
Ignorance truly was bliss.
“Those fucking perverts. If I catch them later, I’m going to rip their balls off.”
Song Song’s muttering would have sent chills down the spines of the Sangdong Guild’s mages if they had heard it.
Kkeokjeong abruptly stopped laughing.
“Huh? What did you just say? Perverts?”
“No. I just said the bugs were disgusting.”
“Is it still bad? I know someone who works in that line of business. Want me to ask them about it?”
Song Song gave a quiet laugh at his genuine concern, then pressed her lips together and pointed at the two people sitting beside her.
“They’re all gone now. Those two took care of it. Especially Butler Kim.”
“Really? Kim hyung—I mean, Guild Master. I guess you know a thing or two about that kind of work.”
Butler Kim answered with an awkward smile.
“Not really. It just so happens that a junior of mine works in that field.”
“Ah, pest control?”
“...Yes. Something like that.”
In a way, monsters were merely enormous pests, so that wasn’t entirely wrong.
Im Kkeokjeong, who had effectively turned one of Bucheon’s leading Hunter Guilds into Cesco, continued in all seriousness.
“Your junior must be pretty good at his job.”
“Oh, he is.”
He was so good at beating them down that he was one of the war heroes of the Great Cataclysm.
Of course, to Butler Kim, Sangdong Guild Master Im Chunsoo was merely one of the trainees he had once worked like a dog.
“Let’s leave it at that. More importantly...”
Team Leader Choi had been grimacing for some time as he struggled to hold back his laughter. He quickly changed the subject.
There happened to be one person who made for a much more suitable topic.
“Why isn’t Jin Taekyung here?”
While they had been chatting and laughing, their scheduled start time had long since passed.
Only now realizing Jin Taekyung’s absence, Im Kkeokjeong nervously stroked his beard.
“What’s going on? Taekyung’s never done this before. When it comes to diligence, he’s the best person I know.”
“I’m well aware of that.”
Team Leader Choi nodded.

He had already investigated Taekyung’s past thoroughly. Judging by the several years documented in the report and everything he had personally witnessed since, Taekyung’s diligence and tenacity were genuine.
The raid starts in two hours...
Had something happened?
Team Leader Choi was still considering the possibilities as he picked up his phone when Song Song, who had been quiet for a while, suddenly spoke.
“Taurus—I mean, Jin Taekyung.”
“He’s right there.”
Her pale, slender finger pointed over Team Leader Choi’s shoulder.
The next moment, the guild members naturally turned in the direction she indicated, and their mouths fell open.
A familiar face filled the eighty-inch television screen mounted on the wall of the Guild House.
“Taekyung! Isn’t that Taekyung?”
“I-I believe that is indeed Hunter Jin Taekyung.”
Even the perpetually composed Butler Kim was so flustered that he stammered.
By then, however, the guild members’ attention had already been seized by the caption beneath Taekyung’s face.
Jin Taekyung (Wonmi-gu, Bucheon. C-rank Hunter)
Live: Tollgate Hero
“Tollgate Hero? What’s that supposed to mean? Why can’t we hear anything?”
“It’s muted! The TV’s on mute! Turn the sound on, quick!”
Only after someone hurriedly fiddled with the television did the blocked sound begin to spill out.
Fwoosh-fwoosh-fwoosh-fwoosh! Rat-a-tat-a-tat!
Along with some incomprehensible noise, Jin Taekyung’s voice continued.
“...And that’s how it happened.”
“I see. Then could you give us a few final words about how you feel?”
“Uh, first of all, I love my family very much, and I’m incredibly grateful to all the members of the Peace Guild. And to the person I like...”
“Yes! I see.”
“W-Wait a second.”
“That’s all the time we have. Viewers, this has been our interview with Jin Taekyung, the Tollgate Hero!”
After one last shot of the reporter’s beaming face, the screen switched to a cosmetics commercial.
Im Kkeokjeong shouted, “What the hell was that? I couldn’t hear anything!”
“Hold on. I’ll search for it right now. Tollgate Hero, Tollgate Hero... Holy crap.”
“Song-i. What is it?”
Song Song had frozen, her eyes wide. Without a word, she held out her phone.
The main page of the web portal was displayed on the screen. The three syllables of Jin Taekyung’s name were plastered across it.
“Jin Taekyung is number one on the real-time search rankings.”
The Guild House fell silent as though someone had dumped ice water over everyone inside.
No one knew what to say about this completely unexpected turn of events.
Then—
Fwoosh-fwoosh-fwoosh-fwoosh! Rat-a-tat-a-tat!
“Whoa.”
“No way.”
It was the same sound they had heard during Jin Taekyung’s interview only a few dozen seconds earlier.
Everyone whipped around to look at the television, only to sigh when they saw the cosmetics commercial was still playing.
But only for a moment.
“Wait. Then why can we still hear it?”
Team Leader Choi and Butler Kim were the first to realize where the noise was coming from. They shouted together.
“Outside!”
“It’s outside! It isn’t the television!”
Crash!
The words had barely left their mouths when everyone sprang to their feet.
“Whoa, what is this?”
“Is this the right place?”
“Yeah, this is the Peace Guild. I heard they remodeled, but it looks incredible.”
“Would it be possible to interview the other guild members as well?”
“No. You cut my interview short earlier.”
“Hunter, about earlier...”
The speaker spell relayed the conversation with perfect clarity.
With the other guild members watching, Team Leader Choi steadied his breathing and brought the message-magic Equipment to his mouth.
“Jin Taekyung. It’s me.”
“Whoa, what the hell? Sound Transmission? Is that you, Team Leader Choi?”
“Yes.”
“What was that? How did you do it?”
Team Leader Choi opened his mouth without hesitation.
It was an instinct etched deep into his bones.
“It’s nothing special. We commissioned Vercheni, a venerable Italian family of artisans, to custom-make it for us...”
Kkeokjeong muttered a string of vicious curses under his breath.
I went to sleep and woke up a star.
I had never imagined I would experience that saying for real in my lifetime.
Especially not in real time like this.
“Hey, registered sibling. I just saw something I can’t believe.”
“Registered sibling? You want to die?”
“No, that’s not the point right now.”
Hayeon’s voice over the phone was filled with shock and disbelief.
“Oppa, your name is on Naver’s real-time search rankings...”
I could easily guess what she was about to say.
I had already received dozens of calls with similar questions over the past few hours.
I cut Hayeon off before she could continue.
“Number one on the real-time search rankings. Yeah, that’s me. It really is.”
“...Seriously? The Seoul Outer Ring Expressway Tollgate Hero? That’s you?”
“Don’t call me that. I’m dying of embarrassment.”
“Wow. I guess it really is you. The second I tapped your name, your profile picture popped up under ‘Person in the News.’ Even after seeing it, I still thought there was no way.”
Even I hadn’t expected it to cause such a huge stir.
Only a few hours had passed, but searching my name online already brought up dozens of clickbait articles.
“What on earth happened? I read the articles, and it sounded insane. You’re not hurt, are you?”
“I didn’t even get a scratch, and it’d take too long to tell you the whole story. What about Mom? Has she heard the news about me?”
“Not yet. But if she finds out you fought monsters like that, she’ll faint.”
Hayeon wasn’t exaggerating.
What kind of creature was an ogre?
Even someone who knew nothing about monsters could search a few times and learn that they were every bit as powerful as their grotesque appearance suggested.
I could already picture how Mom would react when she heard her son had fought such monsters.
“Damn. You’re right.”
“Ugh, I don’t even know anymore. Get home before everything blows up and at least show her your face.”
“Okay. I’ll stop by after the interview.”
“Interview? Are you doing one right now?”
“Yeah.”
“Where? For a women’s magazine or something?”
“The KPS Nine O’Clock News Desk. I’m waiting for my turn.”
“...Holy crap.”
Just as I was about to answer Hayeon, a television-station producer weighed down with Equipment urgently waved at me.
“This is live, so I have to go. See you at home later.”
“Uh-huh? O-Okay...”
I hung up and headed toward a news studio I had only ever seen on television.
Recording Equipment filled the place, and the station staff were all watching me. My mouth went dry, and my legs began to shake.
I’d rather fight a hundred ogres.
Each second felt like an eternity, but at last, the signal I had been waiting for came.
“We’re going live. Stand by... cue!”

paragraphs: Sometimes, a carelessly tossed spark can grow into a massive blaze.
A day passed, then two, then three... and after about a week, that tiny spark had spread into a forest fire—with me standing at its center.
[Korea Daily] The Rise of an F-Rank Hunter. “I Just Followed the Manual.”
[Goryeo Daily] The Birth of a New Hero. “Watch Out, S-Rank Hunters!”
[Happy Thoughts] Man in His Twenties Prevents Major Disaster. “I Only Did What Anyone Should Have Done.”
[Current Hot Topic] Two Gates Open in a Single Day... An Unprecedented Crisis, and a Fierce Clash Between the Ruling and Opposition Parties Over National Defense and Security
[Parliament’s Words of the Day] Freedom Patriot Party Chairman’s Outrageous Remark Draws Attention: “Jin Taekyung Has Thick Arms, So He’s Clearly Conservative. Conservatives Saved the Country.”
Daily newspapers, weekly papers, current-affairs magazines, lifestyle magazines, and more.
The newspapers and magazines piled high on the table all had one thing in common: my face and name were plastered across them.
Even looking at them was enough to make me feel overwhelmed by the sheer volume.
Why are there so many?
How many interviews had I given over the past week?
Every media outlet hungry for an exclusive had seized the opportunity and unleashed a flood of articles.
Reporters had staked out the Guild House and my home, while my personal information, past activities, and photographs circulated across the internet.
Jesus. These people are fucking insane.
I had thought I was somewhat used to fame after becoming fairly well-known in Murim, but compared to this, that had been nothing.
Korea had long been an internet powerhouse, and even those respectable, gray-haired people in their fifties had histories as keyboard warriors.
The saying that you could meet the entire country just by visiting a few major online communities wasn’t baseless nonsense.
“Why is everyone so interested in other people’s business?”
At my mutter, Jinho hyung shrugged while eating bibimbap from a large metal bowl.
“It’s a good thing. You’re famous for doing something good.”
“I don’t know about that. There are all kinds of lunatics out there.”
“Ah, right. What happened with your family...”
Jinho quietly shut his mouth when he saw my expression. I hadn’t looked in a mirror, but I was sure I looked downright murderous.
Of all the people they could’ve messed with, they went after my family?
The world really was a big place, and it was full of lunatics.
After I appeared on the KPS Nine O’Clock News, the public response exploded, and reporters hungry for a fresh scoop combed through everything connected to me with a fine-tooth comb.
The problem was that my family’s personal information had been exposed in the process.
“You know Hayeon called a few days ago, right? Reporters kept following her whenever she went out, so she ordered delivery—and the delivery guy turned out to be a reporter in disguise.”
“Yeah, that bastard really was a hack. I’d heard stories about reporters like that, but I never imagined they’d actually go that far.”
“Some of them even hired Familiar mages.”
If that wasn’t hack journalism and paparazzi behavior, I didn’t know what was.
I saw red when I first heard about it, but before I could personally go after the reporter and the media outlet, netizens rose up like wildfire.
Several massive online communities, each claiming more than a million registered members, were still blazing away with hack reporters as their firewood.

A national petition went up about it, and it passed three million signatures yesterday. The Blue House is supposedly preparing legislation. Looks like they’re going to overhaul the whole system this time. └ We’ll have to wait and see, but I really hope they do. └ They’ll probably clean house while they’re at it. Blinded by their hunger for an exclusive, they messed with someone they never should have touched. └ Me. A man in his twenties. Everyone my age. Loves Jin Taekyung.
The response left me more bewildered than anything else. I was happy, but it also felt like a burden.
I really only did what anyone should have done.
It had been an accident no one could have predicted.

The news kept calling me a hero who had prevented a major disaster, but every now and then, I found myself wondering whether there might have been one fewer casualty if I had been just a little faster.
“What’s with that expression?”
“Huh? Nothing.”
“Someone with nothing wrong doesn’t pick at his food like that.”
“I’ve already eaten three bowls.”
“You normally eat at least five.”
“...That’s true.”
“Hey, Taekyung. I’m not really qualified to give you advice, but let me say one thing.”
It had been a while since I’d heard Jinho sound so serious. He set down his spoon, still smeared with red pepper paste, and continued slowly.
“Don’t try to be a hero.”
“You’re not a god. How can you save everyone? Even gods can’t do that.”
He was right.
I wasn’t denying the existence or power of a god, but that didn’t mean I could reconcile myself to it, either.

The only things I knew for certain were that hundreds of millions of people had died during the Great Cataclysm, that my father had died in an accident, and that my family had lived a poor, desperate life.
“What was your dream again?”
“To let my family live without envying anyone else. To protect the people I care about.”
“Sum it up in one word.”
A quiet laugh escaped me.
Instead of landlord, the word I’d parroted day in and day out, something unexpected came to mind.
The greatest under heaven... no, the greatest of all time?
I briefly lost myself in thought, then hurriedly answered when I saw Jinho’s puzzled expression.
“Hmm. A strong Hunter landlord?”
“Exactly. That’s enough. You’ve practically achieved your dream already, so don’t torment yourself with pointless greed and guilt.”
“Pointless greed...”
“Let me ask you one thing. Taekyung, did you fight those monsters because you wanted all this?”
“Absolutely not.”
“Then that’s enough.”
Jinho grinned and picked up his spoon again.
“Just enjoy it. Think of it as a reward for all the hardship you’ve endured and the good you’ve done. Wouldn’t that make things easier?”
A reward.
I had already received plenty of rewards through the System, but the reward Jinho was talking about meant something completely different.
It wasn’t something material or some kind of power. It was an emotional reward.
He was telling me to find some contentment and room to breathe.
Contentment and room to breathe.
The words felt unfamiliar as I repeated them silently.
Back when I was an F-rank Hunter, I fought monsters for money. Now, I was working even harder to become stronger.
The more I thought about it, the more I realized what a greedy bastard I was.
“Hyung.”
“Yeah? What is it?”
“Nothing. Just... thanks.”
Jinho froze with a heaping spoonful of bibimbap halfway to his mouth.
“Really?”
“I mean it.”
“Then lend me a hundred thousand won.”
“Don’t start talking about money just because things got awkward.”
“I mean it, too.”
What the hell was with this guy?
As I stared at him in disbelief, the phone on the table buzzed, and a text message appeared.
Team Leader Choi Team Leader Choi I’ve arrived. Come down to the underground parking garage right away.
Just as his message said, Team Leader Choi was waiting for me in the underground parking garage.
The problem was that he wasn’t alone.
“I’m from Oh My God News! Could you say a few words about the current situation?”
“Mr. Jin Taekyung, I’m Reporter Hong from Housewives’ Daily. You were voted the number-one ideal man among married women in their forties this week...”
“This is Vivid Current-Affairs Talk! What do you think about the comment in Parliament regarding the size of your arms?”
“Where are you going right now? What did you eat?”
More than twenty people thrust cameras and microphones at me. It was utter chaos.
While I let out a deep sigh, Team Leader Choi calmly pushed back the enemy forces.
“Please step aside.”
“Just a moment. It’ll only take a second.”
“Mr. Jin Taekyung is a member of the Peace Guild. Please submit interview requests through the Guild’s official website.”
When had they even made an official website?
They had posted a massive recruitment notice for new Guild members not long ago, too. It seemed they intended to make the most of this opportunity.
But despite Team Leader Choi’s efforts to stop them, the reporters clung to us stubbornly. Apparently, not getting a single interview over the past few days had eaten away at them.
“You’re the Team Leader of the Peace Guild, right? We weren’t asking you, so move!”
“Yeah, get out of the way! Your website is garbage, too. How long are we supposed to wait after submitting an inquiry before we get an interview?”
“It’s just one word. Why are you acting so precious?”
“Are you looking down on us because we’re a tiny second-rate media outlet?”

“Mr. Jin Taekyung is my team member, and I am currently the Guild’s spokesperson, so I have every right to intervene. The website is functioning normally, I have never played hard to get, and I ignored you because you failed to follow the proper procedure.”
Team Leader Choi answered without so much as blinking as he smoothly pushed the reporters and cameramen aside.
He looked slender, but an incredible amount of strength was packed into that body. He was only using one arm, yet the people blocking our path were pushed back one after another.
“Whoa!”
“Hey, he’s using force now?”
“A Hunter! The Hunter is beating people up!”
Go on, make a whole fucking scene...
I swallowed the words that had risen to my throat.
Just by looking at them, I could tell the reporters in front of us were low quality.

Team Leader Choi had arranged dozens of interviews over the past week as the Guild’s spokesperson. If he was filtering these people out, it didn’t take a taste test to tell whether they were soybean paste or shit.
Why are their questions such garbage in the first place?
They weren’t worth answering. Anything I said would obviously be twisted maliciously before publication.
“We’re coming through.”
Team Leader Choi ignored them and continued clearing a path.
“Whoops!”
Crack!
A camera slipped from someone’s hand, struck the parking-garage floor, and shattered.
The problem was that the entire sequence felt blatantly deliberate.
“My camera! Oh, no!”
His voice was full of anguish, but his eyes gleamed as if he had finally caught us.
Team Leader Choi stared at the cameraman’s terrible acting, then bent down and reached for the broken device.
The cameraman irritably slapped his arm away.
“Don’t touch it! Everything you did was recorded, so you’d better be ready—”
Smack! Crack.
Everyone’s eyes dropped to the floor.
The wristwatch that had fallen from Team Leader Choi’s wrist rolled across the parking-garage floor.
More than ten watch hands. Jewels set densely across its surface. And a face cracked like a spiderweb.
Gulp.
The sound of the cameraman swallowing echoed through the parking garage.
Then Team Leader Choi’s quiet voice pierced everyone’s ears.

“The Universe-302, the final masterpiece personally crafted in his later years by Peter Philip, Switzerland’s greatest watchmaker. How tragic that this beautiful pinnacle of automatic mechanical watchmaking, which survived even the Great Cataclysm, should be destroyed so senselessly.”
Team Leader Choi picked up the watch—Universe, School Bus, or whatever it was—with sorrowful eyes and delivered the final blow.
“I’m suing you.”
At Choi Moses’s miracle, the crowd parted in two.
Vroom.
The luxury sedan glided smoothly over the asphalt.
Team Leader Choi glanced at the rearview mirror and spoke.
“They aren’t following us anymore.”
“...I wouldn’t follow us, either. How much is that watch worth?”
“More than you can imagine. Assuming it’s genuine, of course.”
“Oh, it’s an imitation? No wonder. I thought it was strange that you’d throw away such a valuable luxury watch so easily.”
“You noticed?”
“It would’ve been even stranger if a wristwatch came loose that easily.”
“I only scared them a little. I wore it in case something like this happened. It was a good choice.”
Wasn’t this guy basically Zhuge Liang?
As I admired Team Leader Choi’s clever trick, something suddenly darted in front of the sedan just as we were leaving the officetel neighborhood.
“Team Leader Choi!”
Screeeeeech!
Team Leader Choi hit the brakes half a beat before I shouted. Staring through the windshield at the person in front of us, he muttered,
“He doesn’t look like a reporter.”
I agreed.
An ordinary person could not wear such a relaxed smile in a situation like this.
And...
Even without activating Qi Sense, I could feel the considerable energy coiled within the man smiling at us.
A Hunter. A pretty high-level one, too.
The uninvited guest, a man in his early thirties wearing a suit, tapped on the window.
“Let’s talk.”

[Happy Thoughts] Man in His Twenties Prevents Major Disaster.

[Current Hot Topic] Two Gates Open in a Single Day...
An Unprecedented Crisis, and a Fierce Clash Between the Ruling and Opposition Parties Over National Defense and Security
[Parliament’s Words of the Day] Freedom Patriot Party Chairman’s Outrageous Remark Draws Attention: “Jin Taekyung Has Thick Arms, So He’s Clearly Conservative.

How many people survived because of Taekyung the Lord, and they’re pulling this shit?
I’m embarrassed for them. └ They would’ve done the same thing even if their own families had been there.
They’re just fucking crazy. └ What company is it?
Post the article link. └ Hailey News.
Reporter B.H.Y.
The original’s been deleted, but it’s already too late, LOL. └ Let’s turn it into Hell News. └ It already is.
The site’s been shut down.

What happened to them? └ Everyone involved is having a reunion in the holding cells.
Their lives are probably over. └ The commenter above doesn’t know Hell Joseon.
The ones who gave the orders will get suspended sentences at worst, LOL. └ Nope.
A national petition went up about it, and it passed three million signatures yesterday.
The Blue House is supposedly preparing legislation.
Looks like they’re going to overhaul the whole system this time. └ We’ll have to wait and see, but I really hope they do. └ They’ll probably clean house while they’re at it.
Blinded by their hunger for an exclusive, they messed with someone they never should have touched. └ Me.

Everyone my age.
Loves Jin Taekyung.
The response left me more bewildered than anything else.
I was happy, but it also felt like a burden.
I really only did what anyone should have done.
It had been an accident no one could have predicted.

The news kept calling me a hero who had prevented a major disaster, but every now and then, I found myself wondering whether there might have been one fewer casualty if I had been just a little faster.
“What’s with that expression?”
“Huh?
Nothing.”
“Someone with nothing wrong doesn’t pick at his food like that.”
“I’ve already eaten three bowls.”

“Hey, Taekyung.

“You’re not a god.

chapters.title: Chapter 211
paragraphs: I stared at the man who had suddenly stepped in front of the car.
He’s definitely a Hunter, but...
The reason I found myself thinking that despite sensing his extraordinary energy was his flashy appearance.
From his intricately patterned semi-formal suit to the designer labels covering him from head to toe, everything about him screamed luxury.
Then there was his smooth, taut, blemish-free skin and teeth so white they looked almost unnatural.
No matter how I looked at him, he seemed more like a celebrity than a Hunter.
Maybe that was why he looked strangely familiar.
He’s even more over the top than Team Leader Choi.
They both liked luxury brands, but the man in front of us took it a little too far.
The huge sunglasses he was wearing on such a gloomy day certainly didn’t help.
“Can’t you hear me? Is this thing under a noise spell or something?”
At the man’s mutter, Team Leader Choi lowered the window.
“What can I do for you?”
“Oh, you can hear me. Then why didn’t you answer?”
“We’re short on time. If you have nothing else to say, please step aside.”
“You must be pretty busy.”
“Yes. Very.”
The man studied Team Leader Choi’s calm response with an odd look, then turned to me.
“You’re Jin Taekyung, right? You’re even better-looking in person than you are on-screen. No wonder the women’s online communities went wild.”
“Whoa, really...? Wait, who are you?”
“As you’ve probably guessed, I’m not a reporter trying to get an interview. I run a Guild in Incheon.”
“Oh.”
I could more or less guess what he wanted without asking.
Another recruitment offer, probably.
I was used to it by now.
Ever since I became famous, Guild after Guild had approached me.
Taking down a group of ogres single-handedly had proven my ability, and all the media exposure had given me plenty of publicity.
To them, I was a highly desirable “product” in more ways than one.
“Here. My business card.”
By now, I had become a master at turning people down.
I accepted the card and put on the most natural smile I could manage.
“I’m sorry, but I’m not considering changing Guilds at the moment.”
“Really?”
“Yes. I’m quite satisfied with my current Guild. They were also the first to reach out to me.”
At my immediate answer, a faint smile flickered across Team Leader Choi’s lips in the rearview mirror.
The man looked back and forth between Team Leader Choi and me, then rubbed his chin.
“That’s a shame.”
“I’ll get in touch another time.”
“Still, there’s no harm in having a cup of coffee together, right? I’m a fan.”
“Pardon?”
“Thirty minutes. No, fifteen should be enough. I’m a busy man myself, so I can’t come by often.”
What the hell was this guy talking about?
Making a recruitment offer in front of Team Leader Choi was already incredibly rude, but now he was simply doing whatever he pleased.
He’s crossing the line.
That was the look I was giving the man as I wondered how to deal with him when—
“That’s strange. Did I misread the interview?”
“You said it in Weekly Hunters. You said I was your favorite Hunter.”
I blinked.
Only then did I realize who he was—and why he had seemed so familiar.
“C-Could you be...?”
The man grinned at my reaction.
“That hurts. I went to the trouble of giving you my business card, and you didn’t even look at it properly.”
I hurriedly lowered my gaze to the card.
The metal business card gleamed gold as though it had been plated, and clear letters were engraved across its surface.
Star Guild CEO Won Myunghoon
“W-Whoa!”
Seeing me splutter like Mute Samryong, the man—no, the A-rank Hunter Won Myunghoon—reached through the half-open window and offered me his hand.
“Nice to meet you, Taekyung.”
Won Myunghoon.
He was thirty-nine years old, and his birthday was April 1. He stood 185 centimeters tall, weighed eighty kilograms, and had a well-proportioned physique.

While preparing for the physical education college entrance exams, he awakened as an A-rank Hunter on his twentieth birthday. With his exceptional ability and good looks, he earned a reputation as a man who had it all.
“Do you think that’s all? He has an amazing personality, too. He donates often, and there are countless heartwarming stories about him. He even runs a scholarship foundation...”
Team Leader Choi, who had been listening to my endless stream of information, asked with an incredulous expression,
“How do you know all that? Why have you memorized his physical stats and even his birthday?”
“I told you. He’s my favorite Hunter.”
It was something I said at least once in every interview.
The people I respected most were my parents. My favorite Hunter was Won Myunghoon.
“...Even so. At this point, isn’t it practically love?”
“What a horrifying thing to say. He’s more like a role model. The Won Myunghoon Syndrome. Haven’t you heard of it?”
“I haven’t.”
“Oh, dear...”
“What’s with that pitying look?”
Because I feel sorry for you for not knowing how cool Won Myunghoon is.
Things were very different now, but up through my school days, Won Myunghoon’s influence had been tremendous.
Being an A-rank Hunter was impressive enough, but he also had incredible star power. Whenever you turned on the television, his face was there.
Back then, he had been the very definition of an all-around entertainer.
“Movies, dramas, commercials. He could sing, too, so he even released albums.”
“You mean he was a singer as well? A Hunter?”
“Team Leader, you’d recognize the songs if you heard them. Go, Coward, I Don’t Know Hunters, Escape... He had tons of hits. He even demolished Japan’s Unicorn chart.”
He had been the role model of countless aspiring Hunters and one of the few male singers welcomed at military morale-boosting performances.
I hummed a few lines as a demonstration, and Team Leader Choi showed a flicker of recognition.
“Oh, I think I’ve heard I Don’t Know Hunters before.”
“Right? It’s still on the popular karaoke charts. Anyway, that’s how famous Myunghoon hyung is. There’s even a saying that any Korean man who doesn’t know Won Myunghoon is either a spy or a monster.”
“Is living abroad for a long time really enough to get me called a monster?”
“Who called you a monster? You’re overreacting.”
“Hoo.”
Team Leader Choi shook his head, then suddenly looked puzzled.
“But even taking all that into account, the name Won Myunghoon feels strangely unfamiliar.”
“When did you return to Korea, Team Leader?”
“Three years ago.”
“Ah, then you might not know about that incident. It was pretty shocking, so everyone in the media keeps quiet about it.”
“An incident?”
“Yes. Though I suppose it has already been eight years. What happened was...”
Just then, Won Myunghoon, who had briefly stepped away to use the restroom, came walking toward us from a distance, waving.
“Team Leader, Myunghoon hyung is calling me. I’ll get going.”
“...Go ahead. I have about thirty minutes to spare anyway, so I’ll look at some clothes in the department store nearby.”
“Yes, yes.”
I answered vaguely and ran toward Won Myunghoon.
He let out a quiet laugh at the sight of me. His smile looked so youthful that it was hard to believe he would turn forty in just a few months.
“What about your Team Leader?”
“He went to take care of something. More importantly, hyung, you can speak casually with me.”
“Hyung? The age gap between us is too large for that.”
“Oh, come on. These days, twelve years practically makes us the same age.”
“Should I, then?”
“Yes.”
“Haha. I’m glad to have a good younger brother like you, Taekyung.”
I trembled with emotion.
Good heavens. Won Myunghoon and I were now hyung and dongsaeng.

If Jinho hyung, who had once even managed Won Myunghoon’s fan café, found out about this, he would cling to my trouser leg and refuse to let go. He would insist that the three of us swear a Peach Garden Oath together.
Not a chance.
A pleased smile spread across my face.

Drunk on happiness, I followed Won Myunghoon into a nearby café. A male part-time employee in his early twenties was reading a book behind the counter. He looked up with a mechanical customer-service smile.
“Welcome. May I take your or—”
A brief silence followed.
Then a breathy gasp escaped his lips.
Of course.
He was a hardcore Won Myunghoon fanboy, too. I nudged Won Myunghoon in the side with my elbow and whispered,
“As expected of you, Myunghoon hyung. You’re still incredibly popular.”
“Haha, this is embarrassing. It’s been a while since I gave anyone an autograph.”
Won Myunghoon laughed awkwardly.
Feeling proud for no reason, I puffed out my chest.
That was when—
“Jin Taekyung? You’re Jin Taekyung, right?”
“From the Outer Ring Road a little while ago! The B-rank Gate!”
“I-I am, yes.”
“Wow. That’s fucking awesome.”
Muttering in amazement, the employee hurriedly pulled out a piece of paper and a pen and held them toward me.
“Could you give me your autograph?”
What on earth was going on?
Not Myunghoon hyung... me?
I turned around in bewilderment and found myself looking at Won Myunghoon’s face.
His gaze was cold, his expression stiff.
It was a side of him I had never seen anywhere before. But the next moment, it vanished like a mirage beneath his warm voice.
“What are you waiting for? You should give him your autograph.”
“Pardon? Oh, yes.”
The café lights must have been too bright. I must have seen wrong.
With a strange sense of déjà vu, I took the pen.
“What should I write?”
The employee answered eagerly.
“Please write, ‘Hye-gyeong, I hope you and Jinwoo have a beautiful relationship.’”
Oh, for fuck’s sake.
The initial awkwardness soon faded, and the moment I sat down, I spent more than twenty minutes enthusiastically showing off my fanboy devotion.
“As you know, hyung, there aren’t that many A-rank Hunters who use spears.”
“Hmm. That’s true. Quite a few people started with spears, then switched to swords later.”
Although spears looked easy to use, they were actually very tricky weapons.
Their reach gave you an advantage, but the problem was that you couldn’t always maintain that advantage.
Spears worked well enough in low- and mid-level Gates, but high-level Gates were full of dangers no one could anticipate.
There had even been a time when I considered using a one-handed sword and shield.
“But you stuck with the spear all the way. You even wrote your own manual.”
“That was a long time ago. It must have been... ten years by now.”
“Yes. Exactly ten years ago. I was in my first year of high school, and you were already a ranker.”
Just as there were differences in skill among Peak masters, there were differences among A-rank Hunters.
Of the roughly one hundred thousand Hunters in Korea, the hundred strongest were known as rankers.
“I referred to that manual a lot later, when I was at the training center.”
“Really? I don’t know if it was actually helpful.”
“Of course it was. It helped me a ton.”
“If that’s true, then I’m glad.”
Of course, the manual had only worked up through low-level Gates.
That went without saying in the Murim, where martial arts had developed to a level the modern world couldn’t begin to compare with.
But it helped me a lot back then.
The easiest way to explain it was that the manual had been written at the level of a novice.
You couldn’t teach an ant how a tiger moved.
After I finished praising him from every possible angle, Won Myunghoon tilted his lukewarm coffee cup.
“That’s all in the past.”
“You’re still in your prime and actively working.”
“No. It’s been a long time since I lost my ranker status, and people have mostly forgotten about me.”
Was this because of that incident?

It was unfortunate, but I couldn’t deny it completely. Over the past eight years, countless star Hunters had emerged who could match or surpass Won Myunghoon, and the public had cheered for brighter lights.
“It wasn’t until last year that I finally thought about starting again. As it happened, I also took over a Guild from an acquaintance who was about to retire.”
“The Star Guild?”
I had discreetly searched for it earlier.
Star Guild was the name Won Myunghoon had given it after taking over. Before that, it had been a sizable, established Guild that ranked among the top three in Incheon.
“Yeah. A few lines appeared in the news, but that was the end of it. Did you know about it?”
“Last year... I’m sorry. I was a little busy back then.”
It wasn’t just then. For the past several years, I had repeated the same routine day after day.
Raids, goshiwon, raids.
At the end of the day, I went home to sleep and eat, then headed back out to fight monsters.
Even if I had heard the news, I would have forgotten it soon enough. To me, Won Myunghoon was already a fond memory, not someone who belonged to the present.
“There’s no reason to apologize.”
Won Myunghoon smiled bitterly and continued.
“It’s not like I’m the only flash in the pan. I suppose that was simply the limit of what I could achieve.”
A flash in the pan.
It might have been true because his active career had been so short, but in another sense, it was wrong.
A star?
Even if he had appeared in a few movies, dramas, and commercials and released some albums, Won Myunghoon was first and foremost a Hunter.
He had beaten the incredibly low odds of awakening, and thanks to that, he had seized tremendous wealth and fame.
Even though he had gone through an unfortunate incident...
Maybe this is him returning to his original self.

It wasn’t that my thought was wrong. It was simply different. I had no desire to bring it up and make the atmosphere uncomfortable.
“I see.”
“Then I heard about you. You were incredible. It felt like I was looking at my old self.”
“M-Me?”

“Yeah. I searched for and read your interviews. I was happy and grateful to hear that you were such an enthusiastic fan of mine. Thanks to you, I even received offers to appear on television from several places.”
“Oh.”
Had my interview actually helped Won Myunghoon?
I was scratching my chin with an awkward smile when—
A hand clamped around mine.
“Taekyung. Can I make you an offer?”
“...Hyung?”
Won Myunghoon gripped my hand tightly and spoke with a serious expression.
“Transfer to our Guild. I’ll take responsibility for you, Taekyung. I’ll turn you into a star Hunter.”

sentences.text: I stared at the man who had suddenly stepped in front of the car.
He’s definitely a Hunter, but...
The reason I found myself thinking that despite sensing his extraordinary energy was his flashy appearance.
From his intricately patterned semi-formal suit to the designer labels covering him from head to toe, everything about him screamed luxury.
Then there was his smooth, taut, blemish-free skin and teeth so white they looked almost unnatural.
No matter how I looked at him, he seemed more like a celebrity than a Hunter.
Maybe that was why he looked strangely familiar.
He’s even more over the top than Team Leader Choi.
They both liked luxury brands, but the man in front of us took it a little too far.
The huge sunglasses he was wearing on such a gloomy day certainly didn’t help.
“Can’t you hear me?
Is this thing under a noise spell or something?”
At the man’s mutter, Team Leader Choi lowered the window.
“What can I do for you?”
“Oh, you can hear me.
Then why didn’t you answer?”
“We’re short on time.
If you have nothing else to say, please step aside.”
“You must be pretty busy.”
“Yes.
Very.”
The man studied Team Leader Choi’s calm response with an odd look, then turned to me.
“You’re Jin Taekyung, right?
You’re even better-looking in person than you are on-screen.
No wonder the women’s online communities went wild.”
“Whoa, really...?
Wait, who are you?”
“As you’ve probably guessed, I’m not a reporter trying to get an interview.
I run a Guild in Incheon.”
“Oh.”
I could more or less guess what he wanted without asking.
Another recruitment offer, probably.
I was used to it by now.
Ever since I became famous, Guild after Guild had approached me.
Taking down a group of ogres single-handedly had proven my ability, and all the media exposure had given me plenty of publicity.
To them, I was a highly desirable “product” in more ways than one.
“Here.
My business card.”
By now, I had become a master at turning people down.
I accepted the card and put on the most natural smile I could manage.
“I’m sorry, but I’m not considering changing Guilds at the moment.”
“Really?”
“Yes.
I’m quite satisfied with my current Guild.
They were also the first to reach out to me.”
At my immediate answer, a faint smile flickered across Team Leader Choi’s lips in the rearview mirror.
The man looked back and forth between Team Leader Choi and me, then rubbed his chin.
“That’s a shame.”
“I’ll get in touch another time.”
“Still, there’s no harm in having a cup of coffee together, right?
I’m a fan.”
“Pardon?”
“Thirty minutes.
No, fifteen should be enough.
I’m a busy man myself, so I can’t come by often.”
What the hell was this guy talking about?
Making a recruitment offer in front of Team Leader Choi was already incredibly rude, but now he was simply doing whatever he pleased.
He’s crossing the line.
That was the look I was giving the man as I wondered how to deal with him when—
“That’s strange.
Did I misread the interview?”
“You said it in Weekly Hunters.
You said I was your favorite Hunter.”
I blinked.
Only then did I realize who he was—and why he had seemed so familiar.
“C-Could you be...?”
The man grinned at my reaction.
“That hurts.
I went to the trouble of giving you my business card, and you didn’t even look at it properly.”
I hurriedly lowered my gaze to the card.
The metal business card gleamed gold as though it had been plated, and clear letters were engraved across its surface.
Star Guild CEO Won Myunghoon
“W-Whoa!”
Seeing me splutter like Mute Samryong, the man—no, the A-rank Hunter Won Myunghoon—reached through the half-open window and offered me his hand.
“Nice to meet you, Taekyung.”
Won Myunghoon.
He was thirty-nine years old, and his birthday was April 1.
He stood 185 centimeters tall, weighed eighty kilograms, and had a well-proportioned physique.
While preparing for the physical education college entrance exams, he awakened as an A-rank Hunter on his twentieth birthday.
With his exceptional ability and good looks, he earned a reputation as a man who had it all.
“Do you think that’s all?
He has an amazing personality, too.
He donates often, and there are countless heartwarming stories about him.
He even runs a scholarship foundation...”
Team Leader Choi, who had been listening to my endless stream of information, asked with an incredulous expression,
“How do you know all that?
Why have you memorized his physical stats and even his birthday?”
“I told you.
He’s my favorite Hunter.”
It was something I said at least once in every interview.
The people I respected most were my parents.
My favorite Hunter was Won Myunghoon.
“...Even so.
At this point, isn’t it practically love?”
“What a horrifying thing to say.
He’s more like a role model.
The Won Myunghoon Syndrome.
Haven’t you heard of it?”
“I haven’t.”
“Oh, dear...”
“What’s with that pitying look?”
Because I feel sorry for you for not knowing how cool Won Myunghoon is.
Things were very different now, but up through my school days, Won Myunghoon’s influence had been tremendous.
Being an A-rank Hunter was impressive enough, but he also had incredible star power.
Whenever you turned on the television, his face was there.
Back then, he had been the very definition of an all-around entertainer.
“Movies, dramas, commercials.
He could sing, too, so he even released albums.”
“You mean he was a singer as well?
A Hunter?”
“Team Leader, you’d recognize the songs if you heard them.
Go, Coward, I Don’t Know Hunters, Escape...
He had tons of hits.
He even demolished Japan’s Unicorn chart.”
He had been the role model of countless aspiring Hunters and one of the few male singers welcomed at military morale-boosting performances.
I hummed a few lines as a demonstration, and Team Leader Choi showed a flicker of recognition.
“Oh, I think I’ve heard I Don’t Know Hunters before.”
“Right?
It’s still on the popular karaoke charts.
Anyway, that’s how famous Myunghoon hyung is.
There’s even a saying that any Korean man who doesn’t know Won Myunghoon is either a spy or a monster.”
“Is living abroad for a long time really enough to get me called a monster?”
“Who called you a monster?
You’re overreacting.”
“Hoo.”
Team Leader Choi shook his head, then suddenly looked puzzled.
“But even taking all that into account, the name Won Myunghoon feels strangely unfamiliar.”
“When did you return to Korea, Team Leader?”
“Three years ago.”
“Ah, then you might not know about that incident.
It was pretty shocking, so everyone in the media keeps quiet about it.”
“An incident?”
“Yes.
Though I suppose it has already been eight years.
What happened was...”
Just then, Won Myunghoon, who had briefly stepped away to use the restroom, came walking toward us from a distance, waving.
“Team Leader, Myunghoon hyung is calling me.
I’ll get going.”
“...Go ahead.
I have about thirty minutes to spare anyway, so I’ll look at some clothes in the department store nearby.”
“Yes, yes.”
I answered vaguely and ran toward Won Myunghoon.
He let out a quiet laugh at the sight of me.
His smile looked so youthful that it was hard to believe he would turn forty in just a few months.
“What about your Team Leader?”
“He went to take care of something.
More importantly, hyung, you can speak casually with me.”
“Hyung?
The age gap between us is too large for that.”
“Oh, come on.
These days, twelve years practically makes us the same age.”
“Should I, then?”
“Yes.”
“Haha.
I’m glad to have a good younger brother like you, Taekyung.”
I trembled with emotion.
Good heavens.
Won Myunghoon and I were now hyung and dongsaeng.
If Jinho hyung, who had once even managed Won Myunghoon’s fan café, found out about this, he would cling to my trouser leg and refuse to let go.
He would insist that the three of us swear a Peach Garden Oath together.
Not a chance.
A pleased smile spread across my face.
Drunk on happiness, I followed Won Myunghoon into a nearby café.
A male part-time employee in his early twenties was reading a book behind the counter.
He looked up with a mechanical customer-service smile.
“Welcome.
May I take your or—”
A brief silence followed.
Then a breathy gasp escaped his lips.
Of course.
He was a hardcore Won Myunghoon fanboy, too.
I nudged Won Myunghoon in the side with my elbow and whispered,
“As expected of you, Myunghoon hyung.
You’re still incredibly popular.”
“Haha, this is embarrassing.
It’s been a while since I gave anyone an autograph.”
Won Myunghoon laughed awkwardly.
Feeling proud for no reason, I puffed out my chest.
That was when—
“Jin Taekyung?
You’re Jin Taekyung, right?”
“From the Outer Ring Road a little while ago!
The B-rank Gate!”
“I-I am, yes.”
“Wow.
That’s fucking awesome.”
Muttering in amazement, the employee hurriedly pulled out a piece of paper and a pen and held them toward me.
“Could you give me your autograph?”
What on earth was going on?
Not Myunghoon hyung... me?
I turned around in bewilderment and found myself looking at Won Myunghoon’s face.
His gaze was cold, his expression stiff.
It was a side of him I had never seen anywhere before.
But the next moment, it vanished like a mirage beneath his warm voice.
“What are you waiting for?
You should give him your autograph.”
“Pardon?
Oh, yes.”
The café lights must have been too bright.
I must have seen wrong.
With a strange sense of déjà vu, I took the pen.
“What should I write?”
The employee answered eagerly.
“Please write, ‘Hye-gyeong, I hope you and Jinwoo have a beautiful relationship.’”

chapters.title: Chapter 212
paragraphs: “Transfer to our Guild. I’ll take responsibility for you, Taekyung. I’ll turn you into a star Hunter.”
I blinked.
“A star... Hunter?”
“Yeah. A star Hunter.”
Won Myunghoon continued with absolute confidence.
“Times have changed. People go crazy for Hunters. They envy us for the abilities they don’t have. You know that too, don’t you, Taekyung?”
“That’s true.”
“Do you know what the kids around me wanted to be when I was in elementary school? President. Astronaut. But these days? Children and adults alike all want to be Hunters.”
Wealth and fame.
Those were the two words most people associated with being a Hunter.
Even now, decades after the Great Cataclysm ended, they don’t want to think about the fact that hundreds of Hunters still die in Gates every year.
“You have everything the public wants. Good looks, buzz, and a fresh character unlike anything they’ve seen before.”
Won Myunghoon’s face flushed with excitement. His heated voice continued.
“But how long will that last? The public gets excited quickly and loses interest even faster.”
“Hyung.”

“If you let this opportunity pass, you won’t even become a flash-in-the-pan star, Taekyung. Fortunately, it isn’t too late yet. If you start getting professional management now, appear on television, and work on your image...”
“Wait, wait. Hyung.”
“Huh? Oh. Right.”
Won Myunghoon fell silent, and I scratched my chin.
I hadn’t expected the conversation to go in this direction, but I might as well make things clear while I had the chance.
“You said you weren’t going to try to recruit me. You told Team Leader Choi that, too.”
“I did. But Taekyung, this is a really good opportunity.”
“Uh, I’m sorry, but I have no intention of changing Guilds.”
Won Myunghoon opened and closed his mouth as if he was about to say something, then nodded.
“Right. That’s understandable at your age. Then let’s forget about changing Guilds. How about signing with an entertainment agency instead? It’s pretty common these days.”
“An entertainment agency?”
“Yeah. I happen to own a major stake in one.”
Holding contracts with two Guilds was illegal, but there was nothing wrong with engaging in other kinds of work.
Just as he’d said, it was no longer unusual for high-ranking Hunters to sign with entertainment or management agencies.
But I answered without hesitation.
“No, I don’t need an agency either.”
“What?”
“I’m satisfied with what I have now.”
“...You’re satisfied?”
“Yes.”
Won Myunghoon frowned.
“Taekyung. You don’t seem to understand what I’m saying.”
“You’re saying I won’t become a star if I let this opportunity pass, right? That’s fine. I didn’t do any of this because I wanted to be one.”

“I know. I know, but think it over one more time. Just one regular television show and a few major commercials could bring in billions of won—even tens of billions of won. Can’t you tell just by looking at me?”
Won Myunghoon spread both arms wide. From head to toe, he was dressed in luxury brands whose names and prices I couldn’t even begin to guess.
I suddenly remembered an Internet article I had seen in the past.
A-Rank Hunter Won Myunghoon Purchases Building Worth Tens of Billions of Won in Cheongdam-dong
The man from that article—the man I had admired and envied endlessly—was standing right in front of me.
“I saw your interview. You’ve been pretty busy. Isn’t it time you enjoyed life a little? I heard your dream was to own a building.”
“That’s true.”
It had changed a little, but it was still one of the goals I wanted to achieve.
When I nodded readily, Won Myunghoon flashed me a grin.

“Then signing with an entertainment agency would be much faster than focusing on Guild work. You wouldn’t have to fight monsters in dangerous Gates, either. All you’d have to do is spend a few hours working in a nice, cool studio. Though full makeup can feel a little stifling. Ha-ha.”
“Oh, really?”
“Of course. You just need to get used to smiling brightly and delivering your lines in front of a camera.”
“Then I’d probably prefer Gates. I’m more the physical type, and I don’t like feeling stifled.”
“...What?”
“I also swear a lot in everyday life. It wouldn’t pass broadcast standards. Even if I attracted attention for no reason, my family would just suffer like they are now.”
“T-Taekyung.”
I continued speaking as I watched his obvious bewilderment.
“And as for owning a building, I can become a building owner without doing television or commercials. It’ll take some time, but still.”
“What are you talking about? A-rank Hunters make a lot of money, sure, but do you have any idea how expensive land in Gangnam is?”
“Gangnam?”
“Yeah. Do you even know the current price per pyeong there—?”
I blinked blankly, then let out a quiet laugh.
“Why Gangnam? I can just buy a building near my house.”
“Huh?”
“A three-story neighborhood commercial building would still make me a building owner. I’ve never even considered Gangnam.”
“...A neighborhood commercial building?”
“Yes. It’d be close, so it would be easy to visit, and the rent would come in like clockwork. If Mom says she’s bored after quitting her job, I could set her up with a little snack bar or something.”
“A snack bar?”
The more I said, the more Won Myunghoon’s expression twisted. Had I said something wrong?
“Hyung?”
“Myunghoon hyung. Are you all right?”
Won Myunghoon’s lips moved soundlessly before he let out a trembling breath.
“Taekyung.”
“Yes, hyung.”
“Can you—can you really be satisfied with that?”
“You saw my interview. Until a few months ago, I was an F-rank Hunter. Now I make dozens of times more without having to work myself to death like I did back then. What’s the problem?”
I had no debt, and I had gotten my house back.
Public attention? Fame? I’d already had more than enough of both in the Murim and the modern world.
More than anything, I’d learned just how exhausting and unpleasant the spotlight could be in real life.
I’d also realized what kind of life would make my family and me happier.
“So this is enough for me. Team Leader Choi already showed me a huge pile of commercial offers. There were too many, so I’m planning to pick a few, film them, and then focus on the Guild again.”
I could make plenty of money without entering the entertainment industry.
Won Myunghoon remained silent for a long time after I finished speaking. Finally, his lips parted.
“I see. I understand.”
“You’re not offended because I turned you down, are you?”
“...Of course not.”
Just then, the phone on the table vibrated. I didn’t even need to check who was calling. It was Team Leader Choi.
I looked at the time and realized that we had gone well past the thirty minutes we’d agreed on.
“Hyung, I think I should get going.”
“Already? You must be busy.”
“The Association contacted me and asked me to get my rank reassessed today. I got your number today, so I’ll contact you again soon.”
“Then I’ll see you next time. It was nice meeting you.”
“Let’s go to a coin karaoke room next time. I’ll practice your song before then.”
“A coin karaoke room? Sounds good.”
Just thinking about hearing him perform the original version of Coward, my signature song, live already made my heart race. Maybe I should ask Jinho hyung to come along, too.
“Then I’ll be going. Don’t forget your promise.”
Won Myunghoon nodded with a faint smile as I left the café.
The black sedan parked by the roadside honked.
“Sir, may I clear your cup?”
Won Myunghoon didn’t answer the part-time worker’s question. He stared silently at the empty coffee cup before abruptly speaking.
“Do you perhaps not know who I am?”
“Pardon?”
“Won Myunghoon. Haven’t you heard of me?”
“Of course I have. You released a few famous songs, didn’t you?”
The part-time worker gave an awkward smile and continued.
“Actually, I just looked you up. You’re much more famous than I thought. I only saw you on television a few times when I was young, so I didn’t remember you very well...”
“You looked me up.”
His voice was as dry as sand.
The smile slowly vanished from the part-time worker’s face.

After nervously watching him for a moment, the worker quietly returned to the counter. Some time later, a familiar melody began playing throughout the café, and the corner of Won Myunghoon’s mouth twisted.
It was his own song, released ten years ago.
All of it had become a relic of the past.
“Who does that bastard think he’s mocking...?”
His low voice was buried beneath the music. Won Myunghoon rose from his seat.
His thoughts were consumed by a single person.
Jin Taekyung—a dayfly Hunter who, until only a few months ago, had scraped by going from one F-rank Gate to another.
But now he was someone who received the public’s attention and affection.
“A coin karaoke room, my ass... Some lucky bastard gets one flash of fame and forgets his place.”
Muttering under his breath, Won Myunghoon put on his sunglasses.
His expensive, flashy outfit drew the eyes of people passing on the street, but not one of them recognized him.
“Congratulations, Mr. Jin Taekyung.”
The Bucheon Hunter Association president, a middle-aged man with hair more than half gray, handed me a card with a genial smile.
About half the size of my palm, the card gleamed silver from edge to edge.
Platinum.
The card was made of actual platinum, and everyone dreamed of possessing one, even if only in their sleep.
It means I’ve gained that much wealth and fame.
But perhaps because I’d fully expected this, I felt surprisingly calm as I accepted the card from the Association president amid the barrage of flashes from countless cameras.
I’m a Peak master. Becoming an A-rank Hunter is no big deal.
Still, I felt pretty good.
I grinned and waved at the cameras, and the Association president asked in a robotic tone,
“So, Mr. Jin Taekyung. How do you feel right now?”
Obviously, I feel fantastic.
I was just about to answer when—
Ding.
System You have earned the A-Rank Hunter achievement. - Achievement Reward granted. - Level Up! - You have gained 20 Bonus Points! - Fame increases greatly!
“Oh, fuck.”
Right. There are cameras here.

The Association president froze, his face stricken. The broadcasting staff looked as though they couldn’t believe their ears. Team Leader Choi lowered his head with the hollow expression of a man overcome by post-nut clarity.
I’m fucked.
This had to be one of the worst broadcast disasters in history.
Feeling my throat grow painfully dry, I whispered to the Association president,
“They’ll edit that out, right? You have to make sure they do.”
“Edit it out? Mr. Jin Taekyung, are you out of your mind?”
The Association president’s voice sank ominously low. He looked ready to grab me by the collar on the spot.
“Edit my ass. This is live. What do you call it? An iTube live stream.”
“What?”
“Can’t you see the monitors in front of us? More than fifty thousand people are watching right now.”
Shit. He’s right.
There had been so many people and machines around that I hadn’t noticed, but now I saw five or six monitors set up below the podium, each displaying the Association president and me.
The chat beside the video looked ready to explode from the sheer volume of messages.
“Uh, what do we do?”
“What do you mean, what do we do? Apologize immediately!”
The Association president snapped at me, his face bright red. Just then, the camera director at the very front mouthed something.
“The reaction is good?”
“Huh?”
“What?”
What is that supposed to mean?

sentences.text: “Transfer to our Guild.
I’ll take responsibility for you, Taekyung.
I’ll turn you into a star Hunter.”
I blinked.
“A star...
Hunter?”
“Yeah.
A star Hunter.”
Won Myunghoon continued with absolute confidence.
“Times have changed.
People go crazy for Hunters.
They envy us for the abilities they don’t have.
You know that too, don’t you, Taekyung?”
“That’s true.”
“Do you know what the kids around me wanted to be when I was in elementary school?
President.
Astronaut.
But these days?
Children and adults alike all want to be Hunters.”
Wealth and fame.
Those were the two words most people associated with being a Hunter.
Even now, decades after the Great Cataclysm ended, they don’t want to think about the fact that hundreds of Hunters still die in Gates every year.
“You have everything the public wants.
Good looks, buzz, and a fresh character unlike anything they’ve seen before.”
Won Myunghoon’s face flushed with excitement.
His heated voice continued.
“But how long will that last?
The public gets excited quickly and loses interest even faster.”
“Hyung.”
“If you let this opportunity pass, you won’t even become a flash-in-the-pan star, Taekyung.
Fortunately, it isn’t too late yet.
If you start getting professional management now, appear on television, and work on your image...”
“Wait, wait.
Hyung.”
“Huh?
Oh.
Right.”
Won Myunghoon fell silent, and I scratched my chin.
I hadn’t expected the conversation to go in this direction, but I might as well make things clear while I had the chance.
“You said you weren’t going to try to recruit me.
You told Team Leader Choi that, too.”
“I did.
But Taekyung, this is a really good opportunity.”
“Uh, I’m sorry, but I have no intention of changing Guilds.”
Won Myunghoon opened and closed his mouth as if he was about to say something, then nodded.
“Right.
That’s understandable at your age.
Then let’s forget about changing Guilds.
How about signing with an entertainment agency instead?
It’s pretty common these days.”
“An entertainment agency?”
“Yeah.
I happen to own a major stake in one.”
Holding contracts with two Guilds was illegal, but there was nothing wrong with engaging in other kinds of work.
Just as he’d said, it was no longer unusual for high-ranking Hunters to sign with entertainment or management agencies.
But I answered without hesitation.
“No, I don’t need an agency either.”
“What?”
“I’m satisfied with what I have now.”
“...You’re satisfied?”
“Yes.”
Won Myunghoon frowned.
“Taekyung.
You don’t seem to understand what I’m saying.”
“You’re saying I won’t become a star if I let this opportunity pass, right?
That’s fine.
I didn’t do any of this because I wanted to be one.”
“I know.
I know, but think it over one more time.
Just one regular television show and a few major commercials could bring in billions of won—even tens of billions of won.
Can’t you tell just by looking at me?”
Won Myunghoon spread both arms wide.
From head to toe, he was dressed in luxury brands whose names and prices I couldn’t even begin to guess.
I suddenly remembered an Internet article I had seen in the past.
A-Rank Hunter Won Myunghoon Purchases Building Worth Tens of Billions of Won in Cheongdam-dong
The man from that article—the man I had admired and envied endlessly—was standing right in front of me.
“I saw your interview.
You’ve been pretty busy.
Isn’t it time you enjoyed life a little?
I heard your dream was to own a building.”
“That’s true.”
It had changed a little, but it was still one of the goals I wanted to achieve.
When I nodded readily, Won Myunghoon flashed me a grin.
“Then signing with an entertainment agency would be much faster than focusing on Guild work.
You wouldn’t have to fight monsters in dangerous Gates, either.
All you’d have to do is spend a few hours working in a nice, cool studio.
Though full makeup can feel a little stifling.
Ha-ha.”
“Oh, really?”
“Of course.
You just need to get used to smiling brightly and delivering your lines in front of a camera.”
“Then I’d probably prefer Gates.
I’m more the physical type, and I don’t like feeling stifled.”
“...What?”
“I also swear a lot in everyday life.
It wouldn’t pass broadcast standards.
Even if I attracted attention for no reason, my family would just suffer like they are now.”
“T-Taekyung.”
I continued speaking as I watched his obvious bewilderment.
“And as for owning a building, I can become a building owner without doing television or commercials.
It’ll take some time, but still.”
“What are you talking about?
A-rank Hunters make a lot of money, sure, but do you have any idea how expensive land in Gangnam is?”
“Gangnam?”
“Yeah.
Do you even know the current price per pyeong there—?”
I blinked blankly, then let out a quiet laugh.
“Why Gangnam?
I can just buy a building near my house.”
“Huh?”
“A three-story neighborhood commercial building would still make me a building owner.
I’ve never even considered Gangnam.”
“...A neighborhood commercial building?”
“Yes.
It’d be close, so it would be easy to visit, and the rent would come in like clockwork.
If Mom says she’s bored after quitting her job, I could set her up with a little snack bar or something.”
“A snack bar?”
The more I said, the more Won Myunghoon’s expression twisted.
Had I said something wrong?
“Hyung?”
“Myunghoon hyung.
Are you all right?”
Won Myunghoon’s lips moved soundlessly before he let out a trembling breath.
“Taekyung.”
“Yes, hyung.”
“Can you—can you really be satisfied with that?”
“You saw my interview.
Until a few months ago, I was an F-rank Hunter.
Now I make dozens of times more without having to work myself to death like I did back then.
What’s the problem?”
I had no debt, and I had gotten my house back.
Public attention?
Fame?
I’d already had more than enough of both in the Murim and the modern world.
More than anything, I’d learned just how exhausting and unpleasant the spotlight could be in real life.
I’d also realized what kind of life would make my family and me happier.
“So this is enough for me.
Team Leader Choi already showed me a huge pile of commercial offers.
There were too many, so I’m planning to pick a few, film them, and then focus on the Guild again.”
I could make plenty of money without entering the entertainment industry.
Won Myunghoon remained silent for a long time after I finished speaking.
Finally, his lips parted.
“I see.
I understand.”
“You’re not offended because I turned you down, are you?”
“...Of course not.”
Just then, the phone on the table vibrated.
I didn’t even need to check who was calling.
It was Team Leader Choi.
I looked at the time and realized that we had gone well past the thirty minutes we’d agreed on.
“Hyung, I think I should get going.”
“Already?
You must be busy.”
“The Association contacted me and asked me to get my rank reassessed today.
I got your number today, so I’ll contact you again soon.”
“Then I’ll see you next time.
It was nice meeting you.”
“Let’s go to a coin karaoke room next time.
I’ll practice your song before then.”
“A coin karaoke room?
Sounds good.”
Just thinking about hearing him perform the original version of Coward, my signature song, live already made my heart race.
Maybe I should ask Jinho hyung to come along, too.
“Then I’ll be going.
Don’t forget your promise.”
Won Myunghoon nodded with a faint smile as I left the café.
The black sedan parked by the roadside honked.
“Sir, may I clear your cup?”
Won Myunghoon didn’t answer the part-time worker’s question.
He stared silently at the empty coffee cup before abruptly speaking.
“Do you perhaps not know who I am?”
“Pardon?”
“Won Myunghoon.
Haven’t you heard of me?”
“Of course I have.
You released a few famous songs, didn’t you?”
The part-time worker gave an awkward smile and continued.
“Actually, I just looked you up.
You’re much more famous than I thought.
I only saw you on television a few times when I was young, so I didn’t remember you very well...”
“You looked me up.”
His voice was as dry as sand.
The smile slowly vanished from the part-time worker’s face.
After nervously watching him for a moment, the worker quietly returned to the counter.
Some time later, a familiar melody began playing throughout the café, and the corner of Won Myunghoon’s mouth twisted.
It was his own song, released ten years ago.
All of it had become a relic of the past.
“Who does that bastard think he’s mocking...?”
His low voice was buried beneath the music.
Won Myunghoon rose from his seat.
His thoughts were consumed by a single person.
Jin Taekyung—a dayfly Hunter who, until only a few months ago, had scraped by going from one F-rank Gate to another.
But now he was someone who received the public’s attention and affection.
“A coin karaoke room, my ass...
Some lucky bastard gets one flash of fame and forgets his place.”
Muttering under his breath, Won Myunghoon put on his sunglasses.
His expensive, flashy outfit drew the eyes of people passing on the street, but not one of them recognized him.
“Congratulations, Mr.
Jin Taekyung.”
The Bucheon Hunter Association president, a middle-aged man with hair more than half gray, handed me a card with a genial smile.
About half the size of my palm, the card gleamed silver from edge to edge.
Platinum.
The card was made of actual platinum, and everyone dreamed of possessing one, even if only in their sleep.
It means I’ve gained that much wealth and fame.
But perhaps because I’d fully expected this, I felt surprisingly calm as I accepted the card from the Association president amid the barrage of flashes from countless cameras.
I’m a Peak master.
Becoming an A-rank Hunter is no big deal.
Still, I felt pretty good.
I grinned and waved at the cameras, and the Association president asked in a robotic tone,

Jin Taekyung.
How do you feel right now?”
Obviously, I feel fantastic.
I was just about to answer when—
Ding.
