chapters.title: Chapter 213
paragraphs: “Netizens have some serious firepower. Everyone’s going crazy over the press conference.”
Team Leader Choi’s relaxed voice came from behind me.
Ssshhhwing!
At the same time, razor-sharp claws slashed through the air. I simply leaned my head back to dodge them and muttered,
“Tell me about it. I thought I’d caused a broadcast disaster, but somehow it all worked out.”
“On top of that, everyone’s praising you for going straight to a Gate as soon as the press conference ended.”
“Isn’t it normal for a Hunter to go on a raid?”
“That’s why image is so important. You know the saying, don’t you? Take a shit, and you’ll become famous.”
“...I don’t think that’s quite it.”
Shhhk! Crack!
I knocked aside and shattered every claw aimed at my head, shoulders, and chest.
The creature staggered back with a pained howl. Just as I was about to close in, Team Leader Choi asked,
“Would you like to take one next time?”
“Take what?”
“A shit.”
“I’ll pass.”
I answered firmly and swung my spear shaft.
Wham!
Something crunched, and the creature charging in from the side slammed straight into the ground.
It stood two meters tall—a massive, gray-furred, bipedal wolf with nothing left above its shoulders. I had blown its head off through sheer strength alone.
A System notification rang out at the same time.
Ding.
System You have defeated Lv. 73 Lycanthrope! - You have gained EXP!
The lycanthropes that had watched their fellow die let out a chorus of growls and howls.
- Grrrrr.
- Awooooo.
Their long, vertically slit yellow pupils trembled.
Seeing them hesitate, Team Leader Choi remarked as though he had just realized something.
“This is the first time I’ve seen lycanthropes look so docile.”
“They’re good at controlling their anger. Maybe being half-human means they picked up that trait too.”
Hotheads who claimed to have anger-management issues always followed the same pattern.
They acted like Lü Bu around anyone weaker than them, but the moment they found themselves in front of some muscular tough guys, they became the politest people in the world.
And once they lose the momentum, it’s over.
Slash!
I flicked the sticky blood off my spearhead and beckoned to the creatures with one finger.
“Come on, you sons of bitches.”
- Whiiine.
Their ears had folded halfway back, and their tails were tucked between their legs.
The moment a wolf became a dog, the fight was as good as over.
“You little bastards are cute.”
As I walked toward them with a grin, Team Leader Choi said,
“If possible, please handle them cleanly.”
“Why?”
“So we can take some proof shots. We’re going to post them on the Peace Guild’s official social-media account.”
“Too much pixelation would be a shame. People prefer things uncensored.”
Ah. He had a point.
- Awooooooooo!
As expected, the boss was different from the rest.
Its roar was packed with ferocity and killing intent. Its body was far larger than those of the other lycanthropes, and silver fur covered it from head to toe.
Every inch of it radiated the presence of a boss monster.
“Wow. You’re impressive.”
As I admired it, I made a decision.
I would give this one special treatment.
“One Annihilation.”
Krrrunch. Thud.
The monster’s massive body, a gaping hole torn through its chest, toppled like a rotting old tree.
Ding.

System You have defeated Lv. 83 Silver-Mane Lycanthrope! - You have perfectly cleared the B-Rank Gate, The Lycanthrope’s Black Forest! - You have gained a substantial amount of EXP! - The exit has opened because you defeated the boss monster.
Kiiiiing.
Once the conditions were met, a Gate exit appeared in the center of the clearing. But I still had something left to do.
“All right. Time for the fun part—cleanup.”
The sight of the corpses scattered everywhere filled me with satisfaction.
I was heading toward them with the heart of a farmer bringing in the harvest when Team Leader Choi spoke.
“About Won Myunghoon.”
“Yes?”
I turned at the sudden sound of his voice behind me.
He sat on a flat rock, his entire body protected by a shield spell, staring at a custom-built phone.
There was something odd about his expression.
“Myunghoon hyung?”
“Yes. What happened to Mr. Won Myunghoon eight years ago?”
I had no idea why he was suddenly curious.
I had been a student back then, but I was such a huge fan that I knew the whole story by heart. Explaining all of it would take forever, though.
“Look it up. Everything comes up if you search Sonamu Wiki.”
“People say you should stay off Sonamu Wiki.”
“...They have a point.”
“Just give me a brief explanation. Of all the people around me, you seem to know the most about Mr. Won Myunghoon.”
“Well, if you put it that way...”
I began talking as I skinned a lycanthrope with my dagger.
“Eight years ago, Myunghoon hyung’s career was on the decline. Every movie, drama, and album he released bombed, and then allegations of tax evasion were piled on top of that.”
“That isn’t particularly unusual.”
“No. That industry is always full of scandals.”
“I skimmed through the articles. It seems he was cleared of the tax-evasion allegations.”
“Yes. That ended without any real trouble.”
But that wasn’t the end of it.
Once mud had been splashed onto his clean image, all kinds of speculative articles and rumor sheets about Won Myunghoon began circulating online.
In the end, Won Myunghoon—already past his prime and going through a difficult time—decided to step away from the public eye.
“He said he’d spent too long looking elsewhere and would devote himself to his duties as a Hunter for a while.”
“And then that incident happened?”
“Oh, you read that article?”
“I just did.”
Team Leader Choi held out his phone. The screen, about the size of an adult’s palm, displayed a headline from eight years ago in bold type.
Myeongdong Station Mutated Gate Catastrophe, Around 30 Dead Including A-Rank Hunter Do Minsu... Surviving Won Myunghoon: “Minsu, I’m Sorry.”
The incident had caused a massive uproar and dominated the news at the time.
“Who is Do Minsu?”
“An A-rank star Hunter who was extremely close to Myunghoon hyung. His popularity was soaring, but he died after joining him on a cooperative raid as a social outing.”
No one had expected anything like that to happen when they set out for a B-rank Gate in such a lighthearted mood, as though they were going on a picnic.
Especially not with two A-rank Hunters participating.
The domestic media boiled over like a cauldron on hot coals, then quickly went cold.
“It took several years for him to stand trial over that incident and be cleared of the charges.”
After the long legal fight, all that remained was a reputation covered in filth and the public’s indifference.
He appeared on television a few times afterward, but that was all. Unable to make a comeback, he quietly retired from the entertainment industry.
Though I don’t think he’s given up yet.
If he had let go of all his lingering attachments, he wouldn’t have offered to recruit me and promised to turn me into a star Hunter.
In any case, after listening to the whole story, Team Leader Choi gave a small nod.
“I see.”
“But why are you suddenly asking about that?”
“Won Myunghoon’s name is number one in the real-time search rankings. There are already dozens of related articles.”
“Oh, really?”
“And Jin Taekyung is right alongside him at number one.”
“What?”
What was going on? Could two people be tied for first in the real-time search rankings?
As I tilted my head, Team Leader Choi held out his phone again.
A fresh article posted ten minutes earlier filled the screen.
Jin Taekyung & Won Myunghoon: Successful Fanboy Transferring to Star Guild? A New Star Hunter Is About to Be Born
After a brief silence, I tore my eyes away from the screen.
Team Leader Choi asked,
“Are you transferring?”
No, what the hell was he talking about?
Hyung, I’ll see you again soon.
I hadn’t expected those words, spoken only a few hours ago when I parted ways with Won Myunghoon, to come true so quickly.
Of course, the place where we met again wasn’t a coin karaoke room but the Peace Guild House.
“I’m sorry.”
Won Myunghoon had read the article in the middle of work and rushed over immediately. He bowed politely to every Guild member, including me, then explained in a flustered voice,

“I was surprised too. Someone must have seen us meeting and put out a speculative article... I’ve already filed a complaint with the media outlet and arranged for an immediate statement to be released.”
Team Leader Choi, who had been staring at Won Myunghoon, spoke.
“I saw the article saying the story was baseless a few minutes ago. You work quickly.”
“False information needs to be corrected as soon as possible.”
“False information?”
Team Leader Choi’s long fingers tapped the phone screen.
“But it isn’t entirely baseless, is it? Jin Taekyung told me that you offered to recruit him. In a café with other people around, no less.”
“That...”
“Team Leader Choi, let me explain it again.”
I stepped in for the hesitant Won Myunghoon.
Considering the situation, I had no choice but to reveal the conversation we’d had at the café, and I was already feeling a little guilty about it.
“What happened was—”
But before I could continue, Won Myunghoon’s firm voice cut me off.
“It’s true. I offered to recruit him, and Taekyung turned me down. This all happened because of my own selfishness, so I sincerely apologize.”
“Hmm.”
Who was Won Myunghoon, anyway?
Won Myunghoon wasn’t just an accomplished Hunter. He was a celebrity who had once stood at the very height of popularity.
When someone like him frankly admitted his mistake, accepted responsibility, and bowed with perfect courtesy, there wasn’t much left for anyone to say.
It wasn’t as though he had seriously violated professional courtesy.
Hunters were professionals, plain and simple. As long as the regulations allowed it, they were free to transfer to another Guild or leave one whenever they wanted.
The dozens of recruitment offers I had received before Won Myunghoon’s were no different.
The only difference was that I had arranged a separate meeting with him because I was a fan.
And the subsequent articles about my transfer had already been proven baseless.
Thanks to the swift action from both sides, the situation was already dying down.
Team Leader Choi, who had been deep in thought, finally spoke.
“All right. Let’s put this matter to rest.”
Won Myunghoon’s face brightened.
“I’m relieved to hear you say that. Thank you.”
“Not at all. I have no intention of turning a minor incident into something bigger than it is. Besides, our side shares some of the blame.”
Im Kkeokjeong, who had been watching the situation carefully, cut in with a good-natured grin.
“Yeah, yeah. Now that’s good to see. That’s how people should live—understanding each other.”
Butler Kim and Song Song nodded in agreement.
The atmosphere inside the Guild House, which had been strangely uncomfortable only ten minutes earlier, had turned warm and friendly.
I’m glad this worked out better than expected.
Soon, Won Myunghoon had a cup of coffee in front of him. Wearing an amiable smile, he chatted about one thing after another.
“Taekyung is incredibly devoted to the Peace Guild. I wanted him so badly that I tried to lure him away, but he wouldn’t budge.”
“Haha! This guy’s always been unbeatable when it comes to loyalty.”
“You’re all such wonderful people that I suppose he didn’t want to leave. Now that I’ve met you in person, I understand why Taekyung turned me down without a second thought.”
“Wow. Mr. Won, you really know how to tell people what they want to hear. When I watched you on television, I thought it was all scripted.”
“That earned me plenty of accusations that I was an obnoxious bastard.”
It was in the middle of this friendly conversation that Won Myunghoon casually made another proposal.
“What are your schedules like tomorrow? I was wondering if we could go on a raid together.”
“Tomorrow?”
“A raid?”
Everyone reacted differently, but their eyes all turned toward one person.
Team Leader Choi.
On paper, Butler Kim was the Guild Master. But Won Myunghoon had also realized that Team Leader Choi was the real power in the Guild.
“What do you think, Team Leader? This would be a good opportunity to clear up the suspicions raised by the rumor sheets, and it could also be a valuable experience for the Guild members.”
“I’m not sure.”
Maybe it was because I’d grown used to Team Leader Choi by now.
I could sense something subtly uneasy in his expression.
But his hesitation vanished at Won Myunghoon’s next words.
“It’s an A-rank Gate. Fortunately, our Guild obtained permission to raid it this week. It seems like a shame to let the opportunity go to waste.”
“An A-rank Gate?”
“Yes. We’ll also guarantee you the rights to anything that comes out of the Gate.”
Gate qualification reviews were strict.
As a Guild that had only just begun recruiting members, the Peace Guild would need a considerable amount of time before it could enter an A-rank Gate.
“An A-rank Gate...”
Team Leader Choi murmured under his breath, then finally nodded.

I answered firmly and swung my spear shaft.
Wham!
Something crunched, and the creature charging in from the side slammed straight into the ground.
It stood two meters tall—a massive, gray-furred, bipedal wolf with nothing left above its shoulders.
I had blown its head off through sheer strength alone.
A System notification rang out at the same time.
Ding.
System You have defeated Lv.
73 Lycanthrope! - You have gained EXP!
The lycanthropes that had watched their fellow die let out a chorus of growls and howls.
- Grrrrr.
- Awooooo.
Their long, vertically slit yellow pupils trembled.
Seeing them hesitate, Team Leader Choi remarked as though he had just realized something.
“This is the first time I’ve seen lycanthropes look so docile.”
“They’re good at controlling their anger.
Maybe being half-human means they picked up that trait too.”
Hotheads who claimed to have anger-management issues always followed the same pattern.
They acted like Lü Bu around anyone weaker than them, but the moment they found themselves in front of some muscular tough guys, they became the politest people in the world.
And once they lose the momentum, it’s over.
Slash!
I flicked the sticky blood off my spearhead and beckoned to the creatures with one finger.
“Come on, you sons of bitches.”
- Whiiine.
Their ears had folded halfway back, and their tails were tucked between their legs.
The moment a wolf became a dog, the fight was as good as over.
“You little bastards are cute.”
As I walked toward them with a grin, Team Leader Choi said,
“If possible, please handle them cleanly.”
“Why?”
“So we can take some proof shots.
We’re going to post them on the Peace Guild’s official social-media account.”
“Too much pixelation would be a shame.
People prefer things uncensored.”
Ah.
He had a point.
- Awooooooooo!
As expected, the boss was different from the rest.
Its roar was packed with ferocity and killing intent.
Its body was far larger than those of the other lycanthropes, and silver fur covered it from head to toe.
Every inch of it radiated the presence of a boss monster.
“Wow.
You’re impressive.”
As I admired it, I made a decision.
I would give this one special treatment.
“One Annihilation.”
Krrrunch.
Thud.
The monster’s massive body, a gaping hole torn through its chest, toppled like a rotting old tree.
Ding.
System You have defeated Lv.

83 Silver-Mane Lycanthrope! - You have perfectly cleared the B-Rank Gate, The Lycanthrope’s Black Forest! - You have gained a substantial amount of EXP! - The exit has opened because you defeated the boss monster.
Kiiiiing.
Once the conditions were met, a Gate exit appeared in the center of the clearing.
But I still had something left to do.
“All right.
Time for the fun part—cleanup.”
The sight of the corpses scattered everywhere filled me with satisfaction.
I was heading toward them with the heart of a farmer bringing in the harvest when Team Leader Choi spoke.
“About Won Myunghoon.”
“Yes?”
I turned at the sudden sound of his voice behind me.
He sat on a flat rock, his entire body protected by a shield spell, staring at a custom-built phone.
There was something odd about his expression.
“Myunghoon hyung?”
“Yes.
What happened to Mr.
Won Myunghoon eight years ago?”
I had no idea why he was suddenly curious.
I had been a student back then, but I was such a huge fan that I knew the whole story by heart.
Explaining all of it would take forever, though.
“Look it up.
Everything comes up if you search Sonamu Wiki.”
“People say you should stay off Sonamu Wiki.”
“...They have a point.”
“Just give me a brief explanation.
Of all the people around me, you seem to know the most about Mr.
Won Myunghoon.”
“Well, if you put it that way...”
I began talking as I skinned a lycanthrope with my dagger.
“Eight years ago, Myunghoon hyung’s career was on the decline.
Every movie, drama, and album he released bombed, and then allegations of tax evasion were piled on top of that.”
“That isn’t particularly unusual.”
“No.
That industry is always full of scandals.”
“I skimmed through the articles.
It seems he was cleared of the tax-evasion allegations.”
“Yes.
That ended without any real trouble.”
But that wasn’t the end of it.
Once mud had been splashed onto his clean image, all kinds of speculative articles and rumor sheets about Won Myunghoon began circulating online.
In the end, Won Myunghoon—already past his prime and going through a difficult time—decided to step away from the public eye.
“He said he’d spent too long looking elsewhere and would devote himself to his duties as a Hunter for a while.”
“And then that incident happened?”
“Oh, you read that article?”
“I just did.”
Team Leader Choi held out his phone.
The screen, about the size of an adult’s palm, displayed a headline from eight years ago in bold type.
Myeongdong Station Mutated Gate Catastrophe, Around 30 Dead Including A-Rank Hunter Do Minsu...
Surviving Won Myunghoon: “Minsu, I’m Sorry.”
The incident had caused a massive uproar and dominated the news at the time.
“Who is Do Minsu?”
“An A-rank star Hunter who was extremely close to Myunghoon hyung.
His popularity was soaring, but he died after joining him on a cooperative raid as a social outing.”
No one had expected anything like that to happen when they set out for a B-rank Gate in such a lighthearted mood, as though they were going on a picnic.
Especially not with two A-rank Hunters participating.
The domestic media boiled over like a cauldron on hot coals, then quickly went cold.
“It took several years for him to stand trial over that incident and be cleared of the charges.”
After the long legal fight, all that remained was a reputation covered in filth and the public’s indifference.
He appeared on television a few times afterward, but that was all.
Unable to make a comeback, he quietly retired from the entertainment industry.
Though I don’t think he’s given up yet.
If he had let go of all his lingering attachments, he wouldn’t have offered to recruit me and promised to turn me into a star Hunter.
In any case, after listening to the whole story, Team Leader Choi gave a small nod.
“I see.”
“But why are you suddenly asking about that?”
“Won Myunghoon’s name is number one in the real-time search rankings.
There are already dozens of related articles.”
“Oh, really?”
“And Jin Taekyung is right alongside him at number one.”
“What?”
What was going on?
Could two people be tied for first in the real-time search rankings?
As I tilted my head, Team Leader Choi held out his phone again.
A fresh article posted ten minutes earlier filled the screen.
Jin Taekyung & Won Myunghoon: Successful Fanboy Transferring to Star Guild?
A New Star Hunter Is About to Be Born
After a brief silence, I tore my eyes away from the screen.
Team Leader Choi asked,
“Are you transferring?”
No, what the hell was he talking about?
Hyung, I’ll see you again soon.
I hadn’t expected those words, spoken only a few hours ago when I parted ways with Won Myunghoon, to come true so quickly.
Of course, the place where we met again wasn’t a coin karaoke room but the Peace Guild House.
“I’m sorry.”
Won Myunghoon had read the article in the middle of work and rushed over immediately.
He bowed politely to every Guild member, including me, then explained in a flustered voice,
“I was surprised too.
Someone must have seen us meeting and put out a speculative article...
I’ve already filed a complaint with the media outlet and arranged for an immediate statement to be released.”
Team Leader Choi, who had been staring at Won Myunghoon, spoke.
“I saw the article saying the story was baseless a few minutes ago.
You work quickly.”
“False information needs to be corrected as soon as possible.”
“False information?”
Team Leader Choi’s long fingers tapped the phone screen.
“But it isn’t entirely baseless, is it?
Jin Taekyung told me that you offered to recruit him.
In a café with other people around, no less.”
“That...”
“Team Leader Choi, let me explain it again.”
I stepped in for the hesitant Won Myunghoon.
Considering the situation, I had no choice but to reveal the conversation we’d had at the café, and I was already feeling a little guilty about it.
“What happened was—”
But before I could continue, Won Myunghoon’s firm voice cut me off.
“It’s true.
I offered to recruit him, and Taekyung turned me down.
This all happened because of my own selfishness, so I sincerely apologize.”
“Hmm.”
Who was Won Myunghoon, anyway?
Won Myunghoon wasn’t just an accomplished Hunter.
He was a celebrity who had once stood at the very height of popularity.
When someone like him frankly admitted his mistake, accepted responsibility, and bowed with perfect courtesy, there wasn’t much left for anyone to say.
It wasn’t as though he had seriously violated professional courtesy.
Hunters were professionals, plain and simple.
As long as the regulations allowed it, they were free to transfer to another Guild or leave one whenever they wanted.
The dozens of recruitment offers I had received before Won Myunghoon’s were no different.
The only difference was that I had arranged a separate meeting with him because I was a fan.
And the subsequent articles about my transfer had already been proven baseless.
Thanks to the swift action from both sides, the situation was already dying down.
Team Leader Choi, who had been deep in thought, finally spoke.
“All right.
Let’s put this matter to rest.”
Won Myunghoon’s face brightened.
“I’m relieved to hear you say that.
Thank you.”
“Not at all.
I have no intention of turning a minor incident into something bigger than it is.
Besides, our side shares some of the blame.”
Im Kkeokjeong, who had been watching the situation carefully, cut in with a good-natured grin.
“Yeah, yeah.
Now that’s good to see.
That’s how people should live—understanding each other.”
Butler Kim and Song Song nodded in agreement.
The atmosphere inside the Guild House, which had been strangely uncomfortable only ten minutes earlier, had turned warm and friendly.
I’m glad this worked out better than expected.
Soon, Won Myunghoon had a cup of coffee in front of him.
Wearing an amiable smile, he chatted about one thing after another.
“Taekyung is incredibly devoted to the Peace Guild.
I wanted him so badly that I tried to lure him away, but he wouldn’t budge.”
“Haha!
This guy’s always been unbeatable when it comes to loyalty.”
“You’re all such wonderful people that I suppose he didn’t want to leave.
Now that I’ve met you in person, I understand why Taekyung turned me down without a second thought.”
“Wow.
Mr.
Won, you really know how to tell people what they want to hear.
When I watched you on television, I thought it was all scripted.”
“That earned me plenty of accusations that I was an obnoxious bastard.”
It was in the middle of this friendly conversation that Won Myunghoon casually made another proposal.
“What are your schedules like tomorrow?
I was wondering if we could go on a raid together.”
“Tomorrow?”
“A raid?”
Everyone reacted differently, but their eyes all turned toward one person.
Team Leader Choi.
On paper, Butler Kim was the Guild Master.
But Won Myunghoon had also realized that Team Leader Choi was the real power in the Guild.
“What do you think, Team Leader?
This would be a good opportunity to clear up the suspicions raised by the rumor sheets, and it could also be a valuable experience for the Guild members.”
“I’m not sure.”
Maybe it was because I’d grown used to Team Leader Choi by now.
I could sense something subtly uneasy in his expression.
But his hesitation vanished at Won Myunghoon’s next words.
“It’s an A-rank Gate.
Fortunately, our Guild obtained permission to raid it this week.
It seems like a shame to let the opportunity go to waste.”
“An A-rank Gate?”
“Yes.
We’ll also guarantee you the rights to anything that comes out of the Gate.”
Gate qualification reviews were strict.
As a Guild that had only just begun recruiting members, the Peace Guild would need a considerable amount of time before it could enter an A-rank Gate.
“An A-rank Gate...”
Team Leader Choi murmured under his breath, then finally nodded.

chapters.title: Chapter 214
paragraphs: Once the details of the joint raid had been finalized, Won Myunghoon rose from his seat.
“Then I’ll be going.”
“Hyung, you’re leaving already?”
“It would’ve been nice to have a drink together.”
At Jin Taekyung and Im Kkeokjeong’s regretful tones, Won Myunghoon gave them a genial smile.
“I still have work to do. I am the Guild Master, after all. I can’t cause a mess and then be the only one off having fun.”
“Ah, right.”
After he put it that way, no one could press him to stay.
Telling the others there was no need to walk him out, Won Myunghoon left the Peace Guild House. He strolled away leisurely as he pulled out his phone.
After a few rings, someone answered.
“Yes, CEO.”
“The arrangements are done. We’re holding the joint raid tomorrow at two in the afternoon.”
“That was quick.”
“The bait’s too good. When would people like them ever get a chance to enter an A-rank Gate?”
“Haha. That’s true.”
“We’re only bringing one team from our Guild. You’ve told the guys to keep their mouths shut, right?”
“Don’t you trust me? I handpicked only the ones who know how to follow orders.”
“That’s why you’re Team Leader 1. I’ll be back right away, so choose the list of people participating tomorrow and have it ready.”
“Yes, sir. What about the Peace Guild?”
“This place?”
Won Myunghoon gave a short laugh and continued.
“I came by just in case, but it’s a complete mess. A hodgepodge. They’re a bunch of nobodies without even a proper hierarchy. How impressive could a Guild with only five members possibly be?”
“Even without Jin Taekyung, they still have three B-rank Hunters.”

“That’s all they are. The old man they’ve seated as Guild Master looks like a figurehead. The Team Leader and the woman used to be with the Ares Guild, but they’re nothing worth worrying about. The other one is only D-rank.”
“D-rank? That should make tomorrow’s job easy.”
“Easy?”
The amusement vanished from Won Myunghoon’s voice, leaving it ice-cold.
The sudden change in atmosphere seemed to make the person on the other end flinch. He hurriedly added,
“CEO, that’s not what I meant.”
“Team Leader 1—no, Jonghun.”
“Let’s stay sharp. Why do you think I’m personally running Gates at my age? Am I wrong?”
“I’m sorry.”
“All right. If you understand, do better from now on. Watch what you say.”
“Understood, CEO.”
“Good. See you later.”
After ending the call, Won Myunghoon took out his lip gloss and applied it.
He was only a few months shy of forty.
He spent hundreds of millions of won every year maintaining his appearance, but there was no hiding the passage of time.
“It’s been a while since I was in the spotlight. Maybe I should stop by the salon today.”
Muttering too quietly for anyone to hear, he climbed into the sports car parked by the roadside.
The thought of facing those disgusting monsters again after so long put him in a foul mood. But when he imagined the flower-strewn path awaiting him afterward, he began humming to himself.
The next morning, Jinho hyung sat across from me at the table, unable to tear his eyes away from his phone.
“You haven’t even eaten. What are you looking at so intently?”
“Articles about you.”
“Again?”
“What do you mean, again? I could read these all day.”
Anyone watching him would’ve thought the articles were about Jinho, not me.
These days, checking the online reaction and reporting it to me had become part of his daily routine. He was practically my manager.
“People like you. There are tons of articles about Won Myunghoon, too.”
“Of course there are.”
“You two look good together. So heartwarming... I wish Lord Fuck would swear at me, and so on.”
“There’s even a guy asking to be tied up and beaten.”
The world really was a big place, and it was full of lunatics.
Dumbfounded, I searched for myself. The internet was overflowing with articles about me, while every online community imaginable was packed with nicknames and edited images.
There was even a post summarizing my exploits sitting prominently on the best-posts board.
A Summary of Lord Fuck’s Exploits So Far.txt

Hi. I’m an unemployed guy in my thirties. I was thinking hard about what useless thing to do today when I became curious about Lord Fuck. Most people who know anything about him probably already know all this, but I figured there might be some people who don’t, so I wrote it up. I couldn’t be bothered to move my fingers much, so here’s the short version. 1. Awakened as F-rank at twenty. Spent seven years getting run even harder than a brand-new private, then reawakened. 2. But the Hunter Association played its trap card, so he was measured as C-rank at the time. The accepted scholarly consensus is that the Hunter Association is full of idiots. 3. The bewildered Lord Fuck was snared by an unknown Guild called the Peace Guild. 4. A B-rank Gate erupted while he was going to work in a tracksuit, dragging along slippers. He chewed through the ogres by himself and saved hundreds of people. 5. His life turned around. On the day he received his A-rank Hunter ID, he made that remark in front of fifty thousand people. Acquired the title “Lord Fuck.” That’s about it. I didn’t write anything about his family because I might get sued. A few media outlets have already been taken down. An unemployed thirtysomething like me would be nothing by comparison. If a complaint lands, I’ll get a Mom’s Touch across the back, so cut me some slack. I ate doenjang jjigae for breakfast, scratched my balls, and scribbled this together.
Only one thought came to mind after I finished reading.
It’s way too short.
If I wrote down everything I’d experienced traveling between the modern world and Murim, even a hundred pages wouldn’t be enough.
Well, they’re ordinary people who don’t know anything. I suppose this is only natural.
I scrolled through the comments packed beneath the post.
Of course, I couldn’t read all several hundred of them, so I picked out a few of the best comments.

└ (Best comment) Fuck. I love him. └ I saw Lord Fuck live, and he swears even more colorfully than my grandma. Did he go to some kind of swearing academy? └ But it sounds natural. You can’t hate him. └ We’ve had innocent, good-natured A-rank Hunters appear on TV before, but none of them were ever this down-to-earth. Lol. └ Yeah, that’s why people like him. From the stories he told in the interview about his F-rank days, it sounds like he went through hell. Maybe that’s why. └ Personally, I liked that he went straight to a raid after leaving the Association. It felt like he cared more about a Hunter’s true duty than money. └ Agreed.

└ (Best comment) So what happened to him transferring to the Star Guild? Honestly, I’d rather he just transfer. └ Completely false. He kept sucking up to Won Myunghoon in every interview, so he went to meet him once, and the story got twisted. └ Sucking...? └ There’s my material for today. └ Lord Fuck will do it for free. └ There are so many crazy bastards here.

└ (Best comment) Lord Fuck already has a permanent free pass from criticism, and now Won Myunghoon’s suddenly getting carried by the scruff of his neck. └ Seriously. I’d forgotten Won Myunghoon’s name. I vaguely remember seeing an article a few years ago saying he was cleared in that case. └ Wasn’t he popular? Why did he disappear? └ He was. He was at his peak for his entire career, but the problem was that his career was way too short. By today’s standards, his persona was too predictable, and his acting wasn’t anything special... He only got famous because one of his songs became a hit, and he had tons of fans who were just into his face. Plenty of people still suck up to Won Myunghoon. Jin Taekyung included. └ Sucking...? └ This is the same guy from the comment above. Anyway, apparently the Peace Guild and Star Guild are doing a joint raid today. I’m looking forward to it.
The overall reaction from netizens was favorable.
Apparently, appearing on the news once or twice and doing a few magazine interviews had left quite a good impression.
The public opinion of Myunghoon hyung isn’t too bad, either.
Was it nostalgia?
Although an unpleasant incident had gradually pushed him out of the public eye, plenty of people still remembered Won Myunghoon.
Jinho, sitting across from me, was one of them.
“Don’t forget to get Won Myunghoon’s autograph, okay?”
“Got it. I’m going to get a callus in my ear.”
I gave Jinho, who was as giddy as a teenage girl, a halfhearted answer and rose from my seat.
We’d eaten breakfast late, so it was already past ten. We needed to leave soon if we wanted to finish the final checks before the raid.
“Damn it. If I were a Hunter, I’d get to raid with Won Myunghoon too.”
Jinho muttered wistfully, envy written all over his face.
To be honest, I was a little nervous myself.
An A-rank Gate with Myunghoon hyung.
Part of it was that I would be entering an A-rank Gate for the first time, but the thought of raiding alongside one of my old idols also filled me with anticipation.
I never thought I’d live to see a day like this.
My heart pounding with excitement, I left the house.
If mid- and low-level Gates were grains of sand, an A-rank Gate was a massive boulder.
Even in Korea, a country famous for having so many Gates despite its small territory, A-rank Gates were rare. Competition for the right to raid them was fierce.
For the Peace Guild, which still had only five official members, this was unquestionably an opportunity that would normally be almost impossible to obtain.
And yet...
Why is everyone so relaxed?
Even I, who considered myself the strongest person here, had to swallow nervously. But Team Leader Choi, Butler Kim, and Song-i looked as calm as if they were heading to the neighborhood supermarket.
“Did they change this to a B-rank Gate without telling me?”
Team Leader Choi answered in his usual calm voice.
“It is an A-rank Gate.”
“Then why are you all so composed? Did everyone secretly take Cheongsimhwan?”
“Song-i and I have been to plenty of them. Back when we were with the Ares Guild.”
“Ah. Right.”
Ares was the greatest Guild in Korea—no, in Asia—and a major Guild recognized throughout the world.
Its strength was one thing, but every last member was part of the elite. There was no reason they couldn’t handle an A-rank Gate.
“And as for Butler Kim...”
At Team Leader Choi’s words, Butler Kim smiled.
“I saw more than enough of them during the Great Cataclysm.”
“Back when I was active, monster armies marched down the highways, and flocks of Drakes flew through the sky. Things like that.”
What the hell? That was terrifying.
As expected of someone from the Great Cataclysm generation. His level of experience was on an entirely different scale.
Butler Kim was publicly known as a B-rank Hunter, but he was powerful enough to put Im Chunsoo—an A-rank Hunter and the Guild Master of Sangdong Guild—through PT drills.
What on earth is someone like him doing here?
Team Leader Choi and Butler Kim’s true identities and relationship remained a mystery.
They knew I was curious yet still refused to tell me. They must have their reasons.
That aside...
I turned my gaze toward the last Guild member.
The one person I’d been most worried about.
Contrary to my expectations, Im Kkeokjeong was leaning back against the car seat with a calm expression.
“Are you all right?”
“Of course I’m all right—urrrgh!”
Fine, my ass. You’re nervous as hell.
Perhaps he knew it himself, because he quickly pulled out the black plastic bag he had brought in advance and buried his face in it.
After finishing a bout of retching, Im Kkeokjeong muttered with a deathly pale face,
“I’m fine. Really.”
Im Kkeokjeong might have been fine, but I wasn’t. The very act of letting a D-rank Hunter enter an A-rank Gate was a dangerously reckless decision.
“Uh, I’m only saying this just in case...”
As soon as I cautiously began speaking, Im Kkeokjeong shook his head.
“No. The Guild Master and Team Leader gave me permission, too. I can’t keep imposing on everyone forever. I need to gain some experience.”
“Hmm.”
“Taekyung, I have a wife and children to think about. I’m well past the age where I’d make a decision out of pride or childish bravado. Even if something happens...”
“Ah, I understand. That’s enough.”
I hurriedly cut him off before he could say anything more ominous.
He must have been worrying a lot lately because his rank was so much lower than those of the other Guild members, but he had taken it far too far.
“We’re going in safely and coming out safely. The Star Guild is sending two A-rank Hunters too. And Myunghoon hyung used to be a ranker.”
Between the two Guilds, there were four A-rank Hunters and more than ten B-rank Hunters. They had more than enough strength to cover for Kkeokjeong.
Team Leader Choi nodded as well.
“Nothing will go wrong.”
He was a cautious man. If he had decided to let Im Kkeokjeong participate, it was because he was confident it would be safe.
“Yeah. It will.”
A faint smile appeared on Im Kkeokjeong’s lips.
Just then, tall buildings began rising into view beyond the car windows.
It looked like an entire village—no, a small city.
Its residents and guards were soldiers carrying firearms and Hunters decked out in expensive equipment.
“Wow.”
Unlike me, who let out an exclamation, Team Leader Choi frowned.
“This place...”
After surveying the scene outside, he turned toward the driver of the limousine bus Won Myunghoon had sent especially for us.
“I think you may have brought us to the wrong place.”
“What? That can’t be.”
The driver’s eyes widened as though he had no idea what Team Leader Choi meant.
“The A-rank Gate, Black Wyvern’s Nest. This is the right place. I entered it into the GPS and came straight here.”
“Black Wyvern’s Nest? There must have been some mistake. Won Myunghoon said...”
“Who’s Won Myunghoon? I work for the bus company, so I don’t know him. I came exactly where I was told to go.”
Team Leader Choi and the driver’s voices buzzed in my ears.
Suddenly, my stomach began to churn, and a sharp pain throbbed through my head.
Amid the confusion, a roar I’d heard three years ago tore through my mind.
Kyaaaaaaar!
Eyes stained pitch-black and a tongue like a blade.
The wingbeats that had brought down the cave and the claws that had torn my teammates apart flashed vividly before my eyes, blurring my vision.
The Black Wyvern.
I never thought we’d meet again like this.

The next morning, Jinho hyung sat across from me at the table, unable to tear his eyes away from his phone.
“You haven’t even eaten.
What are you looking at so intently?”
“Articles about you.”
“Again?”
“What do you mean, again?
I could read these all day.”
Anyone watching him would’ve thought the articles were about Jinho, not me.
These days, checking the online reaction and reporting it to me had become part of his daily routine.
He was practically my manager.
“People like you.
There are tons of articles about Won Myunghoon, too.”
“Of course there are.”
“You two look good together.
So heartwarming...
I wish Lord Fuck would swear at me, and so on.”
“There’s even a guy asking to be tied up and beaten.”
The world really was a big place, and it was full of lunatics.
Dumbfounded, I searched for myself.
The internet was overflowing with articles about me, while every online community imaginable was packed with nicknames and edited images.
There was even a post summarizing my exploits sitting prominently on the best-posts board.
A Summary of Lord Fuck’s Exploits So Far.txt
Hi.
I’m an unemployed guy in my thirties.
I was thinking hard about what useless thing to do today when I became curious about Lord Fuck.
Most people who know anything about him probably already know all this, but I figured there might be some people who don’t, so I wrote it up.
I couldn’t be bothered to move my fingers much, so here’s the short version.
Awakened as F-rank at twenty.
Spent seven years getting run even harder than a brand-new private, then reawakened.
But the Hunter Association played its trap card, so he was measured as C-rank at the time.
The accepted scholarly consensus is that the Hunter Association is full of idiots.
The bewildered Lord Fuck was snared by an unknown Guild called the Peace Guild.
A B-rank Gate erupted while he was going to work in a tracksuit, dragging along slippers.
He chewed through the ogres by himself and saved hundreds of people.
His life turned around.
On the day he received his A-rank Hunter ID, he made that remark in front of fifty thousand people.
Acquired the title “Lord Fuck.” That’s about it.
I didn’t write anything about his family because I might get sued.
A few media outlets have already been taken down.
An unemployed thirtysomething like me would be nothing by comparison.
If a complaint lands, I’ll get a Mom’s Touch across the back, so cut me some slack.
I ate doenjang jjigae for breakfast, scratched my balls, and scribbled this together.
Only one thought came to mind after I finished reading.
It’s way too short.
If I wrote down everything I’d experienced traveling between the modern world and Murim, even a hundred pages wouldn’t be enough.
Well, they’re ordinary people who don’t know anything.
I suppose this is only natural.
I scrolled through the comments packed beneath the post.
Of course, I couldn’t read all several hundred of them, so I picked out a few of the best comments.
└ (Best comment) Fuck.
I love him. └ I saw Lord Fuck live, and he swears even more colorfully than my grandma.
Did he go to some kind of swearing academy? └ But it sounds natural.
You can’t hate him. └ We’ve had innocent, good-natured A-rank Hunters appear on TV before, but none of them were ever this down-to-earth.
Lol. └ Yeah, that’s why people like him.
From the stories he told in the interview about his F-rank days, it sounds like he went through hell.
Maybe that’s why. └ Personally, I liked that he went straight to a raid after leaving the Association.
It felt like he cared more about a Hunter’s true duty than money. └ Agreed.
└ (Best comment) So what happened to him transferring to the Star Guild?
Honestly, I’d rather he just transfer. └ Completely false.

He kept sucking up to Won Myunghoon in every interview, so he went to meet him once, and the story got twisted. └ Sucking...? └ There’s my material for today. └ Lord Fuck will do it for free. └ There are so many crazy bastards here.
└ (Best comment) Lord Fuck already has a permanent free pass from criticism, and now Won Myunghoon’s suddenly getting carried by the scruff of his neck. └ Seriously.
I’d forgotten Won Myunghoon’s name.
I vaguely remember seeing an article a few years ago saying he was cleared in that case. └ Wasn’t he popular?
Why did he disappear? └ He was.
He was at his peak for his entire career, but the problem was that his career was way too short.
By today’s standards, his persona was too predictable, and his acting wasn’t anything special...
He only got famous because one of his songs became a hit, and he had tons of fans who were just into his face.
Plenty of people still suck up to Won Myunghoon.
Jin Taekyung included. └ Sucking...? └ This is the same guy from the comment above.
Anyway, apparently the Peace Guild and Star Guild are doing a joint raid today.
I’m looking forward to it.
The overall reaction from netizens was favorable.
Apparently, appearing on the news once or twice and doing a few magazine interviews had left quite a good impression.
The public opinion of Myunghoon hyung isn’t too bad, either.
Was it nostalgia?
Although an unpleasant incident had gradually pushed him out of the public eye, plenty of people still remembered Won Myunghoon.
Jinho, sitting across from me, was one of them.
“Don’t forget to get Won Myunghoon’s autograph, okay?”
“Got it.
I’m going to get a callus in my ear.”
I gave Jinho, who was as giddy as a teenage girl, a halfhearted answer and rose from my seat.
We’d eaten breakfast late, so it was already past ten.
We needed to leave soon if we wanted to finish the final checks before the raid.
“Damn it.
If I were a Hunter, I’d get to raid with Won Myunghoon too.”
Jinho muttered wistfully, envy written all over his face.
To be honest, I was a little nervous myself.
An A-rank Gate with Myunghoon hyung.
Part of it was that I would be entering an A-rank Gate for the first time, but the thought of raiding alongside one of my old idols also filled me with anticipation.
I never thought I’d live to see a day like this.
My heart pounding with excitement, I left the house.
If mid- and low-level Gates were grains of sand, an A-rank Gate was a massive boulder.
Even in Korea, a country famous for having so many Gates despite its small territory, A-rank Gates were rare.
Competition for the right to raid them was fierce.
For the Peace Guild, which still had only five official members, this was unquestionably an opportunity that would normally be almost impossible to obtain.
And yet...
Why is everyone so relaxed?
Even I, who considered myself the strongest person here, had to swallow nervously.
But Team Leader Choi, Butler Kim, and Song-i looked as calm as if they were heading to the neighborhood supermarket.
“Did they change this to a B-rank Gate without telling me?”
Team Leader Choi answered in his usual calm voice.
“It is an A-rank Gate.”
“Then why are you all so composed?
Did everyone secretly take Cheongsimhwan?”
“Song-i and I have been to plenty of them.
Back when we were with the Ares Guild.”
“Ah.
Right.”
Ares was the greatest Guild in Korea—no, in Asia—and a major Guild recognized throughout the world.
Its strength was one thing, but every last member was part of the elite.
There was no reason they couldn’t handle an A-rank Gate.
“And as for Butler Kim...”
At Team Leader Choi’s words, Butler Kim smiled.
“I saw more than enough of them during the Great Cataclysm.”
“Back when I was active, monster armies marched down the highways, and flocks of Drakes flew through the sky.
Things like that.”
What the hell?
That was terrifying.
As expected of someone from the Great Cataclysm generation.
His level of experience was on an entirely different scale.
Butler Kim was publicly known as a B-rank Hunter, but he was powerful enough to put Im Chunsoo—an A-rank Hunter and the Guild Master of Sangdong Guild—through PT drills.
What on earth is someone like him doing here?
Team Leader Choi and Butler Kim’s true identities and relationship remained a mystery.
They knew I was curious yet still refused to tell me.
They must have their reasons.
That aside...
I turned my gaze toward the last Guild member.
The one person I’d been most worried about.
Contrary to my expectations, Im Kkeokjeong was leaning back against the car seat with a calm expression.
“Are you all right?”
“Of course I’m all right—urrrgh!”
Fine, my ass.
You’re nervous as hell.
Perhaps he knew it himself, because he quickly pulled out the black plastic bag he had brought in advance and buried his face in it.
After finishing a bout of retching, Im Kkeokjeong muttered with a deathly pale face,
“I’m fine.
Really.”
Im Kkeokjeong might have been fine, but I wasn’t.
The very act of letting a D-rank Hunter enter an A-rank Gate was a dangerously reckless decision.
“Uh, I’m only saying this just in case...”
As soon as I cautiously began speaking, Im Kkeokjeong shook his head.
“No.
The Guild Master and Team Leader gave me permission, too.
I can’t keep imposing on everyone forever.
I need to gain some experience.”
“Hmm.”
“Taekyung, I have a wife and children to think about.
I’m well past the age where I’d make a decision out of pride or childish bravado.
Even if something happens...”
“Ah, I understand.
That’s enough.”
I hurriedly cut him off before he could say anything more ominous.
He must have been worrying a lot lately because his rank was so much lower than those of the other Guild members, but he had taken it far too far.
“We’re going in safely and coming out safely.
The Star Guild is sending two A-rank Hunters too.
And Myunghoon hyung used to be a ranker.”
Between the two Guilds, there were four A-rank Hunters and more than ten B-rank Hunters.
They had more than enough strength to cover for Kkeokjeong.
Team Leader Choi nodded as well.
“Nothing will go wrong.”
He was a cautious man.
If he had decided to let Im Kkeokjeong participate, it was because he was confident it would be safe.
“Yeah.
It will.”
A faint smile appeared on Im Kkeokjeong’s lips.
Just then, tall buildings began rising into view beyond the car windows.
It looked like an entire village—no, a small city.
Its residents and guards were soldiers carrying firearms and Hunters decked out in expensive equipment.
“Wow.”
Unlike me, who let out an exclamation, Team Leader Choi frowned.
“This place...”
After surveying the scene outside, he turned toward the driver of the limousine bus Won Myunghoon had sent especially for us.
“I think you may have brought us to the wrong place.”
“What?
That can’t be.”
The driver’s eyes widened as though he had no idea what Team Leader Choi meant.
“The A-rank Gate, Black Wyvern’s Nest.
This is the right place.
I entered it into the GPS and came straight here.”
“Black Wyvern’s Nest?
There must have been some mistake.
Won Myunghoon said...”
“Who’s Won Myunghoon?
I work for the bus company, so I don’t know him.
I came exactly where I was told to go.”
Team Leader Choi and the driver’s voices buzzed in my ears.
Suddenly, my stomach began to churn, and a sharp pain throbbed through my head.
Amid the confusion, a roar I’d heard three years ago tore through my mind.
Kyaaaaaaar!
Eyes stained pitch-black and a tongue like a blade.
The wingbeats that had brought down the cave and the claws that had torn my teammates apart flashed vividly before my eyes, blurring my vision.
The Black Wyvern.
I never thought we’d meet again like this.

chapters.title: Chapter 215
paragraphs: Wyvern.
One of the high-tier monsters classified as dragonkin, along with drakes.
Its body was larger than an airplane’s, its hide was tough, and its intelligence was high enough for it to use magic.
It possessed enough power to be called a small dragon without exaggeration.
The creature I had encountered three years ago was something that could not—and should not—have emerged from an E-Rank Gate.
Kyaaaaaaar!
I opened my eyes at the monster’s roar, echoing in the distance.
Instead of a dark, humid cave, I saw a clear sky and the familiar faces of my Guild members.
“Mr. Jin Taekyung, are you all right?”
“Taekyung.”
Their voices were full of concern. I forced my rigid expression to relax.
“Yes. My stomach felt a little queasy. I guess I got motion sickness.”
“Motion sickness? You?”
Motion sickness in a Peak master—or rather, an A-Rank Hunter. Even I knew it was a pathetic excuse.
Even Song-i, who had been keeping her distance from me lately, looked concerned as she asked, “Would you like me to cast a healing spell?”
“No, I’m fine.”
I gave her a feeble smile like the protagonist of The Last Leaf and added, “Just having you beside me is healing enough, Song-i.”
“...Ah. Yes.”
Im Kkeokjeong leaned close and whispered in my ear, “You bastard. How the hell did you come up with a line like that?”
“Was it bad?”
“No, it was insane. The moment I heard it, electricity shot through my whole body.”
Was it really that effective?
My mind had been completely blank, so I’d just blurted out the first thing that came to me.
But judging by Song-i, who had frozen like someone struck by lightning, it did seem to have worked.
Why does it feel like I landed a critical hit?
Meanwhile, the throbbing in my temples and the nausea in my stomach had both subsided.
Just as I was taking a deep breath, the door of the limousine bus we had been riding in opened, and someone appeared.
“Everyone’s here. But...”
Won Myunghoon trailed off at the tense atmosphere inside the bus, then turned to Team Leader Choi.
“Did something happen?”
“Yes. Something serious enough that we need to talk.”
Team Leader Choi answered firmly, then turned toward me.
“You too, Mr. Jin Taekyung.”
“The Star Guild got here ages ago. Where’s the Peace Guild?”
“Wait, isn’t that Jin Taekyung?”
“It is. Won Myunghoon’s beside him, so it’s definitely him.”
“Take pictures quickly. Get ready to interview him in a little while.”
Team Leader Choi, Won Myunghoon, and I moved toward a secluded corner.
The reporters and Hunters who had flocked here after hearing the news stared so intently that I could feel their gazes burning into my face.
Once their persistent attention finally drifted away, Team Leader Choi spoke with a grim expression.
“Why was the location suddenly changed?”
“Changed? What do you mean?”
“Wasn’t Manticore’s Jungle supposed to be today’s raid location?”
“What? That can’t be right. Do you have the contract with you?”
“Here. It’s stated clearly.”
Won Myunghoon hurriedly examined the contract Team Leader Choi handed him. His face twisted violently.
“That bastard, the leader of Team One.”
Judging by his reaction, there seemed to have been a mistake somewhere along the way.
After muttering several curses—unusual for him—Won Myunghoon spoke with an awkward expression.
“I’m sorry. One of our employees made a serious mistake. I don’t know what to say.”
“A mistake. I see.”
Team Leader Choi continued in a dry voice.
“I think it would be best to call off today’s raid.”
“What?”
“This isn’t just any Gate. It’s an A-Rank Gate. Entering without perfect preparation could lead to an accident. And...”
Team Leader Choi trailed off for a moment, his gaze flicking toward me.
He had already investigated my past.
He knew I was the sole survivor of the Sangdong Station Mutated Gate incident three years ago. He also knew I was still suffering from the aftereffects.
“Wyverns are still too much for our Guild members. We appreciate the offer, but I think it would be best for both sides if we withdrew here.”
“Team Leader!”
Despite Won Myunghoon’s flustered cry, Team Leader Choi’s attitude remained as sharp as a blade.
“Wyverns are out of the question. At least for now.”
That was when I abruptly spoke up after watching the situation in silence.
“Let’s do it. The raid.”
“Mr. Jin Taekyung.”
“Plenty of articles have already gone up online, and all these reporters are here. If we call it off now, won’t people start talking?”
I stared past Team Leader Choi and Won Myunghoon, who stood side by side.
Reporters with cameras hanging from their necks were already watching us carefully as they edged closer.
They’ve got one hell of a nose for a story.
They had clearly sensed the tension and were coming over to investigate.
Before Team Leader Choi could say anything, I quickly cut him off.
“It’s not that I particularly care about the articles. It’s just that I’m all right now.”
“Are you sure?”
“Yes.”
Half of that was true. The other half was a lie.
I still wasn’t fine. For the past three years, I had relived the same nightmare over and over, remembering the creature’s roar and my teammates’ screams.
Then I would wake drenched in cold sweat, pretend nothing had happened, and go through another day just like all the others.
But not anymore.
“I can do this. I’m not the same person I was back then.”
I was no longer the utterly powerless F-Rank Hunter I had been. I was a Peak master and an A-Rank Hunter—someone who could stand tall anywhere and call himself strong.
“So it’s fine. No, I want to do it.”
Team Leader Choi stared at me for a long moment, then let out a deep sigh.
“All right. Let’s do it.”
A short while later, we stood before a doorway of ominously rippling mana.
Rolling cameras and incessant flashes captured the members of both Guilds as we began our joint raid.
“Phew.”
I took a deep breath and stepped forward.
Sticky mana coiled around my body as the familiar System notification appeared.
Ding.
System You have entered A-Rank Gate, The Black Wyvern’s Nest. - Upon clearing the Gate, you will receive a Reward commensurate with your performance.
Ssshhh.
When I opened my eyes again, everything around me had changed.
“Huff. Huuuff.”
Im Kkeokjeong, clad in heavy full plate armor, panted raggedly.
An hour had passed since we entered the Gate, and sweat was already pouring down his forehead like rain.
He wasn’t the only one. Most of the more than twenty members of the Star and Peace Guilds trudged along with sweat streaming from their bodies.
Hardly surprising.
I clicked my tongue and looked around.
Beneath the blazing sun, a jungle of trees dozens of meters tall and bizarre-looking plants stretched endlessly into the distance.
The sight alone was suffocating, and air hotter and more humid than a steam sauna completed the picture.
A primeval forest.
It looked exactly like something out of a dinosaur documentary.
The weather aside, the scenery itself was spectacular.
“Wow.”
As I let out an involuntary exclamation, someone came over and tapped me on the shoulder.
“Pretty relaxed, aren’t you?”
“Oh, Myunghoon hyung. Weren’t you up front?”
Our formation had Won Myunghoon in the lead, me in the middle, and Team Leader Choi and Butler Kim bringing up the rear.
Won Myunghoon flashed his white teeth in a grin.
“You have to check behind you sometimes. Everyone else is struggling, but then I spotted some carefree bastard sightseeing by himself, so I came over.”
“What if a wyvern suddenly jumps out?”
“We’re still in the jungle zone, so we’ll only run into minor monsters here. Wyverns nest on cliffs and mountain peaks. We’re nowhere near them yet.”
“Seriously?”
“It’ll take at least half a day to encounter a wyvern, or a full day if we’re unlucky. Enjoy the scenery while you can.”
I had known higher-level Gates were larger, but I hadn’t expected anything on this scale. I shook my head in disbelief.
“This place is incredible. No wonder they give you raid access for a full week.”
“That’s how long these raids take. Once you’ve been through a few A-Rank Gates like this, you’ll be sick of them too.”
“I don’t know about that.”
I probably wouldn’t.
To me, a Gate had long since stopped being a grueling, tedious workplace. It was a place where I could grow even stronger.
“I’m having fun.”
“...Well, I suppose that’s possible.”
Won Myunghoon gave me an odd look, then handed me something.
“Here. Hold on to this.”
“What is it?”
It was a necklace set with a blue jewel. Before I could inspect the Item, Won Myunghoon continued.

“It has a cold spell enchanted into it, so put it on. You’re an A-Rank, so you’ll be fine for now, but the heat will start draining your Stamina later. You’re one of our main combat assets. You need to conserve your strength.”
“You don’t have to give me something like this, hyung.”
“I’m not giving it to you. I’m lending it to you, so take good care of it and return it later.”
Even at a glance, it looked incredibly expensive.
I hesitated, but Won Myunghoon kept urging me, so I had no choice but to put it on.
Ding.
System You have equipped Yeti’s Necklace. - A wind from the snowy plains flows from the necklace.
At the same time as the System notification, a chill cold enough to send shivers down my spine wrapped around my entire body.
“It works well.”
“It looks good on you. Keep it on from now on. I need to go deploy the scouting team.”
Won Myunghoon smiled with satisfaction and strode away. The moment his back disappeared from view, I took off the necklace.
I told him I’m really fine.
Won Myunghoon might have taken my words for modesty, but I’d only been stating a fact.
When I opened my Conception and Governor Vessels in the Murim, I had gained something far better than Yeti’s Necklace.
Unaffected by Cold and Heat.
That was why I hadn’t shed a single drop of sweat. It wouldn’t matter if one hour became ten.
This level of heat couldn’t affect me at all.
It would be far better to give the necklace to someone who actually needed it.
“Uncle.”
“Huff, huff. What?”
Im Kkeokjeong, who had been walking a few steps ahead, turned around. Sweat poured from his head as if someone had installed a sprinkler on top of it.
“Why are you sweating so much? Are you all right?”
“...Do I look all right?”
“No.”
“Then don’t talk to me. I’m dying here.”
“You should’ve worn something cooler. Team Leader Choi has plenty of magical Equipment.”
“I thought we were going to fight a Manticore, so I went all in on defense. At this rate, they’ll be holding my funeral.”
“We can’t have that. You have a wife and children.”
I laughed quietly and put the necklace around his neck myself. Im Kkeokjeong’s eyes widened as the cool wind of the snowy plains washed over him.
“Huh? What’s this?”
“A present. Not that I’m giving it to you, of course. I’m only lending it to you while we’re traveling.”
“Whew. I don’t know what this is, but I can finally breathe again.”
Life returned to his exhausted face. Just as Im Kkeokjeong beamed at me—
—Peeeeep!
A piercing shriek rang out from somewhere.
The birds hiding in the dense forest burst into flight, and branches and leaves came crashing down over everyone’s heads like a torrential downpour.
But no one, including me, paid them any attention.
—Kyaaaaaaak!
A bloodcurdling cry rang out as an enormous shadow engulfed all twenty-odd people.
I looked up and spotted a dark shape circling impossibly high overhead.
“Wyvern...”
Won Myunghoon had been wrong.
Not half a day. Not a full day.
After only one hour—
It had appeared.

Sticky mana coiled around my body as the familiar System notification appeared.
Ding.
System You have entered A-Rank Gate, The Black Wyvern’s Nest. - Upon clearing the Gate, you will receive a Reward commensurate with your performance.
Ssshhh.
When I opened my eyes again, everything around me had changed.
“Huff.
Huuuff.”
Im Kkeokjeong, clad in heavy full plate armor, panted raggedly.
An hour had passed since we entered the Gate, and sweat was already pouring down his forehead like rain.
He wasn’t the only one.
Most of the more than twenty members of the Star and Peace Guilds trudged along with sweat streaming from their bodies.
Hardly surprising.
I clicked my tongue and looked around.
Beneath the blazing sun, a jungle of trees dozens of meters tall and bizarre-looking plants stretched endlessly into the distance.
The sight alone was suffocating, and air hotter and more humid than a steam sauna completed the picture.
A primeval forest.
It looked exactly like something out of a dinosaur documentary.
The weather aside, the scenery itself was spectacular.
“Wow.”
As I let out an involuntary exclamation, someone came over and tapped me on the shoulder.
“Pretty relaxed, aren’t you?”
“Oh, Myunghoon hyung.
Weren’t you up front?”
Our formation had Won Myunghoon in the lead, me in the middle, and Team Leader Choi and Butler Kim bringing up the rear.
Won Myunghoon flashed his white teeth in a grin.
“You have to check behind you sometimes.
Everyone else is struggling, but then I spotted some carefree bastard sightseeing by himself, so I came over.”
“What if a wyvern suddenly jumps out?”
“We’re still in the jungle zone, so we’ll only run into minor monsters here.
Wyverns nest on cliffs and mountain peaks.
We’re nowhere near them yet.”
“Seriously?”
“It’ll take at least half a day to encounter a wyvern, or a full day if we’re unlucky.
Enjoy the scenery while you can.”
I had known higher-level Gates were larger, but I hadn’t expected anything on this scale.
I shook my head in disbelief.
“This place is incredible.
No wonder they give you raid access for a full week.”
“That’s how long these raids take.
Once you’ve been through a few A-Rank Gates like this, you’ll be sick of them too.”
“I don’t know about that.”
I probably wouldn’t.
To me, a Gate had long since stopped being a grueling, tedious workplace.
It was a place where I could grow even stronger.
“I’m having fun.”
“...Well, I suppose that’s possible.”
Won Myunghoon gave me an odd look, then handed me something.
“Here.
Hold on to this.”
“What is it?”
It was a necklace set with a blue jewel.
Before I could inspect the Item, Won Myunghoon continued.
“It has a cold spell enchanted into it, so put it on.
You’re an A-Rank, so you’ll be fine for now, but the heat will start draining your Stamina later.
You’re one of our main combat assets.
You need to conserve your strength.”
“You don’t have to give me something like this, hyung.”
“I’m not giving it to you.
I’m lending it to you, so take good care of it and return it later.”
Even at a glance, it looked incredibly expensive.
I hesitated, but Won Myunghoon kept urging me, so I had no choice but to put it on.
Ding.
System You have equipped Yeti’s Necklace. - A wind from the snowy plains flows from the necklace.
At the same time as the System notification, a chill cold enough to send shivers down my spine wrapped around my entire body.
“It works well.”
“It looks good on you.
Keep it on from now on.
I need to go deploy the scouting team.”
Won Myunghoon smiled with satisfaction and strode away.
The moment his back disappeared from view, I took off the necklace.
I told him I’m really fine.
Won Myunghoon might have taken my words for modesty, but I’d only been stating a fact.
When I opened my Conception and Governor Vessels in the Murim, I had gained something far better than Yeti’s Necklace.
Unaffected by Cold and Heat.
That was why I hadn’t shed a single drop of sweat.
It wouldn’t matter if one hour became ten.
This level of heat couldn’t affect me at all.
It would be far better to give the necklace to someone who actually needed it.
“Uncle.”
“Huff, huff.
What?”
Im Kkeokjeong, who had been walking a few steps ahead, turned around.
Sweat poured from his head as if someone had installed a sprinkler on top of it.
“Why are you sweating so much?
Are you all right?”
“...Do I look all right?”
“No.”
“Then don’t talk to me.
I’m dying here.”
“You should’ve worn something cooler.
Team Leader Choi has plenty of magical Equipment.”
“I thought we were going to fight a Manticore, so I went all in on defense.
At this rate, they’ll be holding my funeral.”
“We can’t have that.
You have a wife and children.”
I laughed quietly and put the necklace around his neck myself.
Im Kkeokjeong’s eyes widened as the cool wind of the snowy plains washed over him.
“Huh?
What’s this?”
“A present.
Not that I’m giving it to you, of course.
I’m only lending it to you while we’re traveling.”
“Whew.
I don’t know what this is, but I can finally breathe again.”
Life returned to his exhausted face.
Just as Im Kkeokjeong beamed at me—
—Peeeeep!
A piercing shriek rang out from somewhere.
The birds hiding in the dense forest burst into flight, and branches and leaves came crashing down over everyone’s heads like a torrential downpour.
But no one, including me, paid them any attention.
—Kyaaaaaaak!
A bloodcurdling cry rang out as an enormous shadow engulfed all twenty-odd people.
I looked up and spotted a dark shape circling impossibly high overhead.
“Wyvern...”
Won Myunghoon had been wrong.
Not half a day.
Not a full day.
After only one hour—
It had appeared.

chapters.title: Chapter 216
paragraphs: The moment I saw the Wyvern circling overhead, only one thought came to mind.
It’s small.
It stretched over twenty meters from head to tail, with a massive body and wings, but it didn’t intimidate me in the slightest.
Maybe it was because of the one I’d encountered three years ago.
Is it because I’ve gotten stronger? No. That thing was much bigger and stronger.
That one had been pitch-black all over. By contrast, the Wyvern circling overhead now had a bright green body.
At the head of the group, Won Myunghoon announced its identity in a powerful voice.
“It’s a Green Wyvern! It’s a relatively weak specimen, so everyone stay calm!”
A man in his early thirties drove a tower shield into the ground and shouted,
“Form up!”
At the command of Star Guild’s second A-Rank Hunter and Team Leader 1, the tanks rushed forward and formed a wall of shields.
“Taekyung, watch yourself!”
Im Kkeokjeong hurriedly called out a warning, then joined the wall of tanks with a spirited yell.
Boom! Boom-boom-boom!
The first row, then the second. Big, beautiful tower shields overlapped in layers, forming a curved defensive barrier.
The mages and healers standing by began chanting their spells.
“Let the wind dwell within you. Haste!”
“Power that shatters stone. Strength!”
“Vitality to the weary flesh. Healing!”
Bright motes of light spread outward like dandelion seeds.
At the same time, a System notification rang out.
Ding.
System Your physical abilities have temporarily increased due to the effects of magic. Agility has increased by 10! Strength has increased by 10! - Fatigue has been restored!
There was a reason people said mages and healers had iron rice bowls.
The so-called three-drug combo of buff spells was far more effective than I had expected.
Is it because they’re all B-Rank?
Every Hunter gathered here was talented enough to be welcomed wherever they went.
But the Green Wyvern circling overhead, watching for an opening, was no easy opponent either.
It was an A-Rank monster, after all.
“Kyaaaaaaak!”
With an earsplitting shriek, it opened its enormous jaws.
The next moment, green slime visible even from a distance poured down like torrential rain.
“It’s poison!”
“Scatter!”
Some people ducked behind the tanks’ shield wall, while others threw themselves toward nearby cover.
I was one of the latter. The moment I took shelter behind a boulder the size of a house, green rain blanketed everything within a radius of about thirty meters.
Thut-thut-thut. Ssssss!
Poison. Acidic poison, at that.
The moment it touched the rock, holes riddled its surface, and an indescribable stench stabbed at my nose.
So even a weak Wyvern is still a Wyvern.
A tiger cub was still a tiger.

The Green Wyvern might have been relatively weak for its kind, but it spewed its poison with frightening speed, and the acid was incredibly potent. Any middling or low-rank Hunters would have melted along with their Equipment.
“Team Leader 1. Casualty report.”
“None.”
Most of the people gathered here were B-Rank Hunters.
Even Im Kkeokjeong, the only real weak link, was a veteran with twenty years of experience.
Team Leader Choi’s top-tier Equipment made up for his lacking physical abilities, so no one had suffered any harm.
“As it should be.”
Won Myunghoon nodded in satisfaction, but the Green Wyvern was thoroughly enraged.
“Kyaaak! Kyaaaaaaak!”
It glared at us through vertically slit pupils, then suddenly folded its wings.
Its massive body, which had been cruising leisurely through the sky, tilted toward the ground and began a steep dive.
Whoooooosh!
The sight of the Wyvern plunging from several hundred meters up brought a crashing airplane to mind.
We could at least block its acidic poison with our shields, but if that thing hit us, we were done for.
Terrified by a situation he had never faced before, Im Kkeokjeong screamed,
“Honey! Jinwoo! Sowon!”
At this rate, he’d start calling out his father’s cousin next.
Unlike Kkeokjeong, however, the Star Guild members remained calm.
Won Myunghoon even flashed me a broad grin.
“Taekyung, want hyung to show you something cool?”
“Yeah.”
Wouldn’t it be better to order everyone to scatter?
There were still several dozen seconds before impact, but how could he be this relaxed?
“Watch carefully. It’ll help you.”
After tossing out those words, Won Myunghoon shifted his spear into a reverse grip.
“Hup.”
Veins bulged across his dense muscles, and an immense amount of mana surged into his spear like a rising tide.
At the same time, a faint line of light appeared along the spearhead.
Ssssss.
It was Spear Energy—a powerful concentration of mana known as Aura in the modern world.
“Kyaaaaaau!”
Perhaps it sensed that power. The Green Wyvern roared and twisted its body, aiming directly for Won Myunghoon and me.
And then—
Thud! Boom!
Won Myunghoon kicked off the ground and charged forward. One step, two, and finally three.
The Green Wyvern, no more than a black speck moments ago, was now only a few meters above us. Its green eyes, each as large as a basketball, flashed, and its rough-scaled jaws opened wide.
Just as its sharp teeth were about to descend upon its small prey—
“Hah!”
With a powerful shout, light shot from Won Myunghoon’s hand.
Whoooooosh! Crunch!
The Aura-wreathed spear pierced straight through the Green Wyvern’s neck. Red blood and green acidic poison sprayed out like a fountain.
Ssssss!
Its pupils contracted to pinpoints as its flesh burned, and its body, dozens of meters long, thrashed wildly.
“Kiiiik! Kiiiiiik!”
Boom! Crash-crash!
Rocks and trees shattered and went flying without distinction.
The Green Wyvern’s wings quivered as it writhed in pain.
Only a few seconds later, its rigidly raised tail dropped limply to the ground.
“Kiiiuuu...”
With its dying cry, the light vanished from its savage eyes.
Then, as if to prove its death, a System notification rang out.
Ding.
System You have defeated Lv. 97 Green Wyvern! - No EXP has been awarded because you made no contribution!
Of course. The credit belonged to one person alone.
I dismissed the holographic window and saw Won Myunghoon pulling his spear from the Green Wyvern’s corpse.
“As expected of our Guild Master!”
“A ranker really is on another level. That Aura was incredible!”
“What ranker? That was a long time ago.”
Won Myunghoon grinned at the cheers ringing out from every direction and walked over to me.
“Did you get a good look?”
“Uh, yes.”
“That was your first time seeing Aura in person, right?”
“Um... that’s right.”
“Haha. You must’ve been surprised if you’re stammering that badly.”
A gravelly voice suddenly cut in.
“Who wouldn’t be?”
It was Team Leader 1, Star Guild’s second-in-command and the main tank of today’s raid team.
He looked like a weasel. Tapping me lightly on the arm, he continued with a shameless grin.
“When I first saw it, I wondered how something like that could even exist. People don’t say you need to wield Aura to be a true A-Rank Hunter for nothing.”
Won Myunghoon made a show of frowning.
“Quit buttering me up, punk. You’re embarrassing me.”
“Come on, how am I buttering you up? You really are that good. It’s not like I’m making it up. Don’t you agree, Hunter Jin Taekyung?”
“Uh... yes.”
“See? I’m not the only one who thinks so.”
I licked my dry lips, unsure what to say. Fortunately, Won Myunghoon spoke before the mood could turn awkward.
“You’re all right except for all the sucking up. Enough flattery. Have the guys clean this up and inspect the Equipment again.”
“Understood, Guild Master. Loyalty!”
After giving an exaggerated salute, Team Leader 1 turned away.
“That guy’s always been like that. He’s flighty and careless enough to send the wrong contract...”
Won Myunghoon’s voice trailed off as he watched Team Leader 1 walk away.
“But, Taekyung.”
“Yes?”
“Are you all right? What’s with that expression you’ve had this whole time?”
“...It’s nothing. I was just a little surprised.”
“Was it the Wyvern? Well, this is your first A-Rank Gate, so that’s understandable. You’ll get used to it.”
I swallowed the words that had risen to my throat. I finally understood how the barber who saw the king’s donkey ears must have felt.
That wasn’t what surprised me.
Trying not to show how confused and frustrated I was, I looked at Won Myunghoon.
He was tall and long-limbed, with a youthful face that made it hard to believe he was nearly forty.
But the real reason I had admired him wasn’t his handsome appearance or his catchy hit songs.
An A-Rank Hunter. A master of the spear. And a ranker.
For as long as I could remember, my idol hadn’t been the celebrity Won Myunghoon, but the Hunter Won Myunghoon.
He was why I had chosen the spear when I became a Hunter. I had read and reread the spear manual he wrote during his ranker days until it fell apart.
But...
Why is he so weak?
The reason I had stood still from beginning to end was simple.
I wanted to witness Won Myunghoon fight with my own eyes.
What I saw went beyond anything I could have imagined—in an entirely different sense.
His movements are slow as hell, everything he does is needlessly flashy, and he can’t even use Aura properly.
Watching him had nearly given me a stroke.
Had Won Myunghoon always been this weak? Or had his skills declined?
My head was full of questions, but if I had to sum up my thoughts in a single line, it would be this:
What the fuck is this?
It was unfair. There was no particular reason for me to feel wronged, but somehow I felt spectacularly cheated!
It was like reserving a full-course meal at a seven-star hotel only to be served braised boneless pollock and beef bibim sauce.
This isn’t what I had in mind. It really isn’t.
Oblivious to my feelings, Won Myunghoon still wore a relaxed, confident smile.
“By the way, where’s the necklace? I don’t see it.”
Was the necklace really the issue right now?
Overcome by an inexplicable sense of emptiness, I answered carelessly.
“...I put it in my pants pocket.”
“Why?”
“Just because. It was getting in the way. Why?”
“No reason. It doesn’t matter as long as you keep it safe.”
Won Myunghoon’s gaze flicked toward my lower body. After confirming the bulge in the pocket of my tight leather pants, he added,
“Whatever you do, don’t lose it. Got it?”
“Yes.”
There was no way I could lose it. No—if I ever did, I’d have no reason to go on living.
My stuff is precious.
It really was a good thing that my body in the Murim and my body in reality were the same.
Thinking of the black anaconda coiled inside my pants lifted my gloomy mood a little.
While the Hunters dismantled the Green Wyvern and cleaned up the area, Won Myunghoon and Team Leader 1 moved to a secluded spot.
“That necklace works well.”
Team Leader 1 grinned.
“It wasn’t easy to get. Even magical scans can’t detect it.”
“Yeah, you did well, but...”
Won Myunghoon suddenly furrowed his brow and continued.
“It’s more effective than I expected. We haven’t even left the jungle yet, and a Wyvern has already appeared.”
“Couldn’t it just be a coincidence? It’s not that rare.”
“It was a coincidence eight years ago, too.”
“...What choice do we have? You can’t predict what’ll happen next inside a Gate.”
“That’s why I hate Gates. With people, you can more or less figure out what the bastard is thinking. But with this fucked-up place, you can’t.”
Won Myunghoon answered in a low voice and looked around.
Everywhere he looked, there was nothing but grass, trees, and strange insects. He wanted to return to the forest of skyscrapers as soon as possible.
“Let’s get started soon. Something bigger and stronger than a Green Wyvern needs to show up.”
“So the surviving witnesses can testify?”
“You’re one smart bastard. I tell you one thing, and you figure out ten.”
A smile formed on Won Myunghoon’s lips.
