“Yeah, you did well, but...”
Won Myunghoon suddenly furrowed his brow and continued.
“It’s more effective than I expected.
We haven’t even left the jungle yet, and a Wyvern has already appeared.”
“Couldn’t it just be a coincidence?
It’s not that rare.”
“It was a coincidence eight years ago, too.”
“...What choice do we have?
You can’t predict what’ll happen next inside a Gate.”
“That’s why I hate Gates.
With people, you can more or less figure out what the bastard is thinking.
But with this fucked-up place, you can’t.”
Won Myunghoon answered in a low voice and looked around.
Everywhere he looked, there was nothing but grass, trees, and strange insects.
He wanted to return to the forest of skyscrapers as soon as possible.
“Let’s get started soon.
Something bigger and stronger than a Green Wyvern needs to show up.”
“So the surviving witnesses can testify?”
“You’re one smart bastard.
I tell you one thing, and you figure out ten.”
A smile formed on Won Myunghoon’s lips.

paragraphs: Bean sprout soup might not look like much, but it contains more ingredients than you’d think.
In that sense, The Black Wyvern’s Nest was like bean sprout soup.
This vast A-Rank Gate was home to more than just Wyverns. All kinds of monsters lived here, like the ingredients that went into bean sprout soup.
—Kweeeek!
At the faint sound of a pig squealing in the distance, I muttered, “...Does bean sprout soup have pork in it?”
Won Myunghoon, who was walking beside me, turned his head.
“Hm? Why are you suddenly talking about pork?”
“It’s nothing. I thought there might be a monster nearby.”
“A monster?”
Won Myunghoon stopped and listened for a moment.
“I don’t hear anything.”
“Uh, well...”
How was I supposed to explain this? As I pondered what to say, Won Myunghoon smiled.
“Haha, you must be tense. Don’t get scared just because this is an A-Rank Gate. Relax.”
“I definitely heard something...”
“You must have imagined it. If there’d been a sound like that, I would’ve noticed it first.”
Faced with his confident tone and smile, I kept my mouth shut.
Won Myunghoon was a famous star, but his reputation as a Hunter was considerable too.
Being a ranker meant placing among the top one hundred out of the tens of thousands of Hunters in Korea.
Compared to him, I was still just a rookie who had only recently begun to stand out.
On the surface, anyway.
There probably wasn’t anyone else in the entire world with as many secrets as I had.
But people saw only what was in front of them and heard only what they wanted to hear.
I swallowed the words that had risen to my throat and nodded.
“I guess I imagined it.”
“That happens. It’s good to stay alert, but don’t worry too much. We’re using detection magic as we go, anyway.”
I stared at Won Myunghoon as he gave my shoulder a knowing pat.
Watching him had left me with a complicated feeling for a while now. How should I put it?
Was this really all there was to him?
A few hours earlier, while watching Won Myunghoon fight the Green Wyvern, I had realized two things.
First, Wyverns weren’t as strong as I’d expected. And second—
Neither is Myunghoon hyung.
He was strong. There was no doubt about that. He could wield Aura, and he had once been skilled enough to become a ranker.
By Murim standards, you could reasonably call him a Peak master.
But that was as far as it went. No—if what Won Myunghoon had shown was the full extent of his ability, he was actually inferior to a Peak master from the Murim.
He doesn’t know how to use his strength properly.
Was it because the environments were different?
Unlike the modern world, the Murim was a brutal place where people had to survive with nothing but a weapon in their hands.
In a world where the sword was closer than the law, martial arts had inevitably been developed to the extreme.
Modern Hunters, on the other hand, focus on raids. And they have magic.
Martial artists constantly honed themselves within the vast discipline of martial arts, while Hunters divided up their roles and pursued maximum efficiency within them.
Neither approach was inherently right or wrong, but one thing was certain.
When it comes to individual combat ability, Hunters are no match for martial artists.
If what he had shown so far was everything he could do, Won Myunghoon was no exception.
The fact that he could wield Aura made no difference.
I really have grown stronger.
It had only been a few months.
Yet I had grown enough to judge an A-Rank Hunter who had been my idol for years.
I’m happy about it, but it’s bittersweet too.
I was still gazing at Won Myunghoon with mixed feelings when—
—Kweeeek!
—Chweek!
The second set of cries was louder and clearer than the first.
Won Myunghoon finally noticed them too. He turned his head and began searching for their source.
“Where the hell did that come from...?”
I pulled the spear from my back and answered, “Five o’clock. About thirty jang away—or rather, a hundred meters.”
“Huh?”
“There are quite a few of them. You should start preparing for the raid.”
“G-Get ready?”
“Yes. Sounds like forty or fifty.”
“What are you—”
Won Myunghoon couldn’t finish.
We had spotted a group of more than forty Orcs approaching through the dense undergrowth.
“Forty-seven. Should I take care of them?”
“Hyung?”
At my call, Won Myunghoon jolted as if waking from sleep.
“Uh, huh?”
“Should I take care of them?”
“...By yourself?”
“Yes. I haven’t warmed up yet.”
“R-right. Do whatever you want.”
“If any of them try to run, please deal with them.”
I finished speaking, swung the spear shaft around a few times, and walked toward them.
It was an ordinary iron spear of the sort you could find anywhere, without a single magical enchantment.
If I use enchanted Equipment for no reason, I’ll have trouble adapting in the Murim.
Magic was astonishingly convenient and useful.
It might help me right away, but in the long run, relying on it would do more harm than good.
I needed to improve my fundamental skills instead of depending on Equipment if I wanted to handle any crisis that came my way.
If I take down all of them, maybe I’ll level up once.
With that happy thought, I kicked off the ground. The wind split around me, whipping through my hair.
Whoooosh!
Whoosh! Slice! Thud-thud-thud!
The spearhead sliced cleanly through an Orc’s throat.
Before its knees even touched the ground, the head of the Orc beside it exploded.
Then another. Two more. Three after that...
Every time a silver streak carved through the air, blood and death followed.
He tore through their ranks unhindered.
Team Leader 1 let out an involuntary gasp, then hurriedly closed his mouth. Won Myunghoon was glaring at him with murder in his eyes.
“Uh, Guild Master. I didn’t mean—”
“You bastard. Is this really the time to stand around enjoying the show?”
“I’m sorry. It just slipped out...”
Team Leader 1 cautiously studied Won Myunghoon’s expression before continuing.
“No, but he really is good, isn’t he?”
“...What do you mean, good?”
“Just look at how he moves. He’s no ordinary A-Rank rookie.”

“He doesn’t seem to be wearing a single piece of magical Equipment, either. You have to give him credit just for having the guts to charge fifty Orcs alone. If someone told me to do that... honestly, I wouldn’t be confident.”
Won Myunghoon licked his lips, his face tight with irritation.
He couldn’t deny anything Team Leader 1 had said. Every last word of it was true.
The longer he watched Jin Taekyung, the more bewildered he became.
What the hell is that guy?
Orcs might be treated like punching bags in fantasy novels, but they were by no means easy monsters.
There were many different species of Orcs and dozens of confirmed tribes. Judging by the crude armor these ones wore, they were B-Rank Orc Warriors.
And yet Jin Taekyung was overwhelming them.
He’s taking on fifty Orc Warriors alone? A brat who only just awakened as an A-Rank?
Won Myunghoon had already investigated him thoroughly.
Jin Taekyung had been a bottom-tier Hunter branded as defective, someone who had started as an F-Rank and was certain to die as an F-Rank.
How could a man who had spent his time fighting goblins in tiny F-Rank Gates do this?
“Guild Master. Guild Master?”
Won Myunghoon snapped out of his thoughts and answered dryly.
“What?”
“Didn’t you hear me? I’ve been asking whether you noticed anything suspicious. You’ve been beside him this whole time.”
“Suspicious?”
“Yes. It’s strange. That Jin Taekyung bastard definitely has something going on.”
After a brief silence, Won Myunghoon gave Team Leader 1 a quick account of what had just happened.
“He knew the Orcs were coming?”
“Keep your voice down. We’re not the only ones here.”

Team Leader 1 glanced behind him. After checking the Peace Guild members watching the battle with peaceful expressions, as if they had come out for a picnic, he whispered in a voice barely louder than an ant.
“My God. How did that bastard know? Do you have any idea?”
“It must have been detection magic. It had to be detection magic.”
“What if it wasn’t detection magic?”
“What?”
Team Leader 1 swallowed hard.
“Guild Master, what if—and this really is just a one-in-a-million possibility...”
“Shut your mouth. I’m not listening to that bullshit.”
“W-we can’t rule it out.”
A dangerous light flashed in Won Myunghoon’s eyes.
“Fuck... Are you saying that bastard Jin Taekyung is stronger than me? Is that what you’re trying to say?”
Overwhelmed by his murderous aura, Team Leader 1 hastily lowered his head.
But Won Myunghoon’s low growl continued to bore into his ears.
“You think I learned Aura by playing Go-Stop? I took in a bastard who had nothing and raised him, and now you think I’m a joke? Does the title of ranker look like a fucking joke to you?”
“N-no, sir.”
At least get your facts straight. When we first met, you and I were about the same. And you only became a ranker because of the fame you built in the entertainment industry and all that lobbying.
Team Leader 1 swallowed the words threatening to spill out.
They had been together for well over ten years. Too much had happened between them to turn back now.
Sensing his resentment, Won Myunghoon glared at him like a venomous snake.
“Our Jonghun’s all grown up.”
Calling him by name rather than title meant something very different.
Several Star Guild members sensed the tension and moved around the two men with practiced ease, blocking them from outsiders’ view.
“Hey, Kim Jonghun.”
Tap, tap.
Won Myunghoon lightly patted Team Leader 1’s cheek and muttered in a voice drier than sand, “Get a grip. If you make a mistake here, we’re all fucked.”
“...Yes, sir.”
“Send a few agile guys to find the boss monster. If that doesn’t work, drag over a few Wyverns that look strong enough.”
“Understood.”
The moment Team Leader 1 answered with a cowed expression, cheers erupted from somewhere.
A middle-aged man with a bandit’s beard was jumping up and down like a live fish.
“Taekyung! You bastard! You magnificent bastard!”
The battle was finally over.
It had taken only about fifteen minutes to wipe out nearly fifty B-Rank Orc Warriors.
Amid the dozens of corpses strewn across the ground, a handsome young man with bold features grinned.
“Ah, now I’m finally warmed up. Myunghoon hyung, I did well, right?”
Won Myunghoon hurriedly turned away to hide the hideous scowl that had twisted his face.
Goddammit...!
Every time he looked at Jin Taekyung, his head burned and his stomach churned.
The bastard had only attracted the media’s attention through sheer luck. He had been handed such a golden opportunity, yet he neither knew how to use his fame nor had any intention of doing so.
To Won Myunghoon, it was all an act—and the source of his disgust.
You’re going to spend your whole life running Gates until you drop dead, yet you don’t even know your place and still have the nerve to reject my offer?
If Jin Taekyung had wanted to become a star Hunter under another major entertainment agency, Won Myunghoon wouldn’t have been this angry.
But Taekyung had rejected him without the slightest hesitation. He had chosen the Peace Guild, little more than a mom-and-pop operation.
Fucking idiot.
He would regret it.
Won Myunghoon muttered those words inwardly and signaled Team Leader 1 with his eyes.
“Great job! Great job, you bastard!”
Thump! Thump!
Im Kkeokjeong snorted excitedly as he pounded me on the shoulder.
“Wow! Fifty Orc Warriors! You really are the greatest Hunter!”
“Calm down.”
“Your movement, your spearmanship, your soul... Just what I’d expect from an A-Rank Hunter. You turned this Gate upside down!”
Why was “soul” in there? And what exactly had I turned upside down?
Unlike me, who was dumbfounded, Im Kkeokjeong showed no sign of calming down.
“I knew you’d become someone like this. Ahem.”
“...You aren’t crying, are you?”
Unable to continue, Im Kkeokjeong’s lips trembled, and he turned his head away.
“Who’s crying? I just... I was remembering the old days.”
“Uncle.”
“Do you remember that time two years ago when we were ambushed in an E-Rank Gate?”
“When...? Oh, right.”
“Yeah. That bastard of a Team Leader was the first to run, and I thought we were all going to die. But you stayed at the rear until the very end and protected the wounded.”
“Was Uncle one of them?”
Im Kkeokjeong nodded, his face full of emotion.
As far as I remembered, I had saved about seven people that day. It wasn’t until now that I learned Im Kkeokjeong had been one of them.
Was that why he recommended me to Team Leader Choi?
“You still remember that?”
“I might forget a wrong done to me, but I’ll never forget a debt for as long as I live.”
“Forget it. It’s all in the past.”
“Anyway, I’m glad to see you doing so well, Taekyung. No matter how hard I try, I’ll never be more than a D-Rank Hunter... but just remember that I’ll always be rooting for you.”
I knew.
It wasn’t just Im Kkeokjeong. The other Guild members had always cared about me too.
I guess I’m lucky when it comes to people.
I looked warmly at the Guild members.
First was Team Leader Choi, our main source of funding.
“Mr. Jin Taekyung.”
“Yes, Team Leader.”
“You truly are remarkable.”
“It was nothing.”
“Your discerning eye is remarkable.”
“That look in your eyes just now must mean you recognized this Frozen Eye around my neck.”
Team Leader Choi smiled proudly and pulled off the necklace.
When did he even put that on? I’d never seen it before today.
“Russia’s foremost jewelry maker, Vladimir Stalin, designed it...”
Fuck. Give me back my touching moment.
I was sighing at his maddening consistency when—
“Hm?”
Team Leader Choi suddenly froze and pointed at Im Kkeokjeong’s neck.
“Is that perhaps Yeti’s Necklace?”
Startled by his greedy stare, Im Kkeokjeong nodded.
“Huh? Uh, yeah.”
“That’s an item that rarely even appears on secondhand markets... Where did you get it?”
“T-this?”
He looked ready to rip off the necklace along with Im Kkeokjeong’s neck.
Sensing a threat to his life, the middle-aged man hurriedly took it off and handed it to me.
“It’s not mine. Taekyung lent it to me.”
“Mr. Jin Taekyung did?”
I nodded.
“I lent it to him. I borrowed it from Myunghoon hyung, though.”
“I see. If you don’t mind, may I examine it for a moment?”
“Well, I don’t see any harm in looking.”
Just as I was about to hand him Yeti’s Necklace, curiosity struck me.
Is this thing really that expensive?
Come to think of it, I haven’t even had it appraised yet.
It wasn’t particularly useful to me, but there was no harm in finding out exactly what it did.
Without giving it much thought, I muttered inwardly.
Item Appraisal.
Ding.

The other Guild members had always cared about me too.
I guess I’m lucky when it comes to people.
I looked warmly at the Guild members.
First was Team Leader Choi, our main source of funding.
“Mr.
Jin Taekyung.”
“Yes, Team Leader.”
“You truly are remarkable.”
“It was nothing.”
“Your discerning eye is remarkable.”
“That look in your eyes just now must mean you recognized this Frozen Eye around my neck.”
Team Leader Choi smiled proudly and pulled off the necklace.
When did he even put that on?
I’d never seen it before today.
“Russia’s foremost jewelry maker, Vladimir Stalin, designed it...”
Fuck.
Give me back my touching moment.
I was sighing at his maddening consistency when—
“Hm?”
Team Leader Choi suddenly froze and pointed at Im Kkeokjeong’s neck.
“Is that perhaps Yeti’s Necklace?”
Startled by his greedy stare, Im Kkeokjeong nodded.
“Huh?
Uh, yeah.”
“That’s an item that rarely even appears on secondhand markets...
Where did you get it?”
“T-this?”
He looked ready to rip off the necklace along with Im Kkeokjeong’s neck.
Sensing a threat to his life, the middle-aged man hurriedly took it off and handed it to me.
“It’s not mine.
Taekyung lent it to me.”
“Mr.
Jin Taekyung did?”
I nodded.
“I lent it to him.
I borrowed it from Myunghoon hyung, though.”
“I see.
If you don’t mind, may I examine it for a moment?”
“Well, I don’t see any harm in looking.”
Just as I was about to hand him Yeti’s Necklace, curiosity struck me.
Is this thing really that expensive?
Come to think of it, I haven’t even had it appraised yet.
It wasn’t particularly useful to me, but there was no harm in finding out exactly what it did.
Without giving it much thought, I muttered inwardly.
Item Appraisal.
Ding.

chapters.title: Chapter 218
paragraphs: “This is...”
After examining Yeti’s Necklace for a long moment, Team Leader Choi’s eyelids began to tremble.
“I’m angry.”
He rarely showed his emotions this openly.
Im Kkeokjeong, who had been squatting quietly, asked with intense curiosity,
“Team Leader Choi, what’s wrong? Is there a problem?”
“There is. A very serious problem.”
Team Leader Choi bit down hard on his lip and continued.
“The supply of this beautiful product is far too limited. That is the greatest problem of all—one that deserves condemnation from people around the world.”
“Just look at it. The artistry of this icicle design! The magical properties that preserve the very chill of the snowy plains!”
Like a North Korean TV announcer passionately praising the Supreme Leader—no, the necklace—Team Leader Choi whipped his head toward me.
“What do you think, Mr. Jin Taekyung?”
“Me?”
Where should I start? How should I put it? What was I even supposed to say?
My hesitation was brief. A voice came from my mouth, calm and gentle enough to surprise even me.
“I’m angry too.”
“What’s wrong?”
“No, it’s nothing.”
Team Leader Choi gave me a strange look before continuing.
“You just seem a little... unfamiliar somehow.”
“Do I?”
I rubbed my chin. The stubble beginning to poke through felt rough against my fingers. Even the sensation felt unfamiliar, almost like touching someone else’s skin.
“Is it because I haven’t shaved?”
“Mr. Jin Taekyung, could it be...”
Just as Team Leader Choi was about to say something, Won Myunghoon approached with a genial smile.
“Wow, that was incredible. Taekyung, you really can fight.”
“...You think so?”
“Your spearmanship was completely different from the manual I wrote. Did you learn it at the training center?”
“No. I just picked up a few things here and there.”
“Here and there? That was way beyond anything you could pick up casually. At this rate, you might catch up to me in a few years. Haha.”
I silently raised the corners of my mouth.
When nobody joined in, his laughter slowly died away. It should have been awkward, but Won Myunghoon changed the subject without missing a beat.
The entire sequence was polished and seamless, like a scene from a TV drama.
“So, what were you doing?”
His mouth was asking the question, but his eyes were already busy taking stock of the situation. His gaze flicked across Yeti’s Necklace in Team Leader Choi’s hand.
“We were looking at the necklace you lent me. Team Leader Choi is really interested in this kind of thing.”
“Team Leader Choi is? Well, I suppose that makes sense. He did seem like the type.”
If Won Myunghoon wrapped himself from head to toe in flashy luxury brands, Team Leader Choi was the exact opposite.
Everything he wore was still expensive, but how should I put it? Refined and understated. Either way, anyone who saw how he normally dressed could tell he had an eye for such things.
But Won Myunghoon’s attention lay elsewhere.
“So, what did you think after seeing it in person?”
“It’s much better in person. If you ever decide to sell it, please contact me.”
“I’m afraid that won’t happen. I treasure it a great deal.”
Something he treasures...
I mulled over his words, then abruptly spoke.
“It must be important.”
“Of course. Very important.”
“I see.”
I held Yeti’s Necklace out to Won Myunghoon.
“I’ll give it back now.”
“Hm?”
“You said it was important to you, hyung. And judging by what Team Leader Choi said, it sounds extremely expensive too.”
“Aren’t you going to take it?”
The necklace swayed in my hand with a metallic clatter.
A brief silence passed. Won Myunghoon gazed at me, and a faint smile appeared on his lips.
“Taekyung.”
“Yes.”
“Your hyung values the bonds between people more than material things.”
“The bonds between people.”
“That’s right. The same goes for the Guild members who came with us today. They stayed by my side through the hardest time of my life.”
“You mean eight years ago?”
“...Well, yes. Anyway, what I’m trying to say is, don’t worry about it too much. What’s so precious about a necklace like that? Right?”
Won Myunghoon patted my shoulder with his broad palm. Unlike mine, his palm was soft, and his fingernails were long.
A thought suddenly occurred to me.
Maybe this person standing in front of me isn’t the person I knew.
“Actually, the necklace is a gift.”
“A gift?”
“Yeah. A gift from your hyung to you.”
Every time Won Myunghoon leaned closer, the strong scent of his cologne washed over me.
“So don’t give it to anyone else. Got it?”
“Taekyung?”
I put the necklace around my neck as I answered.
“Yes. I won’t let anyone else touch it.”
Ding.
System You have equipped Yeti’s Necklace. - The wind of the snowfield flows from the necklace.
As the wind of the snowfield wrapped around my entire body, I recalled the Item Window I had seen just five minutes earlier.

System Item Window Yeti’s Necklace Type: Accessory Grade: Peak Restriction: None Description: A necklace that only an exceptionally skilled Yeti warrior may possess. In truth, however, it is a shackle proving that its wearer was once enslaved by the dragonkin and raised as livestock for food. Anyone who possesses this item becomes a target of dragonkin monsters, regardless of species. Effect: Wind of the Snowfield effect activated.
So I’m a target.
It was hardly a pleasant word.
In more ways than one.
Time passed slowly inside the Gate.

After half a day of travel, we finally left the jungle and entered the wasteland. Yet the only monsters we had encountered so far were the Green Wyvern that had appeared at the beginning, the pack of Orcs I had dealt with, and the Trolls the others were fighting now.
—Gwoooor!
The Troll stood about a head taller than an adult man and had an abnormally large head.
Trolls were monsters with extraordinary regenerative abilities. That was also why they cropped up everywhere as the main ingredient in healing potions.
They could regrow severed arms and legs in a matter of seconds, which naturally made them difficult opponents.
But the Star Guild members were seasoned veterans in their own right.
“The head! Aim for the head!”
“Fire magic!”
Sshhk! Fwoooosh!
In the early days of the Great Cataclysm, Trolls had earned a fearsome reputation as immortal monsters, but their weaknesses had soon been exposed.
The head and the heart. And magic on top of that.
Unless it was an undead monster, death after the cessation of breathing was only natural.
Trolls possessed enough terrifying regenerative power to restore even their heads and hearts, but that didn’t make them truly immortal.
Freeze them with ice or sear them with flames before they could regenerate, and there was little they could do.
“Damage dealers, get in there and carve it up!”
“Mages, stand by!”
Sshh-shh-shhk! Thwack!
—Graaaar!
The Troll toppled backward after losing an arm and a leg.
A moment later, the keen axe blade of a halberd cleaved through the thick fat and muscle of its neck.
Thud! Sshhk!
The Troll’s body flailed, now empty above the shoulders. Soon, new flesh began to writhe and swell across the cut surface.
In a little over a minute, it would have a new neck.
Of course, the Star Guild members had no intention of waiting that long.
“Burn it!”
Fwoooosh! Ssssss!
Bone-chilling cold and skin-scorching flames struck the body.
Unable to regenerate, the Troll shuddered violently once, then fell still.
“Unit Three clear!”
“Help over here! This one’s regenerating!”
With three Hunters assigned to each Troll, the battle ended quickly.
Amid the stench of burning flesh and fat, Won Myunghoon watched from a dozen or so meters away and muttered under his breath.
His voice was so quiet that nobody could make it out over the noise of battle, but to me, it sounded as clear as if he were speaking right beside me.
“Idiots had to stink up the place. I told them to freeze them whenever possible.”
“Hah.”
I barely managed to suppress the hollow laugh trying to escape.
Someone once said that life was a tragedy up close and a comedy from a distance.
But a battle against monsters was a tragedy no matter where you watched it from.
When you could lose your life in an instant, the smell of burning Troll flesh was nothing.
It’s a hundred times better than lying behind a folding screen, smelling your own funeral incense.
But to Won Myunghoon, it was someone else’s problem.
He was frowning and cursing under his breath when he suddenly sensed my gaze and turned toward me.
“Oh, Taekyung.”
His voice was warm, and his forehead had smoothed out as if nothing had happened.
Everything about him was natural.
That only made it feel even more unnatural.
“What is it? Do you have something to say?”
For some reason, it sounded like he was really asking, Did you hear everything I said?
I kept my face blank and answered casually.
“Yes.”
“Really? What is it?”
“I feel a little nauseous. I was fine at first, but... I’ve felt strange ever since we entered the Gate. I even tried healing magic, but it didn’t help much.”
“Ah. That.”
Won Myunghoon let out a quiet laugh.
“It’s because this is your first A-Rank Gate. The amount of magical power distributed inside a Gate is on an entirely different level.”
“Oh, I see.”
“Beginners are all like that. I’m used to it by now.”
I let out an exclamation as if I were hearing this for the first time, even though I already knew everything.
“So I’ll get used to it next time too, right?”
“Next time?”
The corners of Won Myunghoon’s mouth twitched before he nodded.
“That’s right. You’ll be much more used to it next time.”
“I hope I can come with you again then, hyung.”
“Well, I don’t know when I’ll have time. My schedule is packed.”
“You don’t even have time for raids?”
“You may not know this yet, Taekyung, but Guild Masters like me are always busy. We have to coordinate the entire Guild.”
“Ah.”
“It’s the difference between a musician and a conductor. You know what a maestro is, right?”
As Won Myunghoon mimed waving a conductor’s baton, I abruptly asked, “Then did you go to the department store for a Guild-related meeting?”
“Hm?”
“I saw an article about it online. What was the headline again? Ah, I remember.”
Won Myunghoon suddenly lost his words. Watching him, I continued clearly,
“Something like Rising Star Hunter Won Myunghoon Sweeps Up Luxury Goods.”
“Was there an article like that?”
“It was on a Hunter community site for a little while. It got deleted after five minutes.”
“R-really? Are you sure you didn’t misread it?”
“Yes. There’s a Rice Weevil who doesn’t study these days and does nothing but scour the Internet. He lets me know the moment an article appears.”
A deep dimple formed in Won Myunghoon’s handsome face. But this wasn’t the bright smile I remembered seeing on television.
“That can’t be right.”
“Isn’t it?”
“Of course not. I do like shopping, but I’m not that bad. At most, I might go once a month.”
“I heard pictures were uploaded too.”

“You know Dispass, right? The site that specializes in digging up dirt on celebrities. They even interviewed someone from the department store. Apparently, you’re a VVIP who visits five times a week.”
Won Myunghoon licked his dry lips. The dimple had vanished without a trace.
“Taekyung. You don’t actually believe that, do you?”
“Come on, it must be a rumor sheet. You’re busy coordinating the Guild schedule, hyung. Maestro.”
“...Yes, Maestro.”
I vigorously mimed waving a conductor’s baton while Won Myunghoon stared at me with dry eyes.
That was when—
“Hyung! No, CEO!”
The shout rang out across the endless wasteland of dirt, sand, and winding rocky hills. It had come from Star Guild’s Team Leader 1.
He had gone scouting in search of the Wyvern that had been nowhere in sight, and now he was back.
But unlike when he had set out at a leisurely pace, he was sprinting toward us like a madman, his face deathly pale.
“What happened? Where are the others?”
At Won Myunghoon’s question, Team Leader 1 stammered.
“Th-that, th-that...”
I didn’t need to hear the rest.
Seven people had left, but only one had returned. The drops of blood splashed across his face and armor turned my guess into certainty.
“You bastard. Spit it out!”
Team Leader 1 flinched at the thunderous roar.
“We found the Wyvern. We found it.”
“The Wyvern? How many?”
“O-one.”
“What? One?”
An A-Rank Hunter and six B-Rank Hunters made a formation more than capable of dealing with a single Wyvern.
And yet six people had died, while one had fled back alone.
“Is that supposed to be an explanation? Are you messing with me?”
“They’re all dead. We approached while using concealment magic, but... it noticed us.”
“What kind of bullshit is that? How could a Wyvern see through concealment magic?”
Click. Clack-clack.
His teeth chattering from fear, Team Leader 1 finally forced out a single word.
“A-A Named Monster.”
“It’s definitely a Named Monster. This place... it’s a Mutated Gate.”
An A-Rank Mutated Gate.
And a Named Monster.
There was no one among us who didn’t understand what those two words meant.
Amid the suffocating silence, someone muttered in a voice barely loud enough to hear.
“Fuck...”

chapters.title: Chapter 219
paragraphs: From the early days of the Great Cataclysm to the present, humanity had drawn on countless experiences of death and destruction to classify monsters and establish a hierarchy among them.
Accordingly, the Grade of each Gate was determined by the Grade of the monsters inhabiting it.
However...
There are exceptions to every rule.
Mutated Gates were one such exception. They existed outside the boundaries humanity had established. They were, in every sense of the word, mutations.
Gates were already an enigma to humanity, and now another variable had entered the equation.
The worst kind.
A D-Rank monster could appear in an F-Rank Gate. A B-Rank monster could appear in a D-Rank Gate.
That alone was the stuff of nightmares, but an even greater problem remained.
Rare Monsters.
As if running into an unexpected higher-level monster wasn’t bad enough, every one of those creatures possessed strength that surpassed that of other monsters of the same Grade.
That was when the term Rare Monster was first coined.
Before long, someone raised another question.
Then what about the Rare Monsters that appear in A-Rank Mutated Gates? Aren’t they too strong to be considered the same Grade?
For Hunters, A-Rank was the highest level attainable through a single awakening.
Those acknowledged as particularly strong even among A-Rank Hunters received the prestigious Title of ranker.
The same issue applied to monsters. After endless debate within the relevant academic circles, a new term was born.
Named Monster.
True monstrosities that had transcended the limits of A-Rank.
Team Leader 1, the only one to return alive, had said that such a Named Monster was here.
Right where we stood, in the Wyvern’s Nest.
“Bullshit!”
Won Myunghoon seized Team Leader 1 by the collar with a furious shout.
“A Named Monster? There’s no way something like that could be here.”
“I-I’m telling the truth. I saw it clearly with my own eyes.”
Team Leader 1 continued in a trembling voice.
“It was several times larger than an ordinary Wyvern. I could hardly believe it even while I was looking right at it.”
“Shut up!”
But the terror the Named Monster had instilled in Team Leader 1 was beyond anything I could have imagined.
The title of A-Rank Hunter seemed wasted on him. He was as terrified as a seven-year-old child.
“That thing is on a completely different level from any Wyvern we’ve faced before. We need to run. Right now.”
“Kim Jonghun, you son of a...”
Grind.
Won Myunghoon ground his teeth, but that was all he did.

He might have fallen short of my expectations in every possible way, but he was still an A-Rank Hunter who had once risen to the ranks of the rankers. There was no way he didn’t understand what everyone else here already knew.
Won Myunghoon was berating Team Leader 1 merely to hide his own fear.
There must have been signs that this was a Mutated Gate.
I knew them well. I had experienced them myself three years ago.
Strangely few monsters. And far more Magic Gems than the number of defeated monsters should have yielded.
I hadn’t known about the latter. The Star Guild was responsible for handling the spoils, and although this was a joint raid, Won Myunghoon was still the commander with final say over everything.
And that commander just shit the bed.
This was no minor error in judgment.
The creature stalking us somewhere in the wasteland wasn’t an ordinary Wyvern. It was a Named Monster.
“Fucking hell...”
As Won Myunghoon spat out the curse, Team Leader Choi spoke.
“Calm down. Our priority right now should be to withdraw immediately.”
“Calm down? Do I look like I can calm down in a situation like this?”
“I’m telling you to compose yourself and face reality.”
Team Leader Choi continued in the same measured voice.
“Fortunately, it isn’t too late. If we turn back and retrace our route as quickly as possible, we can reach the jungle within an hour. But if we encounter that thing out here in the wasteland...”
“You think I don’t know that? Stop meddling.”
The cheerful, courteous gentleman was gone. Team Leader Choi’s gaze cooled at Won Myunghoon’s irritable response.
“That’s unfortunate. I didn’t expect you to take it that way.”

“Unfortunate? Just because we’re cooperating, you seem to think we’re really equals or something... Fuck, there’s no point in talking. Anyway, stop telling me what to do. I’m already in a shitty mood.”
They said a crisis revealed a person’s true nature.
If that was true, this was all there was to Won Myunghoon. The bitter part was knowing I had once idolized someone like him.
Won Myunghoon turned to the Guild members, his face tense with anxiety.
“Take only the Magic Gems. We’re heading back to the Gate entrance as fast as possible.”
There were two ways out of a Gate: the entrance we had used to come in, and the exit that opened once the boss monster was killed.
Under the circumstances, the former was obviously the right choice.
“Yes, sir.”
The preparations were completed quickly. The only problem was Team Leader 1, who remained deathly pale.
“What’s wrong with that guy?”
Butler Kim, who had stayed one step behind me and kept quiet the entire time, answered my mutter.
“He’s been exposed to a monster’s Fear.”
“An A-Rank Hunter?”
“The opponent is a Named Monster.”
“Oh.”
“And a Grade is merely a measure of strength. It has nothing to do with how strong someone’s mental fortitude is.”
Even so, an A-Rank Hunter had succumbed to Fear.
That left two possibilities. Either Team Leader 1 was weak-willed to begin with, or the Named Monster was simply that powerful.
Personally, I’d prefer the former.
With that thought, I approached Team Leader 1. I only meant to help him up, but he recoiled as if he’d been burned.
“It’s okay. I’m not trying to hurt you. You know me, right?”
“J-Jin Taekyung.”
“You’re still lucid, at least. Now pull yourself together and get up. Unless you’d rather keep sitting there until you become its prey.”
“Gah!”
Sometimes it was better to stoke someone’s fear than inspire courage.
The word prey sent Team Leader 1 shooting to his feet. He glanced around anxiously.
“Th-that thing...?”
“It isn’t here. More importantly, how did you make it back alive?”
I had wanted to ask him that for a while. No one else had thought to once the words Named Monster came out.
Team Leader 1 chewed on his lip.
“I had no choice.”
“...I see.”
He had run away. He had abandoned his team members.
But I didn’t condemn him. Not because I understood, but because I didn’t think I had the right.
Someone else can curse him out, but not me.
Whether he knew what I was thinking or not, Team Leader 1 began rambling incoherently.
“We were approaching carefully, but it saw us. Then it spread its wings—its black wings—wide...”
“Black wings?”
“Y-yes. It was black all over, from its head to the tip of its tail.”
A memory suddenly surfaced.
The screams that had filled the cave. Those enormous wings.
The Wyvern I had encountered back then had also been entirely black.
“A Black Wyvern.”
“No, it was different. It was several times larger and stronger than the Black Wyverns we’ve seen so far. That thing... it’s a real monster.”
Then it couldn’t have been the same creature I’d encountered three years ago.

After the Sangdong Station Mutated Gate incident, I had been subjected to countless investigations. The team dispatched to investigate the truth behind the incident had concluded that the creature didn’t fall far outside the normal range for a Black Wyvern.
Then where is it now?
Monsters inside Gates respawned at regular intervals. By the time the investigators arrived, it had already disappeared.
Whenever I drank, I sometimes found myself wondering.
Where is it now? Did another Hunter kill it? If it’s still alive, will I ever get the chance to take revenge?
Now it’s possible.
As long as we were both alive, the day would eventually come when we met again.
I had left it with an indelible memory, and it had done the same to me.
But apparently, that day wasn’t today.
“Mr. Jin Taekyung.”
“Taekyung!”
The Guild members had finished preparing and were waiting for me. I had just started toward the formation when—
“One eye.”
The single word that suddenly came from Team Leader 1’s mouth made my body freeze.
I slowly turned around. Team Leader 1 pointed to one of his own eyes with a trembling hand.
“What did you just say?”
“That’s right. One of its eyes was ruined. Like something had stabbed it...”
A current ran down my spine. My mind went blank, and my fist clenched on its own.
Three years ago, I had charged at that creature prepared to die.
I had gathered every last ounce of strength and unleashed One Annihilation—no, Stab with All My Strength. The spearhead had buried itself squarely in its eye.
That had been my final act of defiance, and the only mark I’d managed to leave on it.
It’s that bastard.
I didn’t stop to wonder how an ordinary Black Wyvern had become a Named Monster.
Every hair standing on end across my skin bore witness, and my pounding heart served as both prosecutor and judge.
Everything that made me who I was cried out with one voice.
The unidentified Named Monster Team Leader 1 had described was the very creature that had left me with an indelible nightmare three years ago.
We finally meet again.
I didn’t know what to call this feeling.
Fear? Joy?
My whole body trembled with an emotion I couldn’t name.
My senses were drawn tighter and sharper than ever when the thick scent of blood drifted into them.
—Kyaaaaaaaah!
I raised my head at the roar echoing from the distance.
On the horizon of the wasteland beneath the setting sun, a pair of pitch-black wings was flying toward us.
Goddammit. Goddammit. Goddammit!
The same curses kept replaying endlessly in Won Myunghoon’s mind.
His plan was as good as ruined. Now he even had to worry about getting out alive.
A Named Monster.
This was as serious as the situation eight years ago—no, it was even worse.
Won Myunghoon had hurried the Guild members through their preparations and was just about to order them to move out when—
“It’s coming.”
The low voice piercing his ears made his heart plummet.
All the more so because it belonged to Jin Taekyung.
“W-what do you mean?”
“Prepare for battle. Or run for your life.”
“I’m asking what the hell you mean!”
“What else could I mean?”
There was something unfamiliar about Jin Taekyung’s dark, steady gaze.
The man before Won Myunghoon now was neither his rabid fan nor the foolish kid in his twenties who had grinned at him like an idiot.
What is this feeling?
As Won Myunghoon flinched, a dry voice slipped between Jin Taekyung’s lips.
“Take everyone with you. I still have the necklace.”
“...What?”
What the hell was this bastard talking about?
As Won Myunghoon stared at him in confusion, one corner of Jin Taekyung’s mouth curled upward.
“Why are you so surprised? Did you think I wouldn’t know?”
“You—you bastard.”
“Myunghoon hyung. No, Mr. Won Myunghoon.”
Won Myunghoon froze. Not from humiliation, but from the crushing pressure bearing down on him.
A pressure unlike anything he had felt from Jin Taekyung before was pouring off him.
“Whatever you did or planned to do, I’ll let everything up to this point slide. But...”
Beneath the tangled hair falling over his face, his darkened eyes gleamed.
“Never bare your teeth at me again.”
“I’m done. Get lost.”
Won Myunghoon’s lips moved, but no words came out.
He stared at Jin Taekyung with an unreadable look, then spun around.
He could feel the Peace Guild members’ gazes boring into the back of his head. Only now had they realized something had been going on.
Fucking idiots. How dare they...
But it didn’t matter.
Jin Taekyung and those ragtag Guild members would all be dead soon anyway.
A short while later, as Won Myunghoon and the Star Guild members ran with all their might, a roar echoed from far away.

chapters.title: Chapter 220
paragraphs: Won Myunghoon left. Remembering how he had ground his teeth at my attitude yet hadn’t dared attack drew a quiet laugh from me.
If he had, I would’ve made him regret it.
He was a hyena of a man.
Show him weakness, and he bared his teeth. Show him strength, and he hid them.
Judging by everything I had seen of him, his nature probably had something to do with the incident eight years ago as well.
Consider yourself lucky.
No matter how much a hyena leaped or crawled, it was still a beast.
If it knew when to tuck its tail, all I had to do was scare it off.
I had neither reason nor desire to bloody my hands before it actually sank its teeth into my shoulder—especially when I was about to face a real monster.
—Kyaaaaaaaah!
The black dot drew closer.
A rage-filled roar echoed from the far edge of the horizon.
Just as I had recognized it, it had recognized me.
Yes. You remember me too.
That was enough. I was about to face a half-mad Named Monster, but I felt neither fear nor excitement.
Only one thing bothered me, like a thorn caught in my throat.
“Why didn’t you leave?”
Team Leader Choi stared at me with his arms loosely folded.
Instead of answering, he asked a question of his own.
“Who are you asking?”
“All of you.”
I swept my gaze around. Four people stood against the endless wasteland, with rocks and trees scattered here and there behind them.
Team Leader Choi and Butler Kim. Im Kkeokjeong and Song Song.
Not one of them had left.
“You all know that thing coming toward us is a Named Monster, right?”
“We’re all well aware.”
“Then this should be simple. It’s dangerous, so leave while you still can.”
“Where would we retreat to?”
“Where else? Back to the exit we came through.”
“The Star Guild isn’t exactly an ideal group to flee with—especially after making an enemy of their Guild Master.”
I don’t see it that way.
No one knew it yet, but Butler Kim was an A-Rank mage—and one who had lived through the unprecedented war known as the Great Cataclysm.
The Star Guild might have had the advantage in numbers, but even without me, the others wouldn’t be outmatched if they fought Won Myunghoon’s Guild right now.
“That’s a convenient excuse.”
Team Leader Choi stared at me as I smiled.
“Mr. Jin Taekyung.”
“No.”
I cut him off before he could begin, but Team Leader Choi wasn’t the sort to back down quietly.
“Since you’ve left me stuck here with nowhere to go, I think I’ve earned the right to ask a few questions.”
Damn. He has a point.
I answered reluctantly.
“Fine...but keep it short.”
“That monster coming toward us—is it connected to what happened three years ago?”
I hesitated, then nodded.
“You have no intention of retreating.”
My silence was answer enough.
Team Leader Choi let out a low sigh.
“Mr. Jin Taekyung, you’re facing a Named Monster.”
“That’s news to me. All I see is something I need to kill.”
“You need to think about this rationally.”
“Do I look that unstable right now?”
“That...”
Team Leader Choi fell silent.
I was calmer than I had ever been. My heart might have been hammering like mad, but my mind was running through countless ways to deal with the creature.
“Team Leader Choi.”
“I’ve told you my motto in life a few times before, haven’t I?”
Im Kkeokjeong, who had been watching in silence, answered for him.
“Thin and long.”
“You remember too, Uncle?”
“You were a strange kid. Most young men dream big at least once...but you never did.”
“I’ve never been fond of a turbulent life.”
This time, Butler Kim answered with a smile.
“For someone who feels that way, you seem to have come quite far.”
“That’s why I changed it.”
“Big and long. Is that right?”
“Yes. It’s already too late for me to live small. Since things have turned out this way, I’m going to live as big and as long as I can.”
“Good. If you wish, perhaps...”
I knew what he was about to say.
I quietly shook my head. Butler Kim had a far more important task to handle.
“I’m fine. Protect the others.”
“Understood. Even without being asked, I’ll do what must be done to the best of my ability.”
At Butler Kim’s clear-cut answer, Song Song asked with an incredulous expression,
“You’re going to let him fight a Named Monster alone? Are you all out of your minds? One wrong move and we’ll all die. Every last one of us!”
“Then why haven’t you left, Miss Song?”
“...Good question. Why am I still here?”
I watched her sink into thought, then spoke.
“Miss Song.”
“No.”
“Absolutely not.”
“Hunter Jin Taekyung. Please.”
What was with these reactions?
I had barely gotten her name out, yet Song Song, Team Leader Choi, and Butler Kim had all shut me down without hesitation.
“Taekyung, go for it.”
At least Kkeokjeong hyung was on my side.
I looked at the other three with an aggrieved expression.
“I haven’t even said anything yet.”
Song Song answered,
“That’s why I’m saying no.”
“How do you know what I was going to say?”
“Hmm. A confession?”
My head went numb for a moment.
The back of my skull throbbed as though someone had hit it with a hammer.
“Wait. How did you know?”
“Good grief. How could I not know?”
“W-was it that obvious?”
“Yes. Painfully.”
“Then...”
She shook her head without hesitation.
“I’m sorry. I’m not the sort of person who changes her attitude at the drop of a hat just because someone has money or fame.”
“Oh.”
“To be honest, you’re quite a catch, Mr. Taekyung. But when I like someone, I’m the type to reel him in all at once. I can’t keep a whole pond stocked with men.”
After letting everything out in one breath, she blinked.
“Oh. I wasn’t too harsh on someone who’s about to fight a Named Monster, was I?”
I had been opening and closing my mouth like a goldfish, but a quiet laugh soon escaped me.
“Why are you laughing?”
“No reason. I was just thinking how refreshingly straightforward you are.”
She narrowed her eyes at my answer.
“Hold on. Why are you suddenly speaking casually?”
“You said you’re twenty-seven, right? We’re the same age. We can at least be friends, can’t we?”
“Hmm. There’s no such thing as friendship between a man and a woman.”
“We can worry about that if the time comes.”
When Song Song still hesitated, I added,
“We’re guildmates, after all.”
“...When you put it that way, I can’t exactly refuse.”
I grinned at her.
In the end, I had been rejected cleanly, but I didn’t regret it in the slightest. If anything, I felt strangely calm.
If someone saw me like this and asked whether I had really liked Song Song, the answer was yes. There was no question about that.
But even I couldn’t say for certain what I felt now.
I had simply said what I had kept buried in my heart for so long, and regardless of her answer, I felt relieved.
Maybe that was enough for now.
“Let’s have some soju when this is over.”
“My family motto says boys and girls over seven shouldn’t sit together.”
“I meant all of us.”
“...Oh. Right.”
I turned away with a light step.
At that moment, I sensed an enormous flow of mana behind me. I didn’t need to look to know that Butler Kim was layering magical barriers around the others.
I’m counting on you.
It meant the battle was close at hand. Sure enough, the creature that had been no more than a tiny dot was now close enough for even an ordinary person to see clearly.
“Bastard, you’ve gotten big.”
Its body was easily over fifty meters long, and its wings were larger still.
Black scales covered every inch of it, gleaming in the light of the setting sun.
It had grown at least two or three times larger than when I had last seen it three years ago.
Was that even possible?
I had never heard of anything like it.
But there was no mistaking the creature. Its clouded eye was proof.
Its remaining eye, stained crimson, stared directly at me.
—Kraaaaaaaah!
Whoooosh!
A single roar sent a tremendous gust crashing over the wasteland. Dirt and pebbles flew into the air, filling it with a thick cloud of dust.
When the curtain of dust settled, a massive silhouette stood atop a nearby hill.
It’s huge.
And strong.
With my senses stretched wide, I could feel its rage and power.
It was a monster that had broken free of the bounds of A-Rank.
It possessed the majesty befitting a Named Monster.
“So we finally meet.”
Now that I stood face-to-face with it, my chest trembled. Three years ago, I had lost my comrades, and it had lost one eye.
It had been a long, bitter grudge.
Now it was time to end it.
I tightened my grip on the cold spear shaft and slowly walked toward the creature.
“Long time no see. Remember me?”
Wyverns were unquestionably advanced creatures.
It had been cunning and cruel even then. Now that it had become a Named Monster, it naturally possessed even greater strength and Intelligence.
—Grrrrr...
“Looks like you do. So, how’s the eye?”
A crimson flame blazed in its remaining eye. I let out a quiet laugh as the scales across its body bristled.
“You fucking bastard. Who the hell do you think you’re hissing at?”
—Grrrk!
One step.
Then another.
My heart pounded while my mind spun at full speed. Hundreds of ways to carve apart its body and snuff out its life unfolded before my eyes.
“There were some names I wanted you to hear if I ever saw you again. Open your ears and listen carefully.”
Step.
Step.
As the distance between us narrowed, something hot surged from my lower abdomen.
It was like a small sun—the Scorching Yang Qi that had surpassed one jiazi, and the rage that had built and built until it became something solid.
“Kim Hyunsu.”
The face of a straight-laced kid in horn-rimmed glasses appeared before my eyes.
He had been a Hunter for only four months. He was the first to die. One sweep of the creature’s tail had crushed his entire body.
He had been clumsy, but he never lacked enthusiasm. Whenever he had a spare moment, he would come find me with another question.
Deputy Team Leader. How do I do this?
Deputy Team Leader. I don’t understand this part.
Deputy Team Leader...
Sometimes, I thought about him.
I wondered whether he might have survived if I had explained things more thoroughly, if I hadn’t been annoyed by the kid who came to me with dozens of questions every day.
But regret always came too late. Kim Hyunsu had remained twenty forever, and his parents had wailed throughout the funeral for the only son they had lost.
Maybe they still are, even three years later.
There were nine more people like him.
Every one of them had a family and dreams of their own.
“Lee Hyerim. Song Donghyeok, Park Sangho, Kim Haneung, Park Gwanghyeon...”
With every name, I took another step. With every step, memories of that person shimmered before me like heat haze.
That was why my vision blurred.
At least, that was what I chose to believe.
After ten steps, only one name remained.
“...And Hong Cheonsu.”
The round face of a man in his thirties flashed before my eyes.
When I first met him, I was a rookie Hunter barely twenty years old, while he was a ten-year veteran.
After he saved me from being surrounded and nearly killed by goblins, I started calling him hyung.
One perfectly ordinary day, I had suddenly asked him,
Why are you always so good to me?
He had answered,
It kept eating at me, seeing a kid like you struggle. My youngest sibling is about your age.
It wasn’t until the day of his funeral that I learned he had grown up in an orphanage and didn’t have a single relative.
The absurdity of it made me laugh.
In the end, though, I cried.
Because I remembered his final words.
You cocky bastard. Taekyung, go on ahead.
That was how he—Cheonsu hyung—died.
Leaving behind a wonderful spouse and three children.
And now, at this very moment, I stood before the creature. I glared into its enormous red eye and opened my mouth.
“Listen carefully, you fucking lizard bastard.”
I had survived countless crises to say these words.
After three years and ninety-two days, I was finally ready to tear off those wings and drive my spear into its heart.
“This time, I’m not going anywhere.”
Internal energy erupted from my dantian and surged through every limb and bone in my body.
The Scorching Yang Qi raced unchecked toward the cold spearhead. The internal energy flowed in an unbroken stream, tangling like a skein of thread before transforming into something new.
Crackle, crackle, crackle!
Aura. Spear Energy.
It didn’t matter what I called it. I leveled the blue-burning spearhead at the creature.
“You’re...dead today.”

sentences.text: Won Myunghoon left.
Remembering how he had ground his teeth at my attitude yet hadn’t dared attack drew a quiet laugh from me.
If he had, I would’ve made him regret it.
He was a hyena of a man.
Show him weakness, and he bared his teeth.
Show him strength, and he hid them.
Judging by everything I had seen of him, his nature probably had something to do with the incident eight years ago as well.
Consider yourself lucky.
No matter how much a hyena leaped or crawled, it was still a beast.
If it knew when to tuck its tail, all I had to do was scare it off.
I had neither reason nor desire to bloody my hands before it actually sank its teeth into my shoulder—especially when I was about to face a real monster.
—Kyaaaaaaaah!
The black dot drew closer.
A rage-filled roar echoed from the far edge of the horizon.
Just as I had recognized it, it had recognized me.
Yes.
You remember me too.
That was enough.
I was about to face a half-mad Named Monster, but I felt neither fear nor excitement.
Only one thing bothered me, like a thorn caught in my throat.
“Why didn’t you leave?”
Team Leader Choi stared at me with his arms loosely folded.
Instead of answering, he asked a question of his own.
“Who are you asking?”
“All of you.”
I swept my gaze around.
Four people stood against the endless wasteland, with rocks and trees scattered here and there behind them.
Team Leader Choi and Butler Kim.
Im Kkeokjeong and Song Song.
Not one of them had left.
“You all know that thing coming toward us is a Named Monster, right?”
“We’re all well aware.”
“Then this should be simple.
It’s dangerous, so leave while you still can.”
“Where would we retreat to?”
“Where else?
Back to the exit we came through.”
“The Star Guild isn’t exactly an ideal group to flee with—especially after making an enemy of their Guild Master.”
I don’t see it that way.
No one knew it yet, but Butler Kim was an A-Rank mage—and one who had lived through the unprecedented war known as the Great Cataclysm.
The Star Guild might have had the advantage in numbers, but even without me, the others wouldn’t be outmatched if they fought Won Myunghoon’s Guild right now.
“That’s a convenient excuse.”
Team Leader Choi stared at me as I smiled.
“Mr.
Jin Taekyung.”
“No.”
I cut him off before he could begin, but Team Leader Choi wasn’t the sort to back down quietly.
“Since you’ve left me stuck here with nowhere to go, I think I’ve earned the right to ask a few questions.”
Damn.
He has a point.
I answered reluctantly.
“Fine...but keep it short.”
“That monster coming toward us—is it connected to what happened three years ago?”
I hesitated, then nodded.
“You have no intention of retreating.”
My silence was answer enough.
Team Leader Choi let out a low sigh.
“Mr.
Jin Taekyung, you’re facing a Named Monster.”
“That’s news to me.
All I see is something I need to kill.”
“You need to think about this rationally.”
“Do I look that unstable right now?”
“That...”
Team Leader Choi fell silent.
I was calmer than I had ever been.
My heart might have been hammering like mad, but my mind was running through countless ways to deal with the creature.
“Team Leader Choi.”
“I’ve told you my motto in life a few times before, haven’t I?”
Im Kkeokjeong, who had been watching in silence, answered for him.
“Thin and long.”
“You remember too, Uncle?”
“You were a strange kid.
Most young men dream big at least once...but you never did.”
“I’ve never been fond of a turbulent life.”
This time, Butler Kim answered with a smile.
“For someone who feels that way, you seem to have come quite far.”
“That’s why I changed it.”
“Big and long.
Is that right?”
“Yes.
It’s already too late for me to live small.
Since things have turned out this way, I’m going to live as big and as long as I can.”
“Good.
If you wish, perhaps...”
I knew what he was about to say.
I quietly shook my head.
Butler Kim had a far more important task to handle.
“I’m fine.
Protect the others.”
“Understood.
Even without being asked, I’ll do what must be done to the best of my ability.”
At Butler Kim’s clear-cut answer, Song Song asked with an incredulous expression,
“You’re going to let him fight a Named Monster alone?
Are you all out of your minds?
One wrong move and we’ll all die.
Every last one of us!”
“Then why haven’t you left, Miss Song?”
“...Good question.
Why am I still here?”
I watched her sink into thought, then spoke.
“Miss Song.”
“No.”
“Absolutely not.”
“Hunter Jin Taekyung.
Please.”
What was with these reactions?
I had barely gotten her name out, yet Song Song, Team Leader Choi, and Butler Kim had all shut me down without hesitation.
“Taekyung, go for it.”
At least Kkeokjeong hyung was on my side.
I looked at the other three with an aggrieved expression.
“I haven’t even said anything yet.”
Song Song answered,
“That’s why I’m saying no.”
“How do you know what I was going to say?”
“Hmm.
A confession?”
My head went numb for a moment.
The back of my skull throbbed as though someone had hit it with a hammer.
“Wait.
How did you know?”
“Good grief.
How could I not know?”
“W-was it that obvious?”
“Yes.
Painfully.”
“Then...”
She shook her head without hesitation.
“I’m sorry.
I’m not the sort of person who changes her attitude at the drop of a hat just because someone has money or fame.”
“Oh.”
“To be honest, you’re quite a catch, Mr.
Taekyung.
But when I like someone, I’m the type to reel him in all at once.
I can’t keep a whole pond stocked with men.”
After letting everything out in one breath, she blinked.
“Oh.
I wasn’t too harsh on someone who’s about to fight a Named Monster, was I?”
I had been opening and closing my mouth like a goldfish, but a quiet laugh soon escaped me.
“Why are you laughing?”
“No reason.
I was just thinking how refreshingly straightforward you are.”
She narrowed her eyes at my answer.
“Hold on.
Why are you suddenly speaking casually?”

We’re the same age.
We can at least be friends, can’t we?”
