chapters.title: Chapter 221
paragraphs: Ding.

System You have achieved the Achievement Manifestation of Qi! This is truly an outstanding achievement! An Achievement reward will be granted! Spear Energy is now available! The effect of Unaffected by a Hundred Poisons has taken root in your body! You have acquired a large amount of EXP! Level Up! Level Up! You have acquired 100 additional Bonus Points!
The System notifications echoed in my ears like a ringing bell. But my gaze remained fixed solely on the spear.
Ssssss.
Blue flames flickered over the spearhead. A thrilling shiver raced up my spine.
I did it.
Today, I had taken one step toward a higher realm and conquered one of the peaks of the perilous mountain known as martial arts.
At the same time, I knew one thing for certain.
I can kill it.
No more thoughts or words were needed. All that remained was to act and make those long years of waiting a reality.
But I wasn’t the only one who had been waiting for this touching reunion.
Its lone eye bulging wide, the creature let out a furious roar.
—Kraaaaaaaah!
No, it was closer to a thunderclap than a roar.
Gooooooom—

Tremendous wind pressure poured from a maw large enough to swallow a car whole and bore down on the ground. The compressed air burst around me, and it felt as though a thousand-geun boulder were crushing my shoulders.
Air Breath.
One branch of a unique ability granted only to dragonkin.
Since a Named Monster was using it, even a capable Hunter would have had their eardrums burst and been forced to their knees.
But not me.
Crack. Grrrk.
I silently pressed forward against the crushing pressure.
With every step, my ankles sank into the ground and the pressure grew stronger, but it couldn’t stop me.
The creature might have surpassed the limits of an ordinary monster, but I wasn’t afraid.
Because so have I.
At least in terms of physical ability, I could already be called superhuman.
Strength, speed, stamina—when it came to everything that determined the outcome of a battle, I stood one step ahead of a Peak master at my level, or an A-Rank Hunter.
“Ahh, that’s refreshing.”
I raised my head with a grin.
Atop its skyscraper-sized torso, the red eye of the creature blasting out Air Breath wavered when it saw my smile.
“What was that? A fan set to high?”
—Kraaaaaaaah!
“Turn it off! You’re blowing yellow dust everywhere, you bastard!”
As I shouted, I swung the spear toward the sky with all my strength.
Whoooooosh!
The blue flame of qi carved a semicircle through the air, burning through it. In that instant, the pressure crushing my body vanished, and I became as light as a feather.
Now!
Boom!
With a single stomp, I shot forward like an arrow.
The confused creature twisted its head and unleashed another Air Breath, but it couldn’t keep up with my speed.
Whoosh! Rat-a-tat-tat!
Clad in nothing but light leather armor and carrying a single spear, I streaked across the battlefield like lightning. In the blink of an eye, I was right in front of it.
—Grrrrrk?
The startled creature spread its folded wings wide. But by then, I had already leaped with all my strength.
Boom!
With a powerful tremor, I soared into the air. Through my hair streaming in the wind, I saw the creature’s knee beneath its flashing black scales.
The exact spot known as the cruciate ligament.
“You’re exempt from military service, you bastard!”
With that shout, I drove my spear in with all my strength.
Thrust! Shrrrk!
The Wyvern’s hide and scales, said to withstand ordinary magic and weapons alike, split open in an instant.
A sharp, satisfying jolt traveled through my fingertips, like harpooning a fish.
It went in!
The blue-burning Spear Energy cut through and shattered everything in its path.
Once the spearhead opened a gap, the rest was easy. Like hammering in a nail, I slammed my fist against the butt of the two-meter spear and drove it deep into the creature’s knee.
Boom! Fwoooosh!
Dark blood erupted like a fountain. Just as the creature spread its wings to take flight, it dropped to one knee with a scream.
—Graaaaaaaah!
But I didn’t stop there. I stepped onto the end of the spear lodged in its knee and used its spring to launch myself upward.
As I shot several more meters into the air, a dagger appeared in my hand.
If I don’t have one, I can just take one out.
I had countless weapons stored in my Inventory, both in Murim and in the real world.
They had cost me a fortune, but if it meant killing this creature, I wouldn’t mind spending ten times as much.
Thrust!
I suddenly remembered training in the Wall Lizard Technique back in Murim. The cliff I had scaled then was even higher, and there had hardly been anything to use as a foothold.
And whenever I thought I’d made some progress, a certain lunatic would start dropping rocks on me.
Compared to that, this was nothing.
I drove my dagger into the creature’s enormous body again and again, climbing higher and higher.
Thrust, thrust! Thrust-thrust-thrust!
Against Spear Energy, neither hide harder than plate armor nor scales capable of deflecting low-level magic were of any use.
Imagine something the size of your palm crawling up your body and hammering nails into you over and over.
That was exactly what the creature was going through.
—Kraaaaaaah!
Unable to endure the relentless pain, it writhed and roared. It was trying to shake me off, but it was one step too late.
By then, I was already savoring the sensation of floating through the air.
Open Inventory. Equip spear.
The next instant, a solid spear shaft filled my empty hand.
The Scorching Yang Qi that had surpassed one jiazi when I opened my Conception and Governor Vessels surged toward the spearhead like an ebbing tide.
Whoooooosh. Ssssss!
Blue flames enveloped the spearhead without leaving the slightest gap.
Flickering in the darkness, they were the tail of a meteor.
And I was the meteor itself.
“Where do you think you’re going?”
With that quiet murmur, I became one with the spear and plunged downward. My target was its wing, which served as both foreleg and arm.
Blinded by pain for a moment, the creature had no way to stop the meteor.
Fwoosh! Shraaaaaak!

Scorching Yang Qi blazed like a miniature sun, slicing through hide and scales and burning the flesh beneath. The wing, more than ten meters from top to bottom, split in two along the path of the spearhead.
—Krrrk...!
It was probably the worst pain the creature had ever experienced. The red eye of a beast that had spent its entire life as a predator flew wide.
—Kraaaaaaaaaah!
I landed lightly on the ground and regarded it with a cold, steady gaze.
Its fifty-meter bulk writhed within the billowing cloud of dust.
“Does it hurt?”
—Kwak! Kraaaaaah!
“That little?”
Compared to what it had done three years ago, this was nothing.
A single flap of its wings had shattered entire bodies. Heads clutched in its claws had vanished without a trace. Those swallowed by its enormous maw hadn’t even left corpses behind.
That was when I first learned how much blood and how many organs the human body contained.
How brutally a person could die.
“You bastard. I wouldn’t be satisfied even if I chewed you to death.”
An eye for an eye. A tooth for a tooth.
It would die here today, by my hand. And it would die horribly—exactly as I had imagined countless times before.
“This is just the beginning. Quit whining and get up.”
Whoooosh.
The wind stirred by my swinging spear swept away the dust.
Covered in blood and dirt, the creature glared at me as it panted heavily.
—Krrrk.
Dozens of blades were embedded throughout its body, and blood poured from its open wounds like waterfalls.
Of the wings that symbolized the Wyvern, only one remained.
It was still enormous and imposing, but there was no longer any trace of the dignity befitting a dragonkin offshoot and a Named Monster.
—Grrrrr...
Its eye, brimming with resentment and killing intent, glared at me.
The emotions conveyed by that gaze were unlike anything I had ever known from a monster.
“Watch how you look at me, or I’ll pluck that eye out first.”
I tossed out the words and began walking toward it.
That was when it happened.
—Hu. man.
A single word made me doubt my own ears.
My feet froze. The corner of my eye twitched involuntarily.
What did I just hear?
But I hadn’t misheard it. The creature’s maw shifted, and a clearer pronunciation emerged.
—Do. you. want. to. kill. me?
A monster was speaking.
That very monster.
A groan slipped through my parted lips.
“This is impossible...”
—It’s. dif.fer.ent. from. be.fore.
The instant it finished speaking, its red eye turned completely bloodred.
And then...
—Heal.
Sssssss.
Magical power began gathering around the creature.
Carus the One-Eyed.
That was the Black Wyvern’s name.
Before earning that name, he had survived countless crises. He had fought not only monsters, but humans as well.
He had fought hundreds of battles where victory meant claiming prey and defeat meant becoming prey.
That day in the past had been no different.
Not until one human took his eye.
How dare he? How dare a human lower than a bug do this to me!
Carus was furious. At the same time, he made a vow.
He would kill the human who had taken his eye. Even if he never found him, he would kill other humans again and again.
Then one day, after endless battle and slaughter, he realized that he had grown to an enormous size and gained tremendous strength.
Why? Did fighting humans make me stronger?
Before long, Carus understood. It wasn’t his battles with humans that had made him stronger, but devouring other monsters.
Each time he did, something inside his body grew more powerful.
What did the humans call it again? Ah, right.
Magic Gems.
Once he understood the source of his strength, Carus began hunting Magic Gems.
He devoured other monsters, and instead of feasting on human flesh, he studied the magic equipment they carried.
So this is how those human bastards use Magic Gems.
The more Magic Gems he absorbed, the higher his Intelligence rose and the stronger he became.
As a Wyvern, a lesser branch of the dragonkin, Carus had possessed remarkable Intelligence to begin with. At last, he set foot in an entirely new realm.
Magic, huh? Should I learn it?
Carus built a new nest in a nameless wasteland. He killed everything that might get in his way and immersed himself in the study of magic.
Then he noticed the humans invading his territory.
I haven’t even finished digesting the Magic Gems I ate earlier...
Knowing that he was still incomplete, Carus decided to be patient.
Even when several humans recklessly approached his nest, he tried to ignore them.
Until he caught that bastard’s scent.
My eye! It’s the human who took my eye!
Carus saw red and immediately raced across the wasteland.
Using one of the humans he had deliberately allowed to escape as a guide, he finally came face-to-face with that bastard.
I’ll kill him! I’ll chew him up, bones and all!
But that bastard was strong. Even Carus, who had absorbed hundreds of Magic Gems, was pushed back helplessly.
Yet he still had one card left to play.
—Heal.
Sssssss.
His wounds closed, and the bleeding stopped. He couldn’t completely restore his torn wing, but this was enough.
—I’ll. kill. you. hu.man.
Jin Taekyung, his face filled with shock, clenched his teeth.
Having already experienced Jin Taekyung’s speed firsthand, Carus cast another spell without hesitation.
—Sloooow!
A faint trace of dragon blood flowed through Carus’s veins.
Five Slow spells stacked atop one another and enveloped Jin Taekyung’s body.
—Kehahahaha!
Carus burst into laughter as he watched Jin Taekyung move as slowly as possible.
That was when Jin Taekyung spoke.
“One hundred points to Agility.”
Whoosh.
Carus blinked.
A spearhead wreathed in blue flames filled his enormous eye.
“What are you looking at, you fucking bastard?”
Crunch!

sentences.text: Ding.
System You have achieved the Achievement Manifestation of Qi!
This is truly an outstanding achievement!
An Achievement reward will be granted!
Spear Energy is now available!
The effect of Unaffected by a Hundred Poisons has taken root in your body!
You have acquired a large amount of EXP!
Level Up!
Level Up!
You have acquired 100 additional Bonus Points!
The System notifications echoed in my ears like a ringing bell.
But my gaze remained fixed solely on the spear.
Ssssss.
Blue flames flickered over the spearhead.
A thrilling shiver raced up my spine.
I did it.
Today, I had taken one step toward a higher realm and conquered one of the peaks of the perilous mountain known as martial arts.
At the same time, I knew one thing for certain.
I can kill it.
No more thoughts or words were needed.
All that remained was to act and make those long years of waiting a reality.
But I wasn’t the only one who had been waiting for this touching reunion.
Its lone eye bulging wide, the creature let out a furious roar.
—Kraaaaaaaah!
No, it was closer to a thunderclap than a roar.
Gooooooom—
Tremendous wind pressure poured from a maw large enough to swallow a car whole and bore down on the ground.
The compressed air burst around me, and it felt as though a thousand-geun boulder were crushing my shoulders.
Air Breath.
One branch of a unique ability granted only to dragonkin.
Since a Named Monster was using it, even a capable Hunter would have had their eardrums burst and been forced to their knees.
But not me.
Crack.
Grrrk.
I silently pressed forward against the crushing pressure.
With every step, my ankles sank into the ground and the pressure grew stronger, but it couldn’t stop me.
The creature might have surpassed the limits of an ordinary monster, but I wasn’t afraid.
Because so have I.
At least in terms of physical ability, I could already be called superhuman.
Strength, speed, stamina—when it came to everything that determined the outcome of a battle, I stood one step ahead of a Peak master at my level, or an A-Rank Hunter.
“Ahh, that’s refreshing.”
I raised my head with a grin.
Atop its skyscraper-sized torso, the red eye of the creature blasting out Air Breath wavered when it saw my smile.
“What was that?
A fan set to high?”
—Kraaaaaaaah!
“Turn it off!
You’re blowing yellow dust everywhere, you bastard!”
As I shouted, I swung the spear toward the sky with all my strength.
Whoooooosh!
The blue flame of qi carved a semicircle through the air, burning through it.
In that instant, the pressure crushing my body vanished, and I became as light as a feather.
Now!
Boom!
With a single stomp, I shot forward like an arrow.
The confused creature twisted its head and unleashed another Air Breath, but it couldn’t keep up with my speed.
Whoosh!
Rat-a-tat-tat!
Clad in nothing but light leather armor and carrying a single spear, I streaked across the battlefield like lightning.
In the blink of an eye, I was right in front of it.
—Grrrrrk?
The startled creature spread its folded wings wide.
But by then, I had already leaped with all my strength.
Boom!
With a powerful tremor, I soared into the air.
Through my hair streaming in the wind, I saw the creature’s knee beneath its flashing black scales.
The exact spot known as the cruciate ligament.
“You’re exempt from military service, you bastard!”
With that shout, I drove my spear in with all my strength.
Thrust!
Shrrrk!
The Wyvern’s hide and scales, said to withstand ordinary magic and weapons alike, split open in an instant.
A sharp, satisfying jolt traveled through my fingertips, like harpooning a fish.
It went in!
The blue-burning Spear Energy cut through and shattered everything in its path.
Once the spearhead opened a gap, the rest was easy.
Like hammering in a nail, I slammed my fist against the butt of the two-meter spear and drove it deep into the creature’s knee.
Boom!
Fwoooosh!
Dark blood erupted like a fountain.
Just as the creature spread its wings to take flight, it dropped to one knee with a scream.
—Graaaaaaaah!
But I didn’t stop there.
I stepped onto the end of the spear lodged in its knee and used its spring to launch myself upward.
As I shot several more meters into the air, a dagger appeared in my hand.
If I don’t have one, I can just take one out.
I had countless weapons stored in my Inventory, both in Murim and in the real world.
They had cost me a fortune, but if it meant killing this creature, I wouldn’t mind spending ten times as much.
Thrust!
I suddenly remembered training in the Wall Lizard Technique back in Murim.
The cliff I had scaled then was even higher, and there had hardly been anything to use as a foothold.
And whenever I thought I’d made some progress, a certain lunatic would start dropping rocks on me.
Compared to that, this was nothing.
I drove my dagger into the creature’s enormous body again and again, climbing higher and higher.
Thrust, thrust!
Thrust-thrust-thrust!
Against Spear Energy, neither hide harder than plate armor nor scales capable of deflecting low-level magic were of any use.
Imagine something the size of your palm crawling up your body and hammering nails into you over and over.
That was exactly what the creature was going through.
—Kraaaaaaah!
Unable to endure the relentless pain, it writhed and roared.
It was trying to shake me off, but it was one step too late.
By then, I was already savoring the sensation of floating through the air.
Open Inventory.
Equip spear.
The next instant, a solid spear shaft filled my empty hand.
The Scorching Yang Qi that had surpassed one jiazi when I opened my Conception and Governor Vessels surged toward the spearhead like an ebbing tide.
Whoooooosh.
Ssssss!
Blue flames enveloped the spearhead without leaving the slightest gap.
Flickering in the darkness, they were the tail of a meteor.
And I was the meteor itself.
“Where do you think you’re going?”
With that quiet murmur, I became one with the spear and plunged downward.
My target was its wing, which served as both foreleg and arm.
Blinded by pain for a moment, the creature had no way to stop the meteor.
Fwoosh!
Shraaaaaak!
Scorching Yang Qi blazed like a miniature sun, slicing through hide and scales and burning the flesh beneath.
The wing, more than ten meters from top to bottom, split in two along the path of the spearhead.
—Krrrk...!
It was probably the worst pain the creature had ever experienced.
The red eye of a beast that had spent its entire life as a predator flew wide.
—Kraaaaaaaaaah!
I landed lightly on the ground and regarded it with a cold, steady gaze.
Its fifty-meter bulk writhed within the billowing cloud of dust.
“Does it hurt?”
—Kwak!
Kraaaaaah!
“That little?”
Compared to what it had done three years ago, this was nothing.
A single flap of its wings had shattered entire bodies.
Heads clutched in its claws had vanished without a trace.
Those swallowed by its enormous maw hadn’t even left corpses behind.
That was when I first learned how much blood and how many organs the human body contained.
How brutally a person could die.
“You bastard.
I wouldn’t be satisfied even if I chewed you to death.”
An eye for an eye.
A tooth for a tooth.
It would die here today, by my hand.
And it would die horribly—exactly as I had imagined countless times before.
“This is just the beginning.
Quit whining and get up.”
Whoooosh.
The wind stirred by my swinging spear swept away the dust.
Covered in blood and dirt, the creature glared at me as it panted heavily.
—Krrrk.
Dozens of blades were embedded throughout its body, and blood poured from its open wounds like waterfalls.
Of the wings that symbolized the Wyvern, only one remained.
It was still enormous and imposing, but there was no longer any trace of the dignity befitting a dragonkin offshoot and a Named Monster.
—Grrrrr...
Its eye, brimming with resentment and killing intent, glared at me.
The emotions conveyed by that gaze were unlike anything I had ever known from a monster.
“Watch how you look at me, or I’ll pluck that eye out first.”
I tossed out the words and began walking toward it.
That was when it happened.
—Hu. man.
A single word made me doubt my own ears.
My feet froze.
The corner of my eye twitched involuntarily.
What did I just hear?
But I hadn’t misheard it.
The creature’s maw shifted, and a clearer pronunciation emerged.
—Do. you. want. to. kill. me?
A monster was speaking.
That very monster.
A groan slipped through my parted lips.
“This is impossible...”
—It’s. dif.fer.ent. from. be.fore.
The instant it finished speaking, its red eye turned completely bloodred.
And then...
—Heal.
Sssssss.
Magical power began gathering around the creature.
Carus the One-Eyed.
That was the Black Wyvern’s name.
Before earning that name, he had survived countless crises.
He had fought not only monsters, but humans as well.
He had fought hundreds of battles where victory meant claiming prey and defeat meant becoming prey.
That day in the past had been no different.
Not until one human took his eye.
How dare he?
How dare a human lower than a bug do this to me!
Carus was furious.
At the same time, he made a vow.
He would kill the human who had taken his eye.
Even if he never found him, he would kill other humans again and again.
Then one day, after endless battle and slaughter, he realized that he had grown to an enormous size and gained tremendous strength.
Why?
Did fighting humans make me stronger?
Before long, Carus understood.
It wasn’t his battles with humans that had made him stronger, but devouring other monsters.
Each time he did, something inside his body grew more powerful.
What did the humans call it again?
Ah, right.
Magic Gems.
Once he understood the source of his strength, Carus began hunting Magic Gems.
He devoured other monsters, and instead of feasting on human flesh, he studied the magic equipment they carried.
So this is how those human bastards use Magic Gems.
The more Magic Gems he absorbed, the higher his Intelligence rose and the stronger he became.
As a Wyvern, a lesser branch of the dragonkin, Carus had possessed remarkable Intelligence to begin with.
At last, he set foot in an entirely new realm.
Magic, huh?
Should I learn it?

I haven’t even finished digesting the Magic Gems I ate earlier...

—Heal.
Sssssss.

—I’ll. kill. you. hu.man.

Having already experienced Jin Taekyung’s speed firsthand, Carus cast another spell without hesitation.
—Sloooow!

Five Slow spells stacked atop one another and enveloped Jin Taekyung’s body.
—Kehahahaha!
Carus burst into laughter as he watched Jin Taekyung move as slowly as possible.
That was when Jin Taekyung spoke.
“One hundred points to Agility.”
Whoosh.
Carus blinked.
A spearhead wreathed in blue flames filled his enormous eye.
“What are you looking at, you fucking bastard?”

chapters.title: Chapter 222
paragraphs: Ssssss.
Blue flames flickered over the spearhead.
They were a concentration of immense qi—powerful enough to pierce even the Wyvern’s steel-like hide and scales.
There was no way they would fail to penetrate its eye, the Wyvern’s only real weakness.
“What are you looking at, you fucking bastard?”
Without the slightest hesitation, I drove my spear into its enormous eye.
Crunch! Ssssss!
Hide? Scales?
Nothing could stop the spearhead.
Blood gushed out as the Scorching Yang Qi burned through its retina. Its vertically slit pupil dilated, and its maw stretched so wide it looked ready to tear apart.
“Graaaaaaaah!”
It was a howl from the depths of its soul.
An inhuman shriek I had never heard before burst from its mouth, which was stretched wide enough to split.
That nearly blew out my eardrums.
Even after raising my internal energy to protect my hearing, my ears were still ringing.
Leaving the spear embedded in its eye, I landed lightly on the ground and watched the creature writhe.
Boom! Kwooooom!
It thrashed wildly, swinging its one intact wing and tail in every direction. Then it suddenly jerked its head up.
“Grrrrr.”
The head of the house-sized monster.
Black blood poured from the eye, which had been half crushed.
It was a horrifying sight—enough to make even a fairly gutsy person step backward. But as I watched, I felt refreshed, as if someone had opened a hole in my chest.
“You’re one dumb son of a bitch. You still haven’t learned your lesson after what happened three years ago?”
Even if it had lost both eyes, it still had other senses.
Its head trembled with pain as it turned directly toward me.
“Hu. man.”
“Why, Wyvern?”
“How. did. you. even?”
I grinned at the disbelief in its voice.
It was almost a shame the bastard couldn’t see my smile.
“If you wish hard enough, the whole universe will help you. Something like that.”
“My. ma. gic. was. per. fect!”
“Oh, I’ll give you that. You caught me by surprise.”
What kind of monster was a Wyvern?
It had a body and wings as large as a building, a hide tough enough to deflect most attacks, and even the ability to use Breath.
It was terrifying enough on pure physical ability alone. I had never dreamed it might know magic too.
Or that one measly Slow spell would cut my Agility by fifty.
According to the System notification, its magic had been amplified several times over by the dragonkin trait.
But I still had one trump card left.
“I’ve saved up quite a few points. Saving is a habit of mine.”
Back when I was a rookie in Murim, I had raised my stats with every point I earned.
I had been weak then, and my situation was so precarious that there was no telling what might happen the next day.
But as I grew stronger, I realized something.
These points could be a weapon too.
Just as martial artists concealed their ultimate techniques until the very end.
“What. kind. of. orc. shit. is. that?”
“What do you think? It means your magic won’t do a damn thing to me.”
I leisurely opened my Inventory and pulled out a new spear. When I tapped the spearhead with my fingernail, a clear ring echoed through the air.
The blind creature jerked at the sound.
“What. are. you. plan. ning?”
“You already know. Why ask?”
Step. Step.
With every step I took toward it, its tightly hunched body flinched.
“We have an outstanding debt to settle. With three years of interest.”
There was no room for compromise. This fight would end only when one of us died.
And I wasn’t the one dying here today.
“I’m going to kill you.”
“Kraaaaaah!”
But the creature wasn’t about to take it lying down.
It had lost one wing and both eyes to me, but it was still a Named Monster. It had enough strength left for one final struggle.
“Heal!”
Sssssss.
Black mana once again enveloped its enormous body. The bleeding stopped at once, and new flesh began to fill the wounds. It was far faster than any healing magic I had ever seen.
And it wasn’t finished.
“Dark. Bin. ding!”
Shrrrrrrk!
Thorny vines erupted without warning from the dusty wasteland and wrapped tightly around my entire body.
At the same time, a System notification sounded.
Beep!

System Lv.??? Carus has used Binding Magic! Due to the dragonkin trait, the magic is enhanced! Strength temporarily decreased by 10! Stamina temporarily decreased by 10! Agility temporarily decreased by 10!
The thorny vines crept upward from my ankles, coiling around my legs, waist, arms, and finally my neck.
Sawtoothed thorns pierced my thin leather armor and dug into my skin.
Beep.
System Paralysis Poison has entered your body! Nerve Poison has entered your body! Status abnormality: Poisoned!
“...Huh. What the hell is this?”
“Grrrrr.”
The creature—or rather, Carus—laughed triumphantly. Its mangled eye was already beginning to return to its original form.
“You. let. your. guard. down. hu. man!”
“Let my guard down?”
I thought for a moment, then nodded.
“Yeah. I did let my guard down.”
“...Why. are. you. so. calm?”
“When someone acts calm in a situation like this, it usually means one of two things. Either they’re bluffing their ass off, or...”
Ding.
System The effect of Unaffected by a Hundred Poisons has been applied! Paralysis Poison has been neutralized! Nerve Poison has been neutralized! Status abnormality: Poisoned has disappeared!
“Or they have a good reason not to worry.”
The instant I finished speaking, I stepped forward.
The thorny vines, each as thick as my thigh, tightened around my entire body, but they couldn’t stop me.
“While I’m at it, I’ll splurge on a bonus. Fifty Strength. Fifty Stamina.”
Ding.
System 100 Bonus Points have been consumed! The points have been applied to your stats!
Crack. Crrrunch.
I tore and shattered the vines with overwhelming power and Strength.
Carus’s magic had been greatly amplified by the dragonkin trait, but the magic itself wasn’t particularly advanced.
“Slow magic, binding magic. What’s next?”
Its eye had already almost completely healed.
When Carus saw me emerge from the vines unharmed, its maw fell open.
“You...you!”
I brushed the pieces of vine from my arm.
“Don’t you have any other spells? You were so confident, I thought you’d at least know how to factor, but it turns out you’ve only mastered addition and subtraction.”
“How. did. you?”
“My own magic.”
“Your. own. ma. gic?”
“Yeah. Magic.”
I shifted the iron spear in my hand into a reverse grip.
That was all the preparation I needed. This spear was my magic, and the creature would never be able to stop it.
“Huuup.”
I drew a deep breath. Every muscle in my body meshed together like tiny gears, and the world slowed.
I leaned back and snapped my arm forward, casting a spell I hadn’t quite memorized.
“Burst, sesame.”
Whoosh! Fwoooooosh!
Against the red sunset staining the horizon, a blue flash plunged into the creature’s eye, which was dyed an even deeper shade of blood.
Burning. Shattering. Bursting.
Crack!
“Graa...aaaaaaah!”
I walked toward it as its agonized scream tore through the air. With every step, familiar faces flashed before my eyes.
Faces I would probably remember until the day I died.
Ever since that day three years ago, shackles had weighed down my ankles.
Anger. Guilt. The desire for revenge. Emotions piled one atop another, layer upon layer.
Their weight had been crushing. So heavy I couldn’t take a single step forward.
But now...
At some point, I had grown strong enough to bear that weight.
At long last, I could offer some comfort to the spirits of those who had died before me.
Yes. Finally.
Just as I murmured those words silently in my heart, mana rippled around the creature writhing in pain.
“Kraaaah! Slow! Dark Binding! Magic Arrow!”
Three spells erupted in rapid succession.
I kicked off the ground and charged forward. The instant I shot beyond Slow’s area of effect like a streak of light, thorny vines and dozens of mana arrows rose to block my path.
Sssshing! Shrrrk!
Everything was sliced apart along the arc of blue flame. Sensing that its attack had failed, the creature beat its one remaining wing.
It was such an enormous target that I didn’t even need to aim. Another flash shot from my hand.
Swoooooosh! Thud!
“Kyaaaaaaah!”
Whoooosh!
A shrill scream rang out. Then its spike-covered tail came hurtling toward me with a terrifying roar as it tore through the air.
Boom!
But I had already leaped half a beat ahead of it.
The rocks scattered across the wasteland like reefs rising from the sea shattered into powder.
Open Inventory. Equip.
As I descended, I swung my spear.
Shraaaak.
The severed tail rolled through the dust with black blood spilling from it.
“Kraaaaah!”
Shrrk. Shrrk. Shrrk.
It was like perfectly meshing gears.
I blocked, dodged, and cut through every attack the creature unleashed in its desperate struggle.
Then I realized that no more attacks were coming and stopped.
“Krrk. Grrrk.”
Two severed wings. A severed tail. Two eyes that could no longer function.
The creature lay submerged in a vast pool of blood, ragged breaths rasping from its maw as though each one might be its last.
I watched it for a while before opening my mouth.
“Do you want to live?”
“Then use your healing magic. I’ll wait.”
“Will. you...save. me?”
“No. It just feels like a waste to send you off like this.”
“Hold out ten more times. I’ll kill you after that.”
The creature’s body trembled. Its gaping eye, pouring dark-red blood like a waterfall, turned toward me.
“You. are. cruel. hu. man.”
“Compared to what you did, this is nothing.”
“I. only. did. what. I. had. to. do.”
“I know.”
Humans killed monsters, and monsters killed humans.
The two sides had been killing each other for decades. It was both history and an inescapable cycle. And...
“I’m no different.”
Completing my revenge—that was what I had to do now.
After a brief silence, a resigned whisper escaped its maw.
“...Kill. me.”
The strength slowly drained from its twitching body.
I aimed my spear between its blood-caked eyes and whispered softly.
“Thank you.”
For staying alive until now.
And for dying by my hand.
With those barely audible words, I drove the spear forward.
Shnk.
The Scorching Yang Qi flowing from the spearhead as it gently pierced through the center of its brow rampaged like a wild beast, devouring and burning everything in its path.
A skull harder than steel. Flesh. Brain matter. Everything else.
Ding.

System You have defeated Lv.115 Carus! You have achieved the Achievement Named Monster Defeated! You have achieved a great Achievement. A corresponding Reward will be granted! You have perfectly cleared the A-Rank Gate, The Black Wyvern’s Nest! Calculating all Rewards... You have acquired an enormous amount of EXP and Fame! Level Up! Level Up! . . .
System notifications washed over me like waves. I released the scorching-hot spear shaft and thought,
I did it. Finally.
What more was there to say?
The shouts of other people brought me back to myself as I stood there in a daze.
“Mr. Jin Taekyung!”
“Taekyung!”
Team Leader Choi. Butler Kim. Im Kkeokjeong. Song Song.
The guildmates I had met through new bonds.
My people.
As I watched them race toward me, I let out a weary laugh.

The thorny vines crept upward from my ankles, coiling around my legs, waist, arms, and finally my neck.
Sawtoothed thorns pierced my thin leather armor and dug into my skin.
Beep.
System Paralysis Poison has entered your body!
Nerve Poison has entered your body!
Status abnormality: Poisoned!
What the hell is this?”
“Grrrrr.”
The creature—or rather, Carus—laughed triumphantly.
Its mangled eye was already beginning to return to its original form.
“You. let. your. guard. down. hu. man!”
“Let my guard down?”
I thought for a moment, then nodded.
“Yeah.
I did let my guard down.”
“...Why. are. you. so. calm?”
“When someone acts calm in a situation like this, it usually means one of two things.
Either they’re bluffing their ass off, or...”
Ding.
System The effect of Unaffected by a Hundred Poisons has been applied!
Paralysis Poison has been neutralized!
Nerve Poison has been neutralized!
Status abnormality: Poisoned has disappeared!
“Or they have a good reason not to worry.”
The instant I finished speaking, I stepped forward.
The thorny vines, each as thick as my thigh, tightened around my entire body, but they couldn’t stop me.
“While I’m at it, I’ll splurge on a bonus.
Fifty Strength.
Fifty Stamina.”
Ding.
System 100 Bonus Points have been consumed!
The points have been applied to your stats!
Crack.
Crrrunch.
I tore and shattered the vines with overwhelming power and Strength.
Carus’s magic had been greatly amplified by the dragonkin trait, but the magic itself wasn’t particularly advanced.
“Slow magic, binding magic.
What’s next?”
Its eye had already almost completely healed.
When Carus saw me emerge from the vines unharmed, its maw fell open.
“You...you!”
I brushed the pieces of vine from my arm.
“Don’t you have any other spells?
You were so confident, I thought you’d at least know how to factor, but it turns out you’ve only mastered addition and subtraction.”
“How. did. you?”
“My own magic.”
“Your. own. ma. gic?”
“Yeah.
Magic.”
I shifted the iron spear in my hand into a reverse grip.
That was all the preparation I needed.
This spear was my magic, and the creature would never be able to stop it.
“Huuup.”
I drew a deep breath.
Every muscle in my body meshed together like tiny gears, and the world slowed.
I leaned back and snapped my arm forward, casting a spell I hadn’t quite memorized.
“Burst, sesame.”
Whoosh!
Fwoooooosh!
Against the red sunset staining the horizon, a blue flash plunged into the creature’s eye, which was dyed an even deeper shade of blood.
Burning.
Shattering.
Bursting.
Crack!
“Graa...aaaaaaah!”
I walked toward it as its agonized scream tore through the air.
With every step, familiar faces flashed before my eyes.
Faces I would probably remember until the day I died.
Ever since that day three years ago, shackles had weighed down my ankles.
Anger.
Guilt.
The desire for revenge.
Emotions piled one atop another, layer upon layer.
Their weight had been crushing.
So heavy I couldn’t take a single step forward.
But now...
At some point, I had grown strong enough to bear that weight.
At long last, I could offer some comfort to the spirits of those who had died before me.
Yes.
Finally.
Just as I murmured those words silently in my heart, mana rippled around the creature writhing in pain.
“Kraaaah!
Slow!
Dark Binding!
Magic Arrow!”
Three spells erupted in rapid succession.
I kicked off the ground and charged forward.
The instant I shot beyond Slow’s area of effect like a streak of light, thorny vines and dozens of mana arrows rose to block my path.
Sssshing!
Shrrrk!
Everything was sliced apart along the arc of blue flame.
Sensing that its attack had failed, the creature beat its one remaining wing.
It was such an enormous target that I didn’t even need to aim.
Another flash shot from my hand.
Swoooooosh!
Thud!
“Kyaaaaaaah!”
Whoooosh!
A shrill scream rang out.
Then its spike-covered tail came hurtling toward me with a terrifying roar as it tore through the air.
Boom!
But I had already leaped half a beat ahead of it.
The rocks scattered across the wasteland like reefs rising from the sea shattered into powder.
Open Inventory.
Equip.
As I descended, I swung my spear.
Shraaaak.
The severed tail rolled through the dust with black blood spilling from it.
“Kraaaaah!”
Shrrk.
Shrrk.
Shrrk.
It was like perfectly meshing gears.
I blocked, dodged, and cut through every attack the creature unleashed in its desperate struggle.
Then I realized that no more attacks were coming and stopped.
“Krrk.
Grrrk.”
Two severed wings.
A severed tail.
Two eyes that could no longer function.
The creature lay submerged in a vast pool of blood, ragged breaths rasping from its maw as though each one might be its last.
I watched it for a while before opening my mouth.
“Do you want to live?”
“Then use your healing magic.
I’ll wait.”
“Will. you...save. me?”
“No.
It just feels like a waste to send you off like this.”
“Hold out ten more times.
I’ll kill you after that.”
The creature’s body trembled.
Its gaping eye, pouring dark-red blood like a waterfall, turned toward me.
“You. are. cruel. hu. man.”
“Compared to what you did, this is nothing.”
“I. only. did. what.
I. had. to. do.”
“I know.”
Humans killed monsters, and monsters killed humans.
The two sides had been killing each other for decades.
It was both history and an inescapable cycle.
And...
“I’m no different.”
Completing my revenge—that was what I had to do now.
After a brief silence, a resigned whisper escaped its maw.
“...Kill. me.”
The strength slowly drained from its twitching body.
I aimed my spear between its blood-caked eyes and whispered softly.
“Thank you.”
For staying alive until now.
And for dying by my hand.
With those barely audible words, I drove the spear forward.
Shnk.
The Scorching Yang Qi flowing from the spearhead as it gently pierced through the center of its brow rampaged like a wild beast, devouring and burning everything in its path.
A skull harder than steel.
Flesh.
Brain matter.
Everything else.
Ding.
System You have defeated Lv.115 Carus!
You have achieved the Achievement Named Monster Defeated!
You have achieved a great Achievement.
A corresponding Reward will be granted!
You have perfectly cleared the A-Rank Gate, The Black Wyvern’s Nest!
Calculating all Rewards...
You have acquired an enormous amount of EXP and Fame!
Level Up!
Level Up! . . .
System notifications washed over me like waves.
I released the scorching-hot spear shaft and thought,
I did it.
Finally.
What more was there to say?
The shouts of other people brought me back to myself as I stood there in a daze.
“Mr.
Jin Taekyung!”
“Taekyung!”
Team Leader Choi.
Butler Kim.
Im Kkeokjeong.
Song Song.
The guildmates I had met through new bonds.
My people.
As I watched them race toward me, I let out a weary laugh.

chapters.title: Chapter 223
paragraphs: A thrill.
That was what everyone who had witnessed the battle felt.
They had known for some time that Jin Taekyung was extraordinarily skilled. They had also known that what they had seen so far wasn’t the full extent of his abilities.
But who knew he was this strong?
Team Leader Choi—or rather, Choi Minwoo—swallowed dryly.
Though it had only been a few months, no one had observed Jin Taekyung more closely than he had.
Yet at that moment, Choi Minwoo realized that every judgment he had made about Jin Taekyung had been wrong.
What... exactly is this man?
Everything he had seen until now had been no more than the tip of the iceberg.
A few months ago, when they had first met at a Hunter staffing agency, Taekyung had volunteered to work as a porter for a few hundred thousand won a day.
Now, he had hunted a Named Monster alone.
And utterly overwhelmed it.
Puhk!
The spearhead infused with Aura pierced the monster between the eyes.
It was the moment an immensely powerful Named Monster died at the hands of a single person.
It was also the moment a new legend was born.
“Young Master.”
Choi Minwoo had been dazed for a moment, but Butler Kim’s call finally brought him back to his senses.
When he looked around, everyone had a similar expression.
Shock. And more shock.
Trembling with an indescribable thrill, they rushed toward Jin Taekyung as if by prior agreement.
“Mr. Jin Taekyung!”
“Taekyung!”
Jin Taekyung smiled at them. It was a relieved smile, as if he had finally cast off even the slightest trace of regret.
Choi Minwoo let out a hollow laugh.
“You can smile at a time like this?”
“I don’t know. I can’t think of anything else to do.”
“Then shout, at least. We’re the only ones here anyway.”
“Something like, ‘I killed a Named Monster!’?”
“Yes. Now it’s finally starting to feel real.”
Choi Minwoo stared at Jin Taekyung as he scratched the back of his head, then abruptly held out his hand.
A sentence he had momentarily forgotten had come back to him.
Something he had wanted to say if—just if—Taekyung won.
“Thank you for all your hard work.”
“You’ve truly been through so much.”
For an instant, Jin Taekyung’s eyelids trembled.
An indescribable emotion flickered through his clear, deep-black eyes. Then he firmly clasped Choi Minwoo’s hand.
“Thank you. All of you.”
For a while, I couldn’t come to my senses amid the barrage of questions and congratulations flying at me from every direction.
“So that was already thirty years ago. The Great Cataclysm was still in full swing at the time...”
“Ah, yes.”
Butler Kim, who rarely showed much emotion, excitedly rattled off one incident after another from the Great Cataclysm.
“My goodness. This isn’t a dream, is it? No, it isn’t, right?”
“Uh, no.”
Song Song stared at me as if she still couldn’t tell whether she was dreaming or awake.
“Sniff. Taekyung! You bastard! Sniff, sob!”
“...Why are you crying again, Uncle?”
“Because I’m proud of you, you punk. I’m proud. Sniff!”
Im Kkeokjeong burst into tears as if his own child had made it back alive.
With all that going on, I didn’t have a chance to check the backlog of System messages.
In the end, Team Leader Choi was the one who brought order to the chaos.
“All right, everyone, calm down. Let’s deal with the cleanup first.”
“That’s a good idea, but...”
I cautiously asked the most important question.
“How are we supposed to clean this up?”
“...Oh. Well, you see...”
Even Team Leader Choi, who was never at a loss in any situation, looked flustered.
Cleaning up after a raid was routine, and the work was generally the same every time.
Check and treat the casualties, then sort through and collect the byproducts. If there was anything else, it was usually just inspecting the Equipment.
But this time was different.
This bastard’s torso alone is over fifty meters long.
And that was only counting its length. Its enormous girth, wings, tail, and everything else were separate problems.
Just thinking about how to deal with it was giving me a headache.
But we can’t just leave it here.
Processing the byproducts meant separating the hide, bones, and flesh.
The Carus I had brought down was a Named Monster, so its rarity and the difficulty of processing it were beyond imagination.
Fuck, what are we supposed to do with the scales?
They weren’t fish scales we could scrape off with a kitchen knife.
Aside from me, someone would have to be at least as capable as Butler Kim or Team Leader Choi to handle the job. Of course, there was one possible solution.
There was one method left.
It was both extremely easy and extremely difficult.
Inventory.
Based on everything I had experienced so far, the Inventory’s capacity was practically infinite. Besides, this was a monster’s corpse, not a living creature.
It was worth a try.
The problem comes afterward.
I could already picture everyone’s reaction if I put Carus’s corpse into my Inventory.
Even if I came clean to the guild members, suspicions would arise unless I intended to keep the byproducts forever.
Reporters are camped out at the Gate entrance, so how did he secretly carry all of it outside? Things like that.
If that happened, it might not be long before the entire country learned my secret.
The front pages of the daily newspapers and every news headline would be decorated with my name.
Breaking News: A-Rank Hunter Jin Taekyung Revealed to Be a System User
Interview with Jin Taekyung: “Martial Arts Were the Easiest Part”
Hunter Association: “Jin Taekyung’s Hunter License Must Be Revoked”
Jin Taekyung Blasts Hunter Association: “Fuck, if You Don’t Like It, Use the System Yourselves”
NASA Official Statement: “We Will Capture Him at All Costs and Subject Him to Experiments”
“Mr. Jin Taekyung? Is something wrong?”
“No. Just thinking about it made me dizzy.”
“Pardon?”
“It’s nothing.”
That could never be allowed to happen. Absolutely not.
In the end, after everyone put their heads together, we settled on one solution.
Team Leader Choi announced the verdict with the solemnity of a judge.
“Let’s bring in outside personnel.”
Gates weren’t immutable spaces, unchanging as evergreen trees.

After a certain amount of time, their destroyed environments and monsters were restored. This phenomenon was called Regen, and the time it took for a Gate to undergo Regen varied according to its Grade.
“As far as I know, A-Rank Gates usually undergo Regen once a week. Today is only the first day, so we have plenty of time.”
We would bring in outside personnel as quickly as possible to speed up the work. For now, it was the most reasonable and feasible option.
There was, however, one small problem with the plan.
“The exit Gate hasn’t opened.”
That was exactly what had happened.
Now that we had beaten the Named Monster to death, the exit should have opened. Yet even after several dozen minutes, it still showed no sign of appearing.
Im Kkeokjeong also looked around anxiously.
“Yeah, why hasn’t it opened? Is the Gate broken?”
What a horrifying thing to say.
As if Login Murim wasn’t enough, now there was Login Gate? If that was what this was, I’d rather bite my tongue and die.
Just as an ominous feeling began creeping over me, Butler Kim spoke.
“It appears the boss monster is still alive.”
“Alive? The boss monster?”
I pointed at Carus’s corpse, which lay facedown in a pool of blood, but Butler Kim shook his head.
“Named Monsters and boss monsters are different. To put it simply...the former is an uninvited guest, while the latter is the original homeowner.”
“The homeowner?”
“Yes. This may be easier to understand. If an armed intruder broke into your home, Hunter Jin Taekyung, what would you do?”
“I’d beat him until he begged me to kill him.”
“...I forgot. I meant if you were an ordinary person.”
“Oh. Then I’d run. If I thought I’d die before I could escape, I’d fight back.”
“The boss monster was no different. A powerful foe it could never hope to defeat appeared, so it fled in fear.”
The inside of a Gate was ultimately a world ruled by the law of the jungle.
The strong reigned, and the weak were trampled.

It might have been different for monsters that lived in tribes, but Wyverns were known to be solitary and ferocious. Carus wouldn’t have stopped after giving the boss monster a few knocks on the head and evicting it.
From the boss monster’s perspective, running away had been a fairly wise decision.
Unfortunately, that just made things more troublesome for us.
There was no way the thing had fled for its life only to hang around nearby grooming its claws.
It would have hidden as far away and as secretly as possible. And with only five people, searching this vast wasteland was impossible.
“Then...”
“We’ll have to go back to the entrance we came through.”
It was the obvious conclusion, and the right person for the job had already been decided.
Without giving it much thought, I shot my hand into the air.
“I’ll go.”
Team Leader Choi asked with concern in his eyes.
“You, Mr. Jin?”
“That seems like the fastest option. Doesn’t it?”
“That’s true, but you must be exhausted after the battle.”
I just leveled up, damn it. Let me go.
I swallowed the words that had risen to my throat and answered instead.
“I’m still full of energy. If you’re worried, I can have someone cast healing magic on me before I leave.”
“As you know, it’s a considerable distance to the entrance.”
“As you know, I’m pretty fast.”
It had taken us quite a while to reach this place the first time, but it would be different if I went alone. I wouldn’t have to stay on guard against monsters or match the pace of a group.
If I ran at full speed, I could reach the Gate entrance within an hour or two.
“Hmm. In that case, I’ll leave it to you. You and Butler Kim can go together.”
“Butler Kim, too?”
Butler Kim stroked his impressively full beard as he answered.
“We need to bring in outside personnel.”
Processing the byproducts of a Named Monster required Hunters who were at least B-Rank, if not A-Rank.
“I know a few people. If I go personally, they’ll probably drop everything and come running.”
That sounded about right.
I still couldn’t forget the sight of the Sangdong Guild Master doing PT exercises while loudly repeating orders.
It was something I could hardly believe even after seeing it.
Knowing Butler Kim’s spectacular track record, I could only nod. We needed him if we wanted to bring in outside personnel.
“So it’ll just be Butler Kim and me?”
“Yes.”
Butler Kim nodded and stepped behind me.
“All right. I’m ready.”
“Pardon?”
“Would you bend over a little?”
“...Why do you need me to bend over?”
No, what exactly was he ready for? Why did I need to bend over?
A terrible suspicion crossed my mind.
“You don’t mean...soap?”
“Please carry me on your back.”
“Oh. Sure.”
Thank goodness. He wasn’t a centaur.
I let out a sigh of relief and willingly offered my back to Butler Kim.
Thud-thud-thud-thud-thud!
With Butler Kim on my back, I raced forward without slowing down.
We ran into a pack of Orcs wandering through the wasteland, but that was the only interruption.
“Fire Rain.”
The magic of an A-Rank mage.
One-third of the Orcs died beneath the downpour of fire, and the rest scattered in every direction.
I felt like a mobile turret.
This isn’t bad.
Just as I was thinking about how much more efficient raids would be if I did them this way, we crossed the barren wasteland and spotted a dense jungle ahead.
“You’re astonishingly fast. We’ve already reached the jungle.”
“I’m going to slow down from here. With all this vegetation, we could get lost.”
“I’ll follow your lead, Hunter Jin Taekyung.”
The jungle was nothing but trees and undergrowth, making it a maze where one could easily lose their way.
We slowed down and continued along our bearings.
That was when it happened.
I suddenly stopped, letting out a hollow laugh.
Puzzled by my abrupt halt, Butler Kim asked,
“What is it?”
“It’s nothing. Just...”
How was I supposed to explain this?
At last, I found the right word and added softly,
“There are hyenas.”
“Hyenas?”
“Yes.”
Stupid, persistent hyenas that kept baring their teeth even after I had let them go once.
I crooked my finger toward the dense undergrowth in the distance.
“Come out, you fucking bastards.”
Rustle.
The undergrowth shook, and the hyenas emerged one by one.
But my eyes were fixed on only one person.
System Lv. 80 Won Myunghoon
“Would you look at this insolent bastard.”
The leader of the hyenas bared his teeth and growled.

“As you know, I’m pretty fast.”
It had taken us quite a while to reach this place the first time, but it would be different if I went alone.
I wouldn’t have to stay on guard against monsters or match the pace of a group.
If I ran at full speed, I could reach the Gate entrance within an hour or two.
“Hmm.
In that case, I’ll leave it to you.
You and Butler Kim can go together.”
“Butler Kim, too?”
Butler Kim stroked his impressively full beard as he answered.
“We need to bring in outside personnel.”
Processing the byproducts of a Named Monster required Hunters who were at least B-Rank, if not A-Rank.
“I know a few people.
If I go personally, they’ll probably drop everything and come running.”
That sounded about right.
I still couldn’t forget the sight of the Sangdong Guild Master doing PT exercises while loudly repeating orders.
It was something I could hardly believe even after seeing it.
Knowing Butler Kim’s spectacular track record, I could only nod.
We needed him if we wanted to bring in outside personnel.
“So it’ll just be Butler Kim and me?”
“Yes.”
Butler Kim nodded and stepped behind me.
“All right.
I’m ready.”
“Pardon?”
“Would you bend over a little?”
“...Why do you need me to bend over?”
No, what exactly was he ready for?
Why did I need to bend over?
A terrible suspicion crossed my mind.
“You don’t mean...soap?”
“Please carry me on your back.”
“Oh.
Sure.”
Thank goodness.
He wasn’t a centaur.
I let out a sigh of relief and willingly offered my back to Butler Kim.
Thud-thud-thud-thud-thud!
With Butler Kim on my back, I raced forward without slowing down.
We ran into a pack of Orcs wandering through the wasteland, but that was the only interruption.
“Fire Rain.”
The magic of an A-Rank mage.
One-third of the Orcs died beneath the downpour of fire, and the rest scattered in every direction.
I felt like a mobile turret.
This isn’t bad.
Just as I was thinking about how much more efficient raids would be if I did them this way, we crossed the barren wasteland and spotted a dense jungle ahead.
“You’re astonishingly fast.
We’ve already reached the jungle.”
“I’m going to slow down from here.
With all this vegetation, we could get lost.”
“I’ll follow your lead, Hunter Jin Taekyung.”
The jungle was nothing but trees and undergrowth, making it a maze where one could easily lose their way.
We slowed down and continued along our bearings.
That was when it happened.
I suddenly stopped, letting out a hollow laugh.
Puzzled by my abrupt halt, Butler Kim asked,
“What is it?”
“It’s nothing.
Just...”
How was I supposed to explain this?
At last, I found the right word and added softly,
“There are hyenas.”
“Hyenas?”
“Yes.”
Stupid, persistent hyenas that kept baring their teeth even after I had let them go once.
I crooked my finger toward the dense undergrowth in the distance.
“Come out, you fucking bastards.”
Rustle.
The undergrowth shook, and the hyenas emerged one by one.
But my eyes were fixed on only one person.
System Lv.
80 Won Myunghoon
“Would you look at this insolent bastard.”
The leader of the hyenas bared his teeth and growled.

paragraphs: A few hours earlier, Won Myunghoon’s shout brought the dozen or so Star Guild members racing back toward the Gate entrance to a halt.
“Wait. Everyone, stop!”
Every eye turned toward him.
The terrifying Named Monster could appear behind them at any moment, yet Won Myunghoon had been lost in thought. At last, he opened his mouth.
“Scout.”
“Yes, Guild Master.”
The Guild member assigned to scouting answered immediately.
He was fast on his feet and skilled with a bow. Thanks to the good luck of drawing lots, he had barely escaped death, unlike his other comrades.
“Report our current location.”
“According to the coordinates, we’re at 175, 37, 990.”
“Fuck the coordinates. How far are we from the Gate entrance?”
“At our current pace, approximately seven minutes.”
“Not far, then. This is the only route to the Gate entrance, right?”
“...Yes. It is, but...”
The scout trailed off with an uneasy expression.
The other Guild members sensed something was wrong and exchanged glances. Then a single sentence turned their unease into reality.
“We’ll set up a cordon here.”
“What?”
“You mean a cordon? In this situation?”
“Guild Master, that’s—”
Normally, the Guild members would have obeyed without complaint, but this time they protested. Won Myunghoon’s eyes turned cold.
“Shut up and follow my orders. I have my reasons.”
“Even so, this isn’t right! We’re dealing with a Named Monster—urk!”
Won Myunghoon seized the throat of the Guild member who had raised his voice the loudest and growled.
“You’re disobeying the Guild Master’s orders inside a Gate? Are you that desperate to die, you son of a bitch...?”
It happened in the blink of an eye.
The atmosphere froze. Everyone present knew Won Myunghoon’s words weren’t aimed at just one man.
They had watched him for years. They knew he was more than capable of carrying out his threat.
“I—I’m sorry.”
“This is your last chance. There won’t be another.”
Thud.
Won Myunghoon turned away from the Guild member, who collapsed to the ground with a white face, and swept his sharp gaze across the area.
“Fucking idiots.”
Even in the face of his unfiltered abuse, a dozen pairs of eyes remained fixed on the ground.
They had spent years dealing with Won Myunghoon. This was nothing new.
They had to be even more careful around him inside a Gate. He was an A-Rank Hunter—a powerhouse none of them could defeat even if they attacked him together.
“Do your brains not work? Do I look stupid enough to take on a Named Monster?”
The bowed heads slowly began to rise.
“Then...”
“We’ll deal with those losers.”
“You mean the Peace Guild?”
“By now, they should all be dead.”
While fleeing in a panic, they had heard the monster’s roar. Just hearing it had weakened their knees and sent chills down their spines. It was terror itself.
They hadn’t even seen what the creature looked like, and that was precisely why they were still alive.
How could five people possibly fight something like that? They must all be dead by now.
Every one of them shared that opinion.
Everyone except Won Myunghoon.
“What if even one of them survives and escapes?”
“Th—that...”
“No way.”
They hadn’t considered that possibility.
Under normal circumstances, they might have. But fear of the Named Monster and their desperate will to survive had paralyzed their minds.
Won Myunghoon addressed the hesitant Guild members in a firm voice.
“If even one of those losers gets out of the Gate alive, every last one of us is finished.”
“An A-Rank Hunter who’s been soaking up the media spotlight dies, and then one of the surviving Peace Guild members starts talking about us? I don’t need to explain what happens next, do I?”
The media’s attention—no, the entire country’s—would turn toward them.
Investigators would get involved. The press and broadcast media would treat it as a major story, churning out new reports day after day.
Even if the survivor couldn’t provide definitive testimony or physical evidence, the contempt and condemnation directed at them would never disappear.
They might even have to leave the country. They would be reduced to people who needed a visa just to visit their parents’ graves.
The thought alone was horrifying.
“Sometimes, what people believe matters more than the truth. You all learned that eight years ago, didn’t you?”
“Guild Master!”
“That’s—!”
The Star Guild members erupted in agitation.
It was an unspoken taboo, yet Won Myunghoon himself had brought it up.
Wasn’t he the one who had planned everything and recruited them in the first place?
At the Guild members’ hardened gazes, Won Myunghoon let out a quiet laugh.
“Eyes down, you fucking bastards. Before I rip them all out.”

“You joined because you wanted to. Is there a single bastard here who didn’t take my money? You used it to buy houses and cars, drink and chase women, then got married and had kids. Now you’re all living comfortably, pretending to be good fathers and devoted husbands. Aren’t you?”
Won Myunghoon irritably ran a hand through his hair. Whenever his gleaming eyes swept over them, they trembled.
They wanted to deny it, but every word out of his mouth was true.
They had already crossed a river from which there was no return, and Won Myunghoon was the one who had ferried them to the other side.
The ferryman had already hidden the boat. Without his permission, they could never return to the opposite bank.
Not while they still drew breath.
“I won’t waste any more time talking. Hide and form a cordon. When I give the signal, be ready to kill anyone.”
Won Myunghoon’s voice, thick with killing intent, might as well have been a verdict handed down by the Supreme Court.
Realizing there would be no appeal, the Guild members scattered and began forming the cordon.
“Fucking idiots. It’s already been eight years...”
As Won Myunghoon spat the words through clenched teeth, one of the Guild members cautiously approached him.
“Guild Master.”
“What?”
“Team Leader 1, sir—I mean, what should we do with Team Leader 1?”
“Kim Jonghun? Where the hell is that bastard?”
“We moved him over there for now.”
Won Myunghoon turned his head in the direction the Guild member pointed and let out a hollow laugh.
Only a few meters away, Kim Jonghun was pale and clacking his teeth together. He looked like a man possessed.
“Pathetic bastard. I was the idiot for keeping something like that around and calling him an A-Rank Hunter.”
Won Myunghoon clicked his tongue softly and waved a hand.
“Handle it quietly.”
“What? I—I can’t!”
“What the hell does that mean?”
“I mean I won’t commit murder.”
“What? What the hell is going through that lunatic head of yours—wait.”
Won Myunghoon had been about to smack the Guild member when he suddenly stopped.
He had only meant for them to keep Jonghun quiet with Silence magic or whatever else was necessary.
But did they really need to?
Come to think of it, no one knows more about my secrets than he does.
He had used Jonghun as his right-hand man for a full ten years. The man had a certain low cunning, and his skills as a Hunter were excellent.
Even when that incident had occurred eight years ago, Won Myunghoon had believed that Team Leader 1, if no one else, would never betray him.
If he opened his mouth, he wouldn’t have gotten off unscathed either.
It wasn’t a matter of trust, but mutual interests.
The scale of their greed might differ, but in a sense, the two of them were cut from the same cloth.
But...
He’s useless now.
Won Myunghoon had seen plenty of people exposed to the Fear of high-level monsters.
Their symptoms varied, but they all had one thing in common.
Junk.
Once fear had been branded into their souls, they could never return to the way they had been.
Some went mad and were locked away in special wards. Even those who managed to recover could consider their lives as Hunters over.
He knows more about my secrets than anyone, and he’s the one who personally acquired Yeti’s Necklace.
On top of that, his credentials as an A-Rank Hunter were now worth no more than the paper they were printed on.
Won Myunghoon deliberated only briefly, then reached his decision even faster.
“Tie him up. I have a use for him.”
“What?”
“When that Named Monster comes, don’t you think we’ll need at least one piece of prey to throw to it?”
“It works out well in more ways than one. Since Jin Taekyung is dead, we need to throw in an A-Rank Hunter from our side to make the story convincing.”
Won Myunghoon patted the frozen Guild member on the shoulder as he passed, then concealed himself in the nearby undergrowth.
Come on. Anyone. Come.
He didn’t have to wait long.
When he saw two people emerge through the undergrowth several dozen meters away, the corners of his mouth lifted.
The old Guild Master and Jin Taekyung. Are the others all dead?
Jin Taekyung was covered in blood from head to toe, with an old mage carried on his back.
No matter how Won Myunghoon looked at them, they resembled nothing so much as wounded survivors of a lost battle.
This should be easy.
Jin Taekyung in particular—Won Myunghoon wanted to kill that bastard with his own hands.
He had just finished preparing to signal the Guild members when—
“Come out, you fucking bastards.”
Jin Taekyung crooked a finger directly toward the undergrowth where Won Myunghoon was hiding.
The smile at Won Myunghoon’s lips vanished without a trace.
“Would you look at this insolent bastard.”
Seeing Won Myunghoon’s twisted face, I couldn’t help but laugh under my breath.
How should I put it? I felt like I’d just seen how low a human being could sink.
“You’re laughing?”
Apparently, my reaction made him even angrier. He licked his dry lips and exhaled a hot breath.
“You bastard...do you not understand what kind of situation you’re in?”
“I understand perfectly.”
“And someone who understands the situation is grinning?”
“Choose your words carefully. Hearing you say that makes me want to split your head open.”
“...What?”
“You should’ve stopped when I called you Mr. Won Myunghoon. Won Myunghoon, you fucking bastard.”
The hyenas’ faces went blank.
Won Myunghoon’s lips remained tightly sealed for a long moment before finally opening.
“Have you lost your mind?”
“I’m as sane as ever. Aren’t I, Butler Kim?”
Still on my back and watching the situation unfold, Butler Kim answered.
“Entirely normal. Never losing one’s composure, no matter the situation, is one of the basic qualities a Hunter should possess.”
“What about that bastard?”
“If this had happened during the Great Cataclysm, we wouldn’t have found so much as his corpse. Those were somewhat rougher times.”
“That’s what he says.”
Bang!
A single punch shattered a tree thick enough for a man to wrap both arms around.
Won Myunghoon’s face flushed bright red as he glared at Butler Kim and me.
“You fucking bastards!”
“What a rude bastard. There’s nothing he won’t say to an elder, is there? Right?”
Butler Kim answered calmly.
“The young man does seem somewhat lacking in manners. But isn’t this a good world we live in? We should give him a chance.”
“Is that so?”
“Life is a series of choices. And from what I can see, you appear to have already made yours.”
“You’re a ghost.”
“I don’t particularly care for that word. I am somewhat advanced in age, after all.”
“Sorry. I didn’t mean anything by it.”
“I’ll get down first. One, two, three.”
Crack.
As Butler Kim hopped down from my back, the sound of a bone slipping out of place came from his knee.
“Oh dear, are you all right?”
“My knee has been troubling me. Heal.”
When the glow faded, he tapped his knee a few times and smiled.
“I’m fine now.”
“Wow.”
Magic really was incredibly convenient.
After letting out that exclamation, I turned my head toward the knife-like gazes stabbing in from every direction.
A dozen or so Star Guild members, including Won Myunghoon, were glaring at us as if they wanted to tear us apart and kill us.
“What the fuck are you trying to do?”
“What else? I helped him down. I thought he might get shaken around too much during the fight.”
“Fight?”
“What? Didn’t you come here to fight me?”
“Of course not.”
Won Myunghoon added with a savage laugh,
“We came to kill every last one of you.”
“Oh... You sound exactly like a villain in a web novel.”
I was fairly impressed.
At the same time, the last of my hesitation faded, and my mind became clear.
Right. I just had to do it.
“Thanks for saying that. My headache’s completely gone. Maybe you’re not a son of a bitch after all—maybe you’re Dogvorin.”
“You bastard!”
“Maybe not. Then let’s go?”
“...What?”
Whoosh!
I suddenly found myself wondering what expression Won Myunghoon was wearing.
But then I realized it didn’t matter.
Whatever expression he had worn until now, the one he was about to make had already been decided.
“Bear with the pain. No crying.”
Crack!
As he hurriedly turned and swung his arm, I caught it and twisted it.
The bone snapped in an instant. His grip went limp, and the spear slipped from his hand.
His smooth, unlined face twisted like a demon’s as a scream burst from his throat.
“Gyaaaaaaaaaaah!”
“Didn’t I tell you?”
I continued in a calm voice.
“Never bare your teeth at me again.”
At the same time, I drove my tightly clenched fist into his maw.
Crunch!
