Whatever expression he had worn until now, the one he was about to make had already been decided.
“Bear with the pain.
No crying.”
Crack!
As he hurriedly turned and swung his arm, I caught it and twisted it.
The bone snapped in an instant.
His grip went limp, and the spear slipped from his hand.
His smooth, unlined face twisted like a demon’s as a scream burst from his throat.
“Gyaaaaaaaaaaah!”
“Didn’t I tell you?”
I continued in a calm voice.
“Never bare your teeth at me again.”
At the same time, I drove my tightly clenched fist into his maw.
Crunch!

chapters.title: Chapter 225
paragraphs: Crack!
With a grisly crunch, white teeth shot into the air.
He had taken such meticulous care of them that they gleamed even in the darkness. Not that it mattered anymore.
“Puh-haaaack!”
Thud!
Won Myunghoon flew several meters before slamming his back into a tree and coughing.
The teeth left in his mouth tumbled out with the blood. When he finally raised his head, his face was twisted in shock.
“H-How could this...”
It had all happened in the blink of an eye.
And it wasn’t only Won Myunghoon. Every Star Guild member stared at me in disbelief.
“What do you mean, how? I’m stronger than you. That’s how.”
“T-That can’t be.”
“Yeah. It can.”
I gave him a breezy answer and took a single step forward. Won Myunghoon began to tremble.
“Don’t come any closer!”
“Did I come looking for you? You’re the ones who were waiting for me.”
It was already too late to turn back. I intended to make sure they understood exactly what happened when they bared their teeth at me.
Perhaps sensing the danger, Won Myunghoon shrieked as if having a fit.
“What are you waiting for, you bastards?”
“G-Guild Master.”
“There are only two of them! If we back down now, every last one of us is going to die!”
The hesitant Star Guild members raised their weapons at his command. Won Myunghoon gritted the few teeth he had left.
“I’ll handle this bastard. Get the old man first!”
I stopped.
“What did you just say?”
“Why? Did I hit a nerve?”
Won Myunghoon snorted and glared at me with blazing eyes.
“Jin Taekyung, you bastard. I don’t know what kind of bullshit trick you pulled, but it ends here.”
“Bullshit trick?”
“Don’t play dumb. You obviously found some high-performance acceleration Equipment somewhere and put it on...”
“Oh, that’s what you meant?”
My eyes widened in surprise.
Won Myunghoon’s imagination was impressive. He had somehow managed to rationalize his defeat.
“That’s a pretty original theory. But isn’t the hostage routine a little cliché by comparison?”
“It may be cliché, but the important thing is that it always works.”
“I don’t know about that...”
I let my voice trail off.
While Won Myunghoon and I exchanged those few words, the Star Guild members charged toward Butler Kim with their tanks leading the way.
“I think things might be a little different this time.”
“What?”
The moment Won Myunghoon questioned me, Butler Kim—who had been massaging his lower back—drove his long staff into the ground.
It was a light movement. Yet the power flowing from the tip of his staff shook the earth.
Then his deep voice rang out, like the final switch on a bomb.
“Turn it upside down. Earthquake.”
Rumble!
The primeval forest convulsed.
Cracks split the solid ground. Dirt and rocks shot into the air, exposing the trunks of trees that had sunk their roots deep into the earth. Flocks of nameless birds took flight.
—Screeeech!
They were the only ones able to escape the earthquake.
Unfortunately for the Star Guild members, they had no wings. The cracked and shattered ground surged up like triangular waves and swallowed them whole.
“Everyone, get out of the—urk!”
“Gyaaaaaaah!”
Rooooar!
Once the waves had swept past, only scattered groans and screams drifted through the forest.
The Star Guild members lay crushed beneath an enormous weight of earth and rubble, barely managing to keep their heads exposed as they gasped for breath.
The man who had incapacitated around a dozen veteran B-Rank Hunters with a single spell could not have looked more at ease.
“Young men these days have no respect for their Senior. Stop struggling and close your eyes, all of you—unless you want to be buried alive.”
His voice was chilling, unlike anything I had ever heard from him before.
Only then did the Star Guild members realize the true extent of Butler Kim’s abilities. Their faces went pale, and they lowered their heads.
Well, except for one person.
“An A-Rank mage...!”

A-Rank Hunters were rare, but A-Rank mages and healers were rarer still. The Star Guild members had probably never expected Butler Kim—who always kept his hands folded behind his back and laughed amiably—to be an A-Rank mage.
I grinned at the trembling Won Myunghoon.
“The hostage situation failed. What are you going to do now?”
“That’s why I told you not to bare your teeth.”
Won Myunghoon had been standing there blankly, as if his soul had left his body. At last, he managed to speak.
“What are you? What are all of you?”
“You already know. We’re the Peace Guild. We’d like to live up to our name, but no one around us seems willing to cooperate.”
Won Myunghoon bit his lip.
He could never have imagined that one bad decision would lead to this.
But it was already too late to turn back. A cornered hyena had only two choices left.
Run. Or submit.
Won Myunghoon chose the latter.
Clang!
The spear slipped from his hand and rolled across the ground.
“...I surrender.”
“You surrender?”
I walked toward him. When I kicked the fallen spear far away, he lowered his head in resignation.
“Just like that?”
Even with me standing right in front of him, he didn’t move. I addressed him as he stood there silently with his head bowed.
“Once we get out, you’re looking at life in prison at the very least. You know how serious a crime this is inside a Gate, don’t you?”
After a moment’s hesitation, Won Myunghoon spoke.
“Because it’s better than dying.”
“Better than dying... Yeah, that’s true.”
As long as he survived, there would still be a chance. Death, on the other hand, meant a complete end. Whatever lay beyond it was something he would only discover afterward.
People with a lot to lose tended to fear death. Won Myunghoon was no exception.
“Raise your head.”
“...All right.”
I stared into his eyes.
An unknowable light swirled within those twin pupils, dark as the abyss.
Fear of the future awaiting him. Anxiety over death.
And then...
Thump!
“Taekyung. Please.”
“Just once. Give me one last chance. Killing someone like me will only leave a bad taste in your mouth.”
“It’ll leave a bad taste, but you won’t be punished. If you’re threatened with murder in a Gate, self-defense is recognized. You know that too.”
“B-But still.”
Won Myunghoon swallowed hard.
“If you kill me, it’s murder. That doesn’t change the fact that you’ll become a murderer.”
Murderer.
The word rolling around on the tip of my tongue left a foul taste.
I looked down at Won Myunghoon, kneeling before me and begging for his life in a servile voice, then spoke.
“I’ll trust you.”
“Taekyung!”
“But do me a favor. Don’t betray that trust.”
I tossed him a rope and told him to bind himself. The moment I turned away—
“Ha-ha-ha! You stupid bastard!”
A triumphant shout rang out, and killing intent flared behind me.
I turned my head. Won Myunghoon was already right on top of me, an Aura-infused dagger clutched in his hand.
“Die!”
Whoosh! Slash!
A brief rush of displaced air—and a fountain of blood sprayed upward. The triumphant joy lighting Won Myunghoon’s face gave way to bewilderment.
Thud.
A moment later, something fell to the ground.
It was Won Myunghoon’s wrist, cleanly severed and still clutching the dagger whose Aura had vanished.
“You needed to be at least twice that fast.”
I flicked the blood from the dagger in my hand. In that split second, I had drawn a weapon from my Inventory, and the fight had ended just as quickly.
A brief silence followed, though it felt like an eternity.
Then Won Myunghoon’s mouth slowly fell open, and a horrific scream burst from it.
“Gyaaaaaaaaaaah!”
As I watched him writhe in agony, my heart remained as still and peaceful as a lake.
I felt no betrayal at having trusted someone I should never have trusted. Not even the slightest regret.
Because...
“Thanks. You did exactly what I trusted you to do.”
I had never trusted Won Myunghoon in the first place.
Not since I received Yeti’s Necklace. Not since the moment he ignored my warning and bared his teeth at me again.
“You were always exactly this kind of man.”
“Urgh, gyaaaaah!”
“If I leave you alive, you’ll bare your teeth at me again someday. Like a thorn stuck in my throat, you’ll find some way to come back as long as you survive.”
Slice. Slice.
My dagger severed the tendons in his calf. Blood spattered, and his knee buckled. Just as I pressed the razor-sharp blade against his throat—
“Hunter Jin Taekyung!”
Several dozen meters away, Butler Kim was watching me with concern in his eyes.
“There is no need to go that far.”
“You’re right. That’s why I let him go once.”
“But killing a monster and murdering a person are different. I would rather do it myself—”
I answered calmly.
“I know.”
“...Pardon?”
“I know that perfectly well.”
How many people had I killed by now? Dozens? No, a hundred?
The world I had lived in had never been forgiving. In Gates, I had to kill monsters. In the Murim, I had to kill people.
I was no lofty junzi. I was a Hunter and a martial artist with a family and people I had to protect. If surviving and becoming stronger meant getting blood on my hands, I would do it willingly.
To me, there was little difference between a monster and Won Myunghoon.
Because he’s an enemy.
Whoever the enemy might be, if they could someday bring harm to me or my people, the right thing to do was eliminate the threat at its source.
“So don’t stop me.”
Butler Kim had fought his way through countless battlefields himself.
That brief exchange must have been enough for him to understand what kind of person I was—and what I had decided to do.
He regarded me with a grave look, then gave a small nod.
“Urgh. P-Please, spare me...”
“Spare you?”
I looked down at the groaning Won Myunghoon.
He had once been the idol I looked up to as a child—the man who shone brighter than anyone among countless stars.
But now I would seal those old memories inside a time capsule and bury them deep underground.
I whispered quietly.
“If you were going to kill someone, you should’ve been prepared to die.”
“Ta-Taekyung. Please...”
Slice!
The dagger cut deep into his throat. Won Myunghoon’s eyes bulged as he stared up at me pleadingly.
He tried to cover the wound with his one remaining hand, but he could stop neither the blood nor his life from pouring out.
Grrrgh. Thud.
The moment his body collapsed with a wet, rattling gurgle—
System You have defeated Lv. 80 Won Myunghoon! - You have acquired a considerable amount of EXP!
The System announced the enemy’s death.
“Let’s go.”
Butler Kim nodded as he watched me with a strange look in his eyes.
“We have more baggage to take with us now.”
He waved his staff, and the Star Guild members buried beneath the earth floated gently into the air.
As I watched magical ropes being summoned and binding them tightly together like strings of dried fish, I suddenly spoke.
“Wait a moment, Butler Kim.”
“We need to add one more person.”
A short while later, I followed my Qi Sense and found a gagged man.
For some reason, he had been bound tightly to a tree. And I recognized his face.
“The Star Guild’s Team One Leader?”
Most of the reporters who had flocked to cover the joint raid by the Peace Guild and the Star Guild—or rather, Jin Taekyung and Won Myunghoon’s raid—had left long ago.
But there were always exceptions. One was a young man in thick, horn-rimmed glasses, eating ramen.
“Being the youngest is miserable. Just miserable.”
His colleague snickered and picked up a piece of instant kimchi.
“You’ve only been here two months, and you already have plenty to say.”
“Come on, Senior. You haven’t been here that long either.”
“Hey. Back in my day, I kept my mouth shut and worked. If they told me to stay, I stayed. If they told me to do something, I did it.”
“But isn’t this a bit much? How can they make us wait around for days just to cover one Hunter?”
“You haven’t changed since college. If you don’t like it, stick around long enough to build up some seniority.”
The young man stared glumly into his cup ramen, where beads of oil floated across the surface.
“It’s an A-Rank Gate. It’ll take at least three days for them to come out...”
“Three days? We should count ourselves lucky if they don’t stay the whole week.”
“A week?”
“It’s an A-Rank Gate. Once they’re inside, they might as well get everything they can out of it.”
The young man shuddered as if the mere thought gave him goose bumps.
Seeing groups of other junior reporters in the same miserable situation eating nearby only made him feel worse.
“I wish they’d come out soon.”
“They definitely won’t be out today. Like you said, even if they’re quick, it’ll still take three days. Get some sleep. Want to hit a sauna together? Maybe play some billiards?”
“Billiards?”
“Yeah. There’s plenty to do around here. The local businesses just rip you off.”
“Then maybe one game of billiards...”
Tempted by his Senior’s offer, the young reporter had just begun to rise when—
Whoooooosh.
The enormous door looming before them—the Gate—gave off a strange sound.
The mana that had lain as still as the surface of a lake began to swirl, and urgent shouts erupted from every direction.
“The Gate! The Gate is opening!”
“Already? What the hell?”
“The cameras! Get them over here, now!”
The area fell into chaos in an instant. The reporters who had been idly passing the time shot to their feet and crowded in front of the Gate.
The young reporter and his Senior were no exception. They claimed a spot at the front faster than anyone else, their minds reeling.
“What’s going on? Why are they coming out already?”
“How should I know? Set up the equipment!”
Cameras began rolling, and flashes burst without pause.
The reporters had sensed that something had happened, and their prediction proved exactly right.
Whoosh!
Around a dozen people burst from the swirling vortex of mana.
Everyone who saw them stared with their mouths hanging open.
“...W-What happened?”

chapters.title: Chapter 226
paragraphs: Click, click!
A barrage of camera flashes blinded me. You’d think I would have gotten used to it by now, but apparently I really was a caterpillar that had to eat pine needles.
“Mr. Jin Taekyung! Did you clear the Gate?”
“If not, why did you come out so quickly?”
Questions rained down from the reporters. If the Gate security guards hadn’t been there, they looked ready to jam their microphones into my mouth already.
But the initial frenzy soon died down, and confused voices rose to fill the void.
“But... why is Jin Taekyung covered in blood like that?”
“The numbers don’t add up, either. The people behind him are Star Guild members.”
“They’re even tied up.”
“Where’s Won Myunghoon? I don’t see him, either!”
I could more or less imagine how we looked on camera.
There was me, drenched in the blood of monsters and Won Myunghoon. A dozen or so Star Guild members tied together in a line. And Butler Kim holding the rope as though he were walking a dog.
I can’t blame them for reacting like that.
I licked my dry lips, then shook my head at Butler Kim as he started to step forward on my behalf.
He had tried to stop me, and I had refused. This had happened because of my choice, so it was only right that I deal with the aftermath myself.
“Mr. Jin Taekyung! What happened?”
“Please, just give us one comment!”
The confused murmuring didn’t last long. The moment the reporters caught the scent of a scoop, they went wild.
I calmly watched the frenzied press corps before asking the young reporter at the front a question. He wore thick, horn-rimmed glasses.
“Who do you work for?”
The young man flinched.
“Pardon? M-Me?”
“Yes. You.”
“Uh, well, I...”
He had been shouting the loudest from the front, but apparently hadn’t expected anything like this to happen.
After a brief panic, he finally managed to answer.
“H-HunterTV.”
“Oh. Them.”
HunterTV was a channel that focused on Hunter-related issues and information.
It was a cable channel, but it was also a major broadcaster whose ratings surpassed those of terrestrial networks.
Since it was connected to what I was about to say, both the reporter and I were lucky.
“I’ll take your questions.”
“Pardon?”
“There are too many microphones. I’d rather focus on one.”
“So... an exclusive?”
“Call it whatever you want. Shall we begin?”
He looked like a greenhorn, but a reporter was still a reporter.
The bewilderment vanished from his face, and his eyes gleamed behind his glasses.
“How about broadcasting it live?”
“Live?”
“Yes. Like at the Association last time. We can stream it in real time.”
A live stream.
After a moment’s thought, I nodded.
“Let’s do that.”
iTube was the number-one video-sharing website.

Countless channels, belonging to everyone from individuals to major organizations, were registered on the platform. Among them, HunterTV was a massive channel with several million subscribers in Korea alone.
At the same moment, the phones of HunterTV subscribers going about their daily lives all buzzed with the same notification.
Bzzzz.
[HunterTV has started a live stream.]
[“Jin Taekyung Exclusive Live Broadcast.”]
The view count hit 100,000 in no time.
The sudden influx of viewers had left the screen black, but the chat was already blazing like a furnace packed with firewood.

└ What is this? Why is there suddenly an exclusive Jin Taekyung live broadcast? └ No idea. Feels like it hasn’t even been a day since Lord Fuck entered the Gate. └ It’s an A-Rank Gate. He’s already out? └ This buffering is absolute garbage. └ Now I want some Butter Rings. └ Oh, the picture’s up. └ Everyone shut up and welcome Lord Fuck with the proper reverence.
Pop.
The brief but seemingly endless buffering finally ended, and the video began to play.
The moment the viewers saw the enormous Gate and the young man standing before it, their fingers flew across their screens.
└ It’s Lord Fuck! └ Oh my god, fuck. └ Please insult me! └ Smack my ass, too! └ Cut it out, you lunatics.
Jin Taekyung’s popularity was through the roof.

He had saved countless lives by suppressing a B-Rank Gate. His approachable, down-to-earth demeanor, unexpected from an A-Rank Hunter, and even the bizarre spectacle of him accidentally swearing during an official press conference had kept him at the center of attention day after day.
But the excitement didn’t last long. The viewers soon noticed that something was wrong.

└ Why does he look like that? └ Did Lord Fuck get hurt? He’s covered in blood. └ Half the people are missing, too. And the ones there are tied up;; └ What the hell is this? Something happened. └ What’s HunterTV doing? If you started a broadcast, at least ask some questions.
Perhaps mindful of the chaos in the chat, the HunterTV reporter finally spoke.
“I’ll get straight to the point. What happened inside the Gate?”
“It would take too long to explain everything from beginning to end... Is it all right if I summarize?”
“Please do.”
Vrrrrr.
The camera zoomed in until Jin Taekyung’s face filled the screen.
His face was smeared with blood and dust, but his eyes shone calmly. Then a composed voice flowed between his parted lips.
“There was a Named Monster.”
“It was a Mutated Gate.”
In an instant, the noise at the scene vanished as though someone had pressed the mute button.
The chat froze for a moment, then began racing upward.
└ ?? └ ??? └ Wait, why is there a Named Monster here └ They must all be dead. No wonder so many people are missing;; └ Is Won Myunghoon dead, too? I haven’t seen him since earlier; └ Holy shit...
A major incident.
The same words flashed through everyone’s minds.
Even the reporter holding the microphone out to Jin Taekyung forgot his job and stood there with his mouth hanging open.
A Named Monster.
Everyone knew the kind of destruction one could cause.
Five years earlier, a Named Monster that appeared in Central and South America had possessed enough power to destroy a small city by itself.
Although it had finally been defeated after several days of fighting, the damage had been enormous.
Hundreds of Hunters had died, along with ten times as many civilians.
The incident had drawn the attention of the entire world. There wasn’t a reporter or viewer who hadn’t heard of it.

└ If it really was a Named Monster, surviving was a miracle; └ No. Wait a second. └ Then that means there’s still a Named Monster inside the Gate └ So what? It’s inside the Gate. Isn’t it fine? └ Did this bastard just get here from Mars? You idiot, don’t you know what happens when the mana level exceeds a Gate’s capacity? The monsters come pouring out. └ That catastrophe in Central and South America a few years ago happened because the mana level exceeded the limit and the Gate opened;; └ The Black Wyvern’s Nest? Does anyone know where that is? └ Holy shit;; Get the reporters out of there first.
The reporters who had been staring back and forth between Jin Taekyung and the chat as if hypnotized suddenly snapped out of it.
“A Named Monster!”
“Hey, get out of here right now! Grab the cameras!”
No scoop was worth more than their lives.
Just as the reporters, sensing the threat of death, began wading into chaos, someone who had been watching the entire situation finally spoke.
“Ah, I already took down the raid monster, so you don’t have to worry too much.”
His clear voice rang in everyone’s ears.
The reporters who had been trying to flee in a panic and the viewers staring at their phone screens while swallowing nervously both wondered if they had heard correctly.
“Pardon?”
“...What did you say?”

└ ??? └ I think I heard that wrong. └ What did Lord Fuck just say? └ He says he killed a Named Monster...? └ Who did? └ Lord Fuck. └ What did he kill? └ A Named Monster. └ Can he even do that? └ I don’t know...
The camera, which had been shaking as though caught in an earthquake, steadied and refocused. Dozens of cameras turned toward the young man’s perfectly calm face.
The reporter in horn-rimmed glasses asked Jin Taekyung in a trembling voice,
“C-Could you say that one more time?”
“It’s just as I said.”
“Then you really killed the Named Monster...”
“Yes. I killed it.”
He killed it? A Named Monster?
Everyone’s jaws dropped at the unbelievable words that had come from Jin Taekyung’s mouth. One reporter finally recovered enough to blurt out a question.
“T-Then did the others die in the process?”
“Seven people died. The rest are safe...”
His voice trailed off. After thinking for a moment, he continued in the same unwavering tone.
“Oh, I should add Won Myunghoon to the death toll. That makes eight.”
“W-Won Myunghoon? Why did he...”
“Uh, well...”
Jin Taekyung hesitated briefly before adding,
“I got him.”
“...Pardon?”
“Ah, not got. I killed—no, that sounds strange, too. Give me a moment.”
Before the aftershock of the Named Monster bomb had even faded, a second bomb went off.
The dozens of reporters at the scene and the 100,000 viewers watching the screen were left half dazed.
What the hell is he talking about?
At the exact moment the same thought crossed everyone’s mind, Jin Taekyung finally found what he considered the most appropriate expression.
“This is probably the best way to put it. I ‘disposed of him.’”
At the end of the heavy silence, a single new line appeared in the frozen chat.
└ Did this guy just come back from sorting recyclables at home?
Everything moved swiftly from there. The emergency investigation team dug into the truth of the incident with speed and precision.
Countless eyes were on the case. If they missed even a single detail, they might receive a lifetime’s worth of abuse.
“Handle this properly. Miss even one thing and you’re finished—finished!”
“This has already been reported all the way to the Blue House. If we slip up, we’re all going over the cliff together.”
Both the government and the Hunter Association’s leadership were on edge.
Contrary to their fears, however, it didn’t take long for the whole truth to come to light.
“Holy shit... He killed this thing by himself?”
“He actually killed it.”
The investigators were stunned when they confirmed that the enormous Named Monster lay gruesomely dead.
By then, every Star Guild member who had participated in the raid was tied to a cold metal chair in an interrogation room.
“I don’t know anything.”
“Look, Hunter. The truth will come out soon enough. Why make this difficult?”
“I’m telling you, I don’t know anything.”
“Ha, you bastard... You’d spill everything with one mental spell, but you still have to be annoying.”
“Did you just swear at me? You think being a prosecutor means you can do whatever you want? And don’t you know mental magic is illegal?”
Their lives were on the line. They couldn’t give up the comfortable lives they had enjoyed as B-Rank Hunters and rot in prison for the rest of their days.
The prosecutors were racking their brains over the Star Guild members’ stubborn denials when an unexpected savior appeared.
“I-I’ll tell you everything.”
Kim Jonghun, Team 1 Leader of the Star Guild, was still mentally shaken when he confessed to everything that had happened.
It was a perfect testimony. On top of that, an anonymous informant had sent a USB drive and a note.

The Hapsburphon family, a long-established German family of equipment makers, has produced rare and highly practical items. One of their representative products is the PSV-96K camera, which cannot be detected by any detection magic and functions normally even in Gates with unstable mana...
The prosecutor in charge stared incredulously at the note before asking the investigator,
“What is this supposed to mean?”
“They filmed the entire raid. There’s footage on the USB. Open it and you’ll see. That bastard Won Myunghoon was a real piece of shit.”
“Filming is illegal, isn’t it?”
“It is.”
“It was the Peace Guild, right?”
“Wouldn’t you say so?”
“Let that much slide. Every Guild with enough clout does it. They didn’t leak it to civilians, and thanks to them, we secured conclusive physical evidence. We both benefit from this...”
Bang!
An employee burst through the door and thrust out his phone.
“H-Have you seen this?”
The number-one real-time search term was boldly displayed across the screen:
“Won Myunghoon Raid Footage Leaked.”
As the ugly side of a former star people remembered fondly was revealed, the internet boiled like a cauldron over hot coals.

└ What a fucking bastard. └ My head is ringing. Is this really true? It’s not staged, is it? └ Good riddance. Taekyung was right to kill him. └ Still, it was clearly murder. Did he really have to kill Won Myunghoon...? └ Myunghoon, is that you? └ Does Wi-Fi reach hell? └ Did Yama turn on his hotspot for you? └ You’re calling this murder? Have you never heard of self-defense?
Only two days had passed since the incident. Yet the backlash was fiercer than anything people could remember.
Each time another long-buried suspicion about Won Myunghoon came to light, public fury boiled over anew.
And after every wave of still-smoldering rage had swept through, the discussion always ended with the same question.
└ So what is Jin Taekyung doing? └ At this hour? Probably sleeping. └ Probably sorting recyclables.

chapters.title: Chapter 227
paragraphs: “Thank you for all your hard work.”
A man in a rumpled suit held out his hand.
His skin was dry and his eyes were sunken. Apparently, the investigator hadn’t been exaggerating when he said the man hadn’t been home in a week.
“You’re the one who worked hard, Prosecutor. Me? Not really.”
I shook hands with the prosecutor in charge and looked around.
The spacious room had a soft bed, a sofa, and even a state-of-the-art wall-mounted TV.
When I was first summoned by the prosecutors’ office, I had imagined a cold, dark interrogation room. Instead, they had put me up in a hotel suite.
“I didn’t expect to be treated this well.”
“The higher-ups are very interested in this case. Would you mind if I sat down for a moment?”
“Oh, sure.”
“Thank you.”
The prosecutor answered wearily and collapsed onto the sofa.
“There was some debate, to be honest. We had quite an argument over whether your actions constituted self-defense or excessive force.”
That part had been bothering me, too.
I had killed Won Myunghoon when I could have subdued him. It went beyond the bounds of self-defense.
Of course, even if I went back a week, I would make the same choice.
“So I assume the issue was resolved in my favor?”
“Of course. Do you think I would’ve come alone otherwise? I would’ve brought Hunters from the Ministry of Justice.”
The prosecutor spoke jokingly, but then his eyes fell on the morning paper lying on the table.
The Black Wyvern’s carcass filled nearly the entire front page. He eyed it and smacked his lips.
“Though even if I had brought them, they probably wouldn’t have been much help.”
“I’m a model citizen. The kind who could live just fine without laws.”
“There was a movie called Law Abiding Citizen. The protagonist killed a prosecutor and even a judge.”
What was this? Was he asking me to hit him?
The prosecutor let out a quiet laugh at my expression and stood.
“I should get going. I have an incredible backlog of work.”
“I’m glad I could lend a hand.”
“You didn’t lend a hand. You created the work. Once we started digging, every lead pulled up another, like sweet-potato vines.”
I had suspected that Won Myunghoon had plenty of skeletons in his closet.
But once the investigation began in earnest, so much filth came pouring out of his past that I found myself wondering what kind of bastard he had been.
Among his countless crimes were several cases similar to what had happened a week ago.
The incident eight years ago was no different.
Won Myunghoon had been a monster created by the media.
When his brief burst of popularity faded and the spotlight moved on, he tried to stir up scandals himself to draw the public’s attention back to him.
But in the process, the most popular star Hunter of the time died. Under suspicion from the Association and uneasy scrutiny from the public, Won Myunghoon quietly faded from memory.
“He covered up everything thoroughly. With money, with power, and sometimes by making people disappear in what looked like Gate accidents.”
Naturally, there had also been extensive lobbying to minimize the incidents.
In the end, the political and business figures connected to him had to appear before the cameras in wheelchairs and masks.
Along with their favorite line:
I will cooperate fully with the investigation.
Whether the investigation would be conducted properly, or whether they would cooperate in good faith, remained to be seen. But one thing was certain.
The prosecutor spoke with conviction.
“At least half of them are going down.”
The wildfire was already spreading out of control. Putting it out would take more than uprooting a weed or two.
Won Myunghoon’s death had only been the beginning.
“I hope that’s what happens.”
“It has to. It will.”
He offered what sounded like a farewell and reached for the doorknob. Then he paused and turned around.
“I’ve been so busy that I forgot to say this.”
His previously straight back bent in a deep bow.
“Thank you. All of this is thanks to you, Mr. Jin Taekyung.”
I’m a simple man. I killed the raid monster because I had a grudge to settle, and I killed Won Myunghoon because he was my enemy.
But the world called me a hero who had prevented a major catastrophe and brought justice.
It was a little burdensome, but...
Well, this isn’t so bad either.
I smiled and nodded. A faint smile crossed the prosecutor’s exhausted face.
I followed the investigator I had gotten to know over the past week down to the basement.
“You don’t need to worry. Security is airtight.”
Just as he had said, there wasn’t a reporter—or even a camera—in sight in the underground parking lot.
Instead, some familiar faces were waiting for me.
“Son!”
“Oppa!”
Two people rushed at me with shrieks, and I hugged them both.
No, let me correct that. I hugged Mom and pushed Hayeon away with my palm.
“Son! Are you all right? You’re not hurt anywhere?”
“I’m fine. Just a few scratches.”
Looking as if she’d just had ten years scared off her life, Mom ran her hands over my entire body. Then she sucked in a breath.
“S-Scratches? Where? You’re hurt?”
“No, I misspoke.”
“You said you got scratched!”
“I said I wanted some of your saengchae muchim. The words just came out wrong.”
“Taekyung, you’re lying again, aren’t you? You fought a terrifying monster like that. How could you not have a single injury?”
“It was big, but it was a gentle kid.”
“Son, are you going to keep playing word games? Mom is being serious, so hurry up and take off your clothes.”
“...How am I supposed to do that here? This is driving me crazy.”
I had the reflexes to dodge bullets, but somehow I couldn’t evade Mom’s hands.
Had she learned a grappling technique or something?
As I struggled helplessly, my household-register mate with the other set of chromosomes asked with a shocked expression,
“...Why did I get pushed away?”
“You really have to ask?”
“I’m asking because I don’t know.”
“Then you deserve a hit.”
Flick!
“Ow! Mom! Oppa hit me!”
“Can’t either of you behave?”
Hayeon clutched her forehead with a wounded expression while Mom shouted at us.
In the middle of the chaos, I noticed someone watching us with a smile.
“Don’t just stand there smiling. Please stop them.”
“Isn’t this proof that your family is close? I’m actually jealous.”
His legs were long and straight, like a model’s. He looked as though he had just stepped out of a magazine shoot as he gripped my shoulder firmly.
“You’ve been through a lot, Mr. Jin Taekyung.”
“You too, Team Leader Choi.”
But where was everyone else?
Team Leader Choi noticed me looking around and spoke.
“They all wanted to come, but I stopped them. There are too many eyes watching us.”
“Oh.”
“Reporters are camped out everywhere. I’ll take you home first. We can talk on the way.”
An underground parking lot wasn’t exactly the best place to catch up. Especially not with a prosecutor’s investigator watching us.
We climbed into a high-end sedan with heavily tinted windows. The car purred pleasantly as it wound through the forest of skyscrapers.
“A great deal happened while you were being questioned, though I assume you know most of it.”
“I saw it all on TV. I turned off my phone because I was getting so many calls.”
Network TV, cable, radio.
These days, wherever I turned, I heard my name and Won Myunghoon’s.
Politics, the economy, the Hunter industry—the whole country was in an uproar.
I’ve heard it so much I’m sick of it.
Even the national anthem got tiring after the second verse.
Team Leader Choi glanced at my expression and smiled.
“There’s one important thing I should tell you.”
“It’s not about what we’re having for dinner, is it?”
“No. It’s related to what happened.”
“Team Leader, please. I’m begging you.”
“It concerns the processing of the Named Monster’s byproducts.”
“Please tell me. I’m begging you.”
I sat up straight in the passenger seat and gazed at Team Leader Choi with sparkling eyes.
Mom and Hayeon, sitting in the back, perked up their ears as well.
“Byproducts? Are they really that important?”
“Mom, what are you, someone from the Korean Empire? Of course they’re incredibly important!”
“Oh, please. Mom knows that much. I just don’t have any idea how important...”
Plenty of products made from monster byproducts had been commercialized, but they were still luxuries reserved for the wealthy.
To Mom, who had spent her entire life tightening her belt, they might as well have belonged to another world.
As Mom trailed off, Team Leader Choi explained in a gentle voice.
“It depends on the monster. But in the case of the Named Monster Mr. Jin Taekyung killed, its value is astronomical.”
“R-Really? I only saw it in photographs, but it did look terrifying.”
“As you saw, it was an extremely powerful monster. That’s why it was valued at three hundred billion won.”
“Oh, I see.”
A brief silence followed Mom’s answer.
There wasn’t even the sound of breathing. In the complete silence, I blinked without a word, then barely managed to speak.
“How much?”
“Three hundred billion won.”
Team Leader Choi added in the same calm tone,
“Oh, that’s the auction’s starting price.”
“T-The starting price?”
“Yes. The processing was completed three days ago, and Christie’s has already...”
“Wait. Who’s Christie?”
Hayeon stared at me in disbelief.
“What do you mean, who’s Christie? You don’t know Christie’s?”
What an idiot. And he’s my brother.
That was exactly what her expression said.
I racked my brain to preserve my authority as her older brother, but the only thing the name Christie brought to mind was a beautiful blonde woman.
“A-American billionaire’s daughter?”
“O-Or someone from Hong Kong? European royalty? A Hollywood actress...”
Team Leader Choi came to my rescue as I broke into a cold sweat.
“It’s a famous auction house. Along with Sotheby’s, it competes for the top position in the industry.”
“Oh.”
Maybe I had heard of it. Or maybe I hadn’t.
I had spent my childhood doing nothing but exercising and my adulthood working like an ox. How was I supposed to know about things like that?
Team Leader Choi, who was knowledgeable about such matters, continued smoothly.
“Christie’s approached us first. They offered to charge a much lower commission than Sotheby’s if we entrusted the auction to them.”
“S-So?”
“Christie’s appraisers assessed the value of the byproducts. At present, the starting price is three hundred billion won. Since the decision requires your consent, we’ve put off finalizing it.”
Was this really happening?
I sat there dazed with my mouth hanging open, then smacked Hayeon on the forehead as she poked her head between the driver’s and passenger’s seats.
Smack!
“Ow!”
“It’s real.”
“Why did you hit me?”
“Because I’m precious.”
Only after hearing her scream did it finally sink in.
Before long, I would be an incredibly wealthy man.
“S-Son, what does this mean? Three hundred billion won?”
“Calm down. It’s not all mine.”
I didn’t know how high the final bid would go, but the Hunter industry had clear rules for dividing the proceeds. Raids were team efforts, after all.
Even if I had killed it entirely by myself, the same principle applied.
But Team Leader Choi’s next words left me stunned.
“It’s your share, Mr. Jin Taekyung. Every last won.”
“...Pardon?”
“The others all agreed. So I hope you won’t say anything more about it.”
“They all agreed?”
They could each have received anywhere from several billion won at the low end to tens of billions of won at the high end.
For an ordinary person, it would have been an irresistible temptation—and clearly their right to claim.
As I stared at him in shock, Team Leader Choi smoothly turned the steering wheel and replied,
“Neither I nor the others are shameless enough to take money for standing around and watching. We have at least that much conscience and conviction.”
“You really didn’t have to go that far...”
“It wasn’t something that required any consideration. You’ve shown us enough consideration already, so think about what you want to do with the money.”
Team Leader Choi’s firm words left me speechless.
Three hundred billion won. Christie’s auction.
The words swirled through my head, leaving my thoughts in chaos. Mom and Hayeon had been frozen like statues for a while now, so they were probably even worse off.
This is surreal.
I rubbed my stiff face with one palm.
An unimaginable fortune would soon come rolling into my hands. What should I do with it?
One fantasy led to another. A private jet, a luxury yacht, bundles of cash stacked like mountains, a leopard wearing a collar...
Before long, every one of those fantasies faded like fog.
Only then did my head clear. I finally knew what I should do with the money, and I could see the world around me clearly again.
“Team Leader Choi.”
“Yes?”
“May I ask you for a favor?”
The corner of Team Leader Choi’s mouth lifted slightly.
“Anything.”

chapters.title: Chapter 228
paragraphs: Time flew.
One issue followed another, each bigger than the last, while new truths and suspicions continued surfacing everywhere.
A week passed in the blink of an eye. Then a new article took over the portal sites.
[GojoseonTV] Christie’s Auction Held in Secret. Winner: Qatar’s Prince Cheonsur. Final Bid: Approximately 500 Billion Won!
The short article included only a single photograph, but its impact was enormous.
Behind the broadly grinning Middle Eastern prince in a turban loomed a gigantic carcass.

└ Top Comment: Isn’t that the thing Lord Fuck caught? That Named Monster? └ Yeah I’ve seen it so many times I can recognize it just from the hide pattern. But some lunatic actually paid 500 billion for that thing. └ The Middle Eastern prince’s sheer class blew me away, and Lord Fuck making 500 billion in one shot made me shit myself. └ Son, what did you shit? You haven’t been looking at anything strange, have you? Mom trusts her son. Love you~
Most people were envious or impressed, but some viewed the news less kindly.

└ Top Comment: Jin Taekyung stirred up all kinds of trouble, refused to give a single interview, then sold the monster behind everyone’s backs. Am I the only one bothered by this? └ Personally, I really don’t like him. Killing Won Myunghoon on his own authority was excessive force, if you look at it one way. But the prosecutors’ office only questioned him as a witness and then quietly let the matter fade away. It feels like they’re giving him special treatment because he’s famous. └ Same. Upvoted.
There was a saying that when your cousin bought land, your stomach hurt.
If even the success of friends and relatives could make someone jealous, then a celebrity they knew only through the media stood no chance.
Not long after the article went up, a bloody battle broke out among the netizens.

└ Top Comment: Are the bastards commenting above the Three Stooges? └ I’m more shocked that garbage has over a thousand upvotes lol. Why are there so many bastards who can’t stand seeing someone else succeed? └ Exactly. What trouble did he supposedly cause? Did the Dodong Sect punch a hole through their brains? How many people are alive thanks to Lord Fuck by now? └ Jin Taekyung... Well, look at this rotten son of a—... As a public figure... what a wicked man, filling only his own pockets... Never forget that the entire nation is watching @~! └ “Self-interest,” lol. The only interest here is the deposits building up in your parents’ bodies; what’s coming out of my mouth is pure profanity. └ What are you talking about, public figure? He was a hyung who was wearing sweatpants and boiling ramen in the corner of his room until a month ago. And that way of talking is disgusting. └ You young whippersnappers... Such sharp tongues you have~!!! └ Dentures confiscated for one month. └ Hearing aid confiscated for two months. └ Banned from the senior center for three months.
Even as people everywhere had their dentures and hearing aids confiscated and were banned from the senior center, the fighting didn’t stop.
Despite the fierce backlash, Jin Taekyung’s critics stubbornly continued making their case.

└ You little brats... hehe. You’ve put knives on your fingertips... You ignorant, rotten bastards~~!! Ignoring you... is the answer! @!~~ └ Cane confiscated. └ I don’t use a cane... you bastard~~ └ Wheelchair confiscated. └ You nameless lowlifes... How dare you come here spouting that commie nonsense...!!! └ Park Hyeongseok. I gave you my name. Happy now? └ Young Hyeongseok, go back to your mommy, drink some more milk, and study harder~~`!! └ You go drink some more. └ You goddamn lowborn son of a bitch.
It was a bloodbath.
In a single day, the article reached one million views and racked up tens of thousands of comments.
As the two sides traded barbed comments and snarled at each other, another article went up.
[HunterTV Exclusive] Jin Taekyung Donates Hundreds of Billions to Gate Victims and Establishes Support Foundation
Hunter Jin Taekyung has drawn attention by donating hundreds of billions of won and establishing a support foundation for Gate victims under the name of the Peace Guild.
The necessary procedures had been set in motion even before the Christie’s auction began...

└ Top Comment: Everyone who called him a public figure and accused him of lining his own pockets, assemble. Heads to the floor. └ Tsk, tsk... Nothing has even been properly revealed yet, and you’re already running your filthy mouths... Open your eyes to the truth...! └ LOL. Hey, are you crying? └ LMAOOOOOO └ But seriously What the hell is with him giving away hundreds of billions? Honestly, that’s even more amazing than the satisfaction of seeing all those bastards who were maliciously stirring things up get shut down. └ Agreed. What the hell is Lord Fuck? Is it just easy for someone at his level to make money, so he decided to go big? └ I don’t think that’s it. He just doesn’t seem greedy for money. Either way, I’m genuinely impressed. └ Height, looks, character, money. He has everything. Isn’t that cheating? └ P3C, P3C... └ What does P3C mean? └ Please have a three-centimeter dick. └ Oh.
The battle ended in defeat for the trolls, and public opinion once again filled with admiration for Jin Taekyung.
He had already prevented two major catastrophes and possessed the strength to defeat a Named Monster single-handedly. Now he had shown the generosity to donate hundreds of billions of won as well.
His image as an unassuming hero and a truly big-hearted man was now firmly cemented.
—Let me update you on the progress of the foundation...
“Team Leader Choi.”
I cut off Team Leader Choi’s voice over the phone in a trembling voice.
“That’s enough. Please don’t say any more.”
—...If it pains you that much to part with the money, should I cancel the foundation?
“No. Absolutely not!”
—Then why are you acting like this?
“It still hurts.”
—Pardon?
“It hurts to give it up, but it needs to be done. Please keep going.”
—Is it like looking at a rice cake in a painting?
“No, it’s a rice cake in my hand. I’m starving to death and barely stopping myself from eating it.”
The secret Christie’s auction attended by wealthy people from around the world had ended not long ago.
Exactly twenty-four hours later, an endless string of zeros appeared in my bank account.
Five hundred billion.
To be exact, after every fee had been deducted, it came to roughly 530 billion won.
The unit wasn’t hundreds or thousands. It was eok—hundreds of millions.
It was literally an eok-inducing sum, and I nearly cried out myself.
How much money was this, exactly?
It was an astronomical amount—enough to change my life, no, enough to let me and my descendants live in luxury for generations.
But I had already decided where the money should go and how it could be used in the most proper and worthwhile way.
“So please keep going. I’m leaving it all in your hands, Team Leader Choi.”
—Understood. We’ll begin with the people on the list you gave us last time.
“Please take good care of them.”
The families of the teammates whose lives had stopped on that day three years ago would be the foundation’s first recipients.
The money couldn’t fill the empty spaces left by their lost family members, but it could help them pursue their dreams without having to worry about anything.
—Next are the veterans of the Great Cataclysm and single-parent families. Is that correct?
“Yes. Please proceed that way.”
After exchanging a few more words, I ended the call.
When I left the room, I found Mom and Hayeon sitting at the kitchen table eating fruit.
The moment I approached, a fork with a piece of apple speared on it suddenly appeared in front of me.
“Son, have some apple. It’s sweet.”
“Uh, okay.”
Crunch.
The sweet flesh broke apart in my mouth. I quietly ate the fruit while listening to the two of them talk.
Friends, studying, someone who lived nearby, dramas...
Sometimes I laughed quietly. Other times I nodded along.
Then, without warning, I spoke.
“Everyone’s okay, right?”
“Hm? What do you mean, son?”
“What?”
“I mean... with everything that happened. Anything at all.”
Hayeon cocked her head.
“Are you trying to talk about the money?”
“I knew it. Mom, didn’t I tell you yesterday? I said this guy would definitely be like this.”
Mom smacked Hayeon’s twig-thin forearm.
“You! How can you call your brother, who’s eight years older than you, ‘this guy’?”
“Ow! That hurts. Stop hitting me.”
Hayeon grumbled, folded her arms, and leaned back in her chair.
“Excuse me.”
“...Excuse me?”
“What would you rather I call you? My family-register roommate?”
She was my one and only little sister, eight years younger than me. Normally, I would have flicked her forehead for the fun of it, but somehow, today wasn’t the time.
Hayeon looked at me and let out a deep sigh.
“Oppa.”
“Hm?”
“What does Mom say more than anything else?”
I wondered. What was it?
I didn’t have to think long. I heard it whenever I came home—or at least once every few days over the phone.
“Be careful?”
“Right. You know it well.”
She poked the apple and held the fork out to me.
“Eat. Eat, and be careful.”
“What good would hundreds of billions do us? Forget not being able to spend it all. We obviously wouldn’t even know how to spend it properly.”
I mechanically chewed the apple in my mouth. It was sweet, and it stung like fire—enough to make the tip of my nose tingle.
When did she grow up so much?
This had been a difficult choice for me.
The truth was, I wasn’t particularly good or righteous.

I was just an ordinary older brother who wanted to give his only sister everything she asked for, and an ordinary son who wanted his mother, after all the years she had struggled alone, to finally live in comfort.
And hundreds of billions of won was more than enough to make every fantasy I had ever imagined a reality.
With this much money...
I had agonized over it. Even after making my decision, I kept agonizing.
But all of it had been pointless.
People praised me as both a hero and a big-hearted man, but they were wrong.
My sister, eight years younger than me, had a far bigger heart than I did.
She had inherited all of Mom’s best qualities. Even her eyes curved into the same crescents when she smiled.
“Son, as I always say...”
“No parent in the world could spend money their child earned by shedding blood. Yes, I know.”
“Good. You know it well.”
“But you’ll have to start spending some now. I plan to earn a lot more.”
“Then buy me a massage chair.”
“A massage chair?”
“Yeah. I wondered what I’d want first if my son became successful and offered me a present, but that was the only thing I could think of.”
I laughed along with Mom.
My heart felt lighter, as though I had finally set down a heavy burden I had carried for a long time.
“Then let’s go look at one together tomorrow. We can look at furniture while we’re at it.”
“Furniture?”
“Come to think of it, the furniture in our house is pretty old, too. Mom, when someone offers you something like this, you’re supposed to accept it.”
I wondered what expression she would make when she learned that the furniture was for the house we would soon be moving into.
Even more so when she discovered it was the place where the three of us had lived back when we were a family of four.
I’d love to go there right now, but...
I wanted to save that pleasure for tomorrow—or rather, for what came next.
Realizing the time had finally come, I rose from my seat.
“Where are you going?”
“Son, there’s still plenty of fruit left.”
I smiled broadly at the two disappointed faces and answered,
“It’s okay. I think I’ll take a nap.”
This time, I was going to sleep for a very long time.
Whoooosh.
The winter wind blew, the season already drawing to an end. Darkness had long since swallowed the world outside, while the brightly lit pavilion glowed against the night.
The old man watching the wavering flames suddenly spoke.
“Who’s there?”
A clear voice answered moments later.
“It’s me.”
“...Is that you?”
At first, he hadn’t been able to tell.
In the span of only one or two shichen, the young man’s footsteps had grown as light as his voice.
Has he gained some kind of insight?
Before, the old man had been able to sense his presence from fifty paces away. This time, he hadn’t noticed him until he came within thirty.
He wasn’t sure whether to call that impressive or bizarre.
Though a smile tugged at the corner of his mouth, his voice was gruff.
“Did I not tell you to come at daybreak?”
“I couldn’t wait. I already know my answer, so why waste time?”
“Tsk, tsk. What kind of martial artist has so little patience?”
“You said it yourself, Old Master. Sleep is a luxury for a martial artist. Spend that time training instead. Am I wrong?”
“Hah! You little rascal.”
He was right. That was how a martial artist should behave—and how a Disciple should treat his master’s words as golden law.

“Old Master. Please teach me martial arts.”
Jeok Cheongang, the Fire King, smiled with delight.
“All right. I’ll teach you everything I know.”

chapters.title: Chapter 229
paragraphs: “...You’re leaving? For an entire year?”
“Yes.”
“So you finally decided?”
When I nodded, an indescribably complicated look crossed Jin Wikyung’s face. Joy, disappointment, pride...
After a long silence, he bowed deeply to Jeok Cheongang.
“Please take good care of our youngest—no, of Taekyung, Great Hero Jeok.”
“I heard you, so get up. He may be lacking, as you said, but this old man will guide him properly. Stop worrying. Ahem!”
When did he say that? He asked you to take good care of me. I don’t remember him saying I was lacking.
But there was no reasoning with Jeok Cheongang.
He composed his twitching lips and spoke again.
“Daylight has broken, so I intend to leave at once.”
“What? You mean today?”
“Obviously. Once a man makes up his mind, he must act without hesitation.”
Jin Wikyung’s expression grew even gloomier. He looked back and forth between Jeok Cheongang and me, his face clouded over, then let out a deep sigh.
“Understood. I’ll have your travel bags packed immediately.”
“What do we need travel bags for? This is training, not a tour of the martial world.”
“Where are you headed?”
“Anhui. It won’t take long on foot.”
A sudden sense of foreboding made me ask, “How far is it?”
Jin Wikyung answered, “At least a month.”
“What?”
“And that’s on horseback.”
Has this old man gone senile?
Jeok Cheongang saw my expression and barked, “That’s only for those slowpokes! At this old man’s pace, it won’t even take a month and a half!”
No, damn it. By that logic, a jet would be even faster. So why are we walking?
I quickly grabbed Jin Wikyung’s hand.
“Pack my bags nice and full, please.”
“You little—!”
“Otherwise, I’m not going.”
“What did you say?”
“I’m from a rich family. I have no intention of wandering around begging for food. Since we’re going anyway, we might as well travel in comfort.”
Why go out of my way to suffer when I had money? If I could travel comfortably, that was all that mattered.
I had already left behind a soft bed and logged in. I didn’t want to take things that far.
And besides...
“There are places I need to stop by before we leave.”
“Gnnngh.”
As Jeok Cheongang groaned, Jin Wikyung added, “I also have something important to discuss with you.”
“With me?”
“Yes. It won’t take long.”
“If you intend to waste my time with some trivial matter, forget it.”
Jin Wikyung firmly shook his head.
“It’s important enough that you need to know, Great Hero Jeok.”
What could it be?
Even I hadn’t seen him look this serious in a long time.
Jeok Cheongang studied Jin Wikyung in silence, then clicked his tongue.
“Half a shichen. No longer.”
“That will be enough.”
This time, he turned to me.
“The same goes for you.”
“Yes, sir.”
That was more than enough time for me as well.
Afraid he might change his mind, I answered at once and left the study so the two of them could speak in private.
Clear sunlight and a pleasant breeze greeted me outside. It was hard to call this winter weather anymore.
“Ah, what a beautiful day.”
Finding my next destination was easy.
I looked up at the blue sky, then set off toward the distant cliff.
Whoooosh.
An iron sword cleaved through the air with a heavy rush.
Once, then again, every motion flawless down to the last inch.
How long had it been since he had begun each day with ten thousand strikes?
The young man gripping the sword’s hilt did not know.
He was inside a cave where no light could enter, and he had long since lost all sense of time.
Swish!
The tip of his sword wavered.
The deviation was minute, but to the young man, it was an unforgivable mistake.
By the rule he had set for himself, every mistake meant another hundred strikes.
Again.
The young man silently swung his sword.
It was a brutal physical regimen that had to be completed with raw strength and stamina alone, without using any internal energy.
An ordinary martial artist would have collapsed from exhaustion long ago.
But this young man, Jin Mukyung, was different.
I’ll do it perfectly. No matter how many attempts it takes. No matter how many years.
He had first picked up a sword at the age of five. He loved the whisper of wind against his ears whenever he swung it and the feeling of being drenched in sweat.
More than twenty years passed that way.
At some point, people began calling him by another name.
“Peak at twenty? If that isn’t genius, what is?”
“Are you the Heaven Shaking Sword?”
He had trained simply because he loved martial arts and enjoyed becoming stronger. Yet people called him the pride of his family and a martial arts genius.
There had been times when he took pride in the martial name he had earned.
But then he realized it was all hollow fame—an empty name with nothing behind it.
Cheongpung.
Swish!
The instant the name entered his mind, his sword tip twitched.
Another hundred strikes.
He closed his eyes and forced his breathing under control, but his disturbed heart refused to settle.
Before he knew it, Jin Mukyung was remembering the day he had first met Cheongpung.
He’s strong.
That was his first thought upon seeing the boy.

Cheongpung had a clear, boyish face and an unremarkable build, with a single iron sword hanging carelessly from his waist. His demeanor and posture could not have looked more careless, yet Mukyung had known at once.
And his intuition had soon proved correct.
It had been the most crushing defeat of his life.
The memory of dropping to his knees after some three hundred exchanges made his teeth clench and his grip tighten around the hilt.
Swish! Swish-swish!
Every ripple in his heart revealed itself through his sword.
His stable stance collapsed, and his movements—once as precise as if measured with a ruler—became disordered.
One hundred extra strikes. Two hundred. Three hundred...
Just as his mistakes began to snowball, a familiar voice came from beyond the iron door sealing the training hall.
“Why does it sound so murderous in there?”
Jin Mukyung, who had been swinging his sword as though possessed, froze in place.
“Is that you?”
“Why ask when you already know? You’ll hurt my feelings.”
There was no mistaking him.
Only one person in the Taiyuan Jin Family could speak to Jin Mukyung with such insolence.
Thinking of his younger brother beyond the iron door, Mukyung asked, “How long have you been there?”
“About fifteen minutes?”
“...I see.”
Despite the casual answer, Mukyung’s face darkened.
He had allowed himself to be swept up in his emotions and failed to notice Taekyung’s presence.
“Go away. I’m training.”
“Training, my ass. More like taking out your anger.”
“What?”
“I can hear how furious you are. Whatever you do in that state, it won’t be training.”
Jin Mukyung’s eyes trembled faintly.
He was astonished that Taekyung had seen straight through his condition despite the iron door between them and the distance of more than ten jang.
This guy... Has he improved again already?
His rate of growth was truly terrifying.
Before Mukyung’s surprise could fade, Jin Taekyung continued.
“I’m leaving.”
“You’re leaving?”
“Yeah. I decided to learn martial arts from the Fire King—or rather, the Old Master.”
Mukyung had heard that the Fire King had come to visit the family.
In the past, he would have rushed out of the training hall at once, bowed until his forehead struck the ground, and begged the Fire King to teach him even a single move.
But he had restrained himself.
More than anyone, he knew that this was a process he had to understand for himself.
But why would he teach that boy...? No. There are more than enough reasons.
The man beyond that iron door was the true monster, the one who deserved to be called a genius. The Fire King could hardly have failed to recognize his worth.
Once Mukyung had accepted that, he asked, “Have you become his Disciple?”
“Not exactly. I’m sort of a Disciple, but not a Disciple, while also being kind of a Disciple. Something like that.”
“...What the fuck are you talking about?”
“Don’t bother trying to understand. Is this the first time something like this has happened?”
“That’s true.”
“Yeah. Just let it go.”
A brief silence followed.
Then, as if by agreement, they both chuckled.
Even they had to admit the conversation had taken an absurd turn.
“Did you come here just to tell me that? Were you hoping for a send-off?”
“A send-off? I know better than to expect one.”
“Then what?”
“One year left.”
Taekyung’s calm voice continued.
The Star-Array Grand Banquet.
The Star-Array Grand Banquet.
Jin Mukyung repeated the words like a groan.
A banquet hall for the countless stars adorning the Nine Provinces and Eight Wastes, the Four Seas and Five Lakes.
That was the Star-Array Grand Banquet.
“Why are you telling me?”
“I’m going to attend. Cheongpung and I both are.”
“...What are you trying to say?”
“That’s for you to think about on your own. Oof.”
There came the sound of Taekyung rising, followed by his final words.
“I’m off. See you later.”
Step. Step.
His footsteps gradually receded, then vanished altogether.
Silence settled over the training hall.
Jin Mukyung stared blankly at the iron door beyond which the other’s presence had vanished.
The Star-Array Grand Banquet.
He was no fool.
He knew exactly why Jin Taekyung had come to the training hall and why he had brought up the Star-Array Grand Banquet.
“One year...”
Jin Mukyung murmured under his breath and tightened his grip on the sword.
Before he knew it, his turbulent heart had calmed, and the wavering tip of his sword had stilled.
“Safe travels. I’ll see you then.”
Murmuring the farewell he had failed to give his younger brother before his long journey, Jin Mukyung swung his sword like lightning.
Whoooosh.
A perfect strike, without the slightest deviation.
After leaving the training hall, I headed straight for the study.
What awaited me there was an empty chair and a message from one of the guards.
“He told me to wait at the main gate?”
“Yes. Those were his exact words.”
Did something happen?
Setting the question aside, I made my way to the main gate. Before long, I found several familiar faces waiting for me.
“Captain!”
“Benefactor!”
“You’re finally here, Young Master Jin?”
Hyuk Mujin, Cheongpung, and Wolhwa.
And they weren’t alone.
Over the shoulders of the three who had approached me first, I could see the others as well.
Lee Seowol, awkwardly waving one hand, and the Three Plum Blossom Elites, standing there with expressions that seemed to say they had no idea where they were or who they were.
“How did you all know to come?”
Wolhwa smiled sweetly.
“Because we’re the Lower District Sect.”
“...Did you plant a spy?”
“Oh my, a spy? Why would we need one when we have such an excellent informant right there?”
I followed her pointing finger and found Hyuk Mujin proudly holding out a heavy travel bag.
“The Lesser Family Head ordered me to pack your luggage, Captain!”
“...Oh. So you’re the culprit.”
“Pardon?”
“Nothing. Good job.”

The moment I accepted the travel bag with a sigh, Cheongpung grabbed me by the collar and clung to me.
“Benefactor! I want to go with you! I want to become Grandpa Jeok’s Disciple!”
“Then go get permission.”
“From whom?”

“I already did! He said I could go!”
Baek Museong muttered with the face of a man who had grown weary of life.

That man really is living life on the hardest difficulty.
After finally prying Cheongpung off me, I asked Baek Museong, “What are you planning to do now?”

“Yikes.”

Now that’s mental fortitude.

“Hey.”

“It was nice meeting you, too.”

One person remained.

I didn’t think things had been this awkward at first. I had no idea why Lee Seowol seemed harder to face every time I saw her.
Is it because of the proposal?
Even if it was for a political marriage, a proposal was still a proposal.

“Ah, yes. Then, Young Lady Lee.”
“Yes. Go ahead.”

Great. Nailed it. What better blessing could there be for the leader of an entire sect?

“What are you grinning like a fool for?”
A short old man appeared in the distance.
With Jin Wikyung and Wipeng flanking him, he seized me by the nape before I had a chance to say anything.

“W-wait a second.”
Whoooosh!
But it was already too late.
Everyone’s faces rapidly receded into the distance.
Jin Wikyung waved a handkerchief, his eyes red, and shouted, “My youngest! Come back safe and sound!”
...That only makes me more nervous!

sentences.text: “...You’re leaving?
For an entire year?”
“Yes.”
“So you finally decided?”
When I nodded, an indescribably complicated look crossed Jin Wikyung’s face.
Joy, disappointment, pride...
After a long silence, he bowed deeply to Jeok Cheongang.
“Please take good care of our youngest—no, of Taekyung, Great Hero Jeok.”
“I heard you, so get up.
He may be lacking, as you said, but this old man will guide him properly.
Stop worrying.
Ahem!”
When did he say that?
He asked you to take good care of me.
I don’t remember him saying I was lacking.
But there was no reasoning with Jeok Cheongang.
He composed his twitching lips and spoke again.
“Daylight has broken, so I intend to leave at once.”
“What?
You mean today?”
“Obviously.
Once a man makes up his mind, he must act without hesitation.”
Jin Wikyung’s expression grew even gloomier.
He looked back and forth between Jeok Cheongang and me, his face clouded over, then let out a deep sigh.
“Understood.
I’ll have your travel bags packed immediately.”
“What do we need travel bags for?
This is training, not a tour of the martial world.”
“Where are you headed?”
“Anhui.
It won’t take long on foot.”
A sudden sense of foreboding made me ask, “How far is it?”
Jin Wikyung answered, “At least a month.”
“What?”
“And that’s on horseback.”
Has this old man gone senile?
Jeok Cheongang saw my expression and barked, “That’s only for those slowpokes!
At this old man’s pace, it won’t even take a month and a half!”
No, damn it.
By that logic, a jet would be even faster.
So why are we walking?
I quickly grabbed Jin Wikyung’s hand.
“Pack my bags nice and full, please.”
“You little—!”
“Otherwise, I’m not going.”
“What did you say?”
“I’m from a rich family.
I have no intention of wandering around begging for food.
Since we’re going anyway, we might as well travel in comfort.”
Why go out of my way to suffer when I had money?
If I could travel comfortably, that was all that mattered.
I had already left behind a soft bed and logged in.
I didn’t want to take things that far.
And besides...
“There are places I need to stop by before we leave.”
“Gnnngh.”
As Jeok Cheongang groaned, Jin Wikyung added, “I also have something important to discuss with you.”
“With me?”
“Yes.
It won’t take long.”
“If you intend to waste my time with some trivial matter, forget it.”
Jin Wikyung firmly shook his head.
“It’s important enough that you need to know, Great Hero Jeok.”
What could it be?
Even I hadn’t seen him look this serious in a long time.
Jeok Cheongang studied Jin Wikyung in silence, then clicked his tongue.
“Half a shichen.
No longer.”
“That will be enough.”
This time, he turned to me.
“The same goes for you.”
“Yes, sir.”
That was more than enough time for me as well.
Afraid he might change his mind, I answered at once and left the study so the two of them could speak in private.
Clear sunlight and a pleasant breeze greeted me outside.
It was hard to call this winter weather anymore.
“Ah, what a beautiful day.”
Finding my next destination was easy.
I looked up at the blue sky, then set off toward the distant cliff.
Whoooosh.
An iron sword cleaved through the air with a heavy rush.
Once, then again, every motion flawless down to the last inch.
How long had it been since he had begun each day with ten thousand strikes?
The young man gripping the sword’s hilt did not know.
He was inside a cave where no light could enter, and he had long since lost all sense of time.
Swish!
The tip of his sword wavered.
The deviation was minute, but to the young man, it was an unforgivable mistake.
By the rule he had set for himself, every mistake meant another hundred strikes.
Again.
The young man silently swung his sword.
It was a brutal physical regimen that had to be completed with raw strength and stamina alone, without using any internal energy.
An ordinary martial artist would have collapsed from exhaustion long ago.
But this young man, Jin Mukyung, was different.
I’ll do it perfectly.
No matter how many attempts it takes.
No matter how many years.
He had first picked up a sword at the age of five.
He loved the whisper of wind against his ears whenever he swung it and the feeling of being drenched in sweat.
More than twenty years passed that way.
At some point, people began calling him by another name.
“Peak at twenty?
If that isn’t genius, what is?”
“Are you the Heaven Shaking Sword?”
He had trained simply because he loved martial arts and enjoyed becoming stronger.
Yet people called him the pride of his family and a martial arts genius.
There had been times when he took pride in the martial name he had earned.
But then he realized it was all hollow fame—an empty name with nothing behind it.
Cheongpung.
Swish!
The instant the name entered his mind, his sword tip twitched.
Another hundred strikes.
He closed his eyes and forced his breathing under control, but his disturbed heart refused to settle.

He’s strong.
That was his first thought upon seeing the boy.
Cheongpung had a clear, boyish face and an unremarkable build, with a single iron sword hanging carelessly from his waist.
His demeanor and posture could not have looked more careless, yet Mukyung had known at once.
And his intuition had soon proved correct.
It had been the most crushing defeat of his life.
The memory of dropping to his knees after some three hundred exchanges made his teeth clench and his grip tighten around the hilt.
Swish!
Swish-swish!
Every ripple in his heart revealed itself through his sword.
His stable stance collapsed, and his movements—once as precise as if measured with a ruler—became disordered.
One hundred extra strikes.
Two hundred.
Three hundred...
Just as his mistakes began to snowball, a familiar voice came from beyond the iron door sealing the training hall.
“Why does it sound so murderous in there?”
Jin Mukyung, who had been swinging his sword as though possessed, froze in place.
“Is that you?”
“Why ask when you already know?
You’ll hurt my feelings.”
There was no mistaking him.
Only one person in the Taiyuan Jin Family could speak to Jin Mukyung with such insolence.
Thinking of his younger brother beyond the iron door, Mukyung asked, “How long have you been there?”
“About fifteen minutes?”
“...I see.”
Despite the casual answer, Mukyung’s face darkened.
He had allowed himself to be swept up in his emotions and failed to notice Taekyung’s presence.
“Go away.
I’m training.”
“Training, my ass.
More like taking out your anger.”
“What?”
“I can hear how furious you are.
Whatever you do in that state, it won’t be training.”
Jin Mukyung’s eyes trembled faintly.
He was astonished that Taekyung had seen straight through his condition despite the iron door between them and the distance of more than ten jang.
This guy...
Has he improved again already?
His rate of growth was truly terrifying.
Before Mukyung’s surprise could fade, Jin Taekyung continued.
“I’m leaving.”
“You’re leaving?”
“Yeah.
I decided to learn martial arts from the Fire King—or rather, the Old Master.”
Mukyung had heard that the Fire King had come to visit the family.
In the past, he would have rushed out of the training hall at once, bowed until his forehead struck the ground, and begged the Fire King to teach him even a single move.
But he had restrained himself.
More than anyone, he knew that this was a process he had to understand for himself.
But why would he teach that boy...?
No.
There are more than enough reasons.
The man beyond that iron door was the true monster, the one who deserved to be called a genius.
The Fire King could hardly have failed to recognize his worth.
Once Mukyung had accepted that, he asked, “Have you become his Disciple?”
“Not exactly.
I’m sort of a Disciple, but not a Disciple, while also being kind of a Disciple.
Something like that.”
“...What the fuck are you talking about?”
“Don’t bother trying to understand.
Is this the first time something like this has happened?”
“That’s true.”
“Yeah.
Just let it go.”
A brief silence followed.
Then, as if by agreement, they both chuckled.
Even they had to admit the conversation had taken an absurd turn.
“Did you come here just to tell me that?
Were you hoping for a send-off?”
“A send-off?
I know better than to expect one.”
“Then what?”
“One year left.”
Taekyung’s calm voice continued.
The Star-Array Grand Banquet.
The Star-Array Grand Banquet.
Jin Mukyung repeated the words like a groan.
A banquet hall for the countless stars adorning the Nine Provinces and Eight Wastes, the Four Seas and Five Lakes.
That was the Star-Array Grand Banquet.
“Why are you telling me?”
“I’m going to attend.
Cheongpung and I both are.”
“...What are you trying to say?”
“That’s for you to think about on your own.
Oof.”
There came the sound of Taekyung rising, followed by his final words.
“I’m off.
See you later.”
Step.
Step.
His footsteps gradually receded, then vanished altogether.
Silence settled over the training hall.
Jin Mukyung stared blankly at the iron door beyond which the other’s presence had vanished.
The Star-Array Grand Banquet.
He was no fool.
He knew exactly why Jin Taekyung had come to the training hall and why he had brought up the Star-Array Grand Banquet.
“One year...”
Jin Mukyung murmured under his breath and tightened his grip on the sword.
Before he knew it, his turbulent heart had calmed, and the wavering tip of his sword had stilled.
“Safe travels.
I’ll see you then.”
Murmuring the farewell he had failed to give his younger brother before his long journey, Jin Mukyung swung his sword like lightning.
Whoooosh.
A perfect strike, without the slightest deviation.
After leaving the training hall, I headed straight for the study.
What awaited me there was an empty chair and a message from one of the guards.

“Yes.
Those were his exact words.”
Did something happen?
Setting the question aside, I made my way to the main gate.

“Captain!”

Hyuk Mujin, Cheongpung, and Wolhwa.

Lee Seowol, awkwardly waving one hand, and the Three Plum Blossom Elites, standing there with expressions that seemed to say they had no idea where they were or who they were.
