chapters.title: Chapter 234
paragraphs: Ding.
System Pressure-Point Strike has worn off! You awaken from sleep!
I opened my eyes as the System notifications appeared.
The first things I saw were the waves of branches rippling far below in the night wind and the stars scattered across the pitch-black sky. Cold, hard rock pressed against my back.
I’m outside.
I’d expected as much. Even a preschooler could have guessed that Jeok Cheongang wouldn’t lay me down on a soft duck-down bed.
Besides, my body was sturdy enough to sleep anywhere.
Then why does my body feel so heavy?
Had I been pushing myself too hard lately?
System or not, apparently I was still human after all.
Maybe it was the fifteen-day forced march. My body felt as heavy as if I had an iron ball hanging from it...
Clank.
“Huh?”
Clank?
I turned toward the sound.
Manacles had been fastened tightly around my wrists and ankles, with chains connecting each of them to an iron ball.
“...They really are iron balls.”
What the hell was this?
My brain stopped working for a few seconds. Who was I? Where was I?
And why were these ridiculous things locked onto my limbs?
The answer came quickly. It was an easier question than one plus one.
“Fire King!”
The shout burst from me like a thunderclap.
Smack!
“Ah!”
“What an insolent little bastard.”
Jeok Cheongang, who had nailed me in the back of the head with a pebble, ambled toward me with his feet splayed.
“How dare you throw around my epithet in my presence? Am I your friend?”
I sprang to my feet after rolling across the rock in pain.
Clank.
“What is this?”
“That? An iron ball.”
“I wasn’t asking because I didn’t know what it was.”
“Then why ask when you already know?”
“From now on, these will be your arms and legs. They are training tools passed down through the Fire Gate Clan for generations, so treat them like your own children.”
I was a virgin bachelor who had never even been in a relationship, let alone married, and he was talking about children?
Dumbfounded, I grabbed one of the chains attached to the iron balls and pulled.
Rattle.
I heard metal scraping and felt the tremendous weight behind it.
They were heavy enough that even a decent First Rate martial artist wouldn’t be able to remain standing while wearing them.
“These are training tools passed down through the clan for generations?”
“Did this old man not just say so?”
“How much do they weigh?”
“Not much. About two hundred geun?”
“Oh, and that isn’t their combined weight. Each one weighs two hundred geun.”
Two hundred geun came to 120 kilograms even by modern standards.
With such monstrous things fastened to all four of my limbs, the total weight was...
About five hundred kilograms. Half a ton.
I thought for a moment, then opened my mouth.
“Have you gone senile?”
“...You really will say anything, won’t you?”
I’d said it knowing I would probably get hit, but for some reason, that was the extent of Jeok Cheongang’s reaction.
He stared at me with a complicated expression for a moment before continuing.
“Regardless, you’ll live with those iron balls chained to you from now on. During training, of course, but also while sleeping and eating.”
“Hmm.”
“It’s all part of your training.”
“You’re serious?”
“If you don’t believe me, quit. I won’t bother seeing you off.”
Jeok Cheongang turned away without hesitation, and I hurriedly called after him.
“W-wait!”
“What? I thought you didn’t want to do it.”
“I haven’t even answered yet. You can’t just walk away.”
“So what’s your answer?”
“Well...”
Damn it. This is a serious internal conflict.
But once the initial shock of seeing the iron balls wore off, my mind gradually settled.
It’s not impossible.
I had made it this far after narrowly escaping death dozens of times.
The world wasn’t easy. To receive a reward, you had to pay a corresponding price. That was true in the Murim and in the modern world.
Everyone—not just me—lived through an endless series of Quests.
And...
If this were enough to make me turn back, I never would’ve come this far.
Compared to the fruit I would harvest in the future, this was a bargain.
Having made my decision, I met Jeok Cheongang’s gaze.
“Fine. I’ll do it.”
“I can’t hear you.”
“I said I’ll do it!”
“Ha-ha-ha! Good!”
A smile spread across Jeok Cheongang’s wrinkled lips.
What a sly old man.
He had acted as if he didn’t care either way, but I had known all along that deep down, he wanted me too.
“So what do I start with?”
“You want to begin right away?”
“They say to strike while the iron is hot. If I’m doing this anyway, I might as well start now.”
“You do have a bold streak. But first, you need to eat.”
“What? Why all of a sudden?”
“Do you think training means starving yourself? You need something in your stomach before you can accomplish anything worthwhile.”
I caught the object Jeok Cheongang pulled from inside his robe and tossed to me.
Under the faint moonlight, I peeled away the damp Korean paper to reveal a fasting pill with a reddish cast.
“You should’ve given me jerky instead.”
“Stop complaining and eat it. That isn’t an ordinary fasting pill. It was made using a secret Fire Gate Clan method.”
“What does it do?”
“It’s superior in every respect, but...”
“This stuff makes my stomach feel so bloated. Just looking at it kills my appetite now.”
“It’s especially good for your virility.”
“Wow. My mouth’s watering just looking at it.”
“I’ll enjoy the meal!”
If it was good for virility, I had to eat it. Even if I had no immediate use for it, I still had to eat it.
Thinking of the future, I chewed the fasting pill thoroughly and swallowed it.
Jeok Cheongang watched me intently before asking, “Finished?”
“Yes, Old Master.”
“Well? Feel anything?”
“I’m not sure. I think my sperm count may have gone up a little...”
Jeok Cheongang frowned at my answer and muttered, “Strange. Has it been sitting around so long that the medicine lost its potency?”
“Huh?”
What the hell was he talking about?
The moment I blurted out the question—
Ding.

System You have taken Fire King’s Special Restriction Pill. You feel full! Agility decreases by 100! Strength decreases by 100! Stamina decreases by 100! You cannot use internal energy! The effects will last for one week!
It happened without warning.
The instant the System notification appeared, strength drained from my arms and legs, and my breathing grew short.
Finally, the internal energy flowing steadily through the minor meridians throughout my body descended into my dantian. Then it became completely immobile, as though something had bound it in place.
“Guh!”
Thud!
With all my strength gone at once, my body, which had somehow been supporting the iron balls, sagged.
The half-ton weight pressing down on my entire body made my knees buckle.
“What the hell is this?”
“Heh-heh. The medicine is finally taking effect.”
I stared at Jeok Cheongang, who was letting out a sinister laugh, with my jaw hanging open.
“What the hell did you do, you crazy old man?”
“What did you call me? A crazy old man?”
“Gasp. No, that’s not what I meant.”
“Let’s see... Yes, that should do nicely for your first training exercise.”
As soon as he finished speaking, he extended a wrinkled palm toward me.
An immense flow of qi filled the air. The fierce wind abruptly changed direction and began swirling around him.
A flash of insight struck me.
There’s a cliff below this, isn’t there?
I hurriedly glanced back. The view below the rock was dizzying.
If I fell from here with these insane iron balls attached to me...
“W-wait!”
“Wait for what? Weren’t you the one who said we should strike while the iron was hot?”
“But that was—!”
“Too late.”
Fwoosh!
Compressed air exploded from Jeok Cheongang’s palm. The blast of fist wind, powerful enough to uproot rocks and trees, became a giant’s fist and slammed into me.
Against that powerful wind, even several hundred kilograms of iron balls were useless.
Boom!
Ah, shit.
The next moment, the ground vanished beneath my feet, and I was flung into the air.
Through my upside-down vision, I saw Jeok Cheongang waving at me with a broad grin.
“You have one shichen to make it back up. If you’re even fifteen minutes late, you fail.”
Ding.
System Quest Fire King’s Inferno Training-1 has been created! You cannot refuse this Quest!
“This is fucking bullsh—!”
Before I could finish speaking, gravity bore down on my entire body.
As I plummeted like a streak of light, there was only one thing I could say.
“Aaaaaaaaaaaah!”
My terrified scream shook Mount Jiuhua, submerged in darkness.
Splash—
Far below the sheer cliff, Jeok Cheongang let out a quiet laugh at the sound of water echoing up from below.
A memory from his youth had suddenly come to mind.
“Master! Save me!”
“I’m counting to three. Let go. Three.”
“Please! If I fall from here, your Disciple will die!”
“Two.”
“Master!”
“One.”
His Master had been merciless—harsh enough to seem excessive toward a child who still had baby fuzz on his face.
But without such harsh instruction, neither the Fire Gate Clan of today nor Fire King Jeok Cheongang would exist.
I’ll put you through exactly what I endured... No, I’ll push you even harder.
Jin Taekyung didn’t know it, but Jeok Cheongang did.
They did not have much time.
There was no time to teach him everything gradually, one step at a time.
The heavenly patterns Hong Dao had foreseen told him as much, as did Jeok Cheongang’s current condition.
Hold out until then. This old man will do his best as well.
Jeok Cheongang gazed down the mountain for some time, his eyes unfathomably deep. Then he suddenly muttered, “...Perhaps I shouldn’t have put the iron balls on him.”
He had never imagined that the object meant to restrain criminals of the Fire Gate Clan would be used for something like this.
“Hngh. Hnnnngh!”
Grrrnk. Grrrnnngh.
With every step I took, the ground that had only just begun to thaw sank beneath me. Deep trenches formed in my wake.
But I was used to it by now. Sweat poured off me as I continued up the steep mountain path.
“Huff, huff.”
Ding.
System Extreme Training! Endless effort never betrays you! Strength, Stamina, and Agility have increased by 1 each! Muscles and Bones and Sinews and Meridians have increased by 2 each!
Even a drizzle will soak you through eventually, so these stat increases, though small, helped more than you might think.
If only I didn’t have these fucking iron balls! If only it weren’t for that damn restriction pill!
Without either one, I would have completed the Quest long ago.
But my most important internal energy was restricted, my physical stats had each dropped by 100, and the tremendous weight had been added on top of that. I had no way to endure it.
To top it all off, the time limit was only one shichen.
Shit. Mount Jiuhua isn’t some little hill behind the neighborhood.
It was so grueling that I had even considered breaking the chains connecting the iron balls.
That was before I learned they were made of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron.
They used this stuff for chains? Were they insane?
In the end, I had no choice but to keep going through sheer stubbornness and grit.
One day, two days, three days, four days...
And finally, today—ten days later.
Ding.
System Quest Fire King’s Hellfire Training-1 has been completed! You acquired a substantial amount of EXP! Level Up! You acquired 30 Bonus Points!
With about fifteen minutes left before the deadline, I finally reached the summit.
Thud!
“Yaaaaaah!”
I let the heavy iron balls crash to the ground and released a roar from the depths of my lungs.
The sound startled Jeok Cheongang, who had been nodding off against a rock. He jolted awake.
“W-what happened?”
Damn old man. He was always going on about how martial artists shouldn’t waste time sleeping, yet he slept like a baby while I was going through hell?
Grinding my teeth, I walked toward him.
“Can’t you tell by looking? I climbed Mount Jiuhua within one shichen. I succeeded!”
“Huh? Why are you climbing Mount Jiuhua?”
“What?”
Jeok Cheongang blinked, then hastily shook his head.
“Ah, no. You did pretty well.”
“And?”
“It seems you’re ready for the next stage. I’ve already made the preparations, so take care of it yourself.”
I turned my head toward where his finger was pointing.
Propped against a massive rock was a vest—a huge, incredibly thick vest made of iron.
My fingertips began to tremble despite myself.
“...Is this what I think it is?”
“What were you thinking?”
“That I’m supposed to put this on and repeat exactly what I’ve been doing until now.”
“You rascal. What a joke.”
“Right? Wow, you scared the hell out of me.”
“Ha-ha. What an adorable imagination you have.”
Jeok Cheongang chuckled with the amiable smile of a kindly neighborhood grandfather, then continued.
“If you’ve managed one thing, you should accomplish at least two the next time. Come to think of it, one shichen was far too generous.”
“What?”
“I’ll give you half a shichen. Hurry up, pick it up, put it on, and get back here.”
Ding.
System Quest information has been changed! Repeat Quest Fire King’s Inferno Training-1 has been created!

It was an easier question than one plus one.
“Fire King!”
The shout burst from me like a thunderclap.
Smack!
“Ah!”
“What an insolent little bastard.”
Jeok Cheongang, who had nailed me in the back of the head with a pebble, ambled toward me with his feet splayed.
“How dare you throw around my epithet in my presence?
Am I your friend?”
I sprang to my feet after rolling across the rock in pain.
Clank.
“What is this?”
“That?
An iron ball.”
“I wasn’t asking because I didn’t know what it was.”
“Then why ask when you already know?”
“From now on, these will be your arms and legs.
They are training tools passed down through the Fire Gate Clan for generations, so treat them like your own children.”
I was a virgin bachelor who had never even been in a relationship, let alone married, and he was talking about children?
Dumbfounded, I grabbed one of the chains attached to the iron balls and pulled.
Rattle.
I heard metal scraping and felt the tremendous weight behind it.
They were heavy enough that even a decent First Rate martial artist wouldn’t be able to remain standing while wearing them.
“These are training tools passed down through the clan for generations?”
“Did this old man not just say so?”
“How much do they weigh?”
“Not much.
About two hundred geun?”
“Oh, and that isn’t their combined weight.
Each one weighs two hundred geun.”
Two hundred geun came to 120 kilograms even by modern standards.
With such monstrous things fastened to all four of my limbs, the total weight was...
About five hundred kilograms.
Half a ton.
I thought for a moment, then opened my mouth.
“Have you gone senile?”
“...You really will say anything, won’t you?”
I’d said it knowing I would probably get hit, but for some reason, that was the extent of Jeok Cheongang’s reaction.
He stared at me with a complicated expression for a moment before continuing.
“Regardless, you’ll live with those iron balls chained to you from now on.
During training, of course, but also while sleeping and eating.”
“Hmm.”
“It’s all part of your training.”
“You’re serious?”
“If you don’t believe me, quit.
I won’t bother seeing you off.”
Jeok Cheongang turned away without hesitation, and I hurriedly called after him.
“W-wait!”
“What?
I thought you didn’t want to do it.”
“I haven’t even answered yet.
You can’t just walk away.”
“So what’s your answer?”
“Well...”
Damn it.
This is a serious internal conflict.
But once the initial shock of seeing the iron balls wore off, my mind gradually settled.
It’s not impossible.
I had made it this far after narrowly escaping death dozens of times.
The world wasn’t easy.
To receive a reward, you had to pay a corresponding price.
That was true in the Murim and in the modern world.
Everyone—not just me—lived through an endless series of Quests.
And...
If this were enough to make me turn back, I never would’ve come this far.
Compared to the fruit I would harvest in the future, this was a bargain.
Having made my decision, I met Jeok Cheongang’s gaze.
“Fine.
I’ll do it.”
“I can’t hear you.”
“I said I’ll do it!”
“Ha-ha-ha!
Good!”
A smile spread across Jeok Cheongang’s wrinkled lips.
What a sly old man.
He had acted as if he didn’t care either way, but I had known all along that deep down, he wanted me too.
“So what do I start with?”
“You want to begin right away?”
“They say to strike while the iron is hot.
If I’m doing this anyway, I might as well start now.”
“You do have a bold streak.
But first, you need to eat.”
“What?
Why all of a sudden?”
“Do you think training means starving yourself?
You need something in your stomach before you can accomplish anything worthwhile.”
I caught the object Jeok Cheongang pulled from inside his robe and tossed to me.
Under the faint moonlight, I peeled away the damp Korean paper to reveal a fasting pill with a reddish cast.
“You should’ve given me jerky instead.”
“Stop complaining and eat it.
That isn’t an ordinary fasting pill.
It was made using a secret Fire Gate Clan method.”
“What does it do?”
“It’s superior in every respect, but...”
“This stuff makes my stomach feel so bloated.
Just looking at it kills my appetite now.”
“It’s especially good for your virility.”
“Wow.
My mouth’s watering just looking at it.”
“I’ll enjoy the meal!”
If it was good for virility, I had to eat it.
Even if I had no immediate use for it, I still had to eat it.
Thinking of the future, I chewed the fasting pill thoroughly and swallowed it.
Jeok Cheongang watched me intently before asking, “Finished?”
“Yes, Old Master.”
“Well?
Feel anything?”
“I’m not sure.
I think my sperm count may have gone up a little...”
Jeok Cheongang frowned at my answer and muttered, “Strange.
Has it been sitting around so long that the medicine lost its potency?”
“Huh?”
What the hell was he talking about?
The moment I blurted out the question—
Ding.
System You have taken Fire King’s Special Restriction Pill.
You feel full!
Agility decreases by 100!
Strength decreases by 100!
Stamina decreases by 100!
You cannot use internal energy!
The effects will last for one week!
It happened without warning.
The instant the System notification appeared, strength drained from my arms and legs, and my breathing grew short.
Finally, the internal energy flowing steadily through the minor meridians throughout my body descended into my dantian.
Then it became completely immobile, as though something had bound it in place.
“Guh!”
Thud!
With all my strength gone at once, my body, which had somehow been supporting the iron balls, sagged.
The half-ton weight pressing down on my entire body made my knees buckle.
“What the hell is this?”
“Heh-heh.
The medicine is finally taking effect.”
I stared at Jeok Cheongang, who was letting out a sinister laugh, with my jaw hanging open.
“What the hell did you do, you crazy old man?”
“What did you call me?
A crazy old man?”
“Gasp.
No, that’s not what I meant.”
“Let’s see...
Yes, that should do nicely for your first training exercise.”
As soon as he finished speaking, he extended a wrinkled palm toward me.
An immense flow of qi filled the air.
The fierce wind abruptly changed direction and began swirling around him.
A flash of insight struck me.
There’s a cliff below this, isn’t there?
I hurriedly glanced back.
The view below the rock was dizzying.
If I fell from here with these insane iron balls attached to me...
“W-wait!”
“Wait for what?
Weren’t you the one who said we should strike while the iron was hot?”
“But that was—!”
“Too late.”
Fwoosh!
Compressed air exploded from Jeok Cheongang’s palm.
The blast of fist wind, powerful enough to uproot rocks and trees, became a giant’s fist and slammed into me.
Against that powerful wind, even several hundred kilograms of iron balls were useless.
Boom!
Ah, shit.
The next moment, the ground vanished beneath my feet, and I was flung into the air.
Through my upside-down vision, I saw Jeok Cheongang waving at me with a broad grin.
“You have one shichen to make it back up.
If you’re even fifteen minutes late, you fail.”
Ding.
System Quest Fire King’s Inferno Training-1 has been created!
You cannot refuse this Quest!
“This is fucking bullsh—!”
Before I could finish speaking, gravity bore down on my entire body.
As I plummeted like a streak of light, there was only one thing I could say.
“Aaaaaaaaaaaah!”
My terrified scream shook Mount Jiuhua, submerged in darkness.
Splash—
Far below the sheer cliff, Jeok Cheongang let out a quiet laugh at the sound of water echoing up from below.
A memory from his youth had suddenly come to mind.
“Master!
Save me!”
“I’m counting to three.
Let go.
Three.”
“Please!
If I fall from here, your Disciple will die!”
“Two.”
“Master!”
“One.”
His Master had been merciless—harsh enough to seem excessive toward a child who still had baby fuzz on his face.
But without such harsh instruction, neither the Fire Gate Clan of today nor Fire King Jeok Cheongang would exist.
I’ll put you through exactly what I endured...
No, I’ll push you even harder.
Jin Taekyung didn’t know it, but Jeok Cheongang did.
They did not have much time.
There was no time to teach him everything gradually, one step at a time.
The heavenly patterns Hong Dao had foreseen told him as much, as did Jeok Cheongang’s current condition.
Hold out until then.
This old man will do his best as well.
Jeok Cheongang gazed down the mountain for some time, his eyes unfathomably deep.
Then he suddenly muttered, “...Perhaps I shouldn’t have put the iron balls on him.”
He had never imagined that the object meant to restrain criminals of the Fire Gate Clan would be used for something like this.
“Hngh.
Hnnnngh!”
Grrrnk.
Grrrnnngh.
With every step I took, the ground that had only just begun to thaw sank beneath me.
Deep trenches formed in my wake.
But I was used to it by now.
Sweat poured off me as I continued up the steep mountain path.
“Huff, huff.”
Ding.
System Extreme Training!
Endless effort never betrays you!
Strength, Stamina, and Agility have increased by 1 each!
Muscles and Bones and Sinews and Meridians have increased by 2 each!
Even a drizzle will soak you through eventually, so these stat increases, though small, helped more than you might think.
If only I didn’t have these fucking iron balls!
If only it weren’t for that damn restriction pill!
Without either one, I would have completed the Quest long ago.
But my most important internal energy was restricted, my physical stats had each dropped by 100, and the tremendous weight had been added on top of that.
I had no way to endure it.
To top it all off, the time limit was only one shichen.
Shit.
Mount Jiuhua isn’t some little hill behind the neighborhood.
It was so grueling that I had even considered breaking the chains connecting the iron balls.
That was before I learned they were made of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron.
They used this stuff for chains?
Were they insane?
In the end, I had no choice but to keep going through sheer stubbornness and grit.
One day, two days, three days, four days...
And finally, today—ten days later.
Ding.
System Quest Fire King’s Hellfire Training-1 has been completed!
You acquired a substantial amount of EXP!
Level Up!
You acquired 30 Bonus Points!
With about fifteen minutes left before the deadline, I finally reached the summit.
Thud!
“Yaaaaaah!”
I let the heavy iron balls crash to the ground and released a roar from the depths of my lungs.
The sound startled Jeok Cheongang, who had been nodding off against a rock.
He jolted awake.
“W-what happened?”
Damn old man.
He was always going on about how martial artists shouldn’t waste time sleeping, yet he slept like a baby while I was going through hell?
Grinding my teeth, I walked toward him.
“Can’t you tell by looking?
I climbed Mount Jiuhua within one shichen.
I succeeded!”
“Huh?
Why are you climbing Mount Jiuhua?”
“What?”
Jeok Cheongang blinked, then hastily shook his head.
“Ah, no.
You did pretty well.”
“And?”
“It seems you’re ready for the next stage.
I’ve already made the preparations, so take care of it yourself.”
I turned my head toward where his finger was pointing.
Propped against a massive rock was a vest—a huge, incredibly thick vest made of iron.
My fingertips began to tremble despite myself.
“...Is this what I think it is?”
“What were you thinking?”
“That I’m supposed to put this on and repeat exactly what I’ve been doing until now.”
“You rascal.
What a joke.”
“Right?
Wow, you scared the hell out of me.”
“Ha-ha.
What an adorable imagination you have.”
Jeok Cheongang chuckled with the amiable smile of a kindly neighborhood grandfather, then continued.
“If you’ve managed one thing, you should accomplish at least two the next time.
Come to think of it, one shichen was far too generous.”
“What?”
“I’ll give you half a shichen.
Hurry up, pick it up, put it on, and get back here.”
Ding.
System Quest information has been changed!
Repeat Quest Fire King’s Inferno Training-1 has been created!

chapters.title: Chapter 235
paragraphs: The training Jeok Cheongang put me through was simple.
Take a horse stance beneath the waterfall. Do push-ups. Go fetch me some bird eggs because I feel like eating them...
That much was fine. The problem was the conditions tacked onto every exercise.
“Six shichen in a horse stance.”
“You’re joking, right?”
“Does it sound like I’m joking?”
Whoosh!
The waterfall plunged hundreds of jang. Even with my exceptional physique, a single shichen beneath it left my entire body aching as though it had been smashed apart and my vision swimming.
And he wanted me to stay there for six shichen. In a horse stance, no less.
“Old Master, this is a bit much. If I stay under there for six shichen, I’ll actually die.”
“Have you tried it?”
“Huh?”
“Try it before you say that. If you don’t like it, go back to your family.”
It took me ten full days to complete the Quest.
As a side effect, I briefly lost consciousness. When I opened my eyes again, the iron balls had grown heavier.
“An additional hundred geun. From now on, we’re increasing it to twelve shichen.”
For a moment, I considered using Logout.
But I had to finish the training. It might have looked foolish to others, but it was a rule I had set for myself when I began.
If I go back, my body and mind will grow lax.
Whoosh!
The pressure of the waterfall was terrifying. With my internal energy and physical abilities restricted, I had to endure with nothing but my body and sheer willpower.
When I finally completed the waterfall training, I was left with legs harder than steel—and an unexpected System notification.
System Fire King’s Hellfire Training-2 has been completed successfully! Outstanding achievement: Unmoving achieved! Toughness changes to Endurance! Level Up! Level Up! You acquired 50 Bonus Points!
The training continued without pause. I wasn’t given any time to rest.
I got one shichen of blissful sleep each day. Everything else was part of my training.
“Next are push-ups.”
“That’s too easy. Wait. How many?”
“Ten thousand. Put the iron balls on your back.”
It was the most hellish push-up routine in the world. But I gritted my teeth and did it.
On the day I completed every kind of push-up Jeok Cheongang wanted, the year’s first sprouts were pushing up from the ground.
“The weather has grown warm. I feel like having a swallow’s nest dish for once, so go fetch one.”
“Aren’t swallows migratory birds? They won’t arrive until it gets warmer.”
“What would an ignorant brat like you know? This old man has lived on Mount Jiuhua his entire life. By now, a few impatient swallows should be starting to build their nests.”
“Whew. Where am I supposed to look for them?”
“Cliffs.”
That Quest took the longest. I had to find a swallow’s nest without even knowing where one might be.
By then, I was combing every cliff on Mount Jiuhua while laden with iron balls whose combined weight had long since surpassed a thousand geun.
At last, I found a newly completed swallow’s nest and brought it to Jeok Cheongang.
“Here it is. A swallow’s nest.”
His long silence was followed by a single muttered sentence that was more than enough to snap the last thread of my patience.
“...It really exists.”
“You fucking old bastard!”
My eyes rolled back, and I lunged at Jeok Cheongang. He beat me within an inch of my life.
When I came to again, the iron balls had grown heavier. That was only natural.
“If you’re awake, get moving.”
“Is this a new training routine?”
“It is. In a sense.”
Jeok Cheongang thrust an insane schedule in front of me.
It included every single thing I had done so far, without exception.

“Three round trips up and down Mount Jiuhua in the morning, ten thousand one-armed push-ups on each side at noon. Climb the cliffs, then hold a horse stance beneath the waterfall... Human, are you insane?”
“Another five hundred geun if you don’t like it.”
“I’ve actually wanted to spend every day like this for a long time. I’ll be right back.”
“Good.”
From then on, I did whatever he told me.
I wondered if it was even possible, but once I tried it, it turned out to be possible.
A day passes quickly when your body is exhausted. The more intense the training became, the faster time flew.
The frozen ground thawed, and fresh sprouts emerged.
Two months passed, but my daily routine remained unchanged. The only differences were that the training had become more brutal and the iron balls had grown heavier.
Rustle.
Flowers and grass that had already grown tall brushed against my calves.
High on a peak of Mount Jiuhua, now awash in color, Jeok Cheongang groggily opened his eyes. He had been asleep with his back against a tree.
“Is that you?”
“Who else would come looking for you besides me?”
“I thought you were the Grim Reaper.”
“I think even the Grim Reaper would run away in fear.”
Jeok Cheongang let out a short laugh at my wisecrack.
“You grow more flattering by the day.”
“Yes, and you’ve been sleeping more by the day, Old Master.”
Just as I said, Jeok Cheongang had been sleeping much more often lately. Given his age, perhaps it was only natural.
“I was training.”
“Ah. In your dreams?”
“I was merely resting my eyes.”
“You were snoring.”
“...Ahem. More importantly, what are you doing here instead of training?”
“I’m finished.”
“Already?”
Jeok Cheongang’s eyes widened slightly.
“I wasn’t slacking off, so don’t give me that suspicious look.”
“Who said anything? Fine. Shut your mouth and work on your fists and feet.”
“Yes, sir.”
I promptly took up a stance in a nearby clearing.
Unlike with the spear, I was practically a beginner when it came to fists and feet, so I was still working on the fundamentals.
“You know what you’re supposed to do, right?”
“Yes, yes.”
Ding.
System Repeat Quest Fist-and-Foot Training has been created!
I began with the simplest straight punch.
Each movement came with the insane requirement of a thousand repetitions, but compared to everything I had already done, it was easy.
The fact that I think this is easy means I’m going insane too.
I let out a deep sigh and began throwing punches.
Whoosh! Bam!
The wind split around my fists, and compressed air burst outward.
In the past, I had simply relied on strength, speed, and internal energy. Now I could execute each movement precisely and control the amount of force behind it.
Clatter!
How long had I listened to the chains connected to my wrists sway and rattle? I kept driving my fists into an imaginary point without pause until I heard a System notification in my ear.
Ding.

System Repeat Quest Fist-and-Foot Training has been completed successfully! Flawless movements without a single error! Strength, Stamina, and Agility have each increased by 1! You have not yet learned fist-and-foot martial arts. Additional rewards will be granted when you acquire a related martial art in the future!
The repeat Quest gave worthwhile rewards. They diminished with each repetition, but even this much was more than enough to be grateful for.
I could probably do this another two or three times.
No Quest, no reward.
I relaxed my stance and walked over to Jeok Cheongang. Just as before, he was leaning against the tree, looking in my direction.
“Old Master. I’m finished.”
“Old Master.”
“Uh... huh?”
He snapped awake and looked up at me.
“What is it?”
“I finished the fist-and-foot training.”
“What did you finish?”
“The fist-and-foot training. Fists and feet!”
“What are you talking about?”
“You told me to do it about a shichen ago.”
“What?”
Jeok Cheongang furrowed his brow.
“When did I do that?”
“Huh?”
“Why are you suddenly spouting such nonsense? This old man has been sitting here watching you with both eyes wide open.”
What the hell is going on here?
Utterly bewildered, I asked, “Why are you doing this to me?”
“What?”
“Are you doing this on purpose to make me train more? You didn’t have to go this far. I was planning to keep training anyway.”
“What kind of nonsense are you spouting?”
Jeok Cheongang was about to erupt in anger when he suddenly closed his mouth.
For an instant, unknowable emotions passed across his wrinkled face. After a long silence, he finally spoke.
“You’re a perceptive one. If you’ve figured it out, go practice your fists and feet some more.”
Ding. A notification appeared, telling me that another Quest had been created, but I didn’t move an inch.
I stared at Jeok Cheongang for a long moment before suddenly opening my mouth.
“Old Master. I just want to ask you something.”
Jeok Cheongang’s shrewd gray eyes trembled.
The suspicion that had crossed my mind—Could it be?—hardened into certainty.
“Are you feeling unwell?”
It wasn’t an easy subject to bring up, so I had phrased it indirectly. But there was no doubt he understood what I meant.
After a suffocating silence, a sigh-like word escaped Jeok Cheongang’s lips.
“...Follow me. There is somewhere we need to go together.”
Dementia.
Even in the modern world, with all its advances in magical medicine, dementia remained impossible to cure completely.
Its progression could only be slowed. Everyone was equal before the curse of time.
Why didn’t I realize it?
Thinking back, there had definitely been warning signs. He had been sleeping more with each passing day, and I had noticed bouts of forgetfulness like the one just now several times before.
Even so, I hadn’t been particularly suspicious because he wasn’t an ordinary old man.
Fire King Jeok Cheongang.
I had never imagined that a Supreme Peak master whose martial arts had reached the heavens could suffer from the infirmities of old age.
Perhaps it was a truth that even Jeok Cheongang himself wanted to deny.
“The history of our sect stretches back hundreds of years.”
Jeok Cheongang’s voice echoed through the cave.
It was as hot and humid as a steam sauna inside, and the heat intensified the deeper we went.
I had already been staying on Mount Jiuhua for more than two months, but I had never once visited this place.
“Our founding ancestor was the greatest under heaven of his era. However, his forthright nature earned him many enemies.”
His calm voice continued like flowing water.
He told me the history of the Fire Gate Clan from its founding to the present day.
From the first Sect Leader to Jeok Cheongang’s master, the seventeenth Sect Leader.
Some had ventured into the Murim and made their names known throughout the world. Others had spent their entire lives secluded in the countryside, quietly raising their successors.
Countless sects had disappeared over the past several hundred years, but the Fire Gate Clan had preserved its lineage.
“Even that became uncertain in this old man’s generation. It is all due to my lack of virtue.”
After about half an hour, we finally stopped walking.
By then, my entire body was drenched in sweat from the heat radiating beyond a moss-covered stone gate.
“This place is...”
“The Fire Gate Cavern. This is where our sect began, and where its legacy continues.”
Jeok Cheongang gazed at the stone gate with a nostalgic expression before placing his palm against its surface.
The instant the Scorching Yang Qi flowing from his fingertips touched the gate, an intricately engraved sun emblem began to glow. The firmly sealed stone door slowly slid open.
“...Whoa.”
I stared into the Fire Gate Cavern, entranced.
The space was several times larger than the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s training hall. Seventeen urns stood around a blue-white flame.
It wasn’t difficult to guess what they contained.
The former Sect Leaders of the Fire Gate Clan.
They were probably funeral urns holding their remains. As if confirming my guess, Jeok Cheongang immediately prostrated himself before them.
“Your unworthy Disciple, Jeok Cheongang, pays his respects to the Sect Ancestors.”
He rose and beckoned to me.
“Come in.”
“Ah, yes. Excuse me.”
The instant I carefully stepped into the Fire Gate Cavern, a System notification pierced my ears.
Ding.

System You have entered Fire Gate Cavern! The effects of Fire Gate Clan martial arts are amplified when learned! Your Scorching Yang Qi is reacting intensely! The restriction on internal energy has been lifted!
Hummm.
The internal energy in my dantian, awakened from its long slumber, spread through my limbs and body.
Seeing my astonishment, Jeok Cheongang spoke as though he had expected this.
“Your internal energy comes from the Blazing Flame Divine Pill. It is only natural that it would react to the Fire Gate Cavern.”
It found its roots. Is that it?
It was a strange feeling. My internal energy surged like a living creature, and my heart pounded along with it. Though this was my first time setting foot here, the place felt strangely familiar.
“Sit.”
We sat facing each other with the flame between us.
Beyond the blue-white fire, Jeok Cheongang’s face looked noticeably older.
“I will pass on our sect’s martial arts to you.”
“What? Did you think I would suddenly tell you to become my Disciple?”
“To be honest... yes, I did.”

“A master and Disciple are not bound together out of necessity or coercion. Besides, this old man already suffers from the infirmities of old age. Learning from me will place you in great danger as well.”
Everything Jeok Cheongang said was perfectly reasonable.
If he became confused about the formula of an internal cultivation technique, if he forgot even a single word, I would cross an irreversible river.
The river of qi deviation—or death.
“Can you learn martial arts from someone like me?”
I took a deep breath.
Only after turning it over from every angle did I finally reach a single conclusion.
“I will.”
“I’ll say it again...”
“I trust you, Old Master. That’s enough.”
For a moment, Jeok Cheongang was speechless as indescribable emotions crossed his face.
Then a smile spread across his wrinkled lips.
“Then we are alike in that regard.”
One-person succession, passed only to the worthy.
For hundreds of years, the Fire Gate Clan’s legacy had been entrusted to a single talented individual who could be trusted not to use it for evil.
The fact that Jeok Cheongang had brought me here, to the Fire Gate Cavern, meant that he already trusted me.
Fire King Jeok Cheongang trusts me. He chose me. He intends to pass everything the Fire Gate Clan has to me.
My heart swelled at the thought. As though it had sensed my emotions, the blue-white flame surged violently.
Ding.
System Quest Heir of the Blazing Flame has been created!
Along with the System notification, Jeok Cheongang reached out his hand. As Seizing an Object Through Empty Space took effect, the lid of a dark metal box that had risen from the flames opened.
I read the title of the old book floating toward me.
“Fire Gate Divine Technique...”
I knew instinctively that this martial art was the foundation of the Fire Gate Clan—practically its entire legacy.
Jeok Cheongang had risen to his feet and now stood directly behind me.
“We’ll begin at once, so sit cross-legged and close your eyes. From now on, circulate your energy according to the formula I teach you.”
I followed his instructions and closed my eyes. In the darkness, the blue-white flame seemed to flicker before me.
At last, Jeok Cheongang’s voice pierced my ears.
“What about your fist-and-foot training?”
“Did you finish your training and start slacking off? Wait, fuck, that startled me. This is the Fire Gate Cavern. What the hell is this?”
Oh, fuck. Dementia...
After that day, the two people who had caused such a commotion on Mount Jiuhua for some time vanished without a trace.
While they were gone, the trees sprouted green leaves, the flowers bloomed in full, and the swallows built their nests along the cliffs.
From green, to autumn foliage, and then to white snow.
Until Mount Jiuhua changed its clothes three times.

“Next are push-ups.”
“That’s too easy.
Wait.
How many?”
“Ten thousand.
Put the iron balls on your back.”
It was the most hellish push-up routine in the world.
But I gritted my teeth and did it.
On the day I completed every kind of push-up Jeok Cheongang wanted, the year’s first sprouts were pushing up from the ground.
“The weather has grown warm.
I feel like having a swallow’s nest dish for once, so go fetch one.”
“Aren’t swallows migratory birds?
They won’t arrive until it gets warmer.”
“What would an ignorant brat like you know?
This old man has lived on Mount Jiuhua his entire life.
By now, a few impatient swallows should be starting to build their nests.”
“Whew.
Where am I supposed to look for them?”
“Cliffs.”
That Quest took the longest.
I had to find a swallow’s nest without even knowing where one might be.
By then, I was combing every cliff on Mount Jiuhua while laden with iron balls whose combined weight had long since surpassed a thousand geun.
At last, I found a newly completed swallow’s nest and brought it to Jeok Cheongang.
“Here it is.
A swallow’s nest.”
His long silence was followed by a single muttered sentence that was more than enough to snap the last thread of my patience.
“...It really exists.”
“You fucking old bastard!”
My eyes rolled back, and I lunged at Jeok Cheongang.
He beat me within an inch of my life.
When I came to again, the iron balls had grown heavier.
That was only natural.
“If you’re awake, get moving.”
“Is this a new training routine?”
“It is.
In a sense.”
Jeok Cheongang thrust an insane schedule in front of me.
It included every single thing I had done so far, without exception.
“Three round trips up and down Mount Jiuhua in the morning, ten thousand one-armed push-ups on each side at noon.
Climb the cliffs, then hold a horse stance beneath the waterfall...
Human, are you insane?”
“Another five hundred geun if you don’t like it.”
“I’ve actually wanted to spend every day like this for a long time.
I’ll be right back.”
“Good.”
From then on, I did whatever he told me.
I wondered if it was even possible, but once I tried it, it turned out to be possible.
A day passes quickly when your body is exhausted.
The more intense the training became, the faster time flew.
The frozen ground thawed, and fresh sprouts emerged.
Two months passed, but my daily routine remained unchanged.
The only differences were that the training had become more brutal and the iron balls had grown heavier.
Rustle.
Flowers and grass that had already grown tall brushed against my calves.
High on a peak of Mount Jiuhua, now awash in color, Jeok Cheongang groggily opened his eyes.
He had been asleep with his back against a tree.
“Is that you?”
“Who else would come looking for you besides me?”
“I thought you were the Grim Reaper.”
“I think even the Grim Reaper would run away in fear.”
Jeok Cheongang let out a short laugh at my wisecrack.
“You grow more flattering by the day.”
“Yes, and you’ve been sleeping more by the day, Old Master.”
Just as I said, Jeok Cheongang had been sleeping much more often lately.
Given his age, perhaps it was only natural.
“I was training.”
“Ah.
In your dreams?”
“I was merely resting my eyes.”
“You were snoring.”
“...Ahem.
More importantly, what are you doing here instead of training?”
“I’m finished.”
“Already?”
Jeok Cheongang’s eyes widened slightly.
“I wasn’t slacking off, so don’t give me that suspicious look.”
“Who said anything?
Fine.
Shut your mouth and work on your fists and feet.”
“Yes, sir.”
I promptly took up a stance in a nearby clearing.
Unlike with the spear, I was practically a beginner when it came to fists and feet, so I was still working on the fundamentals.
“You know what you’re supposed to do, right?”
“Yes, yes.”
Ding.
System Repeat Quest Fist-and-Foot Training has been created!
I began with the simplest straight punch.
Each movement came with the insane requirement of a thousand repetitions, but compared to everything I had already done, it was easy.
The fact that I think this is easy means I’m going insane too.
I let out a deep sigh and began throwing punches.
Whoosh!
Bam!
The wind split around my fists, and compressed air burst outward.
In the past, I had simply relied on strength, speed, and internal energy.
Now I could execute each movement precisely and control the amount of force behind it.
Clatter!
How long had I listened to the chains connected to my wrists sway and rattle?
I kept driving my fists into an imaginary point without pause until I heard a System notification in my ear.
Ding.
System Repeat Quest Fist-and-Foot Training has been completed successfully!
Flawless movements without a single error!
Strength, Stamina, and Agility have each increased by 1!
You have not yet learned fist-and-foot martial arts.
Additional rewards will be granted when you acquire a related martial art in the future!
The repeat Quest gave worthwhile rewards.
They diminished with each repetition, but even this much was more than enough to be grateful for.
I could probably do this another two or three times.
No Quest, no reward.
I relaxed my stance and walked over to Jeok Cheongang.
Just as before, he was leaning against the tree, looking in my direction.
“Old Master.
I’m finished.”
“Old Master.”
“Uh... huh?”
He snapped awake and looked up at me.
“What is it?”
“I finished the fist-and-foot training.”
“What did you finish?”
“The fist-and-foot training.
Fists and feet!”
“What are you talking about?”
“You told me to do it about a shichen ago.”
“What?”
Jeok Cheongang furrowed his brow.
“When did I do that?”
“Huh?”
“Why are you suddenly spouting such nonsense?
This old man has been sitting here watching you with both eyes wide open.”
What the hell is going on here?
Utterly bewildered, I asked, “Why are you doing this to me?”
“What?”
“Are you doing this on purpose to make me train more?
You didn’t have to go this far.
I was planning to keep training anyway.”
“What kind of nonsense are you spouting?”
Jeok Cheongang was about to erupt in anger when he suddenly closed his mouth.
For an instant, unknowable emotions passed across his wrinkled face.
After a long silence, he finally spoke.
“You’re a perceptive one.
If you’ve figured it out, go practice your fists and feet some more.”
Ding.
A notification appeared, telling me that another Quest had been created, but I didn’t move an inch.
I stared at Jeok Cheongang for a long moment before suddenly opening my mouth.
“Old Master.
I just want to ask you something.”
Jeok Cheongang’s shrewd gray eyes trembled.
The suspicion that had crossed my mind—Could it be?—hardened into certainty.
“Are you feeling unwell?”
It wasn’t an easy subject to bring up, so I had phrased it indirectly.
But there was no doubt he understood what I meant.
After a suffocating silence, a sigh-like word escaped Jeok Cheongang’s lips.
“...Follow me.
There is somewhere we need to go together.”
Dementia.
Even in the modern world, with all its advances in magical medicine, dementia remained impossible to cure completely.
Its progression could only be slowed.
Everyone was equal before the curse of time.
Why didn’t I realize it?
Thinking back, there had definitely been warning signs.
He had been sleeping more with each passing day, and I had noticed bouts of forgetfulness like the one just now several times before.
Even so, I hadn’t been particularly suspicious because he wasn’t an ordinary old man.
Fire King Jeok Cheongang.
I had never imagined that a Supreme Peak master whose martial arts had reached the heavens could suffer from the infirmities of old age.
Perhaps it was a truth that even Jeok Cheongang himself wanted to deny.
“The history of our sect stretches back hundreds of years.”
Jeok Cheongang’s voice echoed through the cave.
It was as hot and humid as a steam sauna inside, and the heat intensified the deeper we went.
I had already been staying on Mount Jiuhua for more than two months, but I had never once visited this place.
“Our founding ancestor was the greatest under heaven of his era.
However, his forthright nature earned him many enemies.”
His calm voice continued like flowing water.
He told me the history of the Fire Gate Clan from its founding to the present day.
From the first Sect Leader to Jeok Cheongang’s master, the seventeenth Sect Leader.
Some had ventured into the Murim and made their names known throughout the world.
Others had spent their entire lives secluded in the countryside, quietly raising their successors.
Countless sects had disappeared over the past several hundred years, but the Fire Gate Clan had preserved its lineage.
“Even that became uncertain in this old man’s generation.
It is all due to my lack of virtue.”
After about half an hour, we finally stopped walking.
By then, my entire body was drenched in sweat from the heat radiating beyond a moss-covered stone gate.
“This place is...”
“The Fire Gate Cavern.
This is where our sect began, and where its legacy continues.”
Jeok Cheongang gazed at the stone gate with a nostalgic expression before placing his palm against its surface.
The instant the Scorching Yang Qi flowing from his fingertips touched the gate, an intricately engraved sun emblem began to glow.
The firmly sealed stone door slowly slid open.
“...Whoa.”
I stared into the Fire Gate Cavern, entranced.
The space was several times larger than the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s training hall.
Seventeen urns stood around a blue-white flame.
It wasn’t difficult to guess what they contained.
The former Sect Leaders of the Fire Gate Clan.
They were probably funeral urns holding their remains.
As if confirming my guess, Jeok Cheongang immediately prostrated himself before them.
“Your unworthy Disciple, Jeok Cheongang, pays his respects to the Sect Ancestors.”
He rose and beckoned to me.
“Come in.”
“Ah, yes.
Excuse me.”
The instant I carefully stepped into the Fire Gate Cavern, a System notification pierced my ears.
Ding.
System You have entered Fire Gate Cavern!
The effects of Fire Gate Clan martial arts are amplified when learned!
Your Scorching Yang Qi is reacting intensely!
The restriction on internal energy has been lifted!
Hummm.
The internal energy in my dantian, awakened from its long slumber, spread through my limbs and body.
Seeing my astonishment, Jeok Cheongang spoke as though he had expected this.
“Your internal energy comes from the Blazing Flame Divine Pill.
It is only natural that it would react to the Fire Gate Cavern.”
It found its roots.
Is that it?
It was a strange feeling.
My internal energy surged like a living creature, and my heart pounded along with it.
Though this was my first time setting foot here, the place felt strangely familiar.
“Sit.”
We sat facing each other with the flame between us.
Beyond the blue-white fire, Jeok Cheongang’s face looked noticeably older.
“I will pass on our sect’s martial arts to you.”
“What?
Did you think I would suddenly tell you to become my Disciple?”
“To be honest... yes, I did.”
“A master and Disciple are not bound together out of necessity or coercion.
Besides, this old man already suffers from the infirmities of old age.
Learning from me will place you in great danger as well.”
Everything Jeok Cheongang said was perfectly reasonable.
If he became confused about the formula of an internal cultivation technique, if he forgot even a single word, I would cross an irreversible river.
The river of qi deviation—or death.
“Can you learn martial arts from someone like me?”
I took a deep breath.
Only after turning it over from every angle did I finally reach a single conclusion.
“I will.”
“I’ll say it again...”
“I trust you, Old Master.
That’s enough.”
For a moment, Jeok Cheongang was speechless as indescribable emotions crossed his face.
Then a smile spread across his wrinkled lips.
“Then we are alike in that regard.”
One-person succession, passed only to the worthy.
For hundreds of years, the Fire Gate Clan’s legacy had been entrusted to a single talented individual who could be trusted not to use it for evil.
The fact that Jeok Cheongang had brought me here, to the Fire Gate Cavern, meant that he already trusted me.
Fire King Jeok Cheongang trusts me.
He chose me.
He intends to pass everything the Fire Gate Clan has to me.
My heart swelled at the thought.
As though it had sensed my emotions, the blue-white flame surged violently.
Ding.
System Quest Heir of the Blazing Flame has been created!
Along with the System notification, Jeok Cheongang reached out his hand.
As Seizing an Object Through Empty Space took effect, the lid of a dark metal box that had risen from the flames opened.
I read the title of the old book floating toward me.
“Fire Gate Divine Technique...”
I knew instinctively that this martial art was the foundation of the Fire Gate Clan—practically its entire legacy.
Jeok Cheongang had risen to his feet and now stood directly behind me.
“We’ll begin at once, so sit cross-legged and close your eyes.
From now on, circulate your energy according to the formula I teach you.”
I followed his instructions and closed my eyes.
In the darkness, the blue-white flame seemed to flicker before me.
At last, Jeok Cheongang’s voice pierced my ears.
“What about your fist-and-foot training?”
“Did you finish your training and start slacking off?
Wait, fuck, that startled me.
This is the Fire Gate Cavern.
What the hell is this?”
Oh, fuck.
Dementia...
After that day, the two people who had caused such a commotion on Mount Jiuhua for some time vanished without a trace.
While they were gone, the trees sprouted green leaves, the flowers bloomed in full, and the swallows built their nests along the cliffs.
From green, to autumn foliage, and then to white snow.
Until Mount Jiuhua changed its clothes three times.

chapters.title: Chapter 236
paragraphs: The man gazed at the Four Treasures of the Study, neatly arranged before him.
The brush was made from sable fur, the inkstone from bluish jade, and the ink and paper were tribute goods said to be used by the royal family of Haedong, ten thousand li away.
Every piece was of the finest quality, beyond the means of anyone but the wealthiest.
“Excellent. Simply excellent.”
A satisfied smile spread across his face. The man was famous for his frugality, and the Four Treasures of the Study were the one luxury he allowed himself.
“Well, then. Shall we begin?”
Just as he began happily grinding his ink, the door opened and someone strode toward him without hesitation.
“Anyone who saw you would think you were a Hanlin Academician.”
The uninvited guest was a martial artist covered in dust.
He had narrow, sharply slanted eyes and a well-worn sword at his waist. At the sight of him, the man made a show of hardening his expression.
“A Hanlin Academician? I’d rather you call me a master painter.”
“You still paint?”
“It’s my only pleasure.”
“Unfortunately, you don’t exactly look the part. Would you care to learn some martial arts from me?”
“I must respectfully decline. This is as far as my abilities as a martial artist will ever take me.”
“What a shame. You lack the qualities a martial artist ought to possess.”
“It doesn’t matter. I have a subordinate who’s astonishingly good with a sword. Why else would his epithet be Ghost Sword?”
At the man’s sly response, the uninvited guest’s expression slowly relaxed.
A moment later, as if by prior agreement, they both let out quiet laughs.
“My lord, you haven’t changed.”
“Neither have you, Wipeng.”
They had not seen each other in four whole months, making the reunion all the more welcome.
Jin Wikyung, the Lesser Family Head of the Jin Family of Taiyuan, smiled broadly as he clapped Wipeng on the shoulder.
“What brings you here without any warning? The messenger pigeon said you wouldn’t arrive until noon tomorrow.”
“The Jin Dragon Squad can manage perfectly well without me.”
The Jin Dragon Squad was currently the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s foremost fighting force.
It had been established only a year ago, but every member possessed impressive martial skills, and their loyalty to the family was even greater.
The fact that Wipeng, Jin Wikyung’s trusted subordinate, served as its Commander spoke volumes about the squad’s standing.
“You didn’t slip away on your own without telling anyone, did you? You are the Commander.”
“Of course not. I left that Hyuk fellow in charge. He’ll manage just fine.”
“The acting Deputy Commander?”
“Yes.”
“This was his first mission, wasn’t it? What did you think after watching him?”
Wipeng’s eyebrow twitched.
He had thought he was getting used to Hyuk Mujin, but merely thinking about the man made his head ache.
Still, merit was merit, and personal feelings were personal. He answered with a sigh.
“He’s useful enough. Aside from the fact that he never stops running his mouth.”
“I already had some idea, but he sounds even more cheerful than I expected.”
“He’s so goddamn cheerful it’s a problem.”
“What about everything else?”
“...If you teach him one thing at a time, he learns quickly.”
“If you’re saying that, he must possess considerable martial talent.”
A year earlier, Hyuk Mujin had been granted the honor of joining the Jin Dragon Squad in recognition of his service.
Naturally, Jin Taekyung’s influence had also played a part in that decision.
That fellow is better than he looks. Try training him.
Jin Wikyung had always had a soft spot for his younger brothers.
Thinking Taekyung might be right, he had placed Hyuk Mujin in the Jin Dragon Squad and assigned Wipeng to train him. Sure enough, the young man’s skills improved by the day.
His cheeky, easygoing nature helped him get along well with the other members, and there was no question about his loyalty.
“Ha-ha-ha! As expected of our youngest—he has an eye for people.”
Jin Wikyung laughed heartily. At some point, a bottle of liquor had appeared in his hand.
He filled a cup to the brim, handed it over, and spoke.
“In any case, you’ve worked hard. So, is everything in Northern Gaoyuan settled now?”
“Yes. There shouldn’t be any trouble for at least the next ten years.”
The stabilization of Northern Gaoyuan.
That was why Wipeng had been away from the Jin Family of Taiyuan for the past four months.

Jin Wikyung believed that to become the true hegemon of Shanxi Province, he first needed to subjugate Gaoyuan’s mounted bandits. After months of secret and meticulous preparation, he had unleashed his sharpest weapon against them.
The sword known as Ghost Sword Wipeng.
“We attacked from seven directions, and they collapsed without putting up any meaningful resistance.”
The Murim of Shanxi—particularly the sects and merchant groups in the northern region, which had suffered the worst damage—welcomed the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s bold decision and actively cooperated.
The so-called Seven-Route Army was formed with Wipeng and the Jin Dragon Squad at its forefront. With the merchants’ full support, they were equipped with quality weapons and warhorses.
Powerful reinforcements also joined the campaign.
“The Lower District Sect was frightening. I was reminded once again of how terrifying information can be.”
Having received a considerable share of the northern region’s interests immediately after the war, the Lower District Sect had welcomed Jin Wikyung’s decision with open arms.
Like the seasoned information merchants they were, they monitored the mounted bandits’ every move while spreading false information and laying traps.
Their thoroughness left even Jin Wikyung impressed.
“Everything in this world is put to different use depending on who wields it. The truly frightening one is Wolhwa. She isn’t meant to remain confined to Shanxi Province.”
“Is that so?”
“Can’t you tell from the results? Her true weapon isn’t her beauty. It’s her strategic mind.”
Two thousand.
That was the number of mounted bandits killed or captured in Northern Gaoyuan in that single day.
Seven battles broke out in seven different locations. After claiming seven victories, the army advanced without hesitation.
“After that, we killed or captured every mounted bandit we came across.”
Hundreds of crows wheeled through the sky, while perhaps ten times as many corpses lay scattered across the ground below.
By the time the Seven-Route Army’s horses finally came to a halt, five major mounted-bandit groups had been annihilated and more than ten others had surrendered.
“We had effectively achieved our objective by then.”
“I believe there’s more to the story.”
“Ah. You mean the nomads?”
“Exactly.”
Thanks to their swift, mobile strikes, the Seven-Route Army had suffered few casualties. But the successive battles had left them thoroughly exhausted.
That was when thousands of nomads appeared amid a massive cloud of dust.
“To be honest, even I felt dizzy when I saw them.”
There were thousands of them, and every single one was a master of mounted combat.
No matter how seasoned a Peak master Wipeng was, he had no way to turn the tide of battle alone.
“That was when the incident I reported earlier in my missive occurred.”
“You mean the ones who called themselves khans?”
The great nomadic empire that had once ruled even the Central Plains had long since faded into distant history. But the conquerors’ bloodline had not died out, and neither had the title of khan.
“There were two of them. They came forward first and introduced themselves...”
“Temur and Chinggen, descendants of the Great Khan and members of the Golden Clan.”
“Exactly.”
Wipeng nodded.
The young chieftains of the steppe had each arrived with two thousand riders. They were neither aggressive nor arrogant.
Instead, they cautiously attempted to converse in halting Korean.
“Is there anyone among you from the Jin Family of Taiyuan?”
The battle everyone had expected never took place.
All because of the name of the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.
“The rumor had already reached Gaoyuan. They knew about the relationship between Great Hero Jeok and the Third Young Master, and said they had no wish to become our enemies.”
“That is precisely what puzzles me. It seems rather suspicious that they would back down merely because of the Fire King’s reputation.”
“Ah, that? It didn’t sit right with me either, so I beat the truth out of the mounted-bandit prisoners.”
Wipeng grinned as he continued.

“They’d already been taught a harsh lesson last winter. Great Hero Jeok killed two notorious mounted-bandit leaders from Gaoyuan—Black Sand and the Human Butcher—with a single palm strike. Temur and Chinggen were both there.”
“They were frightened.”
“On the other hand, it benefited them as well. Once the leaders were dead, the mounted-bandit remnants fell into chaos. Temur and Chinggen absorbed them and grew as powerful as they are now.”
Temur and Chinggen had been lucky.
Black Sand and the Human Butcher had died in the same place, and not long afterward, even the Heavenly Wind Band had been annihilated by Jeok Cheongang. A power vacuum had formed.
After swallowing up the mounted-bandit remnants and gathering the scattered nomads, the two men had risen to become powers in Gaoyuan in the span of only a year.
“They said they wanted to remain on friendly terms from now on. They even loaded us down with furs and plundered gold and silver.”
“What? Ha-ha-ha!”
Jin Wikyung burst into delighted laughter.
The outcome could not have been better.
The campaign had further strengthened the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s fame and standing in the Shanxi Murim while also winning the support of its affiliated sects and the common people.
“You’ve worked hard. Much of the credit belongs to you.”
“I don’t know about that, but I do know my cup is empty.”
“Ha-ha! Then let’s drink until we’re both thoroughly drunk tonight.”
The two men traded cups and stories.
So much had happened over the past year that they had no shortage of things to discuss.
“Oh, right. What happened to the Seongun Escort Bureau?”
“We finished dealing with it completely right after you left. Though I suppose we should call it the Jin Family Escort Bureau now.”

Woo Hwangtae, chief of the Seongun Escort Bureau, had fled with his family, taking only a paltry sum with them. It had been discovered that they had bribed several officials and secretly diverted military supplies.
Prince Shangshan, Zhu Bao, an ardent admirer of Jin Taekyung, had of course provided considerable help during the process.
“Our cooperation with the other sects is progressing smoothly as well. An escort caravan traveling through Mount Song to Hefei is already under way.”
“Mount Song and Hefei...?”
“Shaolin and Namgung. It was too good an offer to refuse.”
Shaolin, the Mount Tai and Northern Dipper of the Murim, and the Namgung Family, counted among the foremost of the Five Great Families.
Both were such enormous powers that Jin Wikyung would have been satisfied merely to establish trade with them. Instead, they had approached him first—and offered extremely generous terms at that.
“Great Hero Jeok’s presence has been a tremendous help to our family.”
Jin Wikyung merely smiled at Wipeng’s remark.
He firmly believed that in the Murim, at least, no favor came without a price.
Their goodwill contained the price of two people.
One was the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.
The other was the value of Jin Taekyung, a Sleeping Dragon.
Come to think of it, it’s already been a year since our youngest left.
It had been a year filled with countless hardships and events.
Once the ground thawed, the Star-Array Grand Banquet would be held in Henan. The brothers would meet again there.
Are you staying safe?
Jin Wikyung raised his cup, thinking of his thoughtless youngest brother, who had not contacted him even once. Just then, Wipeng spoke.
“By the way, what were you planning to paint this time?”
“I wonder.”
“You were grinding ink without even deciding what to paint?”
“It happens from time to time. I often spend one or two shichen grinding ink, only to put everything away again.”
“Huh. Are you truly trying to become a master painter now?”
“Put that thought aside for now. But once this painting is complete, I think I’d be happy to be called a master painter.”
“Didn’t you just say you hadn’t decided what to paint?”
“It’s merely that I can’t quite picture what it will look like. I decided on the title long ago.”
“Then what is this magnificent work called?”
Jin Wikyung answered with a smile.
“The Sleeping Dragon Enters Service.”
He was a young man in shabby clothes.
His long, loose hair reached his shoulder blades, and thick stubble covered his chin and upper lip.
The crowning touch was the iron balls dangling from all four limbs, making him look like a convict in a forced-labor camp.
Yet one thing about him was different.
His eyes.
The young man stared into the blue-white flame with a gaze of unfathomable depth, then muttered,
“Ah. This would be the perfect place to grill some meat.”
The next instant—
Fwoosh! Smack!
With a savage crack of displaced air, a wrinkled palm slammed into the back of the young man’s head.
“What an insolent brat! How dare you even think of grilling meat over our sect’s sacred flame!”
The old man was beside himself with rage, but the young man merely grumbled.
“Ah, why not? It should be fine if I just stick it in for a second and pull it right back out.”
“What did you say?”
“You’ve never heard of kiln-roasted pork belly? It’s insanely good.”
“You—you’re dead today!”
Smack! Crash!
On an early spring day, as the earth thawed and fresh shoots poked their heads aboveground, peaceful Mount Jiuhua began to grow noisy.
