“...If you teach him one thing at a time, he learns quickly.”
“If you’re saying that, he must possess considerable martial talent.”
A year earlier, Hyuk Mujin had been granted the honor of joining the Jin Dragon Squad in recognition of his service.
Naturally, Jin Taekyung’s influence had also played a part in that decision.
That fellow is better than he looks.
Try training him.
Jin Wikyung had always had a soft spot for his younger brothers.
Thinking Taekyung might be right, he had placed Hyuk Mujin in the Jin Dragon Squad and assigned Wipeng to train him.
Sure enough, the young man’s skills improved by the day.
His cheeky, easygoing nature helped him get along well with the other members, and there was no question about his loyalty.
“Ha-ha-ha!
As expected of our youngest—he has an eye for people.”
Jin Wikyung laughed heartily.
At some point, a bottle of liquor had appeared in his hand.
He filled a cup to the brim, handed it over, and spoke.
“In any case, you’ve worked hard.
So, is everything in Northern Gaoyuan settled now?”
“Yes.
There shouldn’t be any trouble for at least the next ten years.”
The stabilization of Northern Gaoyuan.
That was why Wipeng had been away from the Jin Family of Taiyuan for the past four months.
Jin Wikyung believed that to become the true hegemon of Shanxi Province, he first needed to subjugate Gaoyuan’s mounted bandits.
After months of secret and meticulous preparation, he had unleashed his sharpest weapon against them.
The sword known as Ghost Sword Wipeng.
“We attacked from seven directions, and they collapsed without putting up any meaningful resistance.”
The Murim of Shanxi—particularly the sects and merchant groups in the northern region, which had suffered the worst damage—welcomed the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s bold decision and actively cooperated.
The so-called Seven-Route Army was formed with Wipeng and the Jin Dragon Squad at its forefront.
With the merchants’ full support, they were equipped with quality weapons and warhorses.
Powerful reinforcements also joined the campaign.
“The Lower District Sect was frightening.
I was reminded once again of how terrifying information can be.”
Having received a considerable share of the northern region’s interests immediately after the war, the Lower District Sect had welcomed Jin Wikyung’s decision with open arms.
Like the seasoned information merchants they were, they monitored the mounted bandits’ every move while spreading false information and laying traps.
Their thoroughness left even Jin Wikyung impressed.
“Everything in this world is put to different use depending on who wields it.
The truly frightening one is Wolhwa.
She isn’t meant to remain confined to Shanxi Province.”
“Is that so?”
“Can’t you tell from the results?
Her true weapon isn’t her beauty.
It’s her strategic mind.”
Two thousand.
That was the number of mounted bandits killed or captured in Northern Gaoyuan in that single day.
Seven battles broke out in seven different locations.
After claiming seven victories, the army advanced without hesitation.
“After that, we killed or captured every mounted bandit we came across.”
Hundreds of crows wheeled through the sky, while perhaps ten times as many corpses lay scattered across the ground below.
By the time the Seven-Route Army’s horses finally came to a halt, five major mounted-bandit groups had been annihilated and more than ten others had surrendered.
“We had effectively achieved our objective by then.”
“I believe there’s more to the story.”
“Ah.
You mean the nomads?”
“Exactly.”
Thanks to their swift, mobile strikes, the Seven-Route Army had suffered few casualties.
But the successive battles had left them thoroughly exhausted.
That was when thousands of nomads appeared amid a massive cloud of dust.
“To be honest, even I felt dizzy when I saw them.”
There were thousands of them, and every single one was a master of mounted combat.
No matter how seasoned a Peak master Wipeng was, he had no way to turn the tide of battle alone.
“That was when the incident I reported earlier in my missive occurred.”
“You mean the ones who called themselves khans?”
The great nomadic empire that had once ruled even the Central Plains had long since faded into distant history.
But the conquerors’ bloodline had not died out, and neither had the title of khan.
“There were two of them.
They came forward first and introduced themselves...”
“Temur and Chinggen, descendants of the Great Khan and members of the Golden Clan.”
“Exactly.”
Wipeng nodded.
The young chieftains of the steppe had each arrived with two thousand riders.
They were neither aggressive nor arrogant.
Instead, they cautiously attempted to converse in halting Korean.
“Is there anyone among you from the Jin Family of Taiyuan?”
The battle everyone had expected never took place.
All because of the name of the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.
“The rumor had already reached Gaoyuan.
They knew about the relationship between Great Hero Jeok and the Third Young Master, and said they had no wish to become our enemies.”
“That is precisely what puzzles me.
It seems rather suspicious that they would back down merely because of the Fire King’s reputation.”
“Ah, that?
It didn’t sit right with me either, so I beat the truth out of the mounted-bandit prisoners.”
Wipeng grinned as he continued.
“They’d already been taught a harsh lesson last winter.
Great Hero Jeok killed two notorious mounted-bandit leaders from Gaoyuan—Black Sand and the Human Butcher—with a single palm strike.
Temur and Chinggen were both there.”
“They were frightened.”
“On the other hand, it benefited them as well.
Once the leaders were dead, the mounted-bandit remnants fell into chaos.
Temur and Chinggen absorbed them and grew as powerful as they are now.”
Temur and Chinggen had been lucky.
Black Sand and the Human Butcher had died in the same place, and not long afterward, even the Heavenly Wind Band had been annihilated by Jeok Cheongang.
A power vacuum had formed.
After swallowing up the mounted-bandit remnants and gathering the scattered nomads, the two men had risen to become powers in Gaoyuan in the span of only a year.
“They said they wanted to remain on friendly terms from now on.
They even loaded us down with furs and plundered gold and silver.”
“What?
Ha-ha-ha!”
Jin Wikyung burst into delighted laughter.
The outcome could not have been better.
The campaign had further strengthened the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s fame and standing in the Shanxi Murim while also winning the support of its affiliated sects and the common people.
“You’ve worked hard.
Much of the credit belongs to you.”
“I don’t know about that, but I do know my cup is empty.”
“Ha-ha!
Then let’s drink until we’re both thoroughly drunk tonight.”
The two men traded cups and stories.
So much had happened over the past year that they had no shortage of things to discuss.
“Oh, right.
What happened to the Seongun Escort Bureau?”
“We finished dealing with it completely right after you left.
Though I suppose we should call it the Jin Family Escort Bureau now.”
Woo Hwangtae, chief of the Seongun Escort Bureau, had fled with his family, taking only a paltry sum with them.
It had been discovered that they had bribed several officials and secretly diverted military supplies.
Prince Shangshan, Zhu Bao, an ardent admirer of Jin Taekyung, had of course provided considerable help during the process.
“Our cooperation with the other sects is progressing smoothly as well.
An escort caravan traveling through Mount Song to Hefei is already under way.”
“Mount Song and Hefei...?”
“Shaolin and Namgung.
It was too good an offer to refuse.”
Shaolin, the Mount Tai and Northern Dipper of the Murim, and the Namgung Family, counted among the foremost of the Five Great Families.
Both were such enormous powers that Jin Wikyung would have been satisfied merely to establish trade with them.
Instead, they had approached him first—and offered extremely generous terms at that.
“Great Hero Jeok’s presence has been a tremendous help to our family.”
Jin Wikyung merely smiled at Wipeng’s remark.
He firmly believed that in the Murim, at least, no favor came without a price.
Their goodwill contained the price of two people.
One was the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang.
The other was the value of Jin Taekyung, a Sleeping Dragon.
Come to think of it, it’s already been a year since our youngest left.
It had been a year filled with countless hardships and events.
Once the ground thawed, the Star-Array Grand Banquet would be held in Henan.
The brothers would meet again there.
Are you staying safe?
Jin Wikyung raised his cup, thinking of his thoughtless youngest brother, who had not contacted him even once.
Just then, Wipeng spoke.
“By the way, what were you planning to paint this time?”
“I wonder.”
“You were grinding ink without even deciding what to paint?”
“It happens from time to time.
I often spend one or two shichen grinding ink, only to put everything away again.”
“Huh.
Are you truly trying to become a master painter now?”
“Put that thought aside for now.
But once this painting is complete, I think I’d be happy to be called a master painter.”
“Didn’t you just say you hadn’t decided what to paint?”
“It’s merely that I can’t quite picture what it will look like.
I decided on the title long ago.”
“Then what is this magnificent work called?”
Jin Wikyung answered with a smile.
“The Sleeping Dragon Enters Service.”
He was a young man in shabby clothes.
His long, loose hair reached his shoulder blades, and thick stubble covered his chin and upper lip.
The crowning touch was the iron balls dangling from all four limbs, making him look like a convict in a forced-labor camp.
Yet one thing about him was different.
His eyes.
The young man stared into the blue-white flame with a gaze of unfathomable depth, then muttered,
“Ah.
This would be the perfect place to grill some meat.”
The next instant—
Fwoosh!
Smack!
With a savage crack of displaced air, a wrinkled palm slammed into the back of the young man’s head.
“What an insolent brat!
How dare you even think of grilling meat over our sect’s sacred flame!”
The old man was beside himself with rage, but the young man merely grumbled.
“Ah, why not?
It should be fine if I just stick it in for a second and pull it right back out.”
“What did you say?”
“You’ve never heard of kiln-roasted pork belly?
It’s insanely good.”
“You—you’re dead today!”
Smack!
Crash!
On an early spring day, as the earth thawed and fresh shoots poked their heads aboveground, peaceful Mount Jiuhua began to grow noisy.

chapters.title: Chapter 237
paragraphs: Jeok Cheongang roared at the top of his lungs.
“You’re a disgrace to our sect!”
“No, I’m not.”
“What do you mean, you’re not? In all the hundreds of years of the Fire Gate Clan’s history, there has never been a bastard who wanted to grill meat over the sacred flame!”
“That’s not what I meant.”
“What?”
“I’m not an official Disciple yet. So I can’t be a disgrace to the Fire Gate Clan.”
His face turned bright red, as though it might burst at any moment.
Before he could shout even louder, I quickly slung my pack over my shoulder.
“If there’s nothing else to pack, let’s get out of here.”
“Y-you little...”
Jeok Cheongang’s fist trembled, but after a moment, he let out a deep sigh.
This was hardly the first time something like this had happened over the past year. Even the famously short-tempered Fire King had reached the point where he simply took it in stride.
Ah, I’m so proud.
I had actually managed to beat the Fire King at something. Somehow, it felt like I had accomplished something incredible.
After glaring at my foolish grin, he turned toward the seventeen ancestral urns and bowed deeply.
“Your unworthy Disciple, Jeok Cheongang, will take his leave. Until then, please remain in good health.”
“Shouldn’t you wish them Buddhahood?”
“...And here, I swear that I will turn that bastard into a proper human being.”
Having firmly renewed his resolve before the seventeen former Sect Leaders, Jeok Cheongang rose to his feet.
“Come. Let’s go, you beast.”
“Wait a moment.”
I slowly looked around the enormous cavern.

This was where I had spent the past year. There had been times when the pain was enough to make me think I would die, and there had been happy moments too. Sometimes, I had been so sick of the place that I wanted to smash through the stone gate and run outside that very instant.
But when had it happened?
Little by little, everything had become familiar, and the happy days had begun to outnumber the painful ones.
Even the tremendous heat pouring from the blue-white flame now felt as warm and cozy as home.
“What are you thinking about so intently?”
“Just...”
What was I supposed to call this feeling?
After a moment’s thought, the words slipped out.
“I was thinking meat would taste really good grilled over that.”
“You little bastaaard!”
Dodging Jeok Cheongang as he flew into a rage, I placed my hand against the stone gate. As I channeled the internal energy from my dantian into it, the tightly sealed door slowly slid open.
System Scorching Sun Divine Arts internal energy detected. - You may freely enter and exit Fire Gate Cavern!
Take care.
Thanks for everything over the past year.
And...
Your unworthy Disciple, Jin Taekyung, will take his leave.
I raced out of the wide-open cavern like the wind. The iron balls dangling from my limbs whipped around like pinwheels.
Mount Jiuhua had been famous since ancient times for its spiritual energy.

With auspicious energy filling the entire mountain, it was only natural for spiritual herbs such as ginseng and He Shou Wu to grow there. To herbalists, the mountain was no different from a gold mine.
“Just you wait. Today, I’m finding one.”
At the foot of Mount Jiuhua, a middle-aged herbalist with the surname Hong pulled the strings of his straw sandals tight.
He had traveled all the way from Sichuan in hopes of striking it rich, only to spend more than fifteen days coming up empty-handed.
“Damn it. What happened to all the spiritual herbs? It’s like every last one has vanished...”
The herbalists who had come with him had already given up and gone home. They had searched everywhere from the foot of Mount Jiuhua to halfway up the mountain without finding a single ginseng root.
There might have been a chance farther up, but something more terrifying than any wild beast lived there.
The Fire King.
Even martial artists who killed people as casually as they ate meals trembled at the mere mention of his name.
Hong had once heard that the Fire King had single-handedly torn apart and killed a thousand vicious fiends of the terrifying Demonic Cult.
When he had asked how such a thing was possible, he had been told that the Fire King was a three-headed, six-armed monster.
But they said it’s safe as long as I don’t go past the midpoint. Don’t be scared, Hong. You have eight mouths to feed.
To cover the cost of coming this far, his wife had even been forced to sell the silver ring she had received as a wedding gift. How could he face her if he went home empty-handed?
Smack! Smack!
The herbalist slapped his cheeks to steel his resolve, then began climbing the mountain.
Less than two shichen later, he encountered the strangest sight he had ever seen.
“So what is samgyeopsal?”
“You don’t know pork belly? Is it called something else here?”
“No, you impudent brat. Just where are you from that you keep going on about what things are called?”
“I’m from Korea! Do you know kimchi?”
“...You grow more insane by the day. Is there something wrong with your Fire Gate Divine Technique?”
A wild-haired freak and a tiny old man were walking down the mountain path, having an incomprehensible conversation.
The pair looked strange enough already, but as they drew closer, the herbalist heard a series of thunderous noises and his eyes widened.
Clank. Rattle. Boom! Rattle-rattle. Boom!
W-what in the world is that?
The source of the heavy noises was the iron balls chained to the freak’s limbs.
The smaller ones were as large as a child’s head, while the larger ones were big enough to fit inside a basket.
With dozens of such vicious objects dangling from his body, the herbalist had no choice but to be shocked.
What am I looking at?
The herbalist stared blankly at the sight, then suddenly jolted.
Two pairs of eyes had drawn close enough to stare directly into his face.
Up close, the freak had a thick beard, while the old man’s face was covered in blotches and more wrinkles than he could count.
“Gyaaaah!”
As the herbalist nearly suffered a fit, the tiny old man addressed him.
“Hey.”
“Y-yes?”
“Where are you headed?”
“I-I’m going to dig up medicinal herbs.”
The herbalist barely managed to squeeze out the words.
He didn’t know why, but instinct told him that something terrible would happen if he failed to answer.
The old man looked him up and down, then clicked his tongue.
“You’ve wasted your time. Don’t put yourself through all that for nothing. Go home.”
“W-wasted my time?”
Despite his terror, the herbalist instantly snapped to attention.
Go home? If he returned empty-handed now, he would have wasted nearly two months of his life.
With the heavy load on his shoulders, that was absolutely unacceptable.
This old man is no ordinary person.
It wasn’t just his unusual appearance. Even his manner of speaking made it sound as though he could see through all the affairs of the world.
The thought flashed through the herbalist’s mind like lightning, and he collapsed to his knees.
“Please help me just this once!”
“Good heavens, what’s gotten into you? What could this old man possibly do to help?”
“No! You’re the Mountain Spirit! You already know everything, don’t you?”
Bafflement spread across the old man’s face.
“...What spirit?”
“Mountain Spiriiit!”
The freak beside him clutched his stomach and burst out laughing.
“Puhahaha! He thinks you’re a Mountain Spirit. Old Master, wasn’t it three months ago that you forgot the formula while circulating your qi and nearly became a ghost?”
Wham! Craaack!
The freak was still roaring with laughter when a single punch from the old man sent him flying dozens of jang away, where he crashed into the ground.
The herbalist’s faith only deepened.
The Mountain Spirit subdued the evil spirit!
It was only natural to trust the white-haired old man more than the ragged freak. The herbalist pleaded once more.
“Mountain Spirit! Please help me just this once!”
“Mountain Spirit, my ass. And there’s nothing this old man can do for you. I already pulled them all up, so what do you expect me to do?”
“P-pulled them up? Who pulled up all the spiritual herbs on Mount Jiuhua?”
“Now you’re finally making sense.”
“W-who would do such a thing...?”
The old man clasped his hands behind his back and gazed toward the distant mountain.
“My, what fine weather.”
“What are you staring at? Whoever pulls them up first gets to keep them.”
Despair crossed the herbalist’s face. Only then did he realize that the old man before him was no immortal.
“Then are you an herbalist too, Elder?”
“Hm? Well, I was for a few days. Digging up medicinal herbs is rather difficult.”
“You tear people’s heads off easily enough.”
The evil spirit—or rather, the freak—had returned and casually joined the conversation while dusting off his clothes.
His manner and tone were so nonchalant that the massive trees snapped apart behind him might as well not have existed.
“My ancestors always said there was no point feeding spiritual herbs to a Disciple. They were absolutely right.”
“Buuurp.”
“You son of a—!”
A dreadful pressure poured from the old man’s clenched fist. At last, the herbalist realized what the two men were.
“M-m-martial artists!”
“Now that you understand, give up and go home. And be careful not to spread unnecessary rumors.”
The freak also offered his advice with a serious expression.

“Whatever you do, don’t go any farther up. They say a monster named Fire King Jeok Cheongang lives there. If he catches you, he’ll chew you up, tear you apart, savor you, and enjoy you while you’re still alive—then kill you.”
It was horrifying even to imagine. The herbalist shuddered as he pictured his own gruesome death.
Judging by the old man’s similar reaction, this Fire King Jeok Cheongang had to be exactly what Hong had heard: a three-headed, six-armed monster.
“Understood? Make sure you remember what I told you.”
“Y-yes, I understand.”
That was the only answer the herbalist could give.
Someone had already beaten him to the herbs, and the two men before him were martial artists. If he made a nuisance of himself, he might lose his head.
His shoulders sagged as he stepped aside to let them pass.
“Oh, wait. Sir, if this is good enough, would you like it?”
Swish.
The freak rummaged through his pack and suddenly held out a ginseng root about three finger joints long.
Startled by the unexpected kindness, the herbalist asked in a trembling voice,
“W-why are you giving this to me?”
“If you go home like this, you’ll have nothing to show for it. Judging by your age, you probably have a family to support too. Where did you come from?”
“S-Sichuan Province.”
“Sichuan Province is fun, isn’t it? I used to play it all the time during evening self-study.”
“Pardon?”
“Never mind. Anyway, you came a long way, so use this to help cover your travel expenses.”
The old man, who had been silently watching, clicked his tongue.
“You little fool. You give him something worth only a few coins, then act like you’ve made some grand gesture. If a man is going to be generous, he should give generously.”
“Come on, that’s all I have left. What else am I supposed to do?”
“You call that ginseng? At least exchange it for silver.”
“How?”
“People determine the value of an object.”
“Oh. I hadn’t thought of that.”
What kind of bizarre conversation was this?
As the herbalist looked back and forth between them, feeling as though he had been bewitched, the freak suddenly shouted at the top of his lungs.
“Anyone want to buy some ginseng?”
It was still early dawn. As the cold wind blew, the trees shuddered.
Then several dozen men appeared on the mountain path below, marching in orderly rows.
Blue martial uniforms and sword sheaths hung from their waists. At a glance, it was obvious that every one of them was a highly trained martial artist.
“Guh!”
The herbalist’s mouth fell open, but the other two remained perfectly calm. The freak gently waved the ginseng root worth three silver nyang.
“I’ll sell it for a hundred silver nyang.”
What a highway robber.
The herbalist swallowed the words that had risen to his throat. Just then, the middle-aged man at the head of the group spoke.
“I’ll buy it.”
The shocks were not over. The old man let out a long yawn and casually added,
“Three hundred silver nyang. You’re the richest man in Anhui, so you can afford that much.”
The middle-aged man bowed deeply.
“That is a small price to pay for offending the Fire King. I’ll buy it.”
The freak grinned.
“Then may I ask the winning bidder’s name?”
“Namgung Ryong.”
The middle-aged man raised his head. The authority possessed only by a leader flashed in his deep-set eyes.
“I am the Family Head of the Namgung Family.”

He thinks you’re a Mountain Spirit.
Old Master, wasn’t it three months ago that you forgot the formula while circulating your qi and nearly became a ghost?”
Wham!
Craaack!
The freak was still roaring with laughter when a single punch from the old man sent him flying dozens of jang away, where he crashed into the ground.
The herbalist’s faith only deepened.
The Mountain Spirit subdued the evil spirit!
It was only natural to trust the white-haired old man more than the ragged freak.
The herbalist pleaded once more.
“Mountain Spirit!
Please help me just this once!”
“Mountain Spirit, my ass.
And there’s nothing this old man can do for you.
I already pulled them all up, so what do you expect me to do?”
“P-pulled them up?
Who pulled up all the spiritual herbs on Mount Jiuhua?”
“Now you’re finally making sense.”
“W-who would do such a thing...?”
The old man clasped his hands behind his back and gazed toward the distant mountain.
“My, what fine weather.”
“What are you staring at?
Whoever pulls them up first gets to keep them.”
Despair crossed the herbalist’s face.
Only then did he realize that the old man before him was no immortal.
“Then are you an herbalist too, Elder?”
“Hm?
Well, I was for a few days.
Digging up medicinal herbs is rather difficult.”
“You tear people’s heads off easily enough.”
The evil spirit—or rather, the freak—had returned and casually joined the conversation while dusting off his clothes.
His manner and tone were so nonchalant that the massive trees snapped apart behind him might as well not have existed.
“My ancestors always said there was no point feeding spiritual herbs to a Disciple.
They were absolutely right.”
“Buuurp.”
“You son of a—!”
A dreadful pressure poured from the old man’s clenched fist.
At last, the herbalist realized what the two men were.
“M-m-martial artists!”
“Now that you understand, give up and go home.
And be careful not to spread unnecessary rumors.”
The freak also offered his advice with a serious expression.
“Whatever you do, don’t go any farther up.
They say a monster named Fire King Jeok Cheongang lives there.
If he catches you, he’ll chew you up, tear you apart, savor you, and enjoy you while you’re still alive—then kill you.”
It was horrifying even to imagine.
The herbalist shuddered as he pictured his own gruesome death.
Judging by the old man’s similar reaction, this Fire King Jeok Cheongang had to be exactly what Hong had heard: a three-headed, six-armed monster.
“Understood?
Make sure you remember what I told you.”
“Y-yes, I understand.”
That was the only answer the herbalist could give.
Someone had already beaten him to the herbs, and the two men before him were martial artists.
If he made a nuisance of himself, he might lose his head.
His shoulders sagged as he stepped aside to let them pass.
“Oh, wait.
Sir, if this is good enough, would you like it?”
Swish.
The freak rummaged through his pack and suddenly held out a ginseng root about three finger joints long.
Startled by the unexpected kindness, the herbalist asked in a trembling voice,
“W-why are you giving this to me?”
“If you go home like this, you’ll have nothing to show for it.
Judging by your age, you probably have a family to support too.
Where did you come from?”
“S-Sichuan Province.”
“Sichuan Province is fun, isn’t it?
I used to play it all the time during evening self-study.”
“Pardon?”
“Never mind.
Anyway, you came a long way, so use this to help cover your travel expenses.”
The old man, who had been silently watching, clicked his tongue.
“You little fool.
You give him something worth only a few coins, then act like you’ve made some grand gesture.
If a man is going to be generous, he should give generously.”
“Come on, that’s all I have left.
What else am I supposed to do?”
“You call that ginseng?
At least exchange it for silver.”
“How?”
“People determine the value of an object.”
“Oh.
I hadn’t thought of that.”
What kind of bizarre conversation was this?
As the herbalist looked back and forth between them, feeling as though he had been bewitched, the freak suddenly shouted at the top of his lungs.
“Anyone want to buy some ginseng?”
It was still early dawn.
As the cold wind blew, the trees shuddered.
Then several dozen men appeared on the mountain path below, marching in orderly rows.
Blue martial uniforms and sword sheaths hung from their waists.
At a glance, it was obvious that every one of them was a highly trained martial artist.
“Guh!”
The herbalist’s mouth fell open, but the other two remained perfectly calm.
The freak gently waved the ginseng root worth three silver nyang.
“I’ll sell it for a hundred silver nyang.”
What a highway robber.
The herbalist swallowed the words that had risen to his throat.
Just then, the middle-aged man at the head of the group spoke.
“I’ll buy it.”
The shocks were not over.
The old man let out a long yawn and casually added,
“Three hundred silver nyang.
You’re the richest man in Anhui, so you can afford that much.”
The middle-aged man bowed deeply.
“That is a small price to pay for offending the Fire King.
I’ll buy it.”
The freak grinned.
“Then may I ask the winning bidder’s name?”
“Namgung Ryong.”
The middle-aged man raised his head.
The authority possessed only by a leader flashed in his deep-set eyes.
“I am the Family Head of the Namgung Family.”

chapters.title: Chapter 238
paragraphs: The Namgung Family.
It was one of the Five Great Families that ruled the Murim alongside the Nine Sects and One Gang.
Their blood relatives alone numbered over a hundred, and once the martial artists under their command were included, their numbers reached into the thousands.
Perhaps that was why the sheer scale of their estate put the Jin Family of Taiyuan to shame.
“Wow.”
How many times larger was it? Five times? Ten?
As if to demonstrate the family’s wealth and authority, the guest room we had been shown was both spacious and lavish.
Jeok Cheongang watched me gape in admiration as though I were pathetic.
“Is this your first time visiting the Namgung Family?”
“...Of course it is.”
“Ah, right.”
It wasn’t as though the Namgung Family were some neighborhood convenience store.
Normally, I would have made at least one more sarcastic remark, but not today.
I knew that Jeok Cheongang and the Namgung Family were not on particularly friendly terms.
All because that bastard Jopil left a pile of shit behind.
When a student did something wrong, the school called his parents.

The Namgung Family was indisputably a great power of the Murim and the hegemon of Anhui. They could hardly have avoided becoming entangled with Jeok Cheongang after he took as his Disciple a murderer who had brutally slain dozens of commoners within the province.
Then again, that’s probably why he came along without complaint.
Remembering something I had heard at an inn in Shanxi Province, I asked, “He was the Azure Sky Sword King, right? The person who came looking for you back then.”
“That’s right. He was the one who first informed me of what had happened, and he was also the one who later granted my request. I owe him a great debt.”
On the day Jeok Cheongang had been unable to bring himself to kill Jopil and let him go, if the Namgung Family had intervened, Jopil would never have made it out of Anhui alive.
The person Jeok Cheongang had gone to see at the time was the Grand Family Head of the Namgung Family, the Azure Sky Sword King.
“What kind of person is he?”
“I have only met him twice, but... the Sword King I know is truly a man obsessed with swords.”
“Oh. A sword nut.”
“A sword nut?”
“It means someone who’s crazy about swords. It’s a compliment, so let it go.”
“There’s no trusting anything you say.”
Pretty sharp.
Jeok Cheongang gave me a suspicious glare, then continued.
“In any case, there is no doubt that he is an unpredictable man. He wanted a duel with this old man in exchange for sparing Jangcheon.”
“A duel?”
“Can you guess what kind of man he is now?”
“Yeah, I’m getting a pretty clear picture.”
A horrific series of murders had taken place in Anhui, yet the Grand Family Head of the Namgung Family—the hegemon of the province—had let the culprit go.
Setting aside the injustice suffered by the victims, it could not have been a welcome outcome for the Namgung Family either.
People would whisper that one of the Five Great Families was incompetent.
He really is a sword nut.
They said Supreme Peak masters trained endlessly for even the slightest scrap of enlightenment.
I had yet to meet the Azure Sky Sword King, but I suspected he was that kind of person.
That aside...
“Who won the duel?”
“The day after his duel with this old man, the Azure Sky Sword King entered seclusion.”
“Oh.”
“The difference was half a form.”
In other words, Jeok Cheongang had won by the narrowest of margins.

Even fights between Third Rate martial artists could be decided by the smallest detail. What, then, of a battle between Supreme Peak masters? The outcome would be decided by a difference as thin as a single strand of silk.
“It happened more than twenty years ago, so he must be even stronger now. He was formidable even then, but I can no longer guarantee victory with any confidence.”
I stared at Jeok Cheongang’s solemn expression.
Even a man with such earth-shaking martial arts was only human.
I had realized that several times during the year we spent together in Fire Gate Cavern, and it had brought us closer.
The infirmities of old age.
A curse wrought by time that even a Supreme Peak master could not overcome.
Fortunately, a stroke of heavenly luck had eased his symptoms. But it had only slowed the wheel already in motion. It could not stop it completely.
Guessing how Jeok Cheongang felt, I put on my brightest expression.
“Come on, don’t worry too much. We didn’t come here to fight. We were simply invited to the Sword King’s birthday celebration.”
“Do you truly think that?”
“Hm?”
“Didn’t this old man tell you? He is obsessed with swords.”
A thought flashed through my mind.
People obsessed with something paid no attention to the world around them. They immersed themselves in it—literally, madly—solely to satisfy their desires.
Alcohol, gambling, drugs... martial arts were no different.
It had been none other than the Azure Sky Sword King who released Jopil so that he could spar with Jeok Cheongang.
“Now that I think about it, the timing is awfully convenient.”
“He must have been waiting.”
“So his birthday is just an excuse?”

“The Azure Sky Sword King is the sort of man who could change his birthday hundreds of times. I suspect the only day that truly matters to him is the day he draws his last breath. That is when he will have no choice but to put down his sword.”
What the hell? That was terrifying.
The bastard wasn’t just a sword nut. He was completely insane.
I was rubbing the goose bumps from my arms when a delicate woman’s voice came from outside the door.
“The Family Head wishes to meet Young Hero Jin.”
Clank, boom. Clank, boom.
The chains clashed, and the iron balls gouged deep into the ground, leaving long tracks behind them.
I glanced back and saw that the entire route I had taken was marked by a line.
Is this Hansel and Gretel?
If the siblings in the fairy tale had possessed something like this, they would never have gotten lost.

Even if they had, there would have been no need to worry. I imagined Hansel strangling the witch with a Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron chain while Gretel smashed her in the back of the head with an iron ball, then shook my head.
“Ugh, no. That’s not it.”
“Young Hero Jin?”
The maid was looking at me as though I were insane. I waved my hand.
“No, it’s nothing. Let’s keep going.”
“No, that’s not what I meant...”
“Yes?”
“I-I beg your pardon, but those things you have with you are rather...”
“Ah.”
The maid was pointing at my iron balls.
Apparently, I had done quite a number on someone else’s courtyard.
Several sturdy servants had gathered by then, filling in the marks I had left with dirt while wearing gloomy expressions.
“I’m sorry. I’ll just carry them, then.”
Clank.
I gathered the chains together and lifted the iron balls.
I had weighed them faithfully during the first few months, but after that, I gave up. Whenever they got heavier, I simply assumed more weight had been added and left it at that.
They must weigh a hell of a lot by now.
In any case, there was no way I could cross the grounds of the Namgung Family like that without attracting attention.
To everyone else, I probably looked like a fruit seller hauling several dozen watermelons.
Every step brought more murmurs to my ears.
“Who is that guy? Have you heard anything?”
“No idea. With those iron balls chained to him, he looks like a prisoner.”
“Can you really say he’s chained to them?”
“...I suppose not.”
“No one could possibly carry that many iron balls of that size. They must be weapons plated with iron.”
“What on earth is he? Judging by his appearance, he’s a beggar among beggars. At that level, he’d be an Elder even in the Beggars’ Sect.”
“He doesn’t have any knots, so I don’t think that’s it...”
As I listened to the Namgung martial artists quietly debate among themselves, one thought crossed my mind.
You fucking bastards.
A beggar among beggars? An Elder of the Beggars’ Sect?
That year in Fire Gate Cavern had been a literal hell of scorching heat.
If a sauna was dangerous to pregnant women and the elderly, Fire Gate Cavern was simply dangerous to human beings.
My sweat had formed puddles, and every breath had felt as though my lungs were burning away.
I’d even deliberately endured it without using Logout.
After going so long without washing, the habit had become so ingrained that I could no longer tell whether I smelled or whether insects were crawling over my body.
I should’ve washed as soon as we arrived.
If we had gone to the inn first, I could have soaked in hot water, but everything had gone wrong when we came straight to the Namgung Family.
Jeok Cheongang had been speaking so seriously about the Azure Sky Sword King. I couldn’t exactly have told him I was going to scrub off some grime first.
“You bastards try it yourselves... It’s not like you’re going to scrub my back.”
The maid’s steps quickened after I muttered that. It was definitely my imagination.
A short while later, I arrived at a pavilion surrounded by tight security.
The Namgung Family’s guards, each with the two characters for Azure Heaven embroidered across his chest, blocked my path.
“Are you Young Hero Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan?”
I concealed my surprise and nodded.
There were ten guards. They ranged in age from their twenties to their forties, and every last one of them was a Peak master.
Good heavens. They were using ten Peak masters merely to guard a pavilion.
Is this why they’re counted among the Five Great Families?
For the first time, I could truly feel the power and status of the Namgung Family.
Perhaps he noticed my reaction, because the youngest-looking guard let out a quiet laugh.
“Disarm yourself.”
I suppressed my surprise and answered, “Disarm myself? I don’t have any weapons on me.”
“Then what do you call the things in your hands?”
“Oh.”
Right. I had these.
If even a ballpoint pen could kill someone, the iron balls I was carrying certainly qualified as weapons.
To me, they were merely heavy clothes I had to wear, but other people saw them differently.
The problem was...
“I’m sorry, but I’m still training. I can’t just take them off whenever I want.”
“Training?”
“Yes.”
It wasn’t a lie. I had grown so accustomed to them that I saw no particular reason to remove the iron balls.
But the young guard looked thoroughly displeased.
“It can’t be helped. Rules are rules.”
“Well, then I can’t help it either.”
Clank.
I deliberately raised my hands and feet one after another.
Shackles were fastened tightly around all four limbs, and unusually gleaming chains connected them to the iron balls.
“These can’t be removed without a key.”
“Who has the key?”
“Of course, the Ol—no, my Master has it.”
“Your Master would be...”
A year had passed since Jeok Cheongang had publicly declared me his Disciple.
Even a servant would know that much. There was no way a Peak master could be unaware of it.
No matter how vast the continent was, the Fire King Jeok Cheongang was one of only a handful of Supreme Peak masters under heaven, and his every move attracted attention.
“Hmm.”
The young guard furrowed his brow as he looked back and forth between me and the iron balls. Then he abruptly said, “We’ll have to cut them off.”
“What?”
No, what the hell had he just said?
Even when I gave him an incredulous look, the young guard remained perfectly confident.
“The Namgung Family has its own rules. Great Hero Jeok will understand.”
“...Uh, I don’t think he will.”
Something Jeok Cheongang had always said in Fire Gate Cavern suddenly came to mind.

“This old man entered the Fire Gate Clan at the age of nine. Say a hundred people began learning martial arts at that age... This old man is the only one who grew as strong as I am now. So how do you think I came this far?”
“How?”

“I shoved aside bastards from the unorthodox factions, sent dark-path figures packing, and killed every bastard who set fires like a Demonic Cultist. In that spirit, add a hundred geun to the iron balls.”
It was a history written in blood and violence.
Even the Roaring Fury Swordsman, the Senior Brother of the Zhongnan Sect’s Sect Leader, had been beaten black and blue. I could only imagine what would happen to this young guard.
I offered him my most sincere advice.
“Do that and you’ll die. Seriously, you’ll be in real trouble.”
“...What did you say?”
“I mean, you won’t die by my hand.”
“How dare you—!”
The young guard shouted angrily and placed his hand on his sword hilt.
That was when a deep, resonant voice infused with internal energy reached everyone’s ears.
“Enough. Let him in.”
It was Namgung Ryong, Family Head of the Namgung Family.

“Do that and you’ll die.
Seriously, you’ll be in real trouble.”
“...What did you say?”
“I mean, you won’t die by my hand.”
“How dare you—!”
The young guard shouted angrily and placed his hand on his sword hilt.
That was when a deep, resonant voice infused with internal energy reached everyone’s ears.
“Enough.
Let him in.”
It was Namgung Ryong, Family Head of the Namgung Family.

chapters.title: Chapter 239
paragraphs: Namgung Ryong was a sharp-featured middle-aged man.

As befitted the Family Head of the venerable martial household known as the Namgung Family, his dignified bearing radiated authority. His lips were pressed into a firm line, revealing something of his stern disposition.
In fact, despite traveling with him all the way from Mount Jiuhua to Hefei, I had heard him say fewer than ten words.
“Would you wait a moment? I have one important matter left to attend to.”
As the Family Head of the Namgung Family, he must have had a considerable workload.
I was used to that from watching Jin Wikyung, so I nodded without complaint.
“Ah, yes.”
Crunch!
Oh, right. I forgot about the iron balls.
The chair had shattered beneath me, unable to bear their weight. Still sitting amid the wreckage, I glanced at Namgung Ryong.
“Oops, what happened here? You should make your chairs a little sturdier...”
“It was made of ebony imported from Nanman. The wood is harder than steel.”
“Just stand.”
A short while later, Namgung Ryong set down the bamboo slips he had been carefully examining and spoke.
“I invited you here as a guest, yet I have treated you poorly. You have my apology.”
“No, it’s fine. You may have been busy.”
“I also owe you an apology for my son’s discourtesy.”
“What do you mean...?”
“I believe I heard some commotion.”
I suddenly remembered the young guard who had aggressively demanded that I disarm myself.
I wondered why the youngest one was acting so cocky...
“He’s your son?”
“He’s my only child, so I doted on him. Perhaps because of that, he still has many shortcomings.”
Yeah, he definitely has shortcomings.
Thinking of the bastard’s sour expression, I nodded.
“It’s all right. I’m sure he’ll improve with time.”
“Was there something else you wanted to say?”
“Ahem. No, nothing.”
Namgung Ryong cleared his throat and continued.
“People around him kept filling his head with talk of his talent for martial arts. You’ve heard the title Sword Dragon, haven’t you?”
“The Sword Dragon?”
“So you have heard of him. Well, it would be impossible not to...”
“I’ve never heard of him before.”
“Oh.”
“That’s a cool title, though.”
“Is it...?”
A dark shadow passed over Namgung Ryong’s face.
“He is well known throughout the martial world as one of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes.”
“Oh, so he’s one of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes. My second elder brother is one of them too.”
“I heard the two of them got into quite a fight as soon as they entered Heaven’s Gate Temple.”
“Good grief. They were young—very young. If they had just enrolled, they would’ve been twenty. That’s the age when people act like that.”
“It’s all right. People that age grow up by beating each other black and blue. But why did you call me here...?”
This man was definitely more of a doting fool than he looked.
Momentarily at a loss after my swift interruption, Namgung Ryong finally spoke.
“It concerns Great Hero Jeok.”
“That old—no, my Master?”
“That’s right.”
He nodded gravely before continuing.
“I’ll be direct. I want you to dissuade Great Hero Jeok.”
My relaxed posture stiffened on its own. I ran a hand over the beard that had grown thick over the past year and asked,
“Is this about his duel with the Azure Sky Sword King... Great Hero Namgung Cheon?”
“That’s right. Do you know what happened between Great Hero Jeok and my father more than twenty years ago?”
“I know roughly what happened. I also know that my Master won.”
“It was by the narrowest of margins. The battle was balanced on a knife’s edge. Either of them could have won.”
Namgung Ryong sighed.
“My father must have been deeply resentful of that defeat. For several years afterward, he devoted himself to secluded training, stewing over it.”
Defeat always cut deep.
And if the person in question was one of the greatest masters in the world—someone who loved martial arts enough to be called sword-crazed—the sense of loss would only be that much greater.
If his own son is talking about it like this, he must’ve been really pissed.
This would be a fight between Supreme Peak masters. Its intensity went without saying, and if things went too far, blood could easily be spilled.
If they had planned to calmly exchange a few moves, laugh good-naturedly, and withdraw, Namgung Ryong would have had no reason to bring this up.
The problem was...
“I’m not confident I can persuade my Master, either. No, I can’t persuade him.”
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, was not the sort of man who would back down merely because someone tried to stop him.
The year I had spent in Fire Gate Cavern had taught me many things. Not only about martial arts, but also about the man beside me.
Jeok Cheongang was not a difficult man to read.
“He’d rather die than back down.”
“You misunderstand me. I’m not saying you should do your best to stop them. I’m saying you must stop them.”
Namgung Ryong stared at me.
“Do you know what will happen if something happens to either of them during this duel?”
“I can make a rough guess.”
The Fire King and the Sword King. Both were giants who ruled over the martial world.
If the worst happened, the aftermath would be like a meteor crashing into the shore of a quiet lake.
“Then you shouldn’t have brought us to the Namgung Family.”
“That...”
“I know. You had no choice. But if even the Family Head can’t persuade his father, what could I possibly do?”
I shook my head. Whatever else I said here would be pointless.
“I’ll at least try talking to him.”
“I’ll do my best as well. I should go see my father immediately.”
“I’m not sure that’ll do you any good...”
“What do you mean?”
“Nothing. Then I’ll be going.”
I gave the puzzled Namgung Ryong a polite bow and turned away.
As soon as I left the pavilion, I found the young guard—or rather, the Lesser Family Head of the Namgung Family, Sword Dragon Namgung Ok—waiting for me with his eyes blazing.
“You bastard!”
“Oh, what now? We’ve never even met before, so why do you keep calling me a bastard?”
“I heard everything from outside. How dare you treat my father with such disrespect? Do you think the great Namgung Family is a joke?”
“What disrespect? I showed him the utmost courtesy, just as I do my Master.”
“What kind of bullshit are you spouting?”
“I’m serious. If you’re that curious, ask my Master. Anyway, I’m leaving.”
I was about to drag the iron balls past Namgung Ok when—
“How dare you!”
Shing! Click!
It happened in an instant.
The blade, radiating a chilling sharpness, had not even been drawn halfway before it disappeared back into its scabbard.
Namgung Ok stared at my hand pressing down on his sword hilt.
“H-how did you...?”
“That isn’t something you should draw and swing around so casually. Keep doing that and you’ll get yourself killed.”
“Act like a gentleman, young man.”
Pat, pat.
I patted the shoulder of the man who had gone rigid as a stone statue, then approached the wide-eyed maidservant.
“Excuse me.”
“Y-yes?”
“Is there a mountain nearby where not many people go?”
“Why would you want to...?”
“No particular reason.”
I glanced at the clear sky and continued.
“I thought I’d get some air.”
I shook off the maidservant, who insisted on accompanying me, and began climbing the mountain path.
It was the height of spring. The mountain was green, and the sky was blue.
I walked past drifting scraps of cloud and birds chattering from the branches. After some time, I entered a broad clearing and suddenly stopped.
“You can come out now.”
Nothing changed. Leaves rippled in the breeze, sparrows chirped as they ceaselessly turned their heads, and unknown wildflowers stood in full bloom.
Yet an incongruous presence towered amid the natural scenery.
Then a voice wormed its way into my ears.
“Not bad. Not bad at all.”
He was a remarkably tall old man. The fingers stroking the beard that reached his chest were knobby, and a fierce light shone from the eyes set deep in their sockets.
I clasped my hands before the old man, who looked remarkably similar to Namgung Ryong.
“It is an honor to meet the Azure Sky Sword King, Great Hero Namgung Cheon.”
The Azure Sky Sword King Namgung Cheon—the Grand Family Head of the Namgung Family and one of the Ten Kings—studied me before abruptly speaking.
“You must have had a reason for calling this old man all the way out here.”
“What do you mean...?”
“Great Hero Jeok took a sly little bastard as his Disciple in his later years. I know exactly what you’re scheming, so there’s no need to play dumb.”
“Ah, I’m sorry if I offended you.”
I scratched the back of my head and grinned. It was embarrassing to have him cut straight to the point, but it also made things easier.
“Did I make it a little... too obvious?”
I had first noticed his presence in the Family Head’s Hall.
Namgung Ryong had failed to sense him, but I had not. The Azure Sky Sword King was the reason I had come up the mountain under the pretense of getting some fresh air.
An unspoken invitation and acceptance had passed between us.
“Hah.”
A breathy sound escaped the Azure Sky Sword King’s lips. His expression seemed to ask what sort of brat he was dealing with.
“You’re an audacious one. Or perhaps you simply have no fear?”
“My Master says I’m just arrogant.”
“Yes, I believe that is the right word. Arrogant... It has been so long since anyone struck me that way that I had forgotten the feeling.”
“Of course. Who would dare act arrogantly toward the Azure Sky Sword King?”
“No one has for decades. Not until you appeared today.”
His fierce eyes fixed on me. That alone made my body hair stand on end and drew every sense taut.
“Speak. Why did you call this old man here?”
I took a deep breath. Then, without hesitation, I dropped to the ground and prostrated myself before the Azure Sky Sword King.
Clatter!
The chains collided, spewing a cacophonous rattle.
“What are you doing?”
“Please reconsider your duel with my Master.”
“Reconsider? Why should this old man do that?”
“I cannot tell you the reason.”
“...What?”
I had no idea what expression the Azure Sky Sword King was making.
But judging by the prickling at the back of my head, as if a blade were stabbing into it, he was clearly debating whether to kill me.
It does sound insane.
He had spent twenty years training for today’s duel.
And now some young brat who looked young enough to be his grandson had suddenly appeared and asked him to cancel it. On top of that, I was telling him I could not explain why.
But the die had already been cast. Pressing my face into the fresh earth, I spoke again.
“I’m sorry. But I cannot tell you the reason.”
“Tell me.”
“I cannot tell you.”
“You bastard!”
Whoooosh!
A tremendous wave of qi swept through the surroundings. Trees snapped, and flowers that had only just borne fruit were ripped out by the roots.
“This is the last time I’ll ask.”
My answer was already decided.
“I cannot tell you.”
As I repeated the same answer like a parrot, tangible killing intent pressed down on my entire body.
After a brief silence, the Azure Sky Sword King spoke.
“Get up.”
Crumble.
Clumps of dirt fell from me as I rose. The Azure Sky Sword King’s voice was as dry as desert sand.
“I waited twenty years.”
“Then please wait one more year.”
I continued calmly.
“I cannot tell you the exact reason, but my Master is not in good condition right now. You didn’t wait twenty years just to claim a victory like that, did you?”
“A victory like that...?”
The Azure Sky Sword King muttered the words under his breath and let out a hollow laugh.
“Great Hero Jeok trained his Disciple well.”
“He’ll be glad to hear that.”
“But you have the look of someone destined to die young. To survive in the martial world, one must possess at least a minimum of courtesy.”
“Are you saying...?”
“Three moves. If you can withstand three moves from this old man, I will grant your request.”
Ding.
System A Sudden Quest, Three-Move Kill, has been generated! - Would you like to accept the Quest?
I looked into his eyes, which boiled like lava.
These were three moves from none other than the Azure Sky Sword King. Three strikes capable of cleaving mountains and splitting rivers would rain down upon me.
I opened my parched lips.
“I’ll do it.”
Ding.
As the System notification announced that the Quest had been accepted, anger flared in the Azure Sky Sword King’s eyes.
“Your recklessness will be the death of you.”
“Maybe. Maybe not. But before that...”
I grinned and raised my arms.
Clank.
Dozens of iron balls swayed with the chains.
“May I take these off?”
“Go ahead. The outcome will not change.”
As the old man stared at me with cold, unyielding eyes, the majesty of an emperor who could force all under heaven to kneel surged from his entire body.
The blue sky overhead began to churn.
“Emperor’s Sword Form. Can you stop it?”
Craaack! Clang!
I tore apart the steel shackles that had bound my limbs for more than a year as easily as sheets of paper.
The instant the chains and iron balls fell to the ground—
Whoosh!
A flash of light burst from the Azure Sky Sword King’s waist.

chapters.title: Chapter 240
paragraphs: Smoke streamed from the old man’s seven orifices.
It was Scorching Yang Qi, so dense it was visible to the naked eye, endlessly coiling around his small frame as it circulated through him.
And then, soon after—
Sssssss.
Five rings rose one after another above the crown of the cross-legged old man.
Some were blue and red, others black and white.
When the final yellow ring took shape, the five vivid rings, one in each of the five directional colors, were complete.
Five Qi Returning to Origin.
Jeok Cheongang, the small-framed old man who had just displayed the dream realm sought by every martial artist in Murim, suddenly opened his eyes.
“Come in.”
The door opened the moment the words left his mouth.
A young man dressed in rags strode inside as though he owned the place and looked around.
“Weren’t you circulating your qi?”
“Some bastard kept pacing outside the door. How was this old man supposed to concentrate with him distracting me?”
“Fair point. Ah, I should’ve just come in and watched the Olympics.”
“It wasn’t the Olympics or whatever you called it. It was Five Qi Returning to Origin.”
“What does it matter? As long as you got the meaning across.”
Jeok Cheongang silently regarded the young man, Jin Taekyung.
“Where have you been?”
“You know where. I went to see Great Hero Namgung Ryong, the Family Head.”
“Family Head Namgung. Right. You did.”
After muttering under his breath, Jeok Cheongang asked, “What did he say?”
“Oh, that.”
Jin Taekyung stretched before continuing.
“The banquet’s been canceled.”
“The banquet was canceled? What does that mean?”
“Well, apparently the Azure Sky Sword King entered seclusion.”
“Seclusion?”
“They say he suddenly gained some minor insight or something. Anyway, that’s how it turned out.”
“Enlightenment...”
Jeok Cheongang gave a small nod.
“That’s quite a coincidence.”
Jin Taekyung stopped twisting his overgrown beard around one finger.
“What is?”
“The Azure Sky Sword King waited more than twenty years for today. Yet of all days, this happened today. How could it not be a coincidence?”
“...Maybe he got a little nervous when it was finally time to fight you?”
“Who knows?”
“Come on, it’s obvious. Don’t you think you’re overthinking it?”
“You think so?”
“Yes. Absolutely.”
Jeok Cheongang stared in silence as Jin Taekyung nodded vigorously.
“W-why?”
“Nothing.”
“There’s no such thing as ‘nothing’!”
“Do I need your permission just to look at your face?”
“Have you never heard of image rights?”
“No. Shut your mouth before I use Flying Over Grass to stomp on your head.”
“Yes, sir.”
But the silence did not last long. Jin Taekyung glanced at the old man, gauging his mood, then spoke again.
“Old Master.”
“What?”
“This whole thing worked out okay, right?”
“There is nothing to call ‘working out.’ The date has merely been postponed for a little while.”
“But we bought some time.”
“Did you think this old man would lose?”
Jin Taekyung hurriedly waved his hands.
“That’s not what I meant. Given the situation, even if you won, it wouldn’t really count as a victory.”
Even if I won, it wouldn’t really count as a victory...
Jeok Cheongang repeated the words silently.
They were true. Had the duel taken place, he would have paid a heavy price regardless of the outcome.
The Azure Sky Sword King was an opponent he would have to face with everything he had.
If Jeok Cheongang suffered an Internal Injury in a fierce duel against him, the essence, qi, and spirit he had barely managed to bring into balance would collapse.
“Old Master?”
Jeok Cheongang raised his head from his thoughts. Jin Taekyung was looking at him with concern.
“Why did you call me?”
“No reason. Do I need permission even to call you once?”
“What a tiresome brat.”
Normally, Jeok Cheongang would have rapped him on the head, but today, he decided to let it slide.
He let out a quiet chuckle and rose from his seat.
“Let’s go.”
“Where?”
“Henan.”
The Star-Array Grand Banquet.
Even now, the most renowned masters of Murim would be gathering in Henan one after another.
Having let all four seasons pass them by, the two of them had taken quite a detour.
“The Namgung Family has no reason to keep us here, and we have no reason to remain. Leaving is only natural.”
“Leaving sounds good, but can’t we soak in some hot water first? I’ve got so much dirt caked onto me that my body feels heavy.”

“You should have brought that up much earlier, you brat. Don’t start pretending to care about cleanliness now. Go get us some travel money. We may be uninvited guests, but they should at least give us that much.”
“Wow. Now you’re even telling me to shake people down.”
“Why, you—!”
“I’m going. I’m going.”
Jin Taekyung grumbled as he left the pavilion.
He did not know that Jeok Cheongang was silently watching him.
Watching the shackles that had been hastily forced shut by sheer strength.
Watching the cleanly severed ends of his sleeves.
The old man watched until the young man’s back had receded into the distance, then muttered,
“...That brat. Going and doing something I never told him to.”
His seasoned gray eyes swept toward a small mountain in the distance.
A faint cloud of dust was dispersing above the ridge covered in blue-green light.
The bright sun slipped behind the mountain, and darkness descended.
The Azure Sky Sword King, Namgung Cheon, stood motionless as the mountain wind whispered through the trees. Then he abruptly spoke.
“Who was that boy?”
Namgung Ryong, the Family Head of the Namgung Family, was standing quietly behind the Azure Sky Sword King. He answered,
“His name is Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan in Shanxi.”
“The Jin Family of Taiyuan?”
“Yes.”
“So a Hidden Dragon was crouching in the borderlands.”
“And the Fire King took that very Hidden Dragon under his wing.”
“You’re wrong.”
The Azure Sky Sword King shook his head.
“The Fire King is the dragon pearl. It wasn’t that he took the Hidden Dragon into his embrace. He became the dragon pearl himself.”
Namgung Ryong could not hide his astonishment. Though father and son had never been close, he knew what kind of man his father was.
One of the things he knew was that his father was a man of few words who was exceedingly stingy with his judgments of others.
Yet the words Hidden Dragon had come from his lips.
He had even said that the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, whose name shook all under heaven, had become the dragon pearl himself.
The man who never once praised even his own grandson...
A pang of hurt mingled with Namgung Ryong’s curiosity.
“Is he truly that extraordinary?”
The Azure Sky Sword King did not answer the cautious question. Instead, he abruptly asked one of his own.
“How far have you mastered the Emperor’s Sword Form?”
“...I have yet to break through the barrier of three-tenths mastery.”
“When I was your age, I had mastered seven-tenths of the Emperor’s Sword Form. I believe that was around the time the world began calling me the Sword King.”
“I apologize.”
Shame filled Namgung Ryong’s reply, but the Azure Sky Sword King paid it no mind.
He had not said it to rebuke his son, who was already sixty years old.
“More than twenty years ago, when my mastery of martial arts reached eight-tenths, a question suddenly occurred to me. I wanted to test my sword.”
Namgung Ryong silently lowered his head. He knew well what had happened afterward.
The clash between the Fire King and the Sword King.
The winner of that earth-shaking battle between two Supreme Peak masters had been the Fire King.
“During my secluded training, I faced countless towering walls. I struck and hammered at them without end, until at last, one of those walls collapsed.”
“Then...!”
“I have only just broken through a single wall. I have not yet achieved Great Completion.”
“Congratulations!”
Namgung Ryong performed a full bow before his father, trembling with excitement.
The Emperor’s Sword Form was the beginning and end of the dozens of secret arts possessed by the Namgung Family.
In the family’s entire history, only the founding Family Head had ever achieved Great Completion of the Emperor’s Sword Form.
True to his greatness as a martial artist, the Azure Sky Sword King had become the first in roughly a century to reach nine-tenths mastery of the Emperor’s Sword Form.
“Congratulations, is it?”
But the Azure Sky Sword King’s expression remained calm. No—he even looked hollow.
“Then let me ask you one thing. Can you withstand three moves of the Emperor’s Sword Form this old man unleashes?”
“How could I possibly dare... Surely?”
The Azure Sky Sword King quietly nodded.
Namgung Ryong’s eyes widened like lanterns.
It was unthinkable—something that neither should nor could have happened.
Yet his father had confirmed it.
That young man had withstood the Emperor’s Sword Form wielded by none other than the Azure Sky Sword King himself.
Even Namgung Ryong, who rarely lost his composure, spoke with a trembling voice.
“B-but he is only twenty-two.”
“Yes, twenty-two. He possesses the Heavenly Martial Physique and has the Fire King Jeok Cheongang as his Master.”
The Azure Sky Sword King raised his head and stared into the dark night sky.

For many long years, from the moment he first entered the world, he had lived under the name Namgung. He had carried the two characters Azure Sky in his heart and learned a sword that resembled the azure heavens.
But today, he had met a dragon soaring into the sky.
I thought one move would be enough.
He had put two-tenths of his power behind his sword, intending to teach the young man some manners.
Then three-tenths.
Then six-tenths.
And yet...
“Three moves. That’s it, right? Thanks for going easy on me.”
The young man had slung the iron balls over his shoulder and left.
All that remained in his wake were hundreds of trees and boulders carved apart by stroke after stroke, along with the mournful cries of birds that had suddenly lost their homes.
A Hidden Dragon. A Hidden Dragon.
The Azure Sky Sword King repeated those words in his mind, then spoke.
“Have they left?”
Namgung Ryong, who had only just gathered his wits, answered, “Yes. They left five shichen ago.”
“Where did they say they were going?”
“Henan. They said they would attend the Star-Array Grand Banquet being held there in one month.”
“The Star-Array Grand Banquet?”
The Azure Sky Sword King let out a hollow laugh.
“Make it clear to your son that he is not to show his face at this Star-Array Grand Banquet.”
Black Mountain Stronghold was a bandit organization based along one of the major routes connecting Henan and Anhui.
Its leader, Heuk Jongpil, was an illiterate former butcher, but he was also a natural-born plunderer and a master who had honed his axe techniques to the Peak realm.
Thanks to that, he commanded more than three hundred underlings and lorded over them like a king.
Not that the Green Forest Alliance didn’t bleed me dry.
No matter how capable Heuk Jongpil was, he was no match for the Green Forest Alliance.

The only reason he had managed to build Black Mountain Stronghold into what it was today was that he paid four-tenths of his monthly profits to the Green Forest Alliance in exchange for various forms of assistance.
For instance, the valuable intelligence delivered by the subordinate who had just entered.
“Boss, a letter arrived from the Green Forest Alliance headquarters! Here—”
Whack!
“You bastard! Don’t you know we’re all illiterate? Read it aloud!”
“It has information about the goods the Geumwa Merchant Group is transporting and the route they’re taking. They say it should arrive within two days.”
“What are you waiting for?”
“Yes?”
“Call everyone!”
The Star-Array Grand Banquet was an important event for martial artists and bandits alike.
Heuk Jongpil gathered all three hundred of his underlings and set up an ambush along the route the Geumwa Merchant Group would take.
Just one big haul. Let us land one.
If they managed to get their hands on even a single top-grade cat’s-eye stone, they would still have a fortune left over after paying tribute to the Green Forest Alliance.
Feeding and arming more than three hundred able-bodied men was no small task.
“They should be here by now... Why haven’t the scouts come back?”
“Who knows? We sent them out a shichen ago, but there hasn’t been any word.”
“Ugh. Trying to run a bandit operation with idiots like these is hard on the body. Hard on the body.”
The next instant, Heuk Jongpil froze mid-grumble.
With a trembling hand, he pointed toward something approaching through the darkness at incredible speed.
“...Hey. What is that?”
“I-I’m not sure either.”
Whoooosh!
Two silhouettes—one large and one small.
A long trail of red qi lingered behind them like the tail of a meteor shower.
Are they ghosts?
Heuk Jongpil was crouching in the grass, watching the sight, when it happened.
The two silhouettes racing along the mountain road at an unbelievable speed abruptly stopped.
A moment later, low voices drifted over.
“Why stick your nose into this?”
“It bugs me. They seem to be with those two who were skulking around earlier.”
“We’re going to be late at this rate, you brat.”
“No matter how late we are, whoever sees the trash first should clean it up.”
“Where did you learn to talk back every single time this old man says something?”
“Bastards like that always set fire to mountains.”
“You little shit! Go break all four of their limbs.”
“Yes, sir.”
Heuk Jongpil had been listening intently to their conversation.
His eyes flew wide.
“W-we’re fucking screwed! Everybody—!”
But his cry went no further.
Whoosh!
A brief rush of wind.
Then someone’s enormous hand settled companionably around his shoulder.
“Everybody, what?”

Five rings rose one after another above the crown of the cross-legged old man.

Five Qi Returning to Origin.

paragraphs: The Star-Array Grand Banquet.
With the most renowned masters in the world gathering in one place to pit their martial arts against one another, the name could not have been more fitting: a banquet of stars.
An old man with deep wrinkles around his eyes packed tobacco into a long-stemmed tobacco pipe as he spoke.
“It could also be called a festival of victory.”
They were in a large inn in southern Henan Province.
From among the people crowding around the old man, someone asked, “Why is that?”

“Why else? If the Central Plains Murim had lost, would there have been a Star-Array Grand Banquet? The Demonic Cult would have ruled the world by now, and they would be holding the Demonic Grand Banquet instead.”
“Ah, that is true.”
“But because we won, the Star-Array Grand Banquet can be held, and the great sects from across the world can gather in one place to renew their shared resolve. Speaking of which...”
The old man fumbled inside his robes, then waved his pipe.
“Does anyone have a light?”
The middle-aged man beside him quickly pulled out a flint and lit it for him.
Crack, crackle! Ssssss.
As the dry tobacco burned, the old man puffed on the stem. After blowing out several streams of smoke, he leaned back leisurely in his chair.
“If there is anything you’re curious about, ask away. This old man will tell you everything he knows.”
The people watching him with shining eyes began raising their hands all at once.
“Me! May I ask first?”
“Great Hero Song, then perhaps...”
“Hey, didn’t you hear me say I was going first?”
“I didn’t hear shit, you unorthodox-faction bastard!”
Wham! Crash!
Fists flew in an instant, and a table broke apart. The onlookers cheered at the sudden fight.
The guests who had kept their distance from the start shook their heads.
“Tsk, tsk. Martial artists.”
“Just let them be. It’s not as if this is the first time we’ve seen it.”
“That’s the problem. There’s never a quiet moment. With the Star-Array Grand Banquet right around the corner, every kind of bastard is flocking to Henan.”
“Our trading run is over anyway. We might as well watch the show and enjoy the benefits.”
The two merchants continued chatting quietly.
Dressed in fine blue silk robes, they were passing cups of liquor between them when a voice suddenly cut in.
“Is that Yeoahong?”
“Hm?”
The merchants stared at the owner of the voice in bewilderment.
A young man had somehow approached their table without either of them noticing. His nostrils flared as he stared intently at the cups in their hands.
“Isn’t that Yeoahong? It looks like it...”
“It—it is. Yeoahong.”
“I knew it.”
As though he had achieved some great enlightenment, the young man slapped his knee and dragged over an empty chair.
“But the color looks a little weak. How much did you pay for this bottle?”
His movements were so smooth and natural that the merchants could only stare blankly at each other.
“H-how much was it?”
“T-two silver nyang.”
The young man sighed.
“What a shame.”
“What do you mean, a shame?”
“This has been mixed with water. Can’t you tell at a glance? Looks like the owner played a little trick on you.”
What?
The merchants’ eyes flashed.
Was Yeoahong normally that expensive?
Two silver nyang was enough to buy two seom of rice and drink strong liquor like water for several months. Mixing water into it was nothing short of outrageous.
“I’m going to—”
One of the merchants was about to spring to his feet, but his companion stopped him.
“Forget it. Nothing good will come from making a fuss. Besides, aren’t we doing the same thing—making a little extra while we can?”
“Ugh.”
The merchant groaned and sat back down.
Meanwhile, the young man was filling his cup to the brim with Yeoahong and gulping it down.
Gulp, gulp, clack!
“Ahh. That’s good.”
The merchants stared at him dumbfounded. Only after a moment did they finally come to their senses.
“What do you think you’re doing?”
“That’s our liquor...”
“My throat was a little dry, so I tried a cup. Is there a problem?”
His answer was so shameless that the two men were left speechless. They only managed to speak after the young man had emptied his third cup.
“Have we met before?”
“Of course.”
“When? Where?”
“Today, here.”
“They say even brushing sleeves with someone creates a connection. Starting today, let’s be friends.”
“Friends?”
The merchants glared at the young man in disbelief.
He was slender and had an approachable expression. He looked no older than his mid-twenties—just a ridiculously young brat.
What the hell does he mean, friends?
They were about to give him a proper tongue-lashing when they noticed the iron sword tucked into his waistband.
A martial artist!
People had always said there was only a fine line between a rogue and a martial artist.
With their merchant guards nowhere nearby, they would unquestionably be the ones to suffer if a dispute broke out.
The merchants swallowed the reprimand that had been about to leave their mouths.
“Listen, Young Brother.”
“Young Brother? I like that form of address.”
“R-really? That’s good, then.”
There was something strangely relaxed about the young man’s grin. Forced smiles appeared on the merchants’ faces.
“Are you a martial artist too, Young Brother?”
“Hmm. I have learned some trifling tricks people call martial arts.”
What? He learned ‘trifling tricks’ called martial arts?
The brat’s already drunk on his own swagger.
The merchants cursed him inwardly before speaking.
“You must be a future pillar of the martial world. If you don’t mind, may I ask which sect you are a Disciple of?”
“Does that matter between friends?”
The young man deftly dodged the question, so one of the merchants revealed their own identity.
“We are merchants belonging to the Geumwa Merchant Group.”
“The Geumwa Merchant Group?”

“It is nothing to boast about, but we are one of the top three merchant groups in Zhejiang Province. We came a long way to deliver supplies for the Star-Array Grand Banquet being held three days from now.”
The other merchant, who had been nodding beside him, eagerly chimed in.
“We even brought a hundred merchant-group guards.”
“Warriors as brave as tigers.”

“The Geumwa Merchant Group... I definitely heard that name this morning.”
The young man thought for a moment, then exclaimed, “Ah!”
“Isn’t that the group that captured hundreds of bandits?”
“That’s right.”
The merchant had answered with his chest puffed out, but he added in a mumble, “To be precise, we didn’t capture them. We picked them up.”
“Picked them up? What does that mean?”
When the young man showed interest, the merchants lowered their voices as much as possible.
What they had encountered before meeting this young brat was far more troubling.

“Well, there were a bunch of bandits lying in the alley the merchant group was passing through, all with broken legs and groaning. As it turned out, they were from Black Mountain Stronghold, which is notorious in the area.”
“Their leader, the Red-Killing Axe Heuk Jongpil, had been turned into a headless corpse.”
“Oh?”
The young man rubbed his smooth, hairless chin.
“So what did you do?”
“What else could we do? We couldn’t exactly kill them all, but leaving them there would have been like throwing silver nyang onto the road. So we tied them all together in a line.”
In the end, the Geumwa Merchant Group handed the remnants of Black Mountain Stronghold over to the authorities and collected an enormous bounty. The rumor spread quickly.
“People have been saying all kinds of things. That they angered a hidden master, that a war broke out between bandit strongholds...”
“It probably was a hidden master. How many people can kill a Peak master like the Red-Killing Axe in One Strike?”
The young man listened quietly, then asked with keen interest, “A Peak master, killed in One Strike?”
The two merchants nodded together.
“That’s right. You’re a martial artist too, so you must know how remarkable that is.”

“What was it again? The underlings said whoever it was had chunks of iron dangling all over them. It was so late at night that they couldn’t make out the person’s face. They just saw a flash, and then the Red-Killing Axe fell.”
“Hmm.”
The young man fell silent for a moment, as though considering something. Then he suddenly spoke.
“That hidden master must be much younger than you think.”
“Good heavens. Do you have some idea who he might be?”
“More or less. Probably dressed in rags, with hair all over the place.”
“Oh! Who is it? Who is that master?”
“But I don’t know the name.”
“Well, I suppose I can get to know him little by little from now on. Thanks for the drink.”
It happened in an instant.

A moment later, the inn’s door closed with a tinkling bell.
“What was that?”

“He called us friends. Damn it.”
The two merchants were staring blankly at each other when someone spoke to them.
“Excuse me, gentlemen.”

No, with a face like that, it was practically certain.

“Huh?”

He drank five bottles of Yeoahong?

The merchants were rummaging through their coin purses with miserable expressions when—
“I’ll pay.”
Clink.
A silk pouch flew from somewhere and landed on the table.
The people inside the inn had fallen silent. Through the crowd, which had split cleanly down the middle, an old man came limping forward.
Tap, tap.
The sound of his wooden prosthetic leg striking the floor pierced everyone’s ears.
“Twenty silver nyang. Use it to pay the bill and get me a quiet room.”
The waiter looked back and forth between the silk pouch and the old man, then bowed politely. He already knew who the man was.
“Yes, Great Hero Song.”
“Well, that settles one matter.”

“We have absolutely nothing to do with him!”

“Heh heh. Isn’t that something for this old man to decide?”

As if to announce that the Star-Array Grand Banquet was only three days away, the streets and inns throughout Henan Province were packed with people.
The problem was that, thanks to that, there was not a single room left for me.
“We have no rooms.”
I had already been turned away from more than twenty inns.

“I told you, there isn’t.”
“I have money.”
I pulled out a grimy silver nyang and held it up. It was my entire fortune and my last hope.
If I hadn’t secretly hidden it away in advance, I wouldn’t even have this.
Jeok Cheongang had run off with my entire coin purse.
Damn old man.

At the very first inn we entered, Jeok Cheongang had been showered with salt by the waiter. After agonizing over whether to set the waiter or the inn on fire, he had come up with a peaceful and spectacular solution.
The Abbot of Shaolin card.
I’m going to Shaolin.
Wow. That option was available? Was dementia the driving force that turned you into a genius?
Shall I use that driving force to snap your neck?
I shouldn’t have run my mouth. Anyway, that’s great. Let’s hurry there, scrub the dirt off with hot water, and eat some Shaolin wild-greens bibimbap.
I’m going alone.
What?

A year ago, you ran your mouth about going to the Star-Array Grand Banquet, and this old man suffered for it despite having no reason to. The preliminary competition will be held in Kaifeng anyway, so don’t let me see your face until then.
No way! How is that fair?
Oh, and hand over your coin purse.
Why do you need my coin purse?
The Fire King has his dignity to consider. Do you expect me to arrive looking like a beggar and eat and bathe for free? I should at least make a small donation.
Oh, and if you come looking for Shaolin, I’ll kill you. Understood?
He wasn’t the Fire King. He was a highway robber. A highway robber.

And this was the last inn anywhere nearby.
