The heavily built waiter scowled.
“...Didn’t you just pull that out of your underwear?”
“I was hiding it.”
I quickly rubbed the silver nyang with my sleeve before holding it out again.
“Want to bite it?”
“Get the hell out of here, you beggar bastard!”
Fucking bastard...
I considered punching him in the face, but turned away weakly.
Nearby, several children were huddled together playing jacks with small stones.
“Kids, do any of your families rent out rooms?”
The chubby-cheeked children shook their heads.
“N-no.”
“My family does, but it’s already full.”
“Oh, I see. All right.”
“And my mom said not to bring in beggar bastards like youuu.”
Listen to the way that little brat talks.
I wanted to storm into his house and yell at his parents to teach him some proper manners, but I held myself back.
Where do I go now?
I was slowly wandering the streets, wondering whether I should go wash myself in a nearby stream, when someone called out.
“Young Hero!”
At first, I didn’t realize they were calling me. Given my current appearance, it was far too absurd to think that someone would address me as a Young Hero.
My clothes were no better than rags, and my hair was a tangled mess. At that moment, I was a perfect specimen of a beggar.
At least I had avoided looking like a prisoner by winding the chains around my body and covering the iron balls with cloth.
But who would call someone like me a Young Hero?
“Me?”
When I turned around, I saw a young man with an approachable expression smiling brightly.
“That’s right. You.”

Crack, crackle!

chapters.title: Chapter 242
paragraphs: He was a young man with an approachable expression.
He looked to be in his mid-to-late twenties at most, with a strangely friendly smile playing on his lips.
“Whew. Why are you walking so fast?”
“Do I know you?”
“No.”
“Then why?”
“They say even brushing sleeves with someone creates a connection, don’t they?”
“We haven’t even brushed sleeves.”
“But we’ve exchanged words, so that counts. Let’s be friends.”
It was one of two things. He was either crazy or a crazy social butterfly.
I took my time looking him over. Beneath his loose robe, I spotted well-developed muscles and the hilt of a sword jutting from his waist.
At the same time, I sensed the qi lying dormant within him.
A Peak master?
I had no idea how old he actually was, but his attainment was fairly impressive.
No, at this level, it could even be called remarkable. Reaching the Peak realm in your twenties was no easy feat.
But how should I put it? The qi I sensed from the young man seemed to amount to exactly that and nothing more.
If I had to put it into words...
An ordinary Peak master?
The Peak realm was already an incredible level, so why did he feel ordinary? Because I was surrounded by too many monsters.
Getting hit with the insane three-hit combo of Jin Mukyung, Cheongpung, and the Fire King was bound to leave side effects like this.
In any case, I had more or less figured him out. I spoke politely to the young man.
“Don’t mind me. Go on your way.”
“Good heavens, isn’t that awfully cold between friends?”
“If we’re friends, can I drop the formal speech?”
“Haha. Of course!”
“Then fuck off, asshole.”
I left him behind and started walking. After standing frozen for a moment, he hurried after me in quick little steps.
“That was the first time anyone has ever insulted me. I was stunned for a moment. Yes, this is what true friendship is!”
“Just go while I’m still asking nicely.”
“What’s your name?”
“Michael Johnson.”
“That’s an unusual name.”
“...You believe that?”
“Jang Sam? Or Yu Pil? Are you perhaps a Disciple of one of the Nine Sects and One Gang or the Five Great Families?”
“Why do you care?”
“Because I’m interested, of course. I heard you killed the Red-Killing Axe with One Strike.”
I stopped dead at the unfamiliar epithet.
“Who?”
“The Stronghold Lord of Black Mountain Stronghold. Was that your doing?”
I recalled the hairy bandit chief I had dealt with on the way here. There had been so many bandits that I had taken him out first to intimidate the rest.
I had thought he was unusually strong for a bandit. Apparently, he had been somewhat famous.
“But how did you find out?”
“I heard it from the Geumwa Merchant Group’s merchants at the inn earlier. They said the surviving bandits claimed it was the work of a strange man carrying iron balls and chains.”
The young man beamed as he pointed to the iron balls strapped to my back.
I had covered them with cloth to disguise them as luggage, since I did not want to invite any strange misunderstandings. But apparently, I could not fool the eyes of a Peak master.
“And then you happened to walk by. My curiosity got the better of me, so I came straight after you.”
“Hmm.”
“So, what’s your name?”
Should I tell him or not?
After a moment’s thought, I opened my mouth. I was beginning to grow curious about which sect this eccentric young man belonged to as well.
“Jin Taekyung. That’s my name.”
“Are you the Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan in Shanxi Province?”
“You know me?”
“Of course I do. I’ve heard so much about the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi becoming the Fire King’s Disciple that my ears are ringing.”
A year could be short or long, depending on how you looked at it.
But it was more than enough time for rumors about me and the Fire King to spread throughout the continent.
“What about you?”
“Ah, as for me...”
The young man grinned and continued.
“Jongni Chu. I’m Jongni Chu from Yunnan. I have my reasons for not revealing my sect, so I hope you’ll understand.”
“Jongni Chu from Yunnan?”
“My epithet is the Always-Victorious Sword. Have you ever heard of me?”
I knew Yunnan, but this was my first time hearing his name or epithet.
Considering I had spent the past year holed up in Fire Gate Cavern, that was only natural.
“Sorry, but I haven’t.”
“Is that so? Well, it’s understandable that you wouldn’t know.”
Would you look at that positivity? Most martial artists his age would have been disappointed, but he showed no sign of it.
The freakishly positive guy continued with a serious expression.
“That’s because I just came up with the epithet. A swordsman who always wins. Isn’t it cool?”
Is he crazy?
As I stood there speechless, Jongni Chu made a motion of twisting his wrist.
“How about it? Shall we have a drink to celebrate becoming friends?”
“Not interested. Besides, there aren’t any seats at the nearby inns.”
“What are you talking about? I’ve been following you this whole time, and every inn had at least one or two seats open.”
“...The waiters said there weren’t any.”
“Hm? Then why did they tell me there were empty seats and invite me inside?”
Damn it. Of course.
Even with the Star-Array Grand Banquet right around the corner, how could every last seat in dozens of inns possibly be taken?
I’m washing because I’m filthy. Because I’m filthy.
I would have to draw water from a stream and wash myself. At this rate, I would end up sleeping on the street despite leaving perfectly good inns unused.
“I know a decent inn, so come with me. I’ll pay for the drinks to celebrate our new friendship.”
“What friendship? You said your name was Jongni Chu, right? You should go on your way too.”
It was not as though I was completely penniless. I had no intention of getting tangled up with some weirdo and wasting time chatting.
Hadn’t someone said there was a stream if I kept following this road?
As I searched my memory and walked on, Jongni Chu called after me.
“Hey, where are you going?”
“None of your business. Don’t follow me.”
“Then answer just one last question! Where can I see you again?”
“The Star-Array Grand Banquet.”
That was my final answer. I used qinggong and quickly left the area. After covering more than a hundred zhang in an instant, I heard Jongni Chu shouting behind me.
“See you next time!”
Not a chance, punk.
One man left, and one remained.
Jongni Chu stared in the direction Jin Taekyung had disappeared and murmured,
“The Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, Jin Taekyung...”

After standing there alone and chuckling to himself for a while, he turned toward an inn not far away.

“Welcome!”
“Do you have any seats left?”
“Of course, sir!”
Jongni Chu’s smile deepened.

When I sat up, the hot water filling the wooden tub sloshed around me.
I had found the battered old tub lying in the grass, filled it with cold stream water, and heated it with Scorching Yang Qi.

“I feel like I’ve undergone Bone Transformation.”
I finally felt alive again.
It would have been nice to have shampoo or body wash, but this was more than enough to satisfy me.
The inventories for Murim and the modern world were separate, so bringing any over had been impossible from the start.
But these clothes are a problem.
I frowned as I put the rags back on. It was hard to tell whether they were clothes or garbage.
The discomfort was one thing, but putting these back on made the bath feel completely pointless.
I wandered through the streets, intending to buy at least one cheap set of clothes.
The streets of Henan had been crowded with people from every class and profession even a year ago, but given the timing, martial artists were especially conspicuous now.
Naturally, snippets of their conversations reached my ears.
“Have you heard? The Sword Dragon of the Namgung Family won’t be participating in this year’s Star-Array Grand Banquet.”
“Good heavens. Why would the Sword Dragon suddenly drop out? Is there some sort of problem?”
“Who knows? It’s a shame. He was one of the favorites to win. The outcome is getting harder and harder to predict.”
“Among the young prodigies, the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes probably have the best chance, but...the age limit is thirty-five. There’s no telling what will happen.”
“That’s a fair point. The world is vast, and there are many masters. A powerful newcomer from outside the Nine Sects and One Gang or the Five Great Families could easily appear.”
“You mean someone like the Heaven Shaking Sword of the Jin Family of Taiyuan and the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi?”
“Exactly. Though I don’t know whether either of them will attend this year’s Star-Array Grand Banquet.”
Hearing them talk about me made my face burn.
I quickened my pace and left the road behind.
As soon as I reached a main street lined with large buildings, a cloth shop displaying silk and dozens of different outfits caught my eye.
“Excuse me.”
“Why, they say clothes make the woman, but those suit you wonderfully. Are you perhaps a fairy? A fairy... What do you want?”
The cloth-shop employee had been enthusiastically showering a group of pretty female customers with flattery, but he frowned the moment I called out to him.
The change in his expression was so extreme that I barely resisted punching him in the face.
“Why do you think I came to a cloth shop?”
“To beg, obviously.”
No matter how ragged my clothes were, there was no hiding my massive frame.
If anything, the rags left so much skin exposed that my muscles stood out even more.
When I stared at him while subtly tensing my body, the employee flinched.
“W-why are you looking at me like that? Was I wrong?”
“That’s enough of the kind of remark you’ll regret. Let me see some clothes.”
“C-clothes?”
“Here. I have money, so don’t treat me like a beggar.”
The employee’s expression changed when I pulled out a silver nyang and waved it around.
Contrary to my expectations, it changed for the worse.
“That’s all?”
“It is. Is there a problem?”
“Good grief. What kind of clothes do you think you can buy with one lousy silver nyang?”
“...One lousy silver nyang?”
Had there been some major currency reform in the past year that caused the value of silver to collapse?
As I stood there in confusion, the employee snorted.
“Did you even read the price list before coming in?”
I reflexively turned and checked the sign.
A wooden board at the front of the shop had these words written across it in enormous letters:
The owner has gone mad! Star-Array Grand Banquet special discount! Martial-artist’s outfit—two silver nyang!
“...Two silver nyang? For a martial-artist’s outfit?”
“With that, you could buy underwear at best. Our cloth shop handles only the finest silk. Even our martial-artist’s outfits are made from Shu brocade.”
So this was a department-store brand.
Of all the places I could have walked into, I had chosen this one. What an embarrassment.
The other employees and customers inside the shop began whispering as they watched me.
“Oh my, he must be a beggar. How pitiful. Don’t you agree, dear?”
“He certainly looks like one. He seems strong enough to put those muscles to use, though. Should we take him in as a servant?”
“You’re so merciful, dear. I’m sure that beggar would be delighted.”
Being called a beggar was irritating enough, but hearing it from a couple made me twice as angry.
I shouted with all the anger I could muster.
“Who are you calling a beggar?”
“Gasp!”
“Eek!”
“H-how dare you!”
People recoiled in fright at my booming shout.
At the same time, several burly employees came rushing over and surrounded me, brandishing clubs threateningly.
“You bastard! How dare you make a scene here!”
“Do you even know where you are, you filthy beggar?”
“What? A beggar? Oh, you sons of bitches...”
Fine. You said it.
I rolled up the sleeve that was already half torn off.
“All right, let’s be a real pain in the ass today. Who owns this place?”
That was when it happened.
“You’re the kind of bastard who won’t come to his senses until he sees a coffin. How dare you make a scene here?”
A grave voice rang in my ears.
I slowly turned around and saw a man.
He wore a bamboo hat pulled low over his face and black silk clothes embroidered with dragons. One hand rested on the hilt of his sword as though he might draw at any moment.
The lips visible beneath the bamboo hat curled as he let out a quiet laugh.
“You seem to have learned a move or two somewhere, but if you don’t want to see blood, step aside.”
I cocked my head.
“And if I don’t?”
“Nameless martial artist, the price of reckless bravado is death.”
The people nearby erupted in cheers at the line straight out of a martial-arts movie.
Once the cheering died down, I spoke.
“Hey, can I ask you one thing?”
The martial artist answered casually,
“Speak. They will be your last words.”
I stared into the shadow beneath the martial artist’s bamboo hat and continued.
“You’re Hyuk Mujin, right?”
I let out a deep sigh and looked up at the sky. A signboard written in vigorous, soaring calligraphy caught my eye.
Hyuk Family Cloth Shop
“You have three seconds. Put your head on the floor.”

chapters.title: Chapter 243
paragraphs: Hyuk Mujin had been living a dream day after day. Every now and then, he even pinched his own cheek.
Mujin, are you really allowed to be this happy? This isn’t a dream, is it?
He had every reason to feel that way.
Just over ten years ago, he had been nothing more than a boy who admired martial artists.
No, I don’t need to go back that far.
Even two years ago, he had thought his life was a cesspool.
His working hours were long and tedious, and his martial arts had stagnated.
And when the person he saw most often was the drunken, good-for-nothing Third Young Master, anyone short of the Buddha himself was bound to take a bleak view of the world.
I held it in and held it in, then finally threw one punch.
The day he drove his fist into the Third Young Master’s jaw, Hyuk Mujin’s life changed.
Countless battles. One brush with death after another...
The Third Young Master—or rather, his Captain—was like a magnet that drew every danger in the world toward him.
Hyuk Mujin fought through the threats flying at them from every direction, and by the time he came to his senses, he had grown by leaps and bounds.
Ohhh, power! Power is surging through me!
...Patient, come over here. Your crazy spell is acting up again, so it’s time for your beating.
Bam! Ba-ba-bam!
He had taken an awful lot of beatings, too. There had even been times when he secretly set out a bowl of pure water and prayed behind Jin Taekyung’s back.
Please, please don’t let the Captain hit me anymore. Just take him somewhere far away.
Had his prayer been answered?
One day, Jin Taekyung left without warning.
As Hyuk Mujin watched him depart with the Fire King, he felt both sad and liberated.
And at last, the prime of his life began.
You’re Hyuk Mujin?
Gasp! Great Hero Wipeng, how do you know me...
Draw your sword. Let’s see what you can do.
He began receiving instruction from Wipeng, the Peak master known as the Ghost Sword.
Did you say the Jin Dragon Squad?
That’s right. It’s made up of the family’s finest. I’ve been appointed its Squad Leader.
Wow! The Jin Dragon Squad! Congratulations!
Pack your things.
Pardon?
You’re the Vice Squad Leader. This is our lord’s command, so you cannot afford a single mistake.
Gasp. I pledge my eternal loyalty to the Jin Family of Taiyuan. At your command! At your command!
He had become Vice Squad Leader of the Jin Dragon Squad, the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s most elite unit.

A young man who had once dreamed of becoming the Master of the Gatekeeper Pavilion had, in just a year or two, grown into a martial artist capable of standing shoulder to shoulder with the family’s leading figures.
They truly had been dreamlike days.
...At least until a moment ago.
“You’re Hyuk Mujin, right?”
Wild hair. A thick, unkempt beard. A muscular beggar dressed in rags.
At the words that came from his mouth, Hyuk Mujin’s hands and feet went numb.
That voice was unmistakably familiar. How had he failed to recognize it at once?
No wonder the back of his head had been itching strangely...
Where did it all go wrong?
Was it when he came to Henan as Jin Wikyung’s escort?
Or when he accepted his father’s request to inspect the Henan branch of the Hyuk Family Cloth Shop?
He didn’t know. There was only one thing he could be certain of.
I’m fucked.
Cold sweat slid down his back as he heard the words that turned his journey to Henan into a journey to hell.
“I’ll give you three seconds. Put your head on the ground.”
His mind screamed no, but his body knew better.
Hyuk Mujin, a rising talent of the Jin Family of Taiyuan and Vice Squad Leader of its most elite unit, slammed his head into the ground with a thunderous cry.
“Yessssss, sir!”
Thud!
A white stone wall, with five or six rooftops visible beyond it.
The large estate where the Jin Family of Taiyuan was staying drew steadily closer.
“This the place?”
Hyuk Mujin answered in a half-dead voice. His once-impressive martial uniform hung in tatters, and one eye was swollen and bruised dark blue.
To borrow his own words from half an hour ago, this was the price of reckless bravado.
“Oh. You found a nice place to stay. The family must be doing pretty well these days.”
I wasn’t the only one who had changed over the past year. Hyuk Mujin had changed, and so had the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s standing.
The fact that they had rented an entire estate this large with the Star-Array Grand Banquet right around the corner told me all I needed to know.
“Lead the way, punk.”
“Urgh! That hurts! It hurts!”
“I’m kicking you because it’s supposed to hurt, punk.”
I walked along, booting him in the rear.
Two Jin Family martial artists standing rigidly on guard before the estate spotted their superior and gaped.
“Gasp!”
“Vice Squad Leader!”
Hyuk Mujin subtly averted his gaze and cleared his throat.
“Ahem. Have you been keeping proper watch? This gentleman is...”
Shing! Shing-shing!
“You bastard!”
“How dare you do this to our Vice Squad Leader!”
He was the Vice Squad Leader of some newly formed unit called the Jin Dragon Squad, and apparently his subordinates thought quite highly of him.
I gave the Jin Dragon Squad members pointing their swords at me an amiable smile.
“Put those away. I’m with the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
“Vice Squad Leader, are you all right?”
“Where did this beggar bastard come from, spouting nonsense?”
At his subordinates’ response, Hyuk Mujin nodded with a stricken expression.
“Not a beggar bastard. He’s the Third Young Master.”
Pardon?
“But no matter how you look at him, he’s a beggar...”
I could let it go once, but not twice.
Hyuk Mujin noticed my expression change and spoke gloomily.
“Hocheol.”
The martial artist named Hocheol promptly answered.
“Yes, Vice Squad Leader.”
“Put your head on the ground.”
Right. That was the least I could expect from my right-hand man.
Leaving Hocheol behind to commune with the earth, I stepped onto the estate grounds. Almost immediately, I came face-to-face with someone strolling through the courtyard.
His eyes trembled with emotion.
Even if ten years had passed instead of one, he would have recognized me. It wouldn’t have mattered how disheveled I looked.
That was what blood ties meant. That was what it meant to be brothers.
“Well, look who it is.”
The massive man staring at me, frozen like a statue, was Jin Wikyung. A radiant smile spread across his face.
He strode toward me and spoke.
“Are you from the Beggars’ Sect?”
Brothers, my ass.
“I recognized you at a glance, actually.”
“Are you kidding me?”
“I’m serious. Did you really think I wouldn’t recognize you, my youngest?”
“Do I look like a complete idiot?”
Don’t try to pull that on me. He had even asked what position I held in the Beggars’ Sect.
Jin Wikyung fidgeted under my stare, then turned to Hyuk Mujin.
“Vice Squad Leader Hyuk. Didn’t I send you a Sound Transmission earlier? I told you I was going to pretend not to recognize him and asked you to play along.”
“Ah, well, you see...”
“That’s what happened, isn’t it? Hmm?”
Hyuk Mujin furrowed his brow.
“Ow. Lesser Family Head, why are you suddenly stepping on my foot?”
“V-Vice Squad Leader Hyuk!”
“Aagh! It hurts!”
He was trying. He really was.
I didn’t need to look under the table to know exactly what was happening.
As I watched the two of them, a quiet laugh escaped me.
They haven’t changed.
Jin Wikyung and Hyuk Mujin.
They were the same two people I remembered. The events of the past year had lent them more experience and composure, but underneath it all, they were unchanged.
That alone was enough.
I wonder how everyone else is doing.
It didn’t take long to find out.
Jin Wikyung gave me a detailed account of everything that had happened since I left, including what had become of the people I had yet to see again.
Lee Seowol was still fighting to restore the Mount Heng Sword Sect to its former glory, while Wolhwa was building a city of entertainment in the relatively desolate reaches of northern Shanxi.
And then...
“Cheongpung is missing?”
“That’s right. Not long after you left, he set out for Huashan with the Three Plum Blossom Elites, but apparently ran away along the way.”
That wasn’t going missing. That was escaping.
From what I heard next, Cheongpung’s disappearance had caused quite an uproar.
An influential Elder from Huashan had even come in person to ask them for a favor—if they saw that Cheongpung bastard, they were to contact him.
“The sect’s most senior elder and its young prodigy vanished one after another. Their reaction was understandable. Just watching them made my heart ache.”
The Sword Saint and Cheongpung... At this point, shouldn’t I start wondering whether they were actually related by blood?
“Huashan is really thriving.”
“It’s still doing better than our family.”
“Why? Didn’t they wipe out the mounted bandits in the north and continue to prosper? That sounds like they’re doing pretty well to me.”
Jin Wikyung shook his head gloomily.
“Huashan at least has a Sect Leader and plenty of disciples. Our Family Head’s seat is vacant.”
“Oh.”
“Perhaps that’s why their situation didn’t feel like someone else’s problem. We agreed to help each other from now on. Struggling martial factions have to support one another.”
So that was how they ended up helping each other out.
I thought of the man who had been missing for years—the Family Head—then promptly erased him from my mind.
In this Murim, he might be my father, but I had never even seen his face. He was a complete stranger.
I felt no familial affection for him, much less any desire to see him.
If I see him, I see him. If not, whatever.
Instead, I was far more concerned about Jin Mukyung, whom I’d traded snarls with every chance we got.
“Come to think of it, where’s Second Hyung? Did he go somewhere?”
Quite a bit of time had passed, but he still hadn’t appeared.
Wipeng might have stayed behind to guard the Jin Family of Taiyuan in Jin Wikyung’s absence, but Jin Mukyung should definitely have come...
“He’s in closed-door training.”
“Huh? Again?”
“Still would be more accurate.”
“...You mean he’s been in there this whole time?”
I was dumbfounded when Jin Wikyung nodded.
In martial-arts novels, everyone and his dog spent decades in closed-door training or meditating before a wall, but anyone who actually tried it would quickly realize it was nearly impossible.
Even a single year would be unbearable without extraordinary mental fortitude.
When did Jin Mukyung enter closed-door training?
It had been right after he lost his duel with Cheongpung, which meant he had been in there for a year and six months by now.
For all that time, he had not taken a single step out of the dark training hall. He had devoted himself to ceaseless training, surviving on water and fasting pills for all three meals.
“Could he have been in there so long that he lost track of the date? Maybe he didn’t know about the Star-Array Grand Banquet.”
“I went to see Mukyung before we left and told him about it. I asked if he wanted to come with us.”
I didn’t need to hear his answer. Jin Mukyung’s absence told me everything.
Jin Wikyung continued in a low voice.
“He said he wouldn’t leave until he achieved Great Completion. He asked me to tell you that.”
Great Completion...
To Jin Mukyung, the Star-Array Grand Banquet was a fruit he could reach simply by stretching out his hand.
He was already one of the foremost young prodigies in the Central Plains. If he entered, he could prove his martial arts and win even greater fame.
But Jin Mukyung had chosen his martial arts over that sweet fruit.
He’s an incredible guy.
While everyone else reached for the fruit and scrambled up the tree, Jin Mukyung had turned his back on it and devoted himself to training.
And one day, when his training was complete, he would possess not the fruit, but the tree itself.
A tree laden with fruit.
Yeah. That’s a true martial artist.
I respected his choice. I didn’t know what lay at the end of the path Jin Mukyung had chosen, but I believed its direction was more correct than anyone else’s.
That was enough.
I murmured with a sigh.
“So that’s how it turned out.”
“Are you disappointed?”
“A little. I was hoping the three of us would get together again.”
“Even without those two, the world is full of exceptional masters. The Ten Dragons and Phoenixes are right there, aren’t they?”
“I guess.”
At my lukewarm response, Jin Wikyung smiled faintly.
“Then I’ll have to turn that disappointment into joy.”
Pardon?
“I brought you a present.”
A present? As I stared at him in confusion, Hyuk Mujin rose from his chair.
A short while later, he returned carrying something long and tightly wrapped in thick cloth.
“Do you know what it is?”
Of course I did. The moment I saw it, my heart began to pound and my fingertips twitched.
It was instinct.
Not Jin Taekyung’s instinct, but a spearman’s.
“This is...”
“Fifteen days ago, Elder Jang Taebo handed this to me and said something.”
Shrrk.
As Hyuk Mujin peeled away the cloth, Jin Wikyung’s voice rang in my ears.
“He said he finally understood how Gan Jiang and Mo Ye must have felt.”
Vrrrrm.
The spear let out a low hum.

sentences.text: Hyuk Mujin had been living a dream day after day.
Every now and then, he even pinched his own cheek.
Mujin, are you really allowed to be this happy?
This isn’t a dream, is it?
He had every reason to feel that way.
Just over ten years ago, he had been nothing more than a boy who admired martial artists.

Even two years ago, he had thought his life was a cesspool.
His working hours were long and tedious, and his martial arts had stagnated.

Countless battles.
One brush with death after another...
The Third Young Master—or rather, his Captain—was like a magnet that drew every danger in the world toward him.
Hyuk Mujin fought through the threats flying at them from every direction, and by the time he came to his senses, he had grown by leaps and bounds.
Ohhh, power!
Power is surging through me!
...Patient, come over here.
Your crazy spell is acting up again, so it’s time for your beating.
Bam!
Ba-ba-bam!
He had taken an awful lot of beatings, too.
There had even been times when he secretly set out a bowl of pure water and prayed behind Jin Taekyung’s back.
Please, please don’t let the Captain hit me anymore.
Just take him somewhere far away.

One day, Jin Taekyung left without warning.

Great Hero Wipeng, how do you know me...

He began receiving instruction from Wipeng, the Peak master known as the Ghost Sword.

It’s made up of the family’s finest.

Wow!

Congratulations!
Pack your things.

This is our lord’s command, so you cannot afford a single mistake.
Gasp.

They truly had been dreamlike days.

“You’re Hyuk Mujin, right?”
Wild hair.
A thick, unkempt beard.
A muscular beggar dressed in rags.
At the words that came from his mouth, Hyuk Mujin’s hands and feet went numb.
That voice was unmistakably familiar.
How had he failed to recognize it at once?
No wonder the back of his head had been itching strangely...
Where did it all go wrong?
Was it when he came to Henan as Jin Wikyung’s escort?
Or when he accepted his father’s request to inspect the Henan branch of the Hyuk Family Cloth Shop?
He didn’t know.
There was only one thing he could be certain of.
I’m fucked.
Cold sweat slid down his back as he heard the words that turned his journey to Henan into a journey to hell.
“I’ll give you three seconds.
Put your head on the ground.”
His mind screamed no, but his body knew better.
Hyuk Mujin, a rising talent of the Jin Family of Taiyuan and Vice Squad Leader of its most elite unit, slammed his head into the ground with a thunderous cry.
“Yessssss, sir!”
Thud!
A white stone wall, with five or six rooftops visible beyond it.
The large estate where the Jin Family of Taiyuan was staying drew steadily closer.
“This the place?”
Hyuk Mujin answered in a half-dead voice.
His once-impressive martial uniform hung in tatters, and one eye was swollen and bruised dark blue.
To borrow his own words from half an hour ago, this was the price of reckless bravado.
“Oh.
You found a nice place to stay.
The family must be doing pretty well these days.”
I wasn’t the only one who had changed over the past year.
Hyuk Mujin had changed, and so had the Jin Family of Taiyuan’s standing.
The fact that they had rented an entire estate this large with the Star-Array Grand Banquet right around the corner told me all I needed to know.
“Lead the way, punk.”
“Urgh!
That hurts!
It hurts!”
“I’m kicking you because it’s supposed to hurt, punk.”
I walked along, booting him in the rear.
Two Jin Family martial artists standing rigidly on guard before the estate spotted their superior and gaped.
“Gasp!”
“Vice Squad Leader!”
Hyuk Mujin subtly averted his gaze and cleared his throat.
“Ahem.
Have you been keeping proper watch?
This gentleman is...”
Shing!
Shing-shing!
“You bastard!”
“How dare you do this to our Vice Squad Leader!”
He was the Vice Squad Leader of some newly formed unit called the Jin Dragon Squad, and apparently his subordinates thought quite highly of him.
I gave the Jin Dragon Squad members pointing their swords at me an amiable smile.
“Put those away.
I’m with the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
“Vice Squad Leader, are you all right?”
“Where did this beggar bastard come from, spouting nonsense?”
At his subordinates’ response, Hyuk Mujin nodded with a stricken expression.
“Not a beggar bastard.
He’s the Third Young Master.”
Pardon?
“But no matter how you look at him, he’s a beggar...”
I could let it go once, but not twice.
Hyuk Mujin noticed my expression change and spoke gloomily.
“Hocheol.”
The martial artist named Hocheol promptly answered.
“Yes, Vice Squad Leader.”
“Put your head on the ground.”
Right.
That was the least I could expect from my right-hand man.
Leaving Hocheol behind to commune with the earth, I stepped onto the estate grounds.
Almost immediately, I came face-to-face with someone strolling through the courtyard.
His eyes trembled with emotion.
Even if ten years had passed instead of one, he would have recognized me.
It wouldn’t have mattered how disheveled I looked.
That was what blood ties meant.
That was what it meant to be brothers.

The massive man staring at me, frozen like a statue, was Jin Wikyung.
A radiant smile spread across his face.
He strode toward me and spoke.
“Are you from the Beggars’ Sect?”
Brothers, my ass.
“I recognized you at a glance, actually.”
“Are you kidding me?”
“I’m serious.
Did you really think I wouldn’t recognize you, my youngest?”

He had even asked what position I held in the Beggars’ Sect.

chapters.title: Chapter 244
paragraphs: I had loved the sea ever since I was a child. I loved its distinctive salty scent that pierced my nose, and I loved standing still and watching the waves crash against the shore.
And now, there was a sea inside me.
The qi sea.
Another name for the dantian.
As always, I swam through that endless sea of qi.
I took hold of the horn of the fire dragon curled within my dantian, leisurely made the rounds of hundreds of acupoints, then opened my eyes.
Ding.

System You have successfully completed circulating your qi! - The realm of the Scorching Sun Divine Arts has risen to the sixth stage! - All Fire Gate Clan martial arts have become more refined and powerful! - All fatigue has been cleared, and all stamina has been restored! Level Up!
Finally, the sixth stage?
I neither saw nor heard any of the other System notifications. The only thing that mattered to me was that the realm of the Scorching Sun Divine Arts had reached the sixth stage.
This is where the real thing begins, right?
The Fire Gate Cavern had been created by the first Sect Leader of the Fire Gate Clan for his successors.
Filled with fire energy, it was ideal for absorbing Scorching Yang Qi and particularly well suited to learning the Fire Gate Clan’s greatest martial arts.
Simply put, it was a double-EXP event zone.
But even that place had a clear limit.
Hmm.
“Why are you groaning like a dog that needs to take a dump?”
That was from a conversation I’d had with Jeok Cheongang around six months after entering the Fire Gate Cavern.
At the time, I was brimming with confidence after achieving the remarkable feat of reaching the third stage of the Scorching Sun Divine Arts.
“Oh, it’s nothing. I was just wondering whether I should spend another year in closed-door training here.”
“Here? In the Fire Gate Cavern?”
“Yes.”
“What about the Star-Array Grand Banquet?”
“I’m improving by leaps and bounds here. Why would I leave? If I stay just one more year... Why are you looking at me like that?”
“It’s nothing. I was merely marveling at how much of a blockhead you are.”
“That sounds like a pretty big deal to me.”
Jeok Cheongang looked at me as though I were hopeless, then let out a deep sigh.
“Do you know how old this old man is?”
“If even you don’t know, how would I?”
“I am one hundred and one years old this year.”
“Oh. One hundred and one Dalmatians.”
“I swear by the ancestors of the Fire Gate Clan, if you spout one more piece of nonsense, I’ll throw your body into the sacred flame as firewood.”
“...Yes, sir.”
“In any case, even this old man, who has lived for so many years, remains at the eighth stage. What was that you were saying?”
“Wait. The eighth stage? Haven’t you already achieved Great Completion?”

“Do you think a divine art is called a divine art for no reason? Although your progress is fast, even the martial arts that can be learned in the Fire Gate Cavern have their limits. In the case of the Scorching Sun Divine Arts, that limit is precisely the fifth stage.”
“...Then what comes after that?”
“Martial arts are like weapons. You must sharpen and hone them without end. The only answer is to gain enlightenment through countless hardships and experiences.”
“Then I should at least reach the fifth stage of the Scorching Sun Divine Arts before our time here is up.”

“Would you look at this greedy brat. Reaching the third stage in a mere six months is already an incredible achievement. Don’t start spouting nonsense just because you have the Heavenly Martial Physique.”
“How long do you think it’ll take me?”
“Who knows? It took this old man exactly five years to go from the third stage to the fifth... Even with the Heavenly Martial Physique, it should take you two years.”
Exactly six months later, I found myself staring at a half-dazed Jeok Cheongang.
“T-This can’t be happening. It makes no sense.”
“But it did happen. Did it really take you five whole years?”
“You little bastard! I was one of the greatest geniuses of my generation!”
“Yeah. Heavenly Martial Physique.”
“This is impossible! Why did it have to be someone like you!”
Remembering Jeok Cheongang howling in despair, I let out a quiet laugh.
Putting the old memory aside, I rose and stood before a large full-length mirror.
Reflected in it was a perfectly proportioned body with compact, powerful muscles, hair carelessly twisted up and tied, and a clean-shaven chin.
It would’ve been fine if I’d left it alone.
Now that the thick beard was gone, my face felt oddly bare. But there had been no overcoming Jin Wikyung’s forceful insistence.

“The Star-Array Grand Banquet is a gathering watched by every martial artist under heaven. The Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi is appearing in the Central Plains, and you plan to go out looking like this? It’s a crime!”
I had thought he was being a little dramatic, but after getting it cut, I liked this better.
Whatever else anyone might say about this body, its face was ridiculously handsome.
You look like a gisaeng’s brother.
I was inwardly muttering the highest compliment one man could give another when I suddenly realized I had forgotten something.
Clink.
“Oh, right. These.”
The shackles, iron chains, and iron ball I had continued to drag around even after arriving at the estate of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
I gazed silently at the objects that had practically become parts of my body, then opened my mouth.
“Inventory open. Summon.”
Whoosh!
The next moment, a solid spear shaft filled my hand.
The weapon summoned from my Inventory was a spear approximately two meters long.
Perhaps because it had been forged from an enormous quantity of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron, it gleamed with a beautiful, translucent light from the spearhead to the butt of the shaft.
“White Flame.”
Vrrrrm. Vrrrrm.
As though it had recognized its own name, a faint vibration traveled from within the shaft.
White Flame was a weapon forged solely for me by Jang Taebo, the former Guild Leader of the Ironcraft Guild and a man hailed as the greatest smith under heaven.
Perhaps that was why White Flame was special.
Both to the naked eye and in the System window.
However...
“Captain, it’s time to leave.”
As Hyuk Mujin’s voice outside the door reminded me, it was time to go.
Sunlight flooded the world outside the window, and the people of the Jin Family of Taiyuan—including Jin Wikyung—were moving about busily.
“All right.”
As I answered, I choked up on the spear and slashed.
With four streaks of light, everything that had bound me for the past year fell away. The shackles, chains, and iron ball rolled noisily across the floor.
Clatter! Boom!
Bang!
Startled by the tremendous noise, Hyuk Mujin opened the door and rushed in.
“What was that?”
“Nothing. Let’s go. Oh, bring the chains with you.”
“...You’re planning to tie me up with those, aren’t you?”
“Those chains are made of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron.”
“Gasp! They’re mine. Mine!”
Clicking my tongue, I stepped outside. Jin Wikyung sat astride a large black horse, and he grinned when he spotted me.
“Let’s go.”
“Yes.”
Our destination was Mount Song.
There, the curtain would rise on the Star-Array Grand Banquet, an event drawing the attention of the entire Murim.
“Yah!”
Jin Wikyung and I led the way, with fifty members of the Jin Dragon Squad following behind us.
Through the rushing wind, someone’s distant cry echoed faintly.
“Wait! Wait for me! Don’t leave me behind!”
I still couldn’t believe that bastard was the Vice Squad Leader.
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, muttered with an annoyed expression.
“...Does this old man really have to attend something like this?”
The Dharma King, Hong Dao, was sitting with an endlessly benevolent expression.
“This old monk is bored enough to attain Buddhahood, so keep your mouth shut and sit still.”
“Why? You said you were bored too.”
“I am already bored. What do you think will happen if an old man with little time left starts whining beside me like a seven-year-old child?”
“I would get annoyed.”
“Exactly. If I become both bored and annoyed, I may smash my wooden fish and return to my quarters.”
“You’ve attained enlightenment.”
“Amitabha. Amitabha.”
Tok. Tok. Tok-tok-tok-tok...
The clear sound of the wooden fish echoed through the room. Those who had been listening with pricked ears looked utterly dumbfounded.
They say the Fire King and Dharma King are famous for their eccentric behavior. I can see why.
Those two haven’t changed at all.
Why won’t that old bastard just die?
Their thoughts differed, as did their clothing and the auras they exuded.
Some were middle-aged men without a single white hair, while others were old men with heads of pure white.
The dozen or so people gathered there, each so different from the others, were not ordinary mortals.
They belonged to the fifteen pillars supporting the Murim of the present day: the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families.
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, was already familiar with some of them.
“Oh, if it isn’t Family Head Namgung.”
Namgung Ryong, the Family Head of the Namgung Family, rose and offered a fist-and-palm salute.
“Please forgive my late greeting. The two of you were having such an entertaining conversation that I found myself listening...”
“It’s fine. I left in a hurry last time and didn’t even get to see your face. My apologies.”
“Not at all. I am the one who should apologize.”
“So, is your son competing in this Star-Array Grand Banquet?”
“He won’t be able to compete this time.”
“That’s unfortunate.”
Jeok Cheongang’s face showed not the slightest trace of regret as his gaze shifted to the man beside Namgung Ryong.
“Who are you?”
The man with the sycophant’s beard asked sourly, “Are you speaking to me?”
“Yes. You, with the beard like a sycophant’s.”
“I am Gong Iljung, Sect Leader of the Zhongnan Sect.”
“Ah. Are you that fellow they call the Wind-and-Cloud War God or something?”
“Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord.”
“What does that matter? Young man, why are you so rigid?”
Gong Iljung, a “young man” who had long since passed sixty, had to steady his breathing.
Only a year earlier, he had been shocked when the Roaring Fury Swordsman—his Senior Brother, who had studied under the same Master—returned with a severe Internal Injury.
But he had to endure it. The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, was quite literally a mad tiger.
“Did you hear about it from your Senior Brother?”
“Keep him under control so he doesn’t come to my attention. Shoving him into the Repentance Cave for about twenty years might not be a bad idea.”
Gong Iljung barely managed to swallow the curse rising to his lips.
What Jeok Cheongang meant was that he could easily live another twenty years, so Gong Iljung had better not act up.
Even those who normally regarded Jeok Cheongang with displeasure inwardly clicked their tongues.
What a vicious old man...
Is he planning to live forever?
You’ve caused enough trouble. Go already, old man. Let the rest of us breathe.
I should have brought my Master.
They might have belonged to different sects, but the Murim had a strict order of seniority.
Jeok Cheongang was a figure from two generations earlier, which naturally placed his seniority far above theirs.
That was one reason the leaders gathered there could do nothing but tremble before him, no matter how much they dominated the world.
Martial arts, seniority, or verbal skill—there was not a single area in which they could beat him.
“Ahem. Ahem.”
“Erhm.”

“Hahahaha! With the tiger away, the fox has been playing king. Jeok Cheongang, have you been well?”
Jeok Cheongang turned toward the thunderous voice, his brow already deeply furrowed. He knew exactly who had arrived.
“Goddammit. You’re still not dead?”
“Listen to the way this little old man talks.”
An enormous old man threw back his head and laughed. Although his mouth split open in a broad grin, his sharp eyes swept over Jeok Cheongang.
“I welcomed a great-great-grandson not long ago. There’s no chance I’ll die before I see that boy get married.”
“A great-great-grandson?”
“What, are you jealous? My great-grandson’s wife is Hebei’s greatest beauty, and the boy looks just like his mother. He’s adorable.”
Jeok Cheongang replied with an indifferent expression.
“The greatest beauty in that neighborhood can’t be trusted. Isn’t Hebei the place where anyone with fists this big and a thick waist gets called Yang Guifei?”
“What!”
“Anyway, congratulations. With ten children, I suppose you’ll never have to worry about heirs.”
“...What kind of bullshit are you trying to pull?”
“What do you mean? To celebrate seeing your great-great-grandson, why don’t you change your title while you’re at it? Forget Thunderbolt Saber King. How about Virility Saber King?”
“GRAAAAGH! You old man!”
“Sit down while I’m asking nicely. Don’t you remember breaking your bones when you challenged me during the Great Faction War?”
Sssshhhh!
Powerful waves of qi poured from the two Supreme Peak masters. Their auras were so overwhelming that everyone present felt a chill run through them.
If the Dharma King had not been there to mediate, blood might have been spilled.

“Now, now. Amitabha, Amitabha... Both of you, calm yourselves. The heroes outside are waiting. How can you make such a disgraceful spectacle? Do you wish to smear the names of the Fire Gate Clan and the Hebei Peng Family with shit here today?”
His final words proved effective. The two men hesitated, then withdrew their auras.

“I’ll be waiting, Virility Saber King.”

The Dharma King, the Thunderbolt Saber King, and the overlords of the various regions followed behind him.
They passed through a corridor draped in blue cloth and stepped out into the blazing sunlight.
Three zhang below, tens of thousands of people gathered at the foot of Mount Song greeted them with a tremendous roar.
“Waaaaaaah!”

sentences.text: I had loved the sea ever since I was a child.
I loved its distinctive salty scent that pierced my nose, and I loved standing still and watching the waves crash against the shore.
And now, there was a sea inside me.
The qi sea.
Another name for the dantian.
As always, I swam through that endless sea of qi.
I took hold of the horn of the fire dragon curled within my dantian, leisurely made the rounds of hundreds of acupoints, then opened my eyes.
Ding.

System You have successfully completed circulating your qi! - The realm of the Scorching Sun Divine Arts has risen to the sixth stage! - All Fire Gate Clan martial arts have become more refined and powerful! - All fatigue has been cleared, and all stamina has been restored!
Level Up!
Finally, the sixth stage?
I neither saw nor heard any of the other System notifications.
The only thing that mattered to me was that the realm of the Scorching Sun Divine Arts had reached the sixth stage.
This is where the real thing begins, right?
The Fire Gate Cavern had been created by the first Sect Leader of the Fire Gate Clan for his successors.
Filled with fire energy, it was ideal for absorbing Scorching Yang Qi and particularly well suited to learning the Fire Gate Clan’s greatest martial arts.
Simply put, it was a double-EXP event zone.
But even that place had a clear limit.
Hmm.
“Why are you groaning like a dog that needs to take a dump?”
That was from a conversation I’d had with Jeok Cheongang around six months after entering the Fire Gate Cavern.
At the time, I was brimming with confidence after achieving the remarkable feat of reaching the third stage of the Scorching Sun Divine Arts.
“Oh, it’s nothing.
I was just wondering whether I should spend another year in closed-door training here.”
“Here?
In the Fire Gate Cavern?”
“Yes.”
“What about the Star-Array Grand Banquet?”
“I’m improving by leaps and bounds here.
Why would I leave?
If I stay just one more year...
Why are you looking at me like that?”
“It’s nothing.
I was merely marveling at how much of a blockhead you are.”
“That sounds like a pretty big deal to me.”
Jeok Cheongang looked at me as though I were hopeless, then let out a deep sigh.
“Do you know how old this old man is?”
“If even you don’t know, how would I?”
“I am one hundred and one years old this year.”
“Oh.
One hundred and one Dalmatians.”
“I swear by the ancestors of the Fire Gate Clan, if you spout one more piece of nonsense, I’ll throw your body into the sacred flame as firewood.”
“...Yes, sir.”
“In any case, even this old man, who has lived for so many years, remains at the eighth stage.
What was that you were saying?”
“Wait.
The eighth stage?
Haven’t you already achieved Great Completion?”
“Do you think a divine art is called a divine art for no reason?
Although your progress is fast, even the martial arts that can be learned in the Fire Gate Cavern have their limits.
In the case of the Scorching Sun Divine Arts, that limit is precisely the fifth stage.”
“...Then what comes after that?”
“Martial arts are like weapons.
You must sharpen and hone them without end.
The only answer is to gain enlightenment through countless hardships and experiences.”
“Then I should at least reach the fifth stage of the Scorching Sun Divine Arts before our time here is up.”
“Would you look at this greedy brat.
Reaching the third stage in a mere six months is already an incredible achievement.
Don’t start spouting nonsense just because you have the Heavenly Martial Physique.”
“How long do you think it’ll take me?”
“Who knows?
It took this old man exactly five years to go from the third stage to the fifth...
Even with the Heavenly Martial Physique, it should take you two years.”
Exactly six months later, I found myself staring at a half-dazed Jeok Cheongang.
“T-This can’t be happening.
It makes no sense.”
“But it did happen.
Did it really take you five whole years?”
“You little bastard!
I was one of the greatest geniuses of my generation!”
“Yeah.
Heavenly Martial Physique.”
“This is impossible!
Why did it have to be someone like you!”
Remembering Jeok Cheongang howling in despair, I let out a quiet laugh.
Putting the old memory aside, I rose and stood before a large full-length mirror.
Reflected in it was a perfectly proportioned body with compact, powerful muscles, hair carelessly twisted up and tied, and a clean-shaven chin.
It would’ve been fine if I’d left it alone.
Now that the thick beard was gone, my face felt oddly bare.
But there had been no overcoming Jin Wikyung’s forceful insistence.
“The Star-Array Grand Banquet is a gathering watched by every martial artist under heaven.
The Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi is appearing in the Central Plains, and you plan to go out looking like this?
It’s a crime!”
I had thought he was being a little dramatic, but after getting it cut, I liked this better.
Whatever else anyone might say about this body, its face was ridiculously handsome.
You look like a gisaeng’s brother.
I was inwardly muttering the highest compliment one man could give another when I suddenly realized I had forgotten something.
Clink.
“Oh, right.
These.”
The shackles, iron chains, and iron ball I had continued to drag around even after arriving at the estate of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
I gazed silently at the objects that had practically become parts of my body, then opened my mouth.
“Inventory open.
Summon.”
Whoosh!
The next moment, a solid spear shaft filled my hand.
The weapon summoned from my Inventory was a spear approximately two meters long.
Perhaps because it had been forged from an enormous quantity of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron, it gleamed with a beautiful, translucent light from the spearhead to the butt of the shaft.
“White Flame.”
Vrrrrm.
Vrrrrm.
As though it had recognized its own name, a faint vibration traveled from within the shaft.
White Flame was a weapon forged solely for me by Jang Taebo, the former Guild Leader of the Ironcraft Guild and a man hailed as the greatest smith under heaven.
Perhaps that was why White Flame was special.
Both to the naked eye and in the System window.
However...
“Captain, it’s time to leave.”
As Hyuk Mujin’s voice outside the door reminded me, it was time to go.
Sunlight flooded the world outside the window, and the people of the Jin Family of Taiyuan—including Jin Wikyung—were moving about busily.
“All right.”
As I answered, I choked up on the spear and slashed.
With four streaks of light, everything that had bound me for the past year fell away.
The shackles, chains, and iron ball rolled noisily across the floor.
Clatter!
Boom!
Bang!
Startled by the tremendous noise, Hyuk Mujin opened the door and rushed in.
“What was that?”
“Nothing.
Let’s go.
Oh, bring the chains with you.”
“...You’re planning to tie me up with those, aren’t you?”
“Those chains are made of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron.”
“Gasp!
They’re mine.
Mine!”
Clicking my tongue, I stepped outside.
Jin Wikyung sat astride a large black horse, and he grinned when he spotted me.
“Let’s go.”
“Yes.”
Our destination was Mount Song.
There, the curtain would rise on the Star-Array Grand Banquet, an event drawing the attention of the entire Murim.
“Yah!”
Jin Wikyung and I led the way, with fifty members of the Jin Dragon Squad following behind us.
Through the rushing wind, someone’s distant cry echoed faintly.
“Wait!
Wait for me!
Don’t leave me behind!”
I still couldn’t believe that bastard was the Vice Squad Leader.
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, muttered with an annoyed expression.
“...Does this old man really have to attend something like this?”
The Dharma King, Hong Dao, was sitting with an endlessly benevolent expression.
“This old monk is bored enough to attain Buddhahood, so keep your mouth shut and sit still.”
“Why?
You said you were bored too.”
“I am already bored.
What do you think will happen if an old man with little time left starts whining beside me like a seven-year-old child?”
“I would get annoyed.”
“Exactly.
If I become both bored and annoyed, I may smash my wooden fish and return to my quarters.”
“You’ve attained enlightenment.”
“Amitabha.
Amitabha.”
Tok.
Tok.

The clear sound of the wooden fish echoed through the room.

I can see why.

They belonged to the fifteen pillars supporting the Murim of the present day: the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families.

My apologies.”

You, with the beard like a sycophant’s.”
