chapters.title: Chapter 245
paragraphs: Waaaaaaah!
The deafening roar of tens of thousands of martial artists made my ears ring.
They had gathered here to attend the Star-Array Grand Banquet, each carrying dreams of rising to prominence, and their cheers seemed endless.
The noise, which seemed as though it would never end, gradually died down the moment Dharma King Hong Dao raised his hand.

In that hand was the Green Jade Buddha Staff, the symbol of a thousand years of Shaolin. Shaolin Temple was the Mount Tai and Northern Dipper of the Murim, and its immense authority silenced the crowd.
The old monk’s deep voice, infused with profound internal energy, spread across the grounds.
“I often look up at the sky. Over the long years, I have seen, read, and watched countless stars.”
I had heard something once.
They said the greatest reason Dharma King Hong Dao had become the Abbot of Shaolin was not his formidable martial arts, but his learning and wisdom.
“The Star-Array Grand Banquet. If you wish to become the brightest star at this banquet, think brightly and act brightly.”
After a brief silence, he added one short sentence.
“That is how one survives even in darkness.”
The shorter a congratulatory speech, the better. Better still if it contained a hint of profound wisdom, and better yet if the speaker was the Abbot of Shaolin.
Another roar of cheers and applause erupted.
“Waaaaaaah!”
As I watched, I suddenly wondered how many of the tens of thousands gathered here had actually understood what he meant.
Probably one in ten.
No, not even one in a hundred.
But I understood. I knew what Hong Dao’s words referred to.
Dark Heaven.
My training in the Fire Gate Cavern had been harsher than everything I had endured before it combined.
Jeok Cheongang had pushed me relentlessly, so much so that he had seemed not merely impatient, but downright anxious.
At first, I had thought it was because of his infirmities of old age.
But before long, Jeok Cheongang revealed something after much deliberation. Only then did I understand his urgency.
Dark Heaven. A powerful enemy that had yet to reveal its true nature.
We don’t have much time. Keep training and preparing. That is the best thing you can do.
I looked at the old man standing to Hong Dao’s right.
His small frame was noticeably different from Hong Dao’s, yet he gave off an overwhelming presence. Jeok Cheongang somehow spotted me and flashed a crooked grin.
He looked visibly older than he had a year ago. My chest churned before I knew it.
You’d better know you’re dead if you don’t win.
Especially if you run into some bastard with the surname Peng. Beat the shit out of him. Break him and tear him apart!
A cold wind swept through my queasy chest.
One dose of the Fire King’s motion-sickness medicine, delivered through Sound Transmission, cured me completely. I quietly looked away.
Until I arrived, I had been fairly confident. But seeing the sheer number of martial artists with my own eyes made it difficult to guarantee victory.
I’d better not answer. If I give him a definite answer and then lose, he’ll ride my ass even more.
In any case, the opening address was over, so the preliminaries would begin soon.
Like a salmon swimming upstream, I pushed through the tightly packed martial artists toward the back. Then I spotted a familiar face.
“Huh?”
What was that guy’s name again?
Oh, right. Jongni Chu of Yunnan. The guy with the self-styled epithet Always-Victorious Sword.
I had wondered why he had come all the way here from some remote backwater. Apparently, he had come for the Star-Array Grand Banquet after all.
With his skills, he should make it pretty far.
I considered saying hello, but decided against it. It seemed like it would only become a hassle.
Instead, I sent a greeting to the guy standing blankly and looking around, one he could not hear.
Yeah. Good luck to you too.
And prayed that, if possible, he wouldn’t run into me.
“I like duels. There are winners and losers, but no draws. What could be more clear-cut than that?”
The middle-aged man muttered in a relaxed voice.
A pair of glasses imported from the Western Regions rested on his nose. They had the marvelous ability to make objects appear several times larger, which naturally made them extremely expensive.
“That’s why people bet money on them. The result is certain.”
Gambling was an inseparable part of the Star-Array Grand Banquet.
From the preliminaries, which filtered out the unqualified among tens of thousands of applicants, to the finals, hundreds of duels would be held.
For that reason, the Star-Array Grand Banquet was not only a feast for the martial artists of the world. It was also the greatest season of the year for gamblers across the continent.
“So, who would you like to bet on, and how much?”
The bald man sitting across from the middle-aged man asked the question. At a glance, he looked like someone with one foot in the underworld, but his manner was polite.
“You’re still as impatient as ever.”
“We have a lot of customers waiting.”
“I see. Well, let’s see...”
After a moment’s pause, the middle-aged man pulled a money pouch from his robes and tossed it onto the table.
Unable to withstand the weight, the pouch opened, and gleaming silver yuanbao spilled across the tabletop with a clatter.
“A thousand silver nyang on the Iron-Water Divine Dragon of the Yangtze River Channel League.”
It was an enormous sum.
Especially considering the preliminaries had not even begun.
The middle-aged man’s nerve was clearly extraordinary.
The bald man’s eyelids trembled as he stared at the silver yuanbao.
“Are you betting on the Iron-Water Divine Dragon to win the whole thing?”
“Of course not. Cheol Soo may be one of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes, but he’s not capable of that yet. His Master, the Seafaring King, would be another matter.”
“Then...?”
“I’m betting he’ll take first place in the preliminaries.”
“Hmm.”
The bald man let out a low groan.
The preliminaries of the Star-Array Grand Banquet were commonly called a “sieve.” With so many applicants, those below the required level had to be filtered out.
Naturally, judging tens of thousands of applicants created countless possible outcomes.
Which also meant the odds would be enormous.
“That’s different from what you said earlier.”
“How so?”
“You said you liked duels because there were only winners and losers, making the result clear-cut.”
“You really shouldn’t gamble.”
The middle-aged man laughed heartily before continuing.
“That’s the kind of wager third-rate gamblers make. All or nothing. One of the two sides is bound to win, so there’s a limit to how much you can earn. But who am I?”
“A Dogon.”
“Exactly. That’s why I like duels. People want the easy road. They don’t want the difficult one.”
“Ah.”
A gambler among gamblers. A gambler who had reached the Peak of his craft was called a Dogon.
The middle-aged man had come here with a conclusion drawn from meticulous research and calculation.
The bald man bowed deeply in admiration.
“I’ve learned a great deal, Great Hero Kwak.”
“If you learned something, you should pay the tuition.”
“What would you like?”
“Keep your mouth shut, just as you have until now.”
“Of course.”
“Then that’s enough. Let’s see... The preliminaries should be starting soon. I’ll have a drink and come back to collect my money.”
He had absolute confidence that his prediction would prove correct.
That was a Dogon for you.
The middle-aged man pushed up his glasses and left.
A swordsman guarding the door, practically dying of curiosity, cautiously asked, “Boss, who was that?”
“That gentleman? A Dogon.”
“Gasp! A Dogon?”
“And one of the most renowned Dogons in the world.”
“Is he really that incredible?”
“There are exactly three legendary Dogons.”
The bald man spread three fingers.
“A-Gwi in Sichuan. Jjak-Gwi in Guangdong. And the last one...”
One of his fingers folded down.
“On a continental scale, that gentleman. Kwak Cheolyung.”
“Kwak Cheolyung...!”
“So go keep an eye on the Iron-Water Divine Dragon. Now that I think about it, that rookie’s gotten pretty damn cocky.”
Whack!
The bald man kicked the swordsman in the shin.
A short while later, he welcomed his next customer. This one was rather strange, with a mask pulled up over his nose.
“Where would you like to place your bet?”
“Will this be kept confidential?”
The masked man’s voice was uneasy.
He flinched as if people beat him up every chance they got. Anyone could tell at a glance that he was a Third Rate martial artist.
The area around his eye is all black and blue. Someone must’ve worked him over pretty good. Well, as long as I get paid, it’s none of my concern.
A gentle smile spread across the bald man’s lips.
It was his professional smile, the one that appeared automatically whenever he saw a sucker.
“Of course. Go ahead.”
The masked man glanced around nervously before pulling out a money pouch.
“A hundred silver nyang on Jin Taekyung, the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, taking first place in the preliminaries.”
“Those from there to here, follow me.”
The Star-Array Grand Banquet had so many participants that it required hundreds of supervisors and multiple testing grounds.
More than a hundred applicants followed their assigned supervisor. Naturally, I was among them.
There really are a lot of people.
Not only were they numerous, but they came in every possible variety.

There were skinny people and fat people, fresh-faced youths with downy hair and wandering martial artists who looked as though they had been through every hardship imaginable. There were women who immediately drew the eye and handsome men with flawlessly smooth features.
A hundred people, a hundred different appearances. The saying fit perfectly.
One massive man stood out even among that crowd. He looked like the very definition of a man’s man, and judging by our eye levels, he was at least a head taller than me.
Fuck, is this the continent or Norway?
He stood over two meters tall. His forearms bulged with enough muscle to look ready to burst, and one bore a tattoo of a salmon impaled on a harpoon.
Even his features looked oddly Western. He looked so much like a Norwegian that I began to wonder if he actually was one.
I stole a sideways glance at him, only for our eyes to meet.
I cautiously opened my mouth.
“Ah, aim fine, thankoo. An’ yoo?”
That wasn’t it. What was it again?
I had stopped studying English after my elementary-school red-pen workbooks, and now I was so nervous the words barely came out.
“Ah! Where are you from?”
Norway answered.
“You fucking asshole, what are you doing?”
“Oh, I’m sorry.”
“You little shit, are you picking a fight with me right now?”
A hearty stream of curses and the gazes of everyone around us came flying my way.
Just as I was about to answer, the supervisor shouted sternly.
“Anyone who causes trouble will be forcibly disqualified!”
Norway opened and closed his mouth like a salmon as he glared at me.
Then a strand of Sound Transmission reached me, carrying an aura and killing intent as rough and sharp as a harpoon.
I’ll make you regret this.
Talk about vicious. A true descendant of the Vikings.
Still, I was the one in the wrong.
I bowed my head in apology and continued walking. A forceful snort sounded behind me, but I pretended not to hear it.
He’s pretty strong, though.
He looked to be in his twenties, yet he was already a formidable opponent. My pulse quickened at the thought that I had encountered someone like him right from the start.
The world really is wide.
If the preliminaries were already this intense, genuine monsters might come crawling out during the main event. Remembering Jeok Cheongang’s warning, I steeled my resolve.
“The first thing we will assess is your fist-and-foot techniques.”
The supervisor led us to an unnamed cliff.
I did not need to ask how the test would be conducted.
Other applicants were already taking it.
Whack! Crack!
“Graaagh!”
A foolish martial artist with his wrist twisted rolled across the ground. The supervisor sighed and broke a bamboo marker.
“Jangyu of the Butterfly Sect, eliminated. Next!”
The next martial artist stepped forward and punched the cliff.
Boom!
This martial artist was around the First Rate level. At least he knew how to put internal energy behind his strike.
A clear mark appeared on the cliff, which was a hard-packed mixture of roughly equal parts rock and soil.
The supervisor measured its depth and width, then nodded.
“Gobul of the Sodang Sect, passed. Next!”
Those who passed moved aside, while Third Rate martial artists whose punches left faint marks—or who hurt their hands with a single blow—were eliminated in droves.
“You’ve seen enough to understand how this works. Let’s begin. Now, let’s see...”
The supervisor pulled out a bamboo marker.
Then he called a name.
“Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
As the gazes of the people around me turned toward me, a System notification rang out.
Ding.
System Quest: Star-Array Grand Banquet has been created.

sentences.text: Waaaaaaah!
The deafening roar of tens of thousands of martial artists made my ears ring.
They had gathered here to attend the Star-Array Grand Banquet, each carrying dreams of rising to prominence, and their cheers seemed endless.
The noise, which seemed as though it would never end, gradually died down the moment Dharma King Hong Dao raised his hand.
In that hand was the Green Jade Buddha Staff, the symbol of a thousand years of Shaolin.
Shaolin Temple was the Mount Tai and Northern Dipper of the Murim, and its immense authority silenced the crowd.
The old monk’s deep voice, infused with profound internal energy, spread across the grounds.
“I often look up at the sky.
Over the long years, I have seen, read, and watched countless stars.”
I had heard something once.
They said the greatest reason Dharma King Hong Dao had become the Abbot of Shaolin was not his formidable martial arts, but his learning and wisdom.
“The Star-Array Grand Banquet.
If you wish to become the brightest star at this banquet, think brightly and act brightly.”
After a brief silence, he added one short sentence.
“That is how one survives even in darkness.”
The shorter a congratulatory speech, the better.
Better still if it contained a hint of profound wisdom, and better yet if the speaker was the Abbot of Shaolin.
Another roar of cheers and applause erupted.
“Waaaaaaah!”
As I watched, I suddenly wondered how many of the tens of thousands gathered here had actually understood what he meant.
Probably one in ten.
No, not even one in a hundred.
But I understood.
I knew what Hong Dao’s words referred to.
Dark Heaven.
My training in the Fire Gate Cavern had been harsher than everything I had endured before it combined.
Jeok Cheongang had pushed me relentlessly, so much so that he had seemed not merely impatient, but downright anxious.
At first, I had thought it was because of his infirmities of old age.
But before long, Jeok Cheongang revealed something after much deliberation.
Only then did I understand his urgency.
Dark Heaven.
A powerful enemy that had yet to reveal its true nature.
We don’t have much time.
Keep training and preparing.
That is the best thing you can do.
I looked at the old man standing to Hong Dao’s right.
His small frame was noticeably different from Hong Dao’s, yet he gave off an overwhelming presence.
Jeok Cheongang somehow spotted me and flashed a crooked grin.
He looked visibly older than he had a year ago.
My chest churned before I knew it.
You’d better know you’re dead if you don’t win.
Especially if you run into some bastard with the surname Peng.
Beat the shit out of him.
Break him and tear him apart!
A cold wind swept through my queasy chest.
One dose of the Fire King’s motion-sickness medicine, delivered through Sound Transmission, cured me completely.
I quietly looked away.
Until I arrived, I had been fairly confident.
But seeing the sheer number of martial artists with my own eyes made it difficult to guarantee victory.
I’d better not answer.
If I give him a definite answer and then lose, he’ll ride my ass even more.
In any case, the opening address was over, so the preliminaries would begin soon.
Like a salmon swimming upstream, I pushed through the tightly packed martial artists toward the back.
Then I spotted a familiar face.
“Huh?”
What was that guy’s name again?
Oh, right.
Jongni Chu of Yunnan.
The guy with the self-styled epithet Always-Victorious Sword.
I had wondered why he had come all the way here from some remote backwater.
Apparently, he had come for the Star-Array Grand Banquet after all.
With his skills, he should make it pretty far.
I considered saying hello, but decided against it.
It seemed like it would only become a hassle.
Instead, I sent a greeting to the guy standing blankly and looking around, one he could not hear.
Yeah.
Good luck to you too.
And prayed that, if possible, he wouldn’t run into me.
“I like duels.
There are winners and losers, but no draws.
What could be more clear-cut than that?”
The middle-aged man muttered in a relaxed voice.
A pair of glasses imported from the Western Regions rested on his nose.
They had the marvelous ability to make objects appear several times larger, which naturally made them extremely expensive.
“That’s why people bet money on them.
The result is certain.”
Gambling was an inseparable part of the Star-Array Grand Banquet.
From the preliminaries, which filtered out the unqualified among tens of thousands of applicants, to the finals, hundreds of duels would be held.
For that reason, the Star-Array Grand Banquet was not only a feast for the martial artists of the world.
It was also the greatest season of the year for gamblers across the continent.
“So, who would you like to bet on, and how much?”
The bald man sitting across from the middle-aged man asked the question.
At a glance, he looked like someone with one foot in the underworld, but his manner was polite.
“You’re still as impatient as ever.”
“We have a lot of customers waiting.”
“I see.
Well, let’s see...”
After a moment’s pause, the middle-aged man pulled a money pouch from his robes and tossed it onto the table.
Unable to withstand the weight, the pouch opened, and gleaming silver yuanbao spilled across the tabletop with a clatter.
“A thousand silver nyang on the Iron-Water Divine Dragon of the Yangtze River Channel League.”
It was an enormous sum.
Especially considering the preliminaries had not even begun.
The middle-aged man’s nerve was clearly extraordinary.
The bald man’s eyelids trembled as he stared at the silver yuanbao.
“Are you betting on the Iron-Water Divine Dragon to win the whole thing?”
“Of course not.
Cheol Soo may be one of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes, but he’s not capable of that yet.
His Master, the Seafaring King, would be another matter.”
“Then...?”
“I’m betting he’ll take first place in the preliminaries.”
“Hmm.”
The bald man let out a low groan.
The preliminaries of the Star-Array Grand Banquet were commonly called a “sieve.” With so many applicants, those below the required level had to be filtered out.
Naturally, judging tens of thousands of applicants created countless possible outcomes.
Which also meant the odds would be enormous.
“That’s different from what you said earlier.”
“How so?”
“You said you liked duels because there were only winners and losers, making the result clear-cut.”
“You really shouldn’t gamble.”
The middle-aged man laughed heartily before continuing.
“That’s the kind of wager third-rate gamblers make.
All or nothing.
One of the two sides is bound to win, so there’s a limit to how much you can earn.
But who am I?”
“A Dogon.”
“Exactly.
That’s why I like duels.
People want the easy road.
They don’t want the difficult one.”
“Ah.”
A gambler among gamblers.
A gambler who had reached the Peak of his craft was called a Dogon.
The middle-aged man had come here with a conclusion drawn from meticulous research and calculation.
The bald man bowed deeply in admiration.
“I’ve learned a great deal, Great Hero Kwak.”
“If you learned something, you should pay the tuition.”
“What would you like?”
“Keep your mouth shut, just as you have until now.”
“Of course.”
“Then that’s enough.
Let’s see...
The preliminaries should be starting soon.
I’ll have a drink and come back to collect my money.”
He had absolute confidence that his prediction would prove correct.
That was a Dogon for you.
The middle-aged man pushed up his glasses and left.
A swordsman guarding the door, practically dying of curiosity, cautiously asked, “Boss, who was that?”
“That gentleman?
A Dogon.”
“Gasp!
A Dogon?”
“And one of the most renowned Dogons in the world.”
“Is he really that incredible?”
“There are exactly three legendary Dogons.”
The bald man spread three fingers.
“A-Gwi in Sichuan.
Jjak-Gwi in Guangdong.
And the last one...”
One of his fingers folded down.
“On a continental scale, that gentleman.
Kwak Cheolyung.”
“Kwak Cheolyung...!”
“So go keep an eye on the Iron-Water Divine Dragon.
Now that I think about it, that rookie’s gotten pretty damn cocky.”
Whack!
The bald man kicked the swordsman in the shin.
A short while later, he welcomed his next customer.
This one was rather strange, with a mask pulled up over his nose.
“Where would you like to place your bet?”
“Will this be kept confidential?”
The masked man’s voice was uneasy.
He flinched as if people beat him up every chance they got.
Anyone could tell at a glance that he was a Third Rate martial artist.
The area around his eye is all black and blue.
Someone must’ve worked him over pretty good.
Well, as long as I get paid, it’s none of my concern.
A gentle smile spread across the bald man’s lips.
It was his professional smile, the one that appeared automatically whenever he saw a sucker.
“Of course.
Go ahead.”
The masked man glanced around nervously before pulling out a money pouch.
“A hundred silver nyang on Jin Taekyung, the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, taking first place in the preliminaries.”
“Those from there to here, follow me.”
The Star-Array Grand Banquet had so many participants that it required hundreds of supervisors and multiple testing grounds.
More than a hundred applicants followed their assigned supervisor.
Naturally, I was among them.
There really are a lot of people.
Not only were they numerous, but they came in every possible variety.
There were skinny people and fat people, fresh-faced youths with downy hair and wandering martial artists who looked as though they had been through every hardship imaginable.
There were women who immediately drew the eye and handsome men with flawlessly smooth features.
A hundred people, a hundred different appearances.
The saying fit perfectly.
One massive man stood out even among that crowd.
He looked like the very definition of a man’s man, and judging by our eye levels, he was at least a head taller than me.
Fuck, is this the continent or Norway?
He stood over two meters tall.
His forearms bulged with enough muscle to look ready to burst, and one bore a tattoo of a salmon impaled on a harpoon.
Even his features looked oddly Western.
He looked so much like a Norwegian that I began to wonder if he actually was one.
I stole a sideways glance at him, only for our eyes to meet.
I cautiously opened my mouth.
“Ah, aim fine, thankoo.
An’ yoo?”
That wasn’t it.
What was it again?
I had stopped studying English after my elementary-school red-pen workbooks, and now I was so nervous the words barely came out.
“Ah!
Where are you from?”
Norway answered.
“You fucking asshole, what are you doing?”
“Oh, I’m sorry.”
“You little shit, are you picking a fight with me right now?”
A hearty stream of curses and the gazes of everyone around us came flying my way.
Just as I was about to answer, the supervisor shouted sternly.
“Anyone who causes trouble will be forcibly disqualified!”
Norway opened and closed his mouth like a salmon as he glared at me.
Then a strand of Sound Transmission reached me, carrying an aura and killing intent as rough and sharp as a harpoon.
I’ll make you regret this.
Talk about vicious.
A true descendant of the Vikings.
Still, I was the one in the wrong.
I bowed my head in apology and continued walking.
A forceful snort sounded behind me, but I pretended not to hear it.
He’s pretty strong, though.
He looked to be in his twenties, yet he was already a formidable opponent.
My pulse quickened at the thought that I had encountered someone like him right from the start.
The world really is wide.
If the preliminaries were already this intense, genuine monsters might come crawling out during the main event.
Remembering Jeok Cheongang’s warning, I steeled my resolve.
“The first thing we will assess is your fist-and-foot techniques.”
The supervisor led us to an unnamed cliff.
I did not need to ask how the test would be conducted.
Other applicants were already taking it.
Whack!
Crack!
“Graaagh!”
A foolish martial artist with his wrist twisted rolled across the ground.
The supervisor sighed and broke a bamboo marker.
“Jangyu of the Butterfly Sect, eliminated.
Next!”
The next martial artist stepped forward and punched the cliff.
Boom!
This martial artist was around the First Rate level.
At least he knew how to put internal energy behind his strike.
A clear mark appeared on the cliff, which was a hard-packed mixture of roughly equal parts rock and soil.
The supervisor measured its depth and width, then nodded.

Let’s begin.
Now, let’s see...”
The supervisor pulled out a bamboo marker.
Then he called a name.
“Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”

Ding.
System Quest: Star-Array Grand Banquet has been created.

chapters.title: Chapter 246
paragraphs: System Quest Star-Array Grand Banquet What more needs to be said? Go forth without hesitation. Become the champion of this banquet watched by all under heaven, leave your mark on the Murim, and bask in glory! Grade: Supreme Peak Restriction: Jin Taekyung Mission: Win the Star-Array Grand Banquet (Incomplete) Reward: ??? Failure: Fire King’s Wrath
I paused at the penalty for failure.
I mean, I might not win the Star-Array Grand Banquet. Is that really something to get angry about?
Imagining Jeok Cheongang flying into a rage left me feeling a little wronged.
Especially after teaching me for barely a year.
Granted, I was an extremely unusual case.
Even so, the fact that the Quest window went out of its way to spell it out suggested just how much Jeok Cheongang expected of me.
“Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan. Where are you?”
“Oh, here.”
At the supervisor’s call, I closed the Quest window and stepped forward.
With every step I took, I felt the people’s gazes on me. Along with them, murmuring voices pierced my ears.
“Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan...”
“The Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi?”
“Is that him? The young man the Fire King took as his Disciple?”
“That’s him. I’m sure of it.”
I also heard Norway’s familiar gruff voice.
“Hmph. So you did have something to rely on. You may look the part, but you’re still a weakling.”
Ignoring the whispers from every direction, I stopped in front of the cliff.
The supervisor, who had been staring at me in surprise, addressed me in a suddenly more respectful tone.
“If the mark is at least three Korean inches deep, you pass. Anything less is a failure.”
“Yes.”
Three Korean inches was roughly ten centimeters.
Any ordinary First Rate master who had consistently trained in fist techniques should be able to pass without much trouble.
But now that it was my turn, I found myself growing tense.
Damn. I have no idea how much force to use.
I honestly had no clue. Exactly how much strength did I need to apply to leave a mark three Korean inches deep?
After staring at it for a moment, I decided to use the Help function.
“Excuse me, Supervisor.”
“Yes?”
“As long as I make the mark at least three Korean inches deep, I pass, right?”
“That is correct. However, once your fist lands, the test is over.”
“Oh, I see.”
Well, that makes it easy.
I nodded, placed my fist against the cliff, and gave it a gentle push.
Thump! Rumble-rumble-rumble!
The cliff face split as softly as tofu. Fragments of rock and clumps of dirt came pouring down.
With my arm buried up to the elbow, I looked at the supervisor.
“I pass. Okay?”
The supervisor’s expression was a sight to behold.
His mouth hanging open, he looked back and forth between my face and the arm embedded in the cliff. Then he stammered out a question.
“H-How did you do that?”
“I pushed.”
“I mean, how did you...”
“I just put some strength into it and pushed.”
“Anyway, I passed, right? My fist never left the cliff, and it went in plenty deep.”
“W-Well...”
The supervisor’s pupils wavered.
“I-I’m not entirely sure. Nothing like this has ever happened before.”
“Then it’s settled. This is how you handle it from now on.”
“Y-Young Hero Jin, I’m sorry, but could you do it a little more normally? I’m finding it rather difficult to judge...”
“Normally?”
I did it this way because I don’t think I can do it normally, you idiot.
I was wondering whether I should just throw a moderately powerful punch when—
“Bwahahaha!”
The sudden burst of laughter made everyone, myself included, turn toward it.
Norway, the massive man who stood out from the crowd, was looking at me with open mockery.
“You’re desperate to stand out, aren’t you?”
I scratched my chin and answered.
“Not particularly. But why are you so desperate to pick a fight with me?”
“You?”
“Yeah. You.”
A vein bulged on Norway’s forehead.
“I heard the Fire King’s Disciple had only just passed the age of twenty.”
“I’m twenty-two. I’m all grown up.”
“I am thirty.”
“Thirty? That’s pretty close to my age. Wanna be friends?”
“How dare a fresh-faced brat like you...”
Does he have a fetish for honorific speech or something?
He glared and stepped forward, but the supervisor moved to stop him.
“Control yourself!”
“To hell with self-restraint. The only person who can speak to me like that is my Master.”
I leisurely folded my arms.
“So this is what you’ve been dying to tell us. Fine, let’s hear it. Who’s your Master?”
“The Seafaring King.”
The Seafaring King? Could it be...?
I cried out in shock.
“Jang Bogo!”
“What the fuck are you talking about? My Master’s name is Pa Ryun! The Seafaring King, Pa Ryun!”
“Oh. Right. Of course not.”
Unlike me, who was disappointed, everyone else reacted strongly to the name that had just come out of Norway’s mouth.
A stir spread among the applicants and supervisors in our group. Even the people being tested more than ten jang away began to murmur.
“Th-The Seafaring King, Pa Ryun!”
“Pa Ryun, the Alliance Leader of the Yangtze River Channel League and one of the Ten Kings?”
“Then that young man must be the Iron-Water Divine Dragon. No wonder he dared to pick a fight with the Fire King’s Disciple.”
“What is going on over there? Two disciples of the Ten Kings in the same group...”
Norway—or rather, the Iron-Water Divine Dragon—snorted at their reactions.
He was probably proud to have such an impressive Master, but pride in his own abilities also showed in every one of his actions.
Well, he’s certainly strong enough to justify it.
Perhaps that was only natural for the Disciple of one of the Ten Kings.
Unlike me, he also seemed to have trained under the Seafaring King, Pa Ryun, since childhood.
I didn’t know exactly how powerful the Yangtze River Channel League was, but he had clearly received unstinting support—martial arts, elixirs, and everything else he could need.
As I watched with my arms folded, the Iron-Water Divine Dragon gave a short laugh.
“So you’re the Fire King’s Disciple? Don’t get cocky just because you come from some provincial martial family and received a mere year of instruction.”
He wasn’t exactly wrong. Shanxi Province lay on the outskirts, far from the Central Plains, and the Jin Family of Taiyuan was indeed a provincial martial family.
That may be true, but...
“You’re a pirate. And your Master is a pirate chief.”
“A pirate? How dare you insult the Yangtze River Channel League! We are heroes who roam the rivers and the open sea!”
“Sure. But boil that down to two syllables and you get ‘pirate,’ don’t you?”
“You insolent wretch! What kind of vile nonsense is that? The heroes of our League are worlds apart from such scum!”
“Worlds apart? Do you guys eat those weird-looking fruits, too? The ones that make you unable to swim?”
“You son of a—!”
“You ate the Son-of-a-Bitch Fruit.”
Crack-crack-crack.
A vicious sound came from the Iron-Water Divine Dragon’s enormous fist.
He glared at me with killing intent in his eyes and stepped forward. The supervisor hurriedly moved between us.
“Wait! If you fight here, you’ll be disqualified—!”
“Move.”
“Gasp!”
Given the scale of the Star-Array Grand Banquet, every supervisor overseeing the examinations was a formidable martial artist, ranging from Supreme First Rate to Peak.
The supervisor assigned to our group was at Supreme First Rate, but the moment the Iron-Water Divine Dragon seized his shoulder, his face turned deathly pale.
“W-What is this...”
“You don’t need to stop me. My Master gave me strict orders to win the Star-Array Grand Banquet, after all.”
“Th-Then...”
“I’m not going to fight. I’m only going to show that brat one move.”
The Iron-Water Divine Dragon released the supervisor and strode toward the cliff. Without the slightest hesitation, he pushed his fist into it.
Craaaack!
Shattering the solid rock, he drove his arm in up to the forearm. Then he looked at me and clicked his tongue.
“This is all you accomplished.”
I had known it from the moment I first saw him, but the Iron-Water Divine Dragon was a master of exceptionally advanced external martial arts.
His size and strength couldn’t be explained by natural gifts alone.
Martial arts had built that body—an external qigong technique of the highest order had tempered it.
“Whoa...!”
“As expected of the Iron-Water Divine Dragon!”
Exclamations rang out at a feat of strength worthy of being called divine.
Even an ordinary Peak master would have found it impossible without using internal energy. Yet the Iron-Water Divine Dragon had done it as easily as breathing.
And, as if to make a point, he had created a hole far deeper than mine.
“The Fire King’s Disciple is impressive too, but is he still outmatched?”
“That’s understandable. He’s much younger, and it’s only been a year since the Fire King took him as his Disciple.”
“The Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi must have been aiming to win as well, but... it looks like that’ll be difficult this time.”
Whatever the people around me were whispering, the Iron-Water Divine Dragon was undeniably impressive.
Regardless of who his Master was, no one could dispute that he was skilled enough to hold his head high anywhere in the Murim.
Clap, clap, clap.
“Now that’s some strength. Congratulations on passing.”
“Pathetic. There’s no need to force yourself to act calm.”
“I mean it.”
The Iron-Water Divine Dragon snorted at my applause and turned toward the supervisor.
After one unbelievable spectacle after another, the supervisor was still dazed.
“Did I pass?”
“Ah. W-Well...”
“It doesn’t matter. I had no intention of stopping here anyway.”
Rumble-rumble-rumble.
The Iron-Water Divine Dragon pulled his arm free with absurd ease and looked around.
Reading the envy, jealousy, and despair in the gazes fixed upon him—the looks people reserved for the strong—he bared his teeth at me.
“Brat, consider it an honor to witness the Ship-Breaking Fist.”
“The Ship-Breaking Fist?”
He didn’t answer.
Instead, internal energy as vast as the open sea surged in waves from his entire body.
His waist, thicker than a bear’s, and his pillar-like arms bent far backward. Blue internal energy, like a flowing river, already surged around his fist.
Gooooong.
The air around us trembled.
Then—
Kkwaaaang!
The Ship-Breaking Fist.
A single punch capable of splitting a sailing ship slammed into the cliff.
A deafening boom rang out, followed by a storm. People covered their faces with both arms and groaned as dirt and fragments of rock rained down.
“Gasp!”
“Urgh!”
Amid the chaos, I stood perfectly still and watched without missing a thing.
That was why, when the dust cloud finally settled, I could fully understand the cries of astonishment that erupted around me.
Wow...
The cliff stretched over a hundred jang in both height and width, a natural formation that had stood there for countless years.
Now, a massive hole had appeared where none had existed before.
No. It would be more accurate to call it a small cave.
It was over ten jang across in every direction and five jang deep.
“I-I can’t believe it.”
“This is the Seafaring King’s unique martial art...!”
An unmistakable tremor passed through the crowd.
Everyone gathered here revered martial arts above all else and yearned to grow stronger.
Their awestruck gazes converged on the martial artist who had just displayed a level of martial arts they couldn’t hope to approach.
“Huff. Huff.”
His broad back heaved. Muscles swollen to the point of tearing rippled beneath his skin.
After catching his breath for a while, the Iron-Water Divine Dragon turned around with a composed expression.
A single short question slipped between his thick lips.
“The result?”
Only then did the supervisor come to his senses and barely manage to speak.
“P-Passed. You passed.”
“I see.”
The Iron-Water Divine Dragon’s lips curled upward as his gaze swept over the crowd.
The heat in his eyes had yet to fade. Finally, they stopped on my face.
“Did you see that?”
I gave a small nod.
“What did you think?”
“It was impressive.”
“And?”
“Hmm. Congratulations on passing.”
“That’s all?”
“What else? You want me to pat you on the ass?”
Grind.
At the sight of the Iron-Water Divine Dragon grinding his teeth, my head instinctively shook from side to side.
I told him it was impressive. What more does he want from me?
What is he, a fucking child?

Maybe it was because he was a pirate, but he was as simpleminded as they came. The fact that he had poured out enough strength to leave himself breathless during the preliminaries was just as ridiculous.
I clicked my tongue inwardly and spoke to the supervisor.
“Let’s keep things moving. We’ve already wasted quite a bit of time.”
“Ah, yes. Understood. Then, next...”
I was turning away as the supervisor called the next name when the Iron-Water Divine Dragon spoke again.
“Looking at you, I can tell what level the Fire Gate Clan is.”
“What?”
I stopped without meaning to. The Iron-Water Divine Dragon continued in a mocking voice.
“Single-heir succession. No teaching to outsiders. It sounds grand, but in the end, aren’t you running away from me like a fucking dog with its tail between its legs?”
“That’s your opinion.”
“Is it only my opinion?”
“What?”
I suddenly looked around.
Countless gazes surrounded the Iron-Water Divine Dragon and me.
I could read the emotions in their eyes.
Disappointment. Contempt.
Beep.

System People are whispering after seeing how terrified you look! - People are beginning to doubt the reputation of the Fire Gate Clan. - People are beginning to doubt the reputation of Jeok Cheongang. Fame decreased by 18! Fame decreased by 20! Fame decreased...
The System notifications pierced my ears.
At that moment, I came to my senses as though waking from a long sleep.
So that’s how it is.
For a moment, I had forgotten.
No—I had known, but I hadn’t truly understood what it meant.
Even though the curtain had risen on the Star-Array Grand Banquet, this magnificent and dazzling stage where the martial artists of the world had gathered in one place...
This is the Central Plains. This is the world.
A world where everything was proven through strength alone.
Winners and losers.
A world divided into those two kinds of people.
That was the Murim.
“Hoo.”
The Iron-Water Divine Dragon sneered when he saw me heave a sigh deep enough to sink the ground.
“Looks like you’re finally ready to give it a try.”
“Yeah. Thanks. That really woke me up.”
“I heard you’re fairly skilled with a spear. I’ll graciously permit you to...”
“You called it the Ship-Breaking Fist, right?”
“Huh?”
“It might be able to split a ship, but a cliff is beyond it.”
Whoosh.
One step.
The distance of five jang vanished.
By the time my foot touched the ground again, I had already passed the Iron-Water Divine Dragon.
A belated cry of shock came from behind me.
“You—!”
Instead of answering, I looked up at the cliff before me.
The fire dragon sleeping in my dantian awoke and surged through every limb and bone. Hundreds of acupoints grew scorching hot.
“Jin Taekyung!”
“You fucking weakling. Consider it an honor to witness the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist.”
Blue flames filled my vision.

Granted, I was an extremely unusual case.
Even so, the fact that the Quest window went out of its way to spell it out suggested just how much Jeok Cheongang expected of me.
“Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
Where are you?”
“Oh, here.”
At the supervisor’s call, I closed the Quest window and stepped forward.
With every step I took, I felt the people’s gazes on me.
Along with them, murmuring voices pierced my ears.
“Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan...”
“The Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi?”
“Is that him?
The young man the Fire King took as his Disciple?”
“That’s him.
I’m sure of it.”
I also heard Norway’s familiar gruff voice.
“Hmph.
So you did have something to rely on.
You may look the part, but you’re still a weakling.”
Ignoring the whispers from every direction, I stopped in front of the cliff.
The supervisor, who had been staring at me in surprise, addressed me in a suddenly more respectful tone.
“If the mark is at least three Korean inches deep, you pass.
Anything less is a failure.”
“Yes.”
Three Korean inches was roughly ten centimeters.
Any ordinary First Rate master who had consistently trained in fist techniques should be able to pass without much trouble.
But now that it was my turn, I found myself growing tense.
Damn.
I have no idea how much force to use.
I honestly had no clue.
Exactly how much strength did I need to apply to leave a mark three Korean inches deep?
After staring at it for a moment, I decided to use the Help function.
“Excuse me, Supervisor.”
“Yes?”
“As long as I make the mark at least three Korean inches deep, I pass, right?”
“That is correct.
However, once your fist lands, the test is over.”
“Oh, I see.”
Well, that makes it easy.
I nodded, placed my fist against the cliff, and gave it a gentle push.
Thump!
Rumble-rumble-rumble!
The cliff face split as softly as tofu.
Fragments of rock and clumps of dirt came pouring down.
With my arm buried up to the elbow, I looked at the supervisor.
“I pass.
Okay?”
The supervisor’s expression was a sight to behold.
His mouth hanging open, he looked back and forth between my face and the arm embedded in the cliff.
Then he stammered out a question.
“H-How did you do that?”
“I pushed.”
“I mean, how did you...”
“I just put some strength into it and pushed.”
“Anyway, I passed, right?
My fist never left the cliff, and it went in plenty deep.”
“W-Well...”
The supervisor’s pupils wavered.
“I-I’m not entirely sure.
Nothing like this has ever happened before.”
“Then it’s settled.
This is how you handle it from now on.”
“Y-Young Hero Jin, I’m sorry, but could you do it a little more normally?
I’m finding it rather difficult to judge...”
“Normally?”
I did it this way because I don’t think I can do it normally, you idiot.
I was wondering whether I should just throw a moderately powerful punch when—
“Bwahahaha!”
The sudden burst of laughter made everyone, myself included, turn toward it.
Norway, the massive man who stood out from the crowd, was looking at me with open mockery.
“You’re desperate to stand out, aren’t you?”
I scratched my chin and answered.
“Not particularly.
But why are you so desperate to pick a fight with me?”
“You?”
“Yeah.
You.”
A vein bulged on Norway’s forehead.
“I heard the Fire King’s Disciple had only just passed the age of twenty.”
“I’m twenty-two.
I’m all grown up.”
“I am thirty.”
“Thirty?
That’s pretty close to my age.
Wanna be friends?”
“How dare a fresh-faced brat like you...”
Does he have a fetish for honorific speech or something?
He glared and stepped forward, but the supervisor moved to stop him.
“Control yourself!”
“To hell with self-restraint.
The only person who can speak to me like that is my Master.”
I leisurely folded my arms.
“So this is what you’ve been dying to tell us.
Fine, let’s hear it.
Who’s your Master?”
“The Seafaring King.”
The Seafaring King?
Could it be...?
I cried out in shock.
“Jang Bogo!”
“What the fuck are you talking about?
My Master’s name is Pa Ryun!
The Seafaring King, Pa Ryun!”
“Oh.
Right.
Of course not.”
Unlike me, who was disappointed, everyone else reacted strongly to the name that had just come out of Norway’s mouth.
A stir spread among the applicants and supervisors in our group.
Even the people being tested more than ten jang away began to murmur.
“Th-The Seafaring King, Pa Ryun!”
“Pa Ryun, the Alliance Leader of the Yangtze River Channel League and one of the Ten Kings?”
“Then that young man must be the Iron-Water Divine Dragon.
No wonder he dared to pick a fight with the Fire King’s Disciple.”
“What is going on over there?
Two disciples of the Ten Kings in the same group...”
Norway—or rather, the Iron-Water Divine Dragon—snorted at their reactions.
He was probably proud to have such an impressive Master, but pride in his own abilities also showed in every one of his actions.
Well, he’s certainly strong enough to justify it.
Perhaps that was only natural for the Disciple of one of the Ten Kings.
Unlike me, he also seemed to have trained under the Seafaring King, Pa Ryun, since childhood.
I didn’t know exactly how powerful the Yangtze River Channel League was, but he had clearly received unstinting support—martial arts, elixirs, and everything else he could need.
As I watched with my arms folded, the Iron-Water Divine Dragon gave a short laugh.
“So you’re the Fire King’s Disciple?
Don’t get cocky just because you come from some provincial martial family and received a mere year of instruction.”
He wasn’t exactly wrong.
Shanxi Province lay on the outskirts, far from the Central Plains, and the Jin Family of Taiyuan was indeed a provincial martial family.
That may be true, but...
“You’re a pirate.
And your Master is a pirate chief.”
“A pirate?
How dare you insult the Yangtze River Channel League!
We are heroes who roam the rivers and the open sea!”
“Sure.
But boil that down to two syllables and you get ‘pirate,’ don’t you?”
“You insolent wretch!
What kind of vile nonsense is that?
The heroes of our League are worlds apart from such scum!”
“Worlds apart?
Do you guys eat those weird-looking fruits, too?
The ones that make you unable to swim?”
“You son of a—!”
“You ate the Son-of-a-Bitch Fruit.”
Crack-crack-crack.
A vicious sound came from the Iron-Water Divine Dragon’s enormous fist.
He glared at me with killing intent in his eyes and stepped forward.
The supervisor hurriedly moved between us.
“Wait!
If you fight here, you’ll be disqualified—!”
“Move.”
“Gasp!”
Given the scale of the Star-Array Grand Banquet, every supervisor overseeing the examinations was a formidable martial artist, ranging from Supreme First Rate to Peak.
The supervisor assigned to our group was at Supreme First Rate, but the moment the Iron-Water Divine Dragon seized his shoulder, his face turned deathly pale.
“W-What is this...”
“You don’t need to stop me.
My Master gave me strict orders to win the Star-Array Grand Banquet, after all.”
“Th-Then...”
“I’m not going to fight.
I’m only going to show that brat one move.”
The Iron-Water Divine Dragon released the supervisor and strode toward the cliff.
Without the slightest hesitation, he pushed his fist into it.
Craaaack!
Shattering the solid rock, he drove his arm in up to the forearm.
Then he looked at me and clicked his tongue.
“This is all you accomplished.”
I had known it from the moment I first saw him, but the Iron-Water Divine Dragon was a master of exceptionally advanced external martial arts.
His size and strength couldn’t be explained by natural gifts alone.
Martial arts had built that body—an external qigong technique of the highest order had tempered it.
“Whoa...!”
“As expected of the Iron-Water Divine Dragon!”
Exclamations rang out at a feat of strength worthy of being called divine.
Even an ordinary Peak master would have found it impossible without using internal energy.
Yet the Iron-Water Divine Dragon had done it as easily as breathing.
And, as if to make a point, he had created a hole far deeper than mine.
“The Fire King’s Disciple is impressive too, but is he still outmatched?”
“That’s understandable.
He’s much younger, and it’s only been a year since the Fire King took him as his Disciple.”
“The Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi must have been aiming to win as well, but... it looks like that’ll be difficult this time.”
Whatever the people around me were whispering, the Iron-Water Divine Dragon was undeniably impressive.
Regardless of who his Master was, no one could dispute that he was skilled enough to hold his head high anywhere in the Murim.
Clap, clap, clap.
“Now that’s some strength.
Congratulations on passing.”
“Pathetic.
There’s no need to force yourself to act calm.”
“I mean it.”
The Iron-Water Divine Dragon snorted at my applause and turned toward the supervisor.
After one unbelievable spectacle after another, the supervisor was still dazed.
“Did I pass?”
“Ah.
W-Well...”
“It doesn’t matter.
I had no intention of stopping here anyway.”
Rumble-rumble-rumble.
The Iron-Water Divine Dragon pulled his arm free with absurd ease and looked around.
Reading the envy, jealousy, and despair in the gazes fixed upon him—the looks people reserved for the strong—he bared his teeth at me.
“Brat, consider it an honor to witness the Ship-Breaking Fist.”
“The Ship-Breaking Fist?”
He didn’t answer.
Instead, internal energy as vast as the open sea surged in waves from his entire body.
His waist, thicker than a bear’s, and his pillar-like arms bent far backward.
Blue internal energy, like a flowing river, already surged around his fist.
Gooooong.
The air around us trembled.
Then—
Kkwaaaang!
The Ship-Breaking Fist.
A single punch capable of splitting a sailing ship slammed into the cliff.
A deafening boom rang out, followed by a storm.
People covered their faces with both arms and groaned as dirt and fragments of rock rained down.
“Gasp!”
“Urgh!”
Amid the chaos, I stood perfectly still and watched without missing a thing.
That was why, when the dust cloud finally settled, I could fully understand the cries of astonishment that erupted around me.
Wow...
The cliff stretched over a hundred jang in both height and width, a natural formation that had stood there for countless years.
Now, a massive hole had appeared where none had existed before.
No.
It would be more accurate to call it a small cave.
It was over ten jang across in every direction and five jang deep.
“I-I can’t believe it.”
“This is the Seafaring King’s unique martial art...!”
An unmistakable tremor passed through the crowd.
Everyone gathered here revered martial arts above all else and yearned to grow stronger.
Their awestruck gazes converged on the martial artist who had just displayed a level of martial arts they couldn’t hope to approach.
“Huff.
Huff.”
His broad back heaved.
Muscles swollen to the point of tearing rippled beneath his skin.
After catching his breath for a while, the Iron-Water Divine Dragon turned around with a composed expression.
A single short question slipped between his thick lips.
“The result?”
Only then did the supervisor come to his senses and barely manage to speak.
“P-Passed.
You passed.”
“I see.”
The Iron-Water Divine Dragon’s lips curled upward as his gaze swept over the crowd.
The heat in his eyes had yet to fade.
Finally, they stopped on my face.
“Did you see that?”
I gave a small nod.
“What did you think?”
“It was impressive.”
“And?”
“Hmm.
Congratulations on passing.”
“That’s all?”
“What else?
You want me to pat you on the ass?”
Grind.
At the sight of the Iron-Water Divine Dragon grinding his teeth, my head instinctively shook from side to side.
I told him it was impressive.
What more does he want from me?
What is he, a fucking child?
Maybe it was because he was a pirate, but he was as simpleminded as they came.
The fact that he had poured out enough strength to leave himself breathless during the preliminaries was just as ridiculous.
I clicked my tongue inwardly and spoke to the supervisor.
“Let’s keep things moving.
We’ve already wasted quite a bit of time.”
“Ah, yes.
Understood.
Then, next...”
I was turning away as the supervisor called the next name when the Iron-Water Divine Dragon spoke again.
“Looking at you, I can tell what level the Fire Gate Clan is.”
“What?”
I stopped without meaning to.
The Iron-Water Divine Dragon continued in a mocking voice.
“Single-heir succession.
No teaching to outsiders.
It sounds grand, but in the end, aren’t you running away from me like a fucking dog with its tail between its legs?”
“That’s your opinion.”
“Is it only my opinion?”
“What?”
I suddenly looked around.
Countless gazes surrounded the Iron-Water Divine Dragon and me.
I could read the emotions in their eyes.
Disappointment.
Contempt.
Beep.

System People are whispering after seeing how terrified you look! - People are beginning to doubt the reputation of the Fire Gate Clan. - People are beginning to doubt the reputation of Jeok Cheongang.
Fame decreased by 18!
Fame decreased by 20!
Fame decreased...
The System notifications pierced my ears.
At that moment, I came to my senses as though waking from a long sleep.
So that’s how it is.
For a moment, I had forgotten.
No—I had known, but I hadn’t truly understood what it meant.
Even though the curtain had risen on the Star-Array Grand Banquet, this magnificent and dazzling stage where the martial artists of the world had gathered in one place...
This is the Central Plains.
This is the world.
A world where everything was proven through strength alone.
Winners and losers.
A world divided into those two kinds of people.
That was the Murim.
“Hoo.”
The Iron-Water Divine Dragon sneered when he saw me heave a sigh deep enough to sink the ground.
“Looks like you’re finally ready to give it a try.”
“Yeah.
Thanks.
That really woke me up.”
“I heard you’re fairly skilled with a spear.
I’ll graciously permit you to...”
“You called it the Ship-Breaking Fist, right?”
“Huh?”
“It might be able to split a ship, but a cliff is beyond it.”
Whoosh.
One step.
The distance of five jang vanished.
By the time my foot touched the ground again, I had already passed the Iron-Water Divine Dragon.
A belated cry of shock came from behind me.
“You—!”
Instead of answering, I looked up at the cliff before me.
The fire dragon sleeping in my dantian awoke and surged through every limb and bone.
Hundreds of acupoints grew scorching hot.
“Jin Taekyung!”
“You fucking weakling.
Consider it an honor to witness the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist.”
Blue flames filled my vision.

chapters.title: Chapter 247
paragraphs: In a dank underground gambling den, a middle-aged man sat in a corner, fiddling with a set of bone tiles. His head drooped.
“...I’m done for.”
A pair of glasses—an item imported from the Western Regions—rested on his nose. Until a few days ago, they would easily have been worth dozens of silver nyang.
Not anymore.
The lenses, said to magnify objects several times over, were cracked like rice paddies in a drought.
Two men watched him from a distance.
“Is that him? Is he really...?”
“That’s Kwak Cheolyung. No doubt about it.”
“Good heavens. I never thought I’d live to see one of the legendary Dogons in person.”
One had narrow, birdlike eyes, while the other sported a goat’s beard. Otherwise, they were ordinary gamblers of the sort one could find anywhere.
As they watched Kwak Cheolyung shuffle the bone tiles again, the goat-bearded man asked, “But what happened to him?”
It was a fair question. Kwak Cheolyung looked dreadful.
His face was haggard, and his beard had gone untrimmed. His silk clothes were black with grime and torn in several places.
They said he had spent his entire life moving from one gambling table to another, amassing an enormous fortune along the way.
Now, however, he looked like nothing more or less than a gambler who had lost everything.
“Did something happen?”
“It did. Something serious.”
The narrow-eyed man nodded. Unlike the goat-bearded man, who had arrived in Henan late, he knew exactly what had happened to Kwak Cheolyung recently.
“What was it? Don’t keep me in suspense. Tell me.”
“He lost a bet.”
“Winning and losing are common in this business, aren’t they?”
“They are. But what if a thousand silver nyang were at stake?”
“Gasp! A thousand silver nyang!”
The goat-bearded man’s eyes widened.
That was enough money for someone to live in luxury for the rest of his life—no, enough for three generations to live like kings.
Regretting that he had missed such a massive game, he smacked his lips and asked, “It must have been the biggest wager since the founding of the country. Who was his opponent? A-Gwi? Or Jjak-Gwi?”

“My friend, I already knew you were hard of hearing, but you’re completely out of touch with recent news. A-Gwi had his wrist cut off by a fellow called the Mount Qingcheng Guillotine a couple of months ago, and Jjak-Gwi disappeared long ago.”
“Then who besides those two could possibly have beaten Kwak Cheolyung?”
“The Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi.”
“Who?”
“Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan. The Fire King’s disciple.”
The Fire King was one of the Ten Kings and a Supreme Peak master whose reputation resounded throughout the world. There was no reason for such a man’s disciple to gamble with a Dogon.
The goat-bearded man thought for a moment before crying out as if in a groan.
“Dodo! He played Dodo at the Star-Array Grand Banquet.”
“Correct.”
The Star-Array Grand Banquet’s betting games were considered the greatest gambling matches anywhere under heaven, and were therefore called Dodo.
At last, the goat-bearded man understood what had happened and clicked his tongue.
“Tsk, tsk. Kwak Cheolyung did something stupid. The odds on the preliminaries may have been high, but he should have realized that meant the risk was high, too.”
“Do you think he bet without thinking? He must have had his reasons for being confident.”
“What did he bet on, and against whom?”
“The Iron-Water Divine Dragon taking first place in the preliminaries.”
“I suppose he’s strong, being the Seafaring King’s disciple, but I don’t think he’s quite that good.”
The narrow-eyed man shook his head.
“He seems to have gained some insight recently. I heard the Iron-Water Divine Dragon blew away a tenth of a cliff with his Ship-Breaking Fist.”
“...Is that even possible?”
The goat-bearded man had heard tales of Murim masters shattering the earth and cleaving the sky, but he had never imagined they were capable of anything like that.
While he was still reeling in astonishment, the narrow-eyed man said something even harder to believe.
“What’s so impossible about it? Right afterward, the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi brought down the entire cliff.”
The goat-bearded man asked haltingly, his eyes as wide as plates.
“H-He brought down a cliff?”
“That’s right. According to the witnesses, the whole thing came crashing down.”
The goat-bearded man said nothing. He merely stared at his friend in disbelief.
“Isn’t that just a wild rumor?”
“Everyone else, myself included, dismissed it as one at first. A man of flesh and blood bringing down a cliff with his bare hands? It didn’t seem possible.”
“Exactly.”
“But what can we do when it’s true? Kwak Cheolyung sitting over there is living proof.”
“Why would Kwak Cheolyung be proof...? Ah. He must have lost a thousand silver nyang.”
“Five thousand.”
“What?”
“What do you think it feels like to lose money in a game you were certain you’d win?”
“C-Could it be...?”
“Is Kwak Cheolyung any different from the rest of us? In the end, he’s just as addicted to gambling.”
The narrow-eyed man looked at Kwak Cheolyung with pity.
The disheveled man was staring blankly at the tiles in his hand.
“Three days ago, when the Iron-Water Divine Dragon withdrew from the Star-Array Grand Banquet and returned to the Yangtze, Kwak Cheolyung completely lost his mind.”
“Did he keep playing Dodo?”
The narrow-eyed man nodded.
“After the Iron-Water Divine Dragon, Kwak Cheolyung chose Jong Sam of the Hunroe Leg. He bet on him receiving the highest score in the leg-technique assessment.”
“That Peak master who was said to have no equal in kicks throughout Guangxi?”
“Yes. Though by now, he probably has quite a few equals. One of his legs was broken.”
“Don’t tell me the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi did that, too.”

“Are you starting to understand? That’s right. The two of them got into a minor dispute and agreed to exchange one clean blow each before calling it even. But one kick from the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi supposedly broke Jong Sam’s shin.”
“H-How?”
“I don’t know. They say he gave it a casual kick, and the shin snapped with a crunch.”
“The Hunroe Leg even struck first, but the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi just scratched his calf a few times afterward, and that was it. And next was probably...”
The stories that continued to pour from the narrow-eyed man’s mouth about the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi were nothing short of shocking.

The Kunlun Sect’s Kunlun Cloud Dragon, said to possess the finest qinggong among all the young prodigies under heaven, leaped five jang from a standing position—only to come crashing down with Jin Taekyung’s foot planted on his face.

The Beggars’ Sect’s Successor Beggar flew into a rage when he could not close the distance between himself and Jin Taekyung during the movement-technique assessment. Unable to contain his anger, he grabbed Taekyung by the back of the neck and was promptly beaten like a dog.
“The fifth assessment was mechanisms and formations. This time, everyone was certain the Zhuge Clan’s Lesser Family Head would take first place, but...”
The goat-bearded man, who had been listening with a vacant expression, cut him off.
“It was the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi again, wasn’t it?”
“Exactly.”
“But seriously, how? What kind of freak is proficient in mechanisms and formations, too?”
“He isn’t. He’s just proficient in martial arts. The ignorant bastard had no idea what anything was, so he smashed everything in his path and forced his way through.”

“Anyway, the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi took first place in the preliminaries, and Kwak Cheolyung, who bet on someone different every time, was left completely penniless. I heard he sank all the money he’d earned into it, then even mortgaged the estate and land where he’d planned to retire to borrow from loan sharks... Tsk, tsk.”
The narrow-eyed man gazed at Kwak Cheolyung with sympathy.
Only a few silver nyang sat before the legendary Dogon who had once amassed a tremendous fortune. They were probably all he had left in the world.
“Whether you earn it or lose it, it all happens in one shot. Isn’t that right?”
Only then did the goat-bearded man come to his senses. He licked his parched lips.
“Five thousand silver nyang. Whoever won that must have hit the jackpot.”
“He certainly struck it rich. Why else would they call him the Gold-Faced Young Master?”
“The Gold-Faced Young Master? Did he bet on the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi?”
The narrow-eyed man nodded.
“He has incredible foresight. He must have won tens of thousands of silver nyang from this Dodo alone. Why else would he go around wearing a mask made of gold?”
“Good heavens.”
“They say he hasn’t even turned thirty yet... I suppose some men are simply destined to succeed.”
“Damn it. Some of us have reached this age without even owning a proper house. Hoo...”
The two men let out a deep sigh.
Then a chair scraped across the floor as someone rose to his feet.
Kwak Cheolyung staggered out of the gambling den. All he held were a few iron coins he had received as a consolation handout.
The Star-Array Grand Banquet was a long race, lasting at least half a month and sometimes as long as a full month.
After the three-day preliminary assessments ended, the applicants were given a day of free time.
That included me.
“Ahem. Ahehem!”
“Youngest! Youngest!”
“Captain! Captaiiin!”
“...Oh, please.”
Don’t. Don’t shout in a place this crowded. I’m already dying from all the attention, and now you’re making even more people stare.
Tap-tap-tap-tap!
I hurried toward my companions as quickly as I could.
As though he had been waiting for me, Jin Wikyung’s bear-like bulk charged forward with both arms spread wide.
“Youngest! My wonderful little brother!”
Whoosh! Grab!
The moment his bear paw locked around my upper body, Hyuk Mujin seized the back of my hand and rubbed his cheek against it.
“Ohhh, Captain! Top scorer in the Star-Array Grand Banquet preliminaries! The pride of the Jin Family of Taiyuan! The beacon of Shanxi Province! Our Captain! My lord!”
Jin Wikyung is my brother, so I’ll let it slide. But what the hell is wrong with Hyuk Mujin?
Doing my best to hide my bewilderment, I asked, “Are you out of your mind?”
“Yes. I’m insane! Your strength has driven me mad!”
“Are you seriously crazy? Let go. Let go already!”
Whack! Whack! Whack!
Even after I struck the crown of his head three times at lightning speed, Hyuk Mujin refused to budge.
Tears welled in his eyes from the pain, but he still would not release my hand.
“Thank you! Thank you for hitting me!”
“...Are you into that kind of thing?”
I had only heard rumors about people who took pleasure in being hit.
I had always wondered why he had never left despite the countless beatings I had given him. Now that I considered the possibility that he was one of those people, a chill ran down my spine.
“Respect-Your-Preferences Fist!”
Thump!
The blow landed squarely on Hyuk Mujin’s temple, and he collapsed to the ground.
At the same time, something bright and glittering slipped from inside his robes and landed on the floor.
“Huh? A gold mask?”
What is this now?
Is it a prop for that kind of play?
With a grave expression, I tucked the mask into my robes.
Hyuk Mujin, you dangerous bastard. This mask is confiscated for life.
Not a chance.
As I steeled my resolve, I noticed someone I had momentarily forgotten.
“Ahem. Ahehem!”
“Do you have a throat problem?”
Jeok Cheongang, who had been staring off at a distant mountain and repeatedly clearing his throat, flinched.
“W-What nonsense are you spouting?”
“You’ve been coughing this whole time.”
“Ahem!”
He kept looking away, clearly wanting to say something but pretending otherwise. The corners of my mouth rose on their own.
“I did well, didn’t I?”
“Perfect scores in all five assessments. Unanimous first place overall. That pretty much says it all, doesn’t it?”
“Ahem. Don’t get so pleased with yourself over something so trivial. Anyone could have done it, so stop making a fuss.”
“I heard it was the first time in the history of the Star-Array Grand Banquet.”
“These were merely the preliminaries. Have you forgotten what this old man told you? The world is vast, and there are many masters.”
“I beat three of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes.”
The Iron-Water Divine Dragon of the Yangtze River Channel League. The Kunlun Cloud Dragon of the Kunlun Sect. And finally, the Divine Marvel Dragon of the Zhuge Clan.
The Beggars’ Sect’s Successor Beggar was a master comparable to them, and the Hunroe Leg was a Peak master who had already made a brilliant name for himself throughout Guangxi.
Their backgrounds and specialties were all different, but the five of them now had one thing in common.
“I beat every last one of them.”
“That...”
For a moment, Jeok Cheongang was at a loss for words. Then he shook his head again and again.
“Bah. Pathetic weaklings.”
“I’m the strong one.”
“There you go, acting cocky again.”
“Could you just tell me I did well? I brought honor to you—Old Master, no, Master—and to the Fire Gate Clan.”
“You still have a long way to go!”
His words were stern, but the corners of his mouth were twitching.
It was obvious that he was barely holding back laughter.
I would have known that even without the Sound Transmission Jin Wikyung sent me a moment later.
—Don’t let it bother you too much. It seems he already went and bragged about you to the leadership to his heart’s content.
“Ahem!”

As if he had overheard us, Jeok Cheongang cleared his throat again at the perfect moment. Forcing a stern expression onto his face, he said, “Do not grow arrogant merely because you defeated a few nobodies. Compose your body and mind, and prepare for the main event. Understood?”
He was right.
Only the preliminaries had ended. The main event, where the true masters would reveal themselves, had not even begun.
Among those who had passed through the sieve of the preliminaries, there were likely quite a few masters comparable to the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes—or even stronger.
I had already spotted several such people while watching the assessments.
The world really is vast. He was right about that.
Anyone who had concealed their true ability during the preliminaries was not only strong, but clever.
I grinned and gave Jeok Cheongang a fist-and-palm salute.
“I’ll keep that in mind, Master.”
“That boy. Ha ha. Ahem!”
An unmistakable smile appeared at the wrinkled corners of Jeok Cheongang’s mouth.
