Not anymore.
The lenses, said to magnify objects several times over, were cracked like rice paddies in a drought.
Two men watched him from a distance.
“Is that him?
Is he really...?”
“That’s Kwak Cheolyung.
No doubt about it.”
“Good heavens.
I never thought I’d live to see one of the legendary Dogons in person.”
One had narrow, birdlike eyes, while the other sported a goat’s beard.
Otherwise, they were ordinary gamblers of the sort one could find anywhere.
As they watched Kwak Cheolyung shuffle the bone tiles again, the goat-bearded man asked, “But what happened to him?”
It was a fair question.
Kwak Cheolyung looked dreadful.
His face was haggard, and his beard had gone untrimmed.
His silk clothes were black with grime and torn in several places.
They said he had spent his entire life moving from one gambling table to another, amassing an enormous fortune along the way.
Now, however, he looked like nothing more or less than a gambler who had lost everything.
“Did something happen?”
“It did.
Something serious.”
The narrow-eyed man nodded.
Unlike the goat-bearded man, who had arrived in Henan late, he knew exactly what had happened to Kwak Cheolyung recently.
“What was it?
Don’t keep me in suspense.
Tell me.”
“He lost a bet.”
“Winning and losing are common in this business, aren’t they?”
“They are.
But what if a thousand silver nyang were at stake?”
“Gasp!
A thousand silver nyang!”
The goat-bearded man’s eyes widened.
That was enough money for someone to live in luxury for the rest of his life—no, enough for three generations to live like kings.
Regretting that he had missed such a massive game, he smacked his lips and asked, “It must have been the biggest wager since the founding of the country.
Who was his opponent?
A-Gwi?
Or Jjak-Gwi?”
“My friend, I already knew you were hard of hearing, but you’re completely out of touch with recent news.
A-Gwi had his wrist cut off by a fellow called the Mount Qingcheng Guillotine a couple of months ago, and Jjak-Gwi disappeared long ago.”
“Then who besides those two could possibly have beaten Kwak Cheolyung?”
“The Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi.”
“Who?”
“Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
The Fire King’s disciple.”
The Fire King was one of the Ten Kings and a Supreme Peak master whose reputation resounded throughout the world.
There was no reason for such a man’s disciple to gamble with a Dogon.
The goat-bearded man thought for a moment before crying out as if in a groan.
“Dodo!
He played Dodo at the Star-Array Grand Banquet.”
“Correct.”
The Star-Array Grand Banquet’s betting games were considered the greatest gambling matches anywhere under heaven, and were therefore called Dodo.
At last, the goat-bearded man understood what had happened and clicked his tongue.
“Tsk, tsk.
Kwak Cheolyung did something stupid.
The odds on the preliminaries may have been high, but he should have realized that meant the risk was high, too.”
“Do you think he bet without thinking?
He must have had his reasons for being confident.”
“What did he bet on, and against whom?”
“The Iron-Water Divine Dragon taking first place in the preliminaries.”
“I suppose he’s strong, being the Seafaring King’s disciple, but I don’t think he’s quite that good.”
The narrow-eyed man shook his head.
“He seems to have gained some insight recently.
I heard the Iron-Water Divine Dragon blew away a tenth of a cliff with his Ship-Breaking Fist.”
“...Is that even possible?”
The goat-bearded man had heard tales of Murim masters shattering the earth and cleaving the sky, but he had never imagined they were capable of anything like that.
While he was still reeling in astonishment, the narrow-eyed man said something even harder to believe.
“What’s so impossible about it?
Right afterward, the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi brought down the entire cliff.”
The goat-bearded man asked haltingly, his eyes as wide as plates.
“H-He brought down a cliff?”
“That’s right.
According to the witnesses, the whole thing came crashing down.”
The goat-bearded man said nothing.
He merely stared at his friend in disbelief.
“Isn’t that just a wild rumor?”
“Everyone else, myself included, dismissed it as one at first.
A man of flesh and blood bringing down a cliff with his bare hands?
It didn’t seem possible.”
“Exactly.”
“But what can we do when it’s true?
Kwak Cheolyung sitting over there is living proof.”
“Why would Kwak Cheolyung be proof...?
Ah.
He must have lost a thousand silver nyang.”
“Five thousand.”
“What?”
“What do you think it feels like to lose money in a game you were certain you’d win?”
“C-Could it be...?”
“Is Kwak Cheolyung any different from the rest of us?
In the end, he’s just as addicted to gambling.”
The narrow-eyed man looked at Kwak Cheolyung with pity.
The disheveled man was staring blankly at the tiles in his hand.
“Three days ago, when the Iron-Water Divine Dragon withdrew from the Star-Array Grand Banquet and returned to the Yangtze, Kwak Cheolyung completely lost his mind.”
“Did he keep playing Dodo?”
The narrow-eyed man nodded.
“After the Iron-Water Divine Dragon, Kwak Cheolyung chose Jong Sam of the Hunroe Leg.
He bet on him receiving the highest score in the leg-technique assessment.”
“That Peak master who was said to have no equal in kicks throughout Guangxi?”
“Yes.
Though by now, he probably has quite a few equals.
One of his legs was broken.”
“Don’t tell me the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi did that, too.”
“Are you starting to understand?
That’s right.
The two of them got into a minor dispute and agreed to exchange one clean blow each before calling it even.
But one kick from the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi supposedly broke Jong Sam’s shin.”
“H-How?”
“I don’t know.
They say he gave it a casual kick, and the shin snapped with a crunch.”
“The Hunroe Leg even struck first, but the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi just scratched his calf a few times afterward, and that was it.
And next was probably...”
The stories that continued to pour from the narrow-eyed man’s mouth about the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi were nothing short of shocking.

The Kunlun Sect’s Kunlun Cloud Dragon, said to possess the finest qinggong among all the young prodigies under heaven, leaped five jang from a standing position—only to come crashing down with Jin Taekyung’s foot planted on his face.
The Beggars’ Sect’s Successor Beggar flew into a rage when he could not close the distance between himself and Jin Taekyung during the movement-technique assessment.
Unable to contain his anger, he grabbed Taekyung by the back of the neck and was promptly beaten like a dog.
“The fifth assessment was mechanisms and formations.
This time, everyone was certain the Zhuge Clan’s Lesser Family Head would take first place, but...”
The goat-bearded man, who had been listening with a vacant expression, cut him off.
“It was the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi again, wasn’t it?”
“Exactly.”
“But seriously, how?
What kind of freak is proficient in mechanisms and formations, too?”
“He isn’t.
He’s just proficient in martial arts.
The ignorant bastard had no idea what anything was, so he smashed everything in his path and forced his way through.”
“Anyway, the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi took first place in the preliminaries, and Kwak Cheolyung, who bet on someone different every time, was left completely penniless.
I heard he sank all the money he’d earned into it, then even mortgaged the estate and land where he’d planned to retire to borrow from loan sharks...
Tsk, tsk.”
The narrow-eyed man gazed at Kwak Cheolyung with sympathy.
Only a few silver nyang sat before the legendary Dogon who had once amassed a tremendous fortune.
They were probably all he had left in the world.
“Whether you earn it or lose it, it all happens in one shot.
Isn’t that right?”
Only then did the goat-bearded man come to his senses.
He licked his parched lips.
“Five thousand silver nyang.
Whoever won that must have hit the jackpot.”
“He certainly struck it rich.
Why else would they call him the Gold-Faced Young Master?”
“The Gold-Faced Young Master?
Did he bet on the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi?”
The narrow-eyed man nodded.
“He has incredible foresight.
He must have won tens of thousands of silver nyang from this Dodo alone.
Why else would he go around wearing a mask made of gold?”
“Good heavens.”
“They say he hasn’t even turned thirty yet...
I suppose some men are simply destined to succeed.”
“Damn it.
Some of us have reached this age without even owning a proper house.
Hoo...”
The two men let out a deep sigh.
Then a chair scraped across the floor as someone rose to his feet.
Kwak Cheolyung staggered out of the gambling den.
All he held were a few iron coins he had received as a consolation handout.
The Star-Array Grand Banquet was a long race, lasting at least half a month and sometimes as long as a full month.
After the three-day preliminary assessments ended, the applicants were given a day of free time.
That included me.
“Ahem.
Ahehem!”
“Youngest!
Youngest!”
“Captain!
Captaiiin!”
“...Oh, please.”
Don’t.
Don’t shout in a place this crowded.
I’m already dying from all the attention, and now you’re making even more people stare.
Tap-tap-tap-tap!
I hurried toward my companions as quickly as I could.
As though he had been waiting for me, Jin Wikyung’s bear-like bulk charged forward with both arms spread wide.
“Youngest!
My wonderful little brother!”
Whoosh!
Grab!
The moment his bear paw locked around my upper body, Hyuk Mujin seized the back of my hand and rubbed his cheek against it.
“Ohhh, Captain!
Top scorer in the Star-Array Grand Banquet preliminaries!
The pride of the Jin Family of Taiyuan!
The beacon of Shanxi Province!
Our Captain!
My lord!”
Jin Wikyung is my brother, so I’ll let it slide.
But what the hell is wrong with Hyuk Mujin?
Doing my best to hide my bewilderment, I asked, “Are you out of your mind?”
“Yes.
I’m insane!
Your strength has driven me mad!”
“Are you seriously crazy?
Let go.
Let go already!”
Whack!
Whack!
Whack!
Even after I struck the crown of his head three times at lightning speed, Hyuk Mujin refused to budge.
Tears welled in his eyes from the pain, but he still would not release my hand.
“Thank you!
Thank you for hitting me!”
“...Are you into that kind of thing?”
I had only heard rumors about people who took pleasure in being hit.
I had always wondered why he had never left despite the countless beatings I had given him.
Now that I considered the possibility that he was one of those people, a chill ran down my spine.
“Respect-Your-Preferences Fist!”
Thump!
The blow landed squarely on Hyuk Mujin’s temple, and he collapsed to the ground.
At the same time, something bright and glittering slipped from inside his robes and landed on the floor.
“Huh?
A gold mask?”
What is this now?
Is it a prop for that kind of play?
With a grave expression, I tucked the mask into my robes.
Hyuk Mujin, you dangerous bastard.
This mask is confiscated for life.
Not a chance.
As I steeled my resolve, I noticed someone I had momentarily forgotten.
“Ahem.
Ahehem!”
“Do you have a throat problem?”
Jeok Cheongang, who had been staring off at a distant mountain and repeatedly clearing his throat, flinched.
“W-What nonsense are you spouting?”
“You’ve been coughing this whole time.”
“Ahem!”
He kept looking away, clearly wanting to say something but pretending otherwise.
The corners of my mouth rose on their own.
“I did well, didn’t I?”
“Perfect scores in all five assessments.
Unanimous first place overall.
That pretty much says it all, doesn’t it?”
“Ahem.
Don’t get so pleased with yourself over something so trivial.
Anyone could have done it, so stop making a fuss.”
“I heard it was the first time in the history of the Star-Array Grand Banquet.”
“These were merely the preliminaries.
Have you forgotten what this old man told you?
The world is vast, and there are many masters.”
“I beat three of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes.”
The Iron-Water Divine Dragon of the Yangtze River Channel League.
The Kunlun Cloud Dragon of the Kunlun Sect.
And finally, the Divine Marvel Dragon of the Zhuge Clan.
The Beggars’ Sect’s Successor Beggar was a master comparable to them, and the Hunroe Leg was a Peak master who had already made a brilliant name for himself throughout Guangxi.
Their backgrounds and specialties were all different, but the five of them now had one thing in common.
“I beat every last one of them.”
“That...”
For a moment, Jeok Cheongang was at a loss for words.
Then he shook his head again and again.
“Bah.
Pathetic weaklings.”
“I’m the strong one.”
“There you go, acting cocky again.”
“Could you just tell me I did well?
I brought honor to you—Old Master, no, Master—and to the Fire Gate Clan.”
“You still have a long way to go!”
His words were stern, but the corners of his mouth were twitching.
It was obvious that he was barely holding back laughter.
I would have known that even without the Sound Transmission Jin Wikyung sent me a moment later.
—Don’t let it bother you too much.
It seems he already went and bragged about you to the leadership to his heart’s content.
“Ahem!”
As if he had overheard us, Jeok Cheongang cleared his throat again at the perfect moment.
Forcing a stern expression onto his face, he said, “Do not grow arrogant merely because you defeated a few nobodies.
Compose your body and mind, and prepare for the main event.
Understood?”
He was right.
Only the preliminaries had ended.
The main event, where the true masters would reveal themselves, had not even begun.
Among those who had passed through the sieve of the preliminaries, there were likely quite a few masters comparable to the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes—or even stronger.
I had already spotted several such people while watching the assessments.
The world really is vast.
He was right about that.
Anyone who had concealed their true ability during the preliminaries was not only strong, but clever.
I grinned and gave Jeok Cheongang a fist-and-palm salute.
“I’ll keep that in mind, Master.”
“That boy.
Ha ha.
Ahem!”
An unmistakable smile appeared at the wrinkled corners of Jeok Cheongang’s mouth.

chapters.title: Chapter 248
paragraphs: Hong Dao, the Dharma King, sat dozing in the main hall when his eyes suddenly opened.
The first thing he saw upon waking was the small back of someone standing motionless, gazing up at the Buddha statue.
“When did you get here?”
“About fifteen minutes ago, I suppose.”
“So, did you go see your proud Disciple?”
Jeok Cheongang answered gruffly without turning around.
“What Disciple? How many times do I have to tell you? He isn’t.”
“Oh, so you are proud of him.”
“Ahem. Of course he should be able to manage at least that much. What’s so special about the Star-Array Grand Banquet preliminaries?”
“You’ve never done anything like that yourself.”
“There was nothing like this in my day. Back then, even the orthodox factions were busy fighting among themselves, going on about the Southern Murim and Northern Murim.”
“That’s true.”
Hong Dao stretched. Cracks echoed from all over his body.
“Still, this is enough to make a ghost wail. I didn’t sense your presence at all. Have you grown even stronger since I last saw you?”
“Why would a ghost wail? Buddha should be furious. The Abbot of Shaolin is dozing in the main hall like a sick chicken.”
“Don’t be so hard on me. We’re growing old together.”
Jeok Cheongang turned around and shouted.
“Who says I’m old? You should have kept up with your martial-arts training. Look at me. Don’t I look spry enough to last another ten years?”
Hong Dao studied Jeok Cheongang, then rolled his prayer beads between his fingers.
“Benefactor Jeok. May you be reborn in the Pure Land.”
“Look at this damn bald monk!”
Hong Dao let out a quiet laugh at his old friend’s reaction.
“I don’t know about ten years, but you should be fine for another three.”
“Was that the heavenly patterns or whatever telling you?”
“The heavenly patterns? According to what this poor monk saw long ago, you should have died years ago.”
“What?”
Jeok Cheongang’s face hardened. He could tell from Hong Dao’s expression and manner that he was serious.
“Why didn’t you tell me sooner?”
“Because the flow changed.”
“The flow changed?”
“The heavens are vast, yet ever-changing. Just as your star was beginning to lose its light, a Morning Star rose in the northern lands.”
“...Jin Taekyung. So it was that boy.”
“The heavenly patterns told this poor monk that the Fire King stood in the Morning Star’s path. I have watched for the past year, and so it proved. Your star now shines brighter than ever.”
Everything that had happened flashed through Jeok Cheongang’s mind.
He had grown old and suffered from the infirmities of old age. He had begun searching for Jangcheon, whom he had sent away long ago, so he could settle his final affairs before leaving this world.
He had intended to deal with his former Disciple—who might still be committing evil somewhere in the world—with his own hands, then entrust the Fire Gate Clan’s future to the Sword Saint of Huashan.
And then...
I met him.
The infirmities of old age were both the curse of passing years and an illness of the heart.
When Jeok Cheongang was about to let go of the word life, a hand named Jin Taekyung reached out and caught it.
And so Jeok Cheongang changed.
The more he watched that talkative, reckless boy, the more the ember lingering in a corner of his heart flared back to life.
Longer. I want to live longer.
To do that, he had to free himself from the infirmities of old age that gnawed at his mind with every passing moment.
Over the past year, he had immersed himself more deeply in martial arts. He learned while teaching, and gained insight through contemplation.
Jin Taekyung was not the only one who had grown in the Fire Gate Cavern. Jeok Cheongang had taken another step forward as well.
“Three years...”
Jeok Cheongang’s low voice echoed through the main hall.
“I’ll turn those three years into ten soon enough. No, a hundred.”
Hong Dao burst into hearty laughter.
“That’s excessive greed. How long exactly do you intend to live?”
“I don’t know. I’ll somehow keep dragging myself along and live.”
“You’d have to undergo Bone Transformation about three times.”
“Damn it. Then I’ll just have to settle for ten years. So you hang on until then, too. You still need to show that you’re going strong.”
Hong Dao silently rolled his prayer beads.

“We are already waves that have flowed past. The Spear King, who was once so robust, and the Wave King, who was more spirited than anyone, have already left this world. The others have grown old enough, too. Someone whose whereabouts are unknown may already be dead.”
The Ten Kings was the name given to the ten Supreme Peak masters who had swept across the Murim during the Great Faction War.
Some had been worn away by time. Others had died at the hands of their enemies.
Though they were called the Ten Kings, there were only eight in reality, and they were now old enough to prepare for death.
Jeok Cheongang let out a low groan, then suddenly shouted.
“Enough of that defeatist talk! What’s with all this gloom?”
But Hong Dao opened his mouth with a peaceful expression.
“Unnamed. I entrusted him with the Green Jade Buddha Staff last night.”
“By the time he finishes his preparations in Arhat Cave and emerges, he should have grown into a worthy vessel. I have already chosen someone to serve as Abbot until then.”
“W-What did you say?”
Jeok Cheongang found himself stammering.
The Green Jade Buddha Staff was a sacred treasure handed down through Shaolin for a thousand years. Hong Dao had not only entrusted such a treasure to his Disciple—he had even chosen the next Abbot.
To Jeok Cheongang, Hong Dao looked like a man preparing to lay everything down and leave.
“You bald monk. Are you, by any chance...”
Jeok Cheongang let the end of his sentence trail off, but what he meant to say was easy enough to guess.
A faint smile touched Hong Dao’s lips.
“This poor monk intends to step down after this Star-Array Grand Banquet. If the heavens permit it, I may cling to life for another year or so. But no longer than that.”
“The heavenly patterns... Is that what they told you?”
“I need to rest. Please leave for today.”
“Hong Dao!”
“Amitabha.”
Hong Dao picked up his wooden fish and began striking it. The clear notes echoed through the main hall, silencing Jeok Cheongang. Only after a long while did he finally turn and leave.
The three days of preliminary assessments had done their job admirably.
Of the more than fifty thousand applicants, only 1 percent—barely five hundred people—had earned the right to advance to the main event.
The organizers gathered them all in one place.
Naturally, I was among them.
“Look over there. It’s Jin Taekyung, the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi.”
“What? That greenhorn? He looks younger than my youngest Junior Brother.”
“What does age matter? Martial talent is what counts. Still, he’s incredible. He’s come this far after becoming the Fire King’s Disciple only a year ago...”
“For fuck’s sake. Is he supposed to have a Heavenly Martial Physique or something?”
I turned toward the voice. A man who looked to be in his early thirties flinched, then quietly avoided my gaze.
He must have thought I was going to say something to him, but he had read me completely wrong.
The guy’s got good instincts.

The System’s possibilities were endless. My Muscles and Bones, which had already been so exceptional that Jeok Cheongang called them the Heavenly Martial Physique, had developed even further during my training on Mount Jiuhua.
Eventually, even Jeok Cheongang had shaken his head again and again.
“Monster. Just how much higher do you intend to climb?”
“I should at least see how far I can go.”
“If this old man had possessed even half your Muscles and Bones, there would be Two Gods in the martial world by now instead of One God.”
“But you don’t.”
“...Add another hundred geun to the iron ball.”
Acting cocky had only made me suffer more, but in the end, every bit of it had helped me immensely.
After all, hard work—no, the System—never betrayed me.
The System paid out points and EXP with perfect precision, and my basic stats were absurdly high, so any martial art I used was several times more effective.
That was how I managed to beat three of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes, each among the best in their respective fields.
The Iron-Water Divine Dragon of the Yangtze River Channel League had even voluntarily withdrawn from the Star-Array Grand Banquet.
When I asked why he would go that far, he said he couldn’t win as long as I was around, so he might as well hurry home.
I couldn’t decide whether that made him simple or smart, but he was definitely a cool guy.
On the other hand...
“Alas, the martial world’s sense of decency has fallen to the ground. How could such a frivolous and violent man gain power? Oh, heavens!”
“You bastard who’d mix rice with dog shit and eat it. Even leaving you in a cesspit for three months and ten days wouldn’t satisfy me.”
“This is impossible. Are you saying this Young Master’s knowledge is inferior to that man’s martial arts? That cannot be. I must establish a new theory of mechanisms and formations.”
Those three were simply beyond saving.
I had been listening to their endless muttering from behind me when I spun around.
“Hey, you three idiots.”
Their muttering stopped dead at my call.
A moment later, the three idiots snapped their heads up and expressed their anger one after another, each in his own way.
“Alas, an idiot? How vulgar.”
The Daoist in spotless white robes was Baek Woo, the Kunlun Cloud Dragon. I had sent him plummeting during the third assessment by stepping on his face.
I learned later that he had severe cleanliness issues and spent two shichen showering as soon as the assessment ended.
“I’ll stuff shit into your mouth, you bastard.”
Unlike Baek Woo, whose mere presence suggested cleanliness, this man reeked of piss and was a beggar to the bone.
Born and raised in the Beggars’ Sect, he had eventually risen to the position of Successor Beggar—the man who would one day lead the sect.
His name was Gung Gibang.
The so-called Beggar Prince, pure-blooded beggar, ultimate beggar.
During the fourth assessment, Gung Gibang had grabbed me by the back of the neck and been rewarded with a punch to the solar plexus.
“Idiot? Was that directed at this Young Master? If you could explain what you intended by it—and, assuming you know the exact meaning of the word idiot, define it for me—I would appreciate it.”
The last was Zhuge Gyun, the Divine Marvel Dragon of the Zhuge Clan.
He wore the neat clothes of a scholar and a tidy hero’s headband. Judging by his clothes alone, he looked like the most sane of the three.

That was only natural, considering he was wedged between a cleanliness-obsessed Daoist who couldn’t stand a single speck of dust on his clothes and a beggar who looked as though he would happily eat filth even if it splashed into his mouth.
But as I had guessed, he was no ordinary eccentric.
He had expressed considerable regret over losing in the mechanisms-and-formations assessment, the fifth one.
Just look at this lineup...
A group more stacked than Manchester United’s squad under Sir Alex Ferguson.
Seeing the three of them lined up together made my breath catch and my vision go dark. I took a moment to compose myself before speaking.
“Shut your mouths, all of you. Stop chattering. You’re driving me crazy.”
“Alas, did you just say ‘shut your mouths’? Fellow Daoist Jin Taekyung, how can every word out of your mouth be so vulgar?”
“A bastard who wouldn’t feel satisfied even after being rolled up in a mat, hung from a post, and beaten with a dog cudgel for forty-five days.”

“‘Shut your mouths. Stop chattering...’ Those are not expressions commonly used in our family. I am personally quite curious, so could you write down some of the words you often use and give me a copy?”
I wanted to beat the crap out of all three of them.
Lamenting the fact that reality wouldn’t allow it, I addressed the three idiots.
“If I meet any of you in a duel, consider yourselves dead.”
As expected, a cudgel was the best medicine for lunatics.
The three idiots clamped their mouths shut and exchanged glances.
Then it happened.
Click. Click.
The sound of something hard striking the floor pierced everyone’s ears.
An old man soon appeared on the dais, one leg fitted with a wooden prosthetic.
“Sorry I’m late. As you can see, my leg’s in this state.”
He grinned, baring yellow teeth, and introduced himself.
“Nice to meet you. I’m Song Ho, the Thousand-Faced Fox.”

When Jeok Cheongang was about to let go of the word life, a hand named Jin Taekyung reached out and caught it.
And so Jeok Cheongang changed.
The more he watched that talkative, reckless boy, the more the ember lingering in a corner of his heart flared back to life.
Longer.
I want to live longer.
To do that, he had to free himself from the infirmities of old age that gnawed at his mind with every passing moment.
Over the past year, he had immersed himself more deeply in martial arts.
He learned while teaching, and gained insight through contemplation.
Jin Taekyung was not the only one who had grown in the Fire Gate Cavern.
Jeok Cheongang had taken another step forward as well.
“Three years...”
Jeok Cheongang’s low voice echoed through the main hall.
“I’ll turn those three years into ten soon enough.
No, a hundred.”
Hong Dao burst into hearty laughter.
“That’s excessive greed.
How long exactly do you intend to live?”
“I don’t know.
I’ll somehow keep dragging myself along and live.”
“You’d have to undergo Bone Transformation about three times.”
“Damn it.
Then I’ll just have to settle for ten years.
So you hang on until then, too.
You still need to show that you’re going strong.”
Hong Dao silently rolled his prayer beads.
“We are already waves that have flowed past.
The Spear King, who was once so robust, and the Wave King, who was more spirited than anyone, have already left this world.
The others have grown old enough, too.
Someone whose whereabouts are unknown may already be dead.”
The Ten Kings was the name given to the ten Supreme Peak masters who had swept across the Murim during the Great Faction War.
Some had been worn away by time.
Others had died at the hands of their enemies.
Though they were called the Ten Kings, there were only eight in reality, and they were now old enough to prepare for death.
Jeok Cheongang let out a low groan, then suddenly shouted.
“Enough of that defeatist talk!
What’s with all this gloom?”
But Hong Dao opened his mouth with a peaceful expression.
“Unnamed.
I entrusted him with the Green Jade Buddha Staff last night.”
“By the time he finishes his preparations in Arhat Cave and emerges, he should have grown into a worthy vessel.
I have already chosen someone to serve as Abbot until then.”
“W-What did you say?”
Jeok Cheongang found himself stammering.
The Green Jade Buddha Staff was a sacred treasure handed down through Shaolin for a thousand years.
Hong Dao had not only entrusted such a treasure to his Disciple—he had even chosen the next Abbot.
To Jeok Cheongang, Hong Dao looked like a man preparing to lay everything down and leave.
“You bald monk.
Are you, by any chance...”
Jeok Cheongang let the end of his sentence trail off, but what he meant to say was easy enough to guess.
A faint smile touched Hong Dao’s lips.
“This poor monk intends to step down after this Star-Array Grand Banquet.
If the heavens permit it, I may cling to life for another year or so.
But no longer than that.”
“The heavenly patterns...
Is that what they told you?”
“I need to rest.
Please leave for today.”
“Hong Dao!”
“Amitabha.”
Hong Dao picked up his wooden fish and began striking it.
The clear notes echoed through the main hall, silencing Jeok Cheongang.
Only after a long while did he finally turn and leave.
The three days of preliminary assessments had done their job admirably.
Of the more than fifty thousand applicants, only 1 percent—barely five hundred people—had earned the right to advance to the main event.
The organizers gathered them all in one place.
Naturally, I was among them.
“Look over there.
It’s Jin Taekyung, the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi.”
“What?
That greenhorn?
He looks younger than my youngest Junior Brother.”
“What does age matter?
Martial talent is what counts.
Still, he’s incredible.
He’s come this far after becoming the Fire King’s Disciple only a year ago...”
“For fuck’s sake.
Is he supposed to have a Heavenly Martial Physique or something?”
I turned toward the voice.
A man who looked to be in his early thirties flinched, then quietly avoided my gaze.
He must have thought I was going to say something to him, but he had read me completely wrong.
The guy’s got good instincts.
The System’s possibilities were endless.
My Muscles and Bones, which had already been so exceptional that Jeok Cheongang called them the Heavenly Martial Physique, had developed even further during my training on Mount Jiuhua.
Eventually, even Jeok Cheongang had shaken his head again and again.
“Monster.
Just how much higher do you intend to climb?”
“I should at least see how far I can go.”
“If this old man had possessed even half your Muscles and Bones, there would be Two Gods in the martial world by now instead of One God.”
“But you don’t.”
“...Add another hundred geun to the iron ball.”
Acting cocky had only made me suffer more, but in the end, every bit of it had helped me immensely.
After all, hard work—no, the System—never betrayed me.
The System paid out points and EXP with perfect precision, and my basic stats were absurdly high, so any martial art I used was several times more effective.
That was how I managed to beat three of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes, each among the best in their respective fields.
The Iron-Water Divine Dragon of the Yangtze River Channel League had even voluntarily withdrawn from the Star-Array Grand Banquet.
When I asked why he would go that far, he said he couldn’t win as long as I was around, so he might as well hurry home.
I couldn’t decide whether that made him simple or smart, but he was definitely a cool guy.
On the other hand...
“Alas, the martial world’s sense of decency has fallen to the ground.
How could such a frivolous and violent man gain power?
Oh, heavens!”
“You bastard who’d mix rice with dog shit and eat it.
Even leaving you in a cesspit for three months and ten days wouldn’t satisfy me.”
“This is impossible.
Are you saying this Young Master’s knowledge is inferior to that man’s martial arts?
That cannot be.
I must establish a new theory of mechanisms and formations.”
Those three were simply beyond saving.
I had been listening to their endless muttering from behind me when I spun around.
“Hey, you three idiots.”
Their muttering stopped dead at my call.
A moment later, the three idiots snapped their heads up and expressed their anger one after another, each in his own way.
“Alas, an idiot?
How vulgar.”
The Daoist in spotless white robes was Baek Woo, the Kunlun Cloud Dragon.
I had sent him plummeting during the third assessment by stepping on his face.
I learned later that he had severe cleanliness issues and spent two shichen showering as soon as the assessment ended.
“I’ll stuff shit into your mouth, you bastard.”
Unlike Baek Woo, whose mere presence suggested cleanliness, this man reeked of piss and was a beggar to the bone.
Born and raised in the Beggars’ Sect, he had eventually risen to the position of Successor Beggar—the man who would one day lead the sect.
His name was Gung Gibang.
The so-called Beggar Prince, pure-blooded beggar, ultimate beggar.
During the fourth assessment, Gung Gibang had grabbed me by the back of the neck and been rewarded with a punch to the solar plexus.
“Idiot?
Was that directed at this Young Master?
If you could explain what you intended by it—and, assuming you know the exact meaning of the word idiot, define it for me—I would appreciate it.”
The last was Zhuge Gyun, the Divine Marvel Dragon of the Zhuge Clan.
He wore the neat clothes of a scholar and a tidy hero’s headband.
Judging by his clothes alone, he looked like the most sane of the three.

That was only natural, considering he was wedged between a cleanliness-obsessed Daoist who couldn’t stand a single speck of dust on his clothes and a beggar who looked as though he would happily eat filth even if it splashed into his mouth.
But as I had guessed, he was no ordinary eccentric.
He had expressed considerable regret over losing in the mechanisms-and-formations assessment, the fifth one.
Just look at this lineup...
A group more stacked than Manchester United’s squad under Sir Alex Ferguson.
Seeing the three of them lined up together made my breath catch and my vision go dark.
I took a moment to compose myself before speaking.
“Shut your mouths, all of you.
Stop chattering.
You’re driving me crazy.”
“Alas, did you just say ‘shut your mouths’?
Fellow Daoist Jin Taekyung, how can every word out of your mouth be so vulgar?”
“A bastard who wouldn’t feel satisfied even after being rolled up in a mat, hung from a post, and beaten with a dog cudgel for forty-five days.”
“‘Shut your mouths.
Stop chattering...’ Those are not expressions commonly used in our family.
I am personally quite curious, so could you write down some of the words you often use and give me a copy?”
I wanted to beat the crap out of all three of them.
Lamenting the fact that reality wouldn’t allow it, I addressed the three idiots.
“If I meet any of you in a duel, consider yourselves dead.”
As expected, a cudgel was the best medicine for lunatics.
The three idiots clamped their mouths shut and exchanged glances.
Then it happened.
Click.
Click.
The sound of something hard striking the floor pierced everyone’s ears.
An old man soon appeared on the dais, one leg fitted with a wooden prosthetic.
“Sorry I’m late.
As you can see, my leg’s in this state.”
He grinned, baring yellow teeth, and introduced himself.
“Nice to meet you.
I’m Song Ho, the Thousand-Faced Fox.”

chapters.title: Chapter 249
paragraphs: The Thousand-Faced Fox. A fox with a thousand faces.
I had never seen a nickname suit someone so poorly.
Song Ho, the old man known as the Thousand-Faced Fox, was bigger than most burly men, with the warm, genial face of the grandfather next door.
He was about as far from a fox as a person could get. If anything, he seemed like the exact opposite.
He looks like that grandpa. The one who stands outside the chicken shop whether it rains or snows.
Put a pair of glasses on him, and they could have been twins.
But while I entertained such carefree thoughts, the air around me was taut as a drawn bowstring.
Faces were tense. I could hear people swallowing nervously.
The Thousand-Faced Fox...
He couldn’t have gotten that nickname for nothing.
Once I changed my perspective, everything began to look different.
The aura I sensed from Song Ho was that of a Peak master—nothing more, nothing less—but there was something else about him.
Something unrelated to martial arts. Something only he possessed.
What is it?
As I studied Song Ho’s profile, his head turned, and our gazes met.
He beckoned me over, so I took a step toward him.
“So you’re the one?”
“Pardon?”
“Jin Taekyung, the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi. I’ve heard plenty about how the Disciple of Great Hero Jeok Cheongang, the Fire King, performed exceptionally well in the preliminaries.”
Judging by the way he spoke, he seemed to have known Jeok Cheongang to some extent. I quickly bowed my head.
“Thank you.”
“And you’re also the reason there are so many more finalists in this Star-Array Grand Banquet.”
I had heard plenty of things said about me, but this was a first.
I tilted my head. “Because of me?”
“Of course.”
A deep smile spread across Song Ho’s lips.
“Aren’t you the one who destroyed every mechanism and formation we installed for the final assessment?”
“Oh.”
“Thanks to you, there must be a hundred more qualifiers. Once you destroyed the core, everyone else had a much easier time passing.”
That happened?
Come to think of it, everyone had seemed to clear the assessment unusually quickly.
At the time, I had simply assumed the locals knew all about mechanisms and formations, unlike a foreigner like me.
“Judging by your expression, you had no idea.”
“Yeah, well. I’m completely clueless when it comes to that stuff.”
“Don’t you regret it?”
“Regret what?”
“Destroying the core of the mechanisms and formations. There could have been far fewer competitors than there are now.”
“Four hundred or five hundred—what’s the difference?”
“‘What’s the difference,’ you say...”
At my breezy answer, Song Ho pointed behind me.
“It won’t be easy.”
I turned in the direction of his finger.
The martial artists filling the training ground—including the three idiots—were all staring at me.
There were more than five hundred of them.
Every single one was either a Supreme First Rate martial artist recognized anywhere under heaven or a Peak master.
Some were scions of prestigious families who had learned martial arts with every possible advantage. Others were wandering martial artists whose bodies bore countless scars like medals.
That is a lot.
But it didn’t matter. Four hundred, five hundred, even a thousand—my answer would remain the same.
I looked at Song Ho and slowly spoke.
“It doesn’t matter. All I have to do is win.”
“What? Ha! Hahaha!”
Damn, that was embarrassing now that I’d actually said it.
Song Ho must have loved my answer, because he burst into laughter. At the same time, though, I had drawn plenty of aggro.
I scratched the back of my head, which was beginning to prickle.
They’re all thinking the same thing, so why pretend otherwise?
Everyone had come to the Star-Array Grand Banquet with a single goal: victory.
At this point, pretending otherwise would have been more ridiculous.
“You’re an interesting young friend. Great Hero Jeok really raised quite the man.”
Song Ho patted me on the shoulder and laughed with satisfaction.
Just then, a middle-aged supervisor who had been about to climb onto the dais spotted him and stopped short.
“Is that you, Sir Song? What brings you here...”
Song Ho’s hand fell from my shoulder.
“I heard the qualifiers had arrived, so I stopped by to see their faces. Aren’t they future pillars of the world?”
He swept a pleased gaze over the crowd, then turned away.
“Then this old relic will take his leave. It was a pleasure, everyone.”
I didn’t answer.
It had lasted only an instant, but I had definitely seen it.
His eyes had narrowed like those of a fox stalking its prey, his gaze suddenly razor-sharp.
The Thousand-Faced Fox.
I was beginning to understand why that genial-looking old man had been given such a nickname.
Where was he looking?
And who had he seen? What had he seen in them?
That gaze had flashed past in an instant, but it had certainly not been the gaze of a Senior surveying juniors far beneath him.
I was quickly scanning everyone’s faces when—
“Hey! Friend!”
At first, I wondered what kind of lunatic was shouting.
A booming voice rang through the quiet training ground as someone waved enthusiastically.
I recognized his face from somewhere and let out a deep sigh.
What? That bastard passed too?
The Always-Victorious Sword, Jongni Chu.
The sight of his beaming smile made my curiosity vanish in an instant.
“All qualifiers, follow me.”
I had no idea how long we walked behind the middle-aged supervisor before we arrived at a long line of carriages stretching into the distance.
“Wait. Where are we going?”
I didn’t know who had asked, but whoever it was must have been getting dirty looks from everyone around him.
The schedule following the preliminaries had already been explained several times.
The middle-aged supervisor answered curtly.
“Luoyang.”
The Star-Array Grand Banquet’s preliminaries had been held on Mount Song with outsiders barred from entering, but the main event would take place in Luoyang, with a different format.
I had heard that spectator stands had even been prepared so people could watch the duels.
That was probably why the main event was called the true beginning of the Star-Array Grand Banquet.
“Everyone, board the carriages. It isn’t far, so we’ll arrive soon.”
Clip-clop-clop!
The instant the carriage doors closed, the horses’ hooves pounded against the ground.
I gazed out the window at Mount Song receding into the distance.
Three days of beautiful memories...
I wish that had been the reason.
The truth was that I simply didn’t want to look at the faces of the idiots riding with me.
“It’s been a while. Have you been well?”
“Fuck off. Don’t talk to me.”
Jongni Chu started us off lightly.
But it was too soon to relax. The war had only just begun.
“Good heavens, gentlemen. Did you hear what that Fellow Daoist just said? ‘Fuck off’! What is he, some common street thug? How vulgar and undignified...”
It was Baek Woo, the Kunlun Cloud Dragon and one of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes.
Without taking my eyes off the window, I said, “Shut your mouth. I won’t say it twice. And this ‘Fellow Daoist’ shit—I’ll turn you into cheese crust with the Flame Divine Palm.”
“What? ‘Shit’? You were speaking to this poor Daoist?”
“Yep.”
“You seem awfully high and mighty just because you happened to get ahead of me once in qinggong...”
“Hey, you.”
I turned my head and stared at Baek Woo.
“I told you to shut up.”
Our gazes collided in midair. A brief silence passed, and we both reached out at the same time.
No—Baek Woo was half a beat faster. He made the first move.
Whoosh! Rattle-rattle-rattle!
And then it was over in an instant.
Baek Woo’s eyes widened as I immobilized both his wrists.
“S-Striking Second, Hitting First?”
“Trying to get the first hit in, you bastard?”
What mattered in a fight was not who moved faster.
The result. The result was all that mattered.
I had definitely started later than Baek Woo, but I reached my target faster. That was all there was to it.
“Your grappling technique is a mess. Did you put everything into qinggong?”
“H-How did you...”
“What do you mean, how? You’re weaker than me, and I’m stronger than you.”
I grinned at his stunned face and continued.
“Now, you have three choices. Number one: take one hard hit from the Flame Divine Palm right now.”

“Judging by your expression, you don’t like that one. Number two: take a gentle hit from the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist. For reference, I brought down a cliff with it. If you think your body is tougher than a cliff, go ahead and try your luck.”
“I-Is there no third option?”
“‘Is there no’? What’s with that formal -so ending? You’re using haoche. Are you from the Lower District Sect? I thought you were from the Kunlun Sect.”
Baek Woo bit down hard on his lip.
“I-I am twenty-six this year. Four years older than you.”
“Oh, four years. Then would you rather take four Flame Divine Palms?”
“Gasp!”
Baek Woo shook his head vigorously.
“All right. Say it again.”
“Is there no third option...please?”
“There is. Number three: keep your mouth shut in front of me from now on.”
“I’ll take that one!”
“Good. Let’s travel in silence.”
I released Baek Woo’s wrists.
Conflict flickered in his eyes, but his face soon fell, and he lowered his head.
Unless he was exceptionally stupid and shameless, that was the obvious response.
That takes care of one, at least.
I looked over the others in turn.
Jongni Chu stared wide-eyed between Baek Woo and me.
Gung Gibang stopped scratching his thigh, while Zhuge Gyun closed the book he had been reading so intently.
“Hey. Beggars’ Sect.”
“Does this bastard only open his mouth when he’s talking about shit?”
Gung Gibang was the quietest of the three idiots. Whenever he did speak, it was usually some curse-like remark that began with dog shit, continued through cow shit, and ended with horse shit.
He was filthy beyond belief.
“Anyway, you get a choice too. The same three I gave him. You heard them, right?”
Gung Gibang nodded, his matted hair bobbing up and down.
“Pick quickly. I can’t be bothered waiting.”
After remaining silent for a while, Gung Gibang finally opened his mouth.
“The Beggars’ Sect’s Eighteen Dragon-Subduing Palms is one of the five greatest martial arts under heaven. Anyone who masters even eight-tenths of it will have few rivals in the world.”
“So?”
“Unfortunately, I have only mastered five-tenths of the Eighteen Dragon-Subduing Palms.”
Gung Gibang continued, his eyes shining with determination.
“Therefore, I choose number three.”
I almost smacked him across the head, but stopped myself. Hitting him would probably only dirty my hand.
“Then keep your mouth shut from now on, Gibang. And make sure you speak politely.”
“G-Gibang? Politely?”
“Might Makes Right. Haven’t you heard of it?”
“Even so, that’s a bit...”
“Oh, right. You’re twenty-six too, aren’t you? Since you’re four years older than me, would you like four Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fists?”
The wavering light in Gung Gibang’s eyes slowly settled.
He clenched his fists and shook out both hands.
Swish! Clack!
With lightning-fast movements, Gung Gibang formed a fist-and-palm salute and bowed his head.
“From now on, I shall call you Jin hyung.”
“Good.”
Having neatly dealt with two of them, I turned toward the last idiot.
Zhuge Gyun had closed his book and was stroking a spotless white fan made from crane feathers.
“Galgyun.”
“My surname is Zhuge. My given name is Gyun.”
“Right. Galgyun. You’ve already chosen, haven’t you?”
“Choosing is difficult.”
“If you still haven’t decided after watching the two Seniors in front of you, then you’ll end up a corpse.”
Zhuge Gyun regarded me calmly.
“My honored ancestor, Zhuge Wuhou, decided to enter public service only after Liu Bei’s Three Visits to the Thatched Cottage.”
“What the hell? I told you to give me a number, and this lunatic starts talking about Romance of the Three Kingdoms. So what am I supposed to do?”
“Three Visits to the Thatched Cottage. Since Wuhou opened his heart after three visits, this Young Master chooses option three.”
As expected of the Zhuge Clan.
Just look at that strategic buildup. He had even dragged his ancestor into it.
Maybe I should turn that crane-feather fan into a blood-feather fan.
Only one person remained, but Jongni Chu gave a sheepish laugh and raised both hands in surrender.
“How frightening. I’ll keep my mouth shut for the entire journey.”
“Don’t keep pestering me. Understood?”
“I understand. If that is what you want, so be it.”
I had no particular grudge against Jongni Chu, so I decided to leave it at that.
Just as I began enjoying the peace I had won by subduing the three idiots, the speeding carriage slowed and soon came to a stop.
“We have arrived at our destination.”
I looked out the window.
Lofty walls dozens of jang high. A massive iron gate. And a signboard bathed in the soft glow of sunset.
Murim Alliance

“I told you to shut up.”
Our gazes collided in midair.
A brief silence passed, and we both reached out at the same time.
No—Baek Woo was half a beat faster.
He made the first move.
Whoosh!
Rattle-rattle-rattle!
And then it was over in an instant.
Baek Woo’s eyes widened as I immobilized both his wrists.
“S-Striking Second, Hitting First?”
“Trying to get the first hit in, you bastard?”
What mattered in a fight was not who moved faster.
The result.
The result was all that mattered.
I had definitely started later than Baek Woo, but I reached my target faster.
That was all there was to it.
“Your grappling technique is a mess.
Did you put everything into qinggong?”
“H-How did you...”
“What do you mean, how?
You’re weaker than me, and I’m stronger than you.”
I grinned at his stunned face and continued.
“Now, you have three choices.
Number one: take one hard hit from the Flame Divine Palm right now.”
“Judging by your expression, you don’t like that one.
Number two: take a gentle hit from the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist.
For reference, I brought down a cliff with it.
If you think your body is tougher than a cliff, go ahead and try your luck.”
“I-Is there no third option?”
“‘Is there no’?
What’s with that formal -so ending?
You’re using haoche.
Are you from the Lower District Sect?
I thought you were from the Kunlun Sect.”
Baek Woo bit down hard on his lip.
“I-I am twenty-six this year.
Four years older than you.”
“Oh, four years.
Then would you rather take four Flame Divine Palms?”
“Gasp!”
Baek Woo shook his head vigorously.
“All right.
Say it again.”
“Is there no third option...please?”
“There is.
Number three: keep your mouth shut in front of me from now on.”
“I’ll take that one!”
“Good.
Let’s travel in silence.”
I released Baek Woo’s wrists.
Conflict flickered in his eyes, but his face soon fell, and he lowered his head.
Unless he was exceptionally stupid and shameless, that was the obvious response.
That takes care of one, at least.
I looked over the others in turn.
Jongni Chu stared wide-eyed between Baek Woo and me.
Gung Gibang stopped scratching his thigh, while Zhuge Gyun closed the book he had been reading so intently.
“Hey.
Beggars’ Sect.”
“Does this bastard only open his mouth when he’s talking about shit?”
Gung Gibang was the quietest of the three idiots.
Whenever he did speak, it was usually some curse-like remark that began with dog shit, continued through cow shit, and ended with horse shit.
He was filthy beyond belief.
“Anyway, you get a choice too.
The same three I gave him.
You heard them, right?”
Gung Gibang nodded, his matted hair bobbing up and down.
“Pick quickly.
I can’t be bothered waiting.”
After remaining silent for a while, Gung Gibang finally opened his mouth.
“The Beggars’ Sect’s Eighteen Dragon-Subduing Palms is one of the five greatest martial arts under heaven.
Anyone who masters even eight-tenths of it will have few rivals in the world.”
“So?”
“Unfortunately, I have only mastered five-tenths of the Eighteen Dragon-Subduing Palms.”
Gung Gibang continued, his eyes shining with determination.
“Therefore, I choose number three.”
I almost smacked him across the head, but stopped myself.
Hitting him would probably only dirty my hand.
“Then keep your mouth shut from now on, Gibang.
And make sure you speak politely.”
“G-Gibang?
Politely?”
“Might Makes Right.
Haven’t you heard of it?”
“Even so, that’s a bit...”
“Oh, right.
You’re twenty-six too, aren’t you?
Since you’re four years older than me, would you like four Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fists?”
The wavering light in Gung Gibang’s eyes slowly settled.
He clenched his fists and shook out both hands.
Swish!
Clack!
With lightning-fast movements, Gung Gibang formed a fist-and-palm salute and bowed his head.
“From now on, I shall call you Jin hyung.”
“Good.”
Having neatly dealt with two of them, I turned toward the last idiot.
Zhuge Gyun had closed his book and was stroking a spotless white fan made from crane feathers.
“Galgyun.”
“My surname is Zhuge.
My given name is Gyun.”
“Right.
Galgyun.
You’ve already chosen, haven’t you?”
“Choosing is difficult.”
“If you still haven’t decided after watching the two Seniors in front of you, then you’ll end up a corpse.”
Zhuge Gyun regarded me calmly.
“My honored ancestor, Zhuge Wuhou, decided to enter public service only after Liu Bei’s Three Visits to the Thatched Cottage.”
“What the hell?
I told you to give me a number, and this lunatic starts talking about Romance of the Three Kingdoms.
So what am I supposed to do?”
“Three Visits to the Thatched Cottage.
Since Wuhou opened his heart after three visits, this Young Master chooses option three.”
As expected of the Zhuge Clan.
Just look at that strategic buildup.
He had even dragged his ancestor into it.
Maybe I should turn that crane-feather fan into a blood-feather fan.
Only one person remained, but Jongni Chu gave a sheepish laugh and raised both hands in surrender.
“How frightening.
I’ll keep my mouth shut for the entire journey.”
“Don’t keep pestering me.
Understood?”
“I understand.
If that is what you want, so be it.”
I had no particular grudge against Jongni Chu, so I decided to leave it at that.
Just as I began enjoying the peace I had won by subduing the three idiots, the speeding carriage slowed and soon came to a stop.
“We have arrived at our destination.”
I looked out the window.
Lofty walls dozens of jang high.
A massive iron gate.
And a signboard bathed in the soft glow of sunset.
Murim Alliance

chapters.title: Chapter 250
paragraphs: The Demonic Cult.
If they had never existed—if those who called themselves the Heavenly Demon Divine Cult had never appeared—the Murim under heaven would never have united as one.
But when Qinghai, Gansu, and Sichuan fell into the Demonic Cult’s hands in a mere four months, everything changed.

The leaders of countless orthodox factions, including the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families, gathered in one place. Even major figures from the unorthodox factions and dark-path forces, such as the Yangtze River Channel League and the Green Forest Alliance, lent their strength.
And at the center of it all stood the Martial God.
An unparalleled master known as the greatest beneath heaven. An invincible man who belonged to no faction.
Let us raise a single flag. It is the only way.
Thus, after years of joining together and splitting apart, the orthodox factions, unorthodox factions, and dark-path forces united beneath a single flag.
The Murim Alliance was born.

Not long after the fierce ten-year Great War ended, the Murim Alliance was dissolved along with the Martial God’s disappearance. But the site where the heroes of old had once gathered remained, carrying on in a new form with new people.
“Good grief, it’s packed.”
A middle-aged man stared wearily at the long line stretching out in front of the Murim Alliance.
They hadn’t even entered yet, and it was already this crowded. Just imagining the chaos inside was enough to make his vision go dark.
To make matters worse, he still hadn’t recovered from yesterday’s drinking.
“Honey, why don’t we just take a lap around the market and go home? Hm?”
At his desperate whisper, his wife firmly shook her head.
“No. Do you have any idea how excited he is? He’s been begging us for three whole days, ever since the main event began.”

“No, no. It’ll be fine. We can take a lap around the market and put some candy in his mouth. That’ll keep him quiet. To hell with the Star-Array Grand Banquet and all that. What’s so impressive about watching Murim people fight anyway... Huh?”
The middle-aged man sucked in a startled breath.
His son, who had been asleep on his wife’s back, was now awake and staring at him.
The boy’s large eyes were moist, as if he might burst into tears at any moment.
“Dad. Aren’t we going to see the Star-Array Grand Banquet?”
“No, son. That’s not what I—”
“Sniff... Sob...”
“W-Wait. Just hear me out.”
“Waaaaaaah!”
“...My boy sure has a powerful set of lungs.”
A short while later, the child held candy in one hand and a wooden doll the size of an adult’s palm in the other.
The unexpected expense left the middle-aged man grumbling.
“Damn thieves. How can a little chunk of wood cost that much?”
But he was still a parent. The sight of his son’s beaming face eased his irritation a little.
“You like it that much?”
“Yes! Jin Taekyung is so cool! The Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi is the best!”
“Jin Taekyung? The Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi? Is that wooden doll’s name Jin Taekyung?”
“Dad, you don’t know Jin Taekyung?”
“O-Of course I do.”
“Really?”
“Of course. There’s nothing your dad doesn’t know.”
He couldn’t sacrifice his dignity as a father over some wooden doll.

Having narrowly escaped the crisis, the middle-aged man waited until his son was looking away, then quietly asked his wife, “Honey. Who’s Jin Taekyung, the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi? You don’t know either, do you?”
“Why wouldn’t I?”
His wife looked at him as if he were hopeless.
“We came here to watch his duel today.”
“The Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, Jin Taekyung. Hyeok has told you over and over that he’s won three straight duels in the main event... How can a father take so little interest in his own child?”
As his wife continued lecturing him, the middle-aged man had only one thought.
I hope this Sleeping Dragon or whatever gets his ass kicked today.
Whoosh!
I calmly watched the sword sweep toward me.
Fast as an arrow, agile as a snake.
After a bewildering series of forms, red Sword Energy shot toward me.
Shhk-shhk-shhk-shhk!
I flipped through the air. The Sword Energy passed less than half a span from me, and I thrust out my fist.
One punch wreathed in blue flame—the first form of the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist.
Boom!
A powerful collision.
Sword Energy and Fist Energy crashed together, sending a thunderous boom across the arena. Stone dust from the dueling platform billowed up, blocking my view.
I stepped forward.
Again. One more time.
Boom! Kraa-boom!
The shock wave bursting from my fist split the air. The flames of the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist devoured the cloud of dust.
Beyond it stood a man.
Blood trickled from the corner of his mouth, his face deathly pale. He clutched a broken sword and stared at me with wide eyes.
“H-How?”
“Well.”
The moment I answered, I kicked off the ground.
Crack.
As my foot left the ground, spiderweb cracks spread across the solid bluestone. I tore through the fierce wind and threw a third punch at him.
“I surrender!”
The words burst from him like a scream.
My fist stopped directly in front of his nose. The pressure from its tremendous speed and force sent his hair whipping back.
The hero’s headband slipped from his forehead, fluttered out of the arena, and landed with a thud.
“S-Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, victory!”
Waaaaah!
At the referee’s declaration, the cheers the crowd had been holding back erupted from every direction.
Hundreds—thousands—of spectators surged to their feet, throwing flowers and all manner of objects.
“Yeah! Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi!”
“Dad! I can’t see! Put me on your shoulders!”
“You’re the best, you punk! I even bought your wooden doll!”
The stands weren’t filled with martial artists alone. Plenty of ordinary people had come from Henan and even farther away to see the Star-Array Grand Banquet.
I waved to one particularly noisy father and son, then turned away.
Ding.

System You won the duel against Black Water Dart! - An overwhelming victory! Everyone who watched the duel offers unreserved praise! - Your Fame increased by 500! - Your Fame increased by 430! - Your Fame increased by...
I listened to the familiar notifications as I stepped down from the dueling platform. At the same moment, someone landed lightly in front of me using an elegant movement technique.
Tap!
“Good heavens, what are all these specks of dust on your precious body? This poor Daoist will wipe them away for you.”
Damn it. This bastard’s here again.
No matter how many times I told him not to come, he refused to fucking listen. There was no helping him.
I snatched the towel from his hand.
“If you’re going to come, at least walk over like a normal person. Stop using the Cloud-Dragon Eight Forms or Oh Tae-sik or whatever.”
Baek Woo, the Kunlun Cloud Dragon, answered glumly.
“It is the Cloud-Dragon Eight Forms. Even so, it is one of the Kunlun Sect’s secret arts. You could at least remember its name...”
“Right. Imagine how heartbroken your Master would be if he saw you using that secret art to deliver towels. He’s probably watching from the VIP seats right now.”
“My Master told me to get along with Fellow Daoist.”
“I heard Great Hero Jeok Cheongang, the Fire King, once saved my Master’s life...”
No wonder Baek Woo had been so unusually friendly since the day after we arrived.
He must have scampered over to his Master to tattle on me, only to have the whole thing blow up in his face.
Then there were my last three duels—or four, counting the one just now. Watching them must have driven one fact home.
I was far stronger than he was.
The same went for the other two idiots.
“Our sect’s Eighteen Dragon-Subduing Palms is one of the five greatest palm arts beneath heaven.”
“Sure. But you’ve only mastered it to the fifth level, right?”
“That is correct.”
“Is that why you brought that?”
“Yes.”
Gung Gibang approached with a solemn expression, carrying a basin of water for me to wash my face.
The whole thing was absurd, but I thanked him, washed my face, and dried it with the towel Baek Woo had brought.
The Beggars’ Sect’s Successor Beggar had brought me water, and the Kunlun Cloud Dragon, one of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes, had brought me a towel.
To everyone else, this must have looked like a very strange sight.
Wait.
Come to think of it, one of them was missing.
“Where’s Galgyun?”
Normally, he would have rushed over by now and started rambling about his ancestor, Zhuge Wuhou, but he was nowhere to be seen.
Baek Woo answered, “Young Master Zhuge went to fight his duel.”
“No wonder he’s not here.”
There were no fewer than five hundred competitors in the main event, so the duels were held in sequence across several different arenas.
Today was the third day. Once all the scheduled duels ended, only around thirty competitors would remain.
There have been more injuries than I expected.
Every participant was a master with at least one remarkable skill.
Injuries were unavoidable. Some people even won a razor-close duel only to withdraw afterward.
I’m the unusual one.
Counting the victory I had just secured, I had won four duels, and not one had lasted more than fifteen minutes.
The longest had gone for a little over two hundred exchanges, and only because I’d wanted to experience my opponent’s unusual martial art.
I’m glad I entered the Star-Array Grand Banquet.
From what I had seen, some of the competitors possessed a deeper understanding of particular martial arts than I did.
I was simply far superior in several other respects, and facing unfamiliar martial arts I had never encountered before was giving me valuable experience.
I never would’ve gained this kind of experience if I’d stayed in Fire Gate Cavern.
My gaze naturally drifted toward the VIP seats.
Jeok Cheongang was trying his hardest to control his expression, while Jin Wikyung looked so delighted he could barely contain himself.
And beside them...
“That old man’s here again today.”
“Who?”
“Who?”
“The Thousand-Faced Fox, Song Ho. He hasn’t missed a single day.”
Baek Woo and Gung Gibang started to turn, then froze.
“Why? Is he that important?”
“Sir Song?”
“You mean the Thousand-Faced Fox?”
They both asked at once, then lowered their voices.
“He is certainly an impressive man. No—perhaps frightening would be more accurate.”
“The Murim Alliance’s Hidden Shadow Pavilion once possessed an intelligence network that rivaled the Beggars’ Sect’s. It may even have surpassed ours.”
“The Hidden Shadow Pavilion?”
Gung Gibang nodded.

“I heard it performed truly astonishing feats during the Great Faction War. Of course, the Thousand-Faced Fox, who was its head, deserves much of the credit for the Hidden Shadow Pavilion’s existence.”
So in modern terms, was he something like the director of the FBI?
If even the Beggars’ Sect’s Successor Beggar spoke of it that way, the Hidden Shadow Pavilion’s intelligence network must have been extraordinary.
Judging from the past tense, it had probably followed the Murim Alliance into dissolution.
The former head of a retired intelligence organization...
As I watched him closely, Song Ho rose from his seat and disappeared somewhere.
I followed his retreating figure with my eyes until it vanished. Then a roar from the crowd rang in my ears.
“Waaaaah!”
“The Life-Sustaining Sword won again!”
I turned toward the cheers and saw Jongni Chu descending from a dueling platform, his clothes reduced to rags.
His entire body glistened with sweat, and he was gasping for breath.
The two idiots muttered as they watched him.
“Life-Sustaining Sword? Whoever came up with that epithet certainly has a way with names.”
“He does keep scraping out victories by a hair. In that sense, the Always-Victorious Sword truly is always victorious.”
The nickname Life-Sustaining Sword had been given to Jongni Chu because he won every match by barely surviving.
Even I hadn’t expected Jongni Chu to reach four wins, but apparently he was stronger in a real fight than I’d thought.
If he’s made it this far, he must have some skill.
Just how did he fight to earn a name like Life-Sustaining Sword?
A quiet laugh escaped me as I watched Jongni Chu frantically gulp down cold water.
Maybe I’ll meet him on the dueling platform later.
I hadn’t had much contact with Jongni Chu since three days ago. We merely acknowledged each other whenever we happened to cross paths.
If our next meeting was on the dueling platform, I might end up feeling a little sorry for him.
“Anyway, thanks for the towel and the water. You can clean these up while you’re at it.”
Baek Woo and Gung Gibang took the towel and basin respectively, then asked, “Where are you going?”
“Our sect’s Eighteen Dragon-Subduing Palms is one of the most renowned martial arts beneath heaven... Where are you going?”
“To watch Gyun’s duel.”
I had heard Zhuge Gyun practiced an unusual fan technique using a folding fan. I figured I might as well watch his duel and broaden my knowledge of martial arts.
I was about to head toward another dueling platform when I suddenly stopped.
“Oh, right. Who did they say his opponent was?”
The Invincible Divine Sword.
Zhuge Gyun gasped for breath.
When he had first heard his opponent’s epithet, he had laughed inwardly. It was far too grand a name for some unknown nobody with no reputation.
But...
How has someone like this remained unknown until now?
The hand gripping his fan trembled.
His legs had already lost half their strength, and merely staying upright was becoming difficult. His eyes ached from straining to follow sword strikes that moved too quickly to see.
The internal energy in his dantian had run dry long ago.
Zhuge Gyun was one of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes, yet he had been reduced to this state while the Invincible Divine Sword remained utterly at ease.
No—he even seemed excited.
“Wow! You’re the first person I’ve ever seen use a fan technique! Do you have another one? Another one?”
At the innocent voice drifting from beneath the deeply lowered bamboo hat, Zhuge Gyun threw away his fan.

“That old man’s here again today.”
“Who?”
“Who?”
“The Thousand-Faced Fox, Song Ho.
He hasn’t missed a single day.”
Baek Woo and Gung Gibang started to turn, then froze.
“Why?
Is he that important?”
“Sir Song?”
“You mean the Thousand-Faced Fox?”
They both asked at once, then lowered their voices.
“He is certainly an impressive man.
No—perhaps frightening would be more accurate.”
“The Murim Alliance’s Hidden Shadow Pavilion once possessed an intelligence network that rivaled the Beggars’ Sect’s.
It may even have surpassed ours.”
“The Hidden Shadow Pavilion?”
Gung Gibang nodded.
“I heard it performed truly astonishing feats during the Great Faction War.
Of course, the Thousand-Faced Fox, who was its head, deserves much of the credit for the Hidden Shadow Pavilion’s existence.”
So in modern terms, was he something like the director of the FBI?
If even the Beggars’ Sect’s Successor Beggar spoke of it that way, the Hidden Shadow Pavilion’s intelligence network must have been extraordinary.
Judging from the past tense, it had probably followed the Murim Alliance into dissolution.
The former head of a retired intelligence organization...
As I watched him closely, Song Ho rose from his seat and disappeared somewhere.
I followed his retreating figure with my eyes until it vanished.
Then a roar from the crowd rang in my ears.
“Waaaaah!”
“The Life-Sustaining Sword won again!”
I turned toward the cheers and saw Jongni Chu descending from a dueling platform, his clothes reduced to rags.
His entire body glistened with sweat, and he was gasping for breath.
The two idiots muttered as they watched him.
“Life-Sustaining Sword?
Whoever came up with that epithet certainly has a way with names.”
“He does keep scraping out victories by a hair.
In that sense, the Always-Victorious Sword truly is always victorious.”
The nickname Life-Sustaining Sword had been given to Jongni Chu because he won every match by barely surviving.
Even I hadn’t expected Jongni Chu to reach four wins, but apparently he was stronger in a real fight than I’d thought.
If he’s made it this far, he must have some skill.
Just how did he fight to earn a name like Life-Sustaining Sword?
A quiet laugh escaped me as I watched Jongni Chu frantically gulp down cold water.
Maybe I’ll meet him on the dueling platform later.
I hadn’t had much contact with Jongni Chu since three days ago.
We merely acknowledged each other whenever we happened to cross paths.
If our next meeting was on the dueling platform, I might end up feeling a little sorry for him.
“Anyway, thanks for the towel and the water.
You can clean these up while you’re at it.”
Baek Woo and Gung Gibang took the towel and basin respectively, then asked, “Where are you going?”
“Our sect’s Eighteen Dragon-Subduing Palms is one of the most renowned martial arts beneath heaven...
Where are you going?”
“To watch Gyun’s duel.”
I had heard Zhuge Gyun practiced an unusual fan technique using a folding fan.
I figured I might as well watch his duel and broaden my knowledge of martial arts.
I was about to head toward another dueling platform when I suddenly stopped.
“Oh, right.
Who did they say his opponent was?”
The Invincible Divine Sword.
Zhuge Gyun gasped for breath.
When he had first heard his opponent’s epithet, he had laughed inwardly.
It was far too grand a name for some unknown nobody with no reputation.
But...
How has someone like this remained unknown until now?
The hand gripping his fan trembled.
His legs had already lost half their strength, and merely staying upright was becoming difficult.
His eyes ached from straining to follow sword strikes that moved too quickly to see.
The internal energy in his dantian had run dry long ago.
Zhuge Gyun was one of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes, yet he had been reduced to this state while the Invincible Divine Sword remained utterly at ease.
No—he even seemed excited.
“Wow!
You’re the first person I’ve ever seen use a fan technique!
Do you have another one?
Another one?”
At the innocent voice drifting from beneath the deeply lowered bamboo hat, Zhuge Gyun threw away his fan.
